attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Tallahassee, FL

He has experience in a wide range of legal matters, including personal injury/wrongful death, collection matters, securities litigation, state licensure defense, product liability litigation, and landlord tenant issues, among others. Additionally, Ken has represented a number of individuals involved in securities litigation, both on the defense and plaintiff sides. attorneys.name: Lesley Turmelle Abbott
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Satellite Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Lesley Turmelle Abbott is a practicing attorney located in Satellite Beach, Florida. She is a member of the Florida Bar Association and Brevard County Bar Association.

Born into an Air Force family, Ms. Abbott has lived all over the country. Many family members were military service members. Her father was in the Air Force and another family member was in the Merchant Marines. She was lucky enough to spend the latter part of her childhood here in Brevard County. Ms. Abbott attended Satellite High School, Brevard Community College and the University of Central Florida.

Ms. Abbott attended Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan, and received her Juris Doctor with a concentration in litigation.

After graduating with her Juris Doctor, Ms. Abbott worked in Waycross, Georgia, as the judicial clerk for Judge Bount, the Chief Judge for five counties in the southern coastal Georgia area. Upon completing her Clerkship, Ms. Abbott returned home to Brevard County, Florida.

Working closely with her clients, Lesley Turmelle Abbott prides herself on developing a relationship with each one, along with an aggressive approach to exceed each client's goals and expectations.

attorneys.name: Kimberly A. Abrams Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Residential Real Estate Closings (Purchase/Sale & Refinance) Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly A. Abrams, Esq. is a graduate of New York University (1988) and the Shepard Broad College of Law at Nova Southeastern University (1992). She was admitted to the practice of law in Florida in 1992 and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida in 1993. She has been practicing in the area of transactional real estate law for over thirty years and thousands of her clients throughout South Florida have benefitted from her experienced counsel, meticulous document preparation services, and attention to detail.

Kimberly is the founder of the Law Office of Kimberly A. Abrams & Associates, P.A. and its subsidiary title company, Evolution Title & Closing Services, LLC, a full-service transactional real estate law firm and title company. From contracts to closings, we provide our clients with professional, knowledgeable and individualized service. Whether you are buying, selling or refinancing a residential or commercial property, our experienced staff will be there with you every step of the way, working in conjunction with you, your realtor, your mortgage company and/or your lender.

Our business has been built on customer referrals. It is thus our goal at the Law Office of Kimberly A. Abrams & Associates, P.A. and our subsidiary title company, Evolution Title & Closing Services, LLC, to ensure that our clients feel confident and secure when working with us and that our office has provided to them the highest level of service and protection. To this end, we maintain open lines of communication; we utilize the most up to date and current resources available to us to ensure the quality of the title that we are insuring and/or conveying; and we deliver prompt and efficient service to all of our clients.

The Law Office of Kimberly A. Abrams & Associates, P.A. and our subsidiary title company, Evolution Title & Closing Services, LLC, is conveniently located in Hollywood - Fort Lauderdale, Florida, just minutes off of I-95 and the Florida Turnpike. Although we primarily serve the tri-county area of South Florida (Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach), we are able to close transactions on properties located in any county in the State of Florida. In addition, as an agent of Old Republic National Title Insurance Company, one of the largest national title underwriters, the Law Office of Kimberly A. Abrams & Associates, P.A. and our subsidiary title company, Evolution Title & Closing Services, LLC, can facilitate the closing of any property located in almost any county of any state within the United States.

attorneys.name: Aya Abunada Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Palm Harbor, FL
attorneys.bio:
Aya Abunada, Esq. was born and raised in Largo, Florida and knew early on that she was born for a career in law. Eager to advance in her career, she obtained her Associates of Arts degree when she was just seventeen years old. Not stopping there, Aya obtained her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of South Florida while preparing to attend law school at Stetson University College of Law. Before graduating with her Juris Doctor degree from Stetson, Aya became an Associate Editor for the Journal of Comparative International Aging Law and Policy and a member of the Pro Bono Committee for the Florida Association for Women Lawyers. During her time in law school, Aya interned with Gulfcoast Legal Services to help individuals in need at their darkest time. There, she heard the stories of families in crisis and was able to witness the importance of championing the rights of the vulnerable. Her love of family law grew, and she knew she had found her passion.

Since graduating law school, Aya has continued to be involved in the local legal community, which included sitting on the Board of Directors for the Young Lawyers Division of the Clearwater Bar Association. She is also an active member of the Canakaris Inn of Court. In her free time, Aya enjoys spending time with friends and family, frequenting theme parks, watching movies, and checking out new restaurants in the area.

attorneys.name: Albert E. Acuña
attorneys.practice_type: Condominium/Homeowners Associations Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Albert E. Acuña, Esq. primarily focuses on community association law (related to condominium and homeowners’ associations) where he works closely with the board of directors and management in order to ensure all of the association’s objectives are realized and that the association is compliant with Chapter 718/720, Florida Statutes and the association’s own governing documents, while doing so in an efficient and economic manner. In addition, Mr. Acuña vigilantly supervises all collections and foreclosure matters for the association in order to create a positive cash flow for the communities he serves. In the case of any litigation-related matters, Mr. Acuña vigorously defends or aggressively prosecutes any litigation matters on behalf of the association, including, but not limited to, the enforcement of the association’s governing documents, documentary issues, turn-over, breach of contract claims and construction-related claims.

Mr. Acuña also handles commercial and real estate litigation matters, and assists clients with business/corporate matters, including, but not limited to, the formation of any appropriate business entity and any partnership disputes. As a former prosecutor who litigated thousands of criminal cases, Mr. Acuña offers clients their constitutionally protected right to a criminal defense.

Mr. Acuña earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2001 and is a member of the Florida Bar and is admitted to the U.S. District Court, Southern and Middle District of Florida. Mr. Acuña has also successfully litigated on numerous occasions before Florida’s Third District Court of Appeals in cases involving community association law, criminal law and commercial issues. Mr. Acuña was recognized as a "Rising Star" by Florida Super Lawyers in 2014. Only 2.5 percent of Florida attorneys receive this honor each year. Rising Stars are chosen by their peers as being amongst the top up-and-coming lawyers (40 years old or younger, or in practice for 10 years or less) in the state.

Mr. Acuña is confident the level of service and loyalty he will provide his prospective clients will be unsurpassed, and looks forward to meeting with you with regard to your legal concerns or needs.

attorneys.name: Kevin P. Ackerman Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Nationality Law Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kevin became a lawyer so he could make a difference. The firm's mission is to provide all members of the community access to legal representation regardless of position, race, origin, or status. We place an emphasis on representing those who are often overlooked in the system whether poor, persons of color, minority, or immigrant.

Kevin earned his J.D. from St. Thomas University School of Law, where he was awarded a Merit Scholarship, served on the Moot Court Board, and participated in the school bankruptcy clinic. Prior to establishing his own practice, Kevin spent several years at boutique law firms where he represented numerous individuals and companies in complex commercial, real estate, bankruptcy, and personal injury cases. Experienced in high-conflict litigation negotiation, Kevin can achieve your best results through mediation or in the courtroom. Kevin strives to be your attorney for life by using a compassionate and caring approach to the practice of law.

The legal team at The Ackerman Law Firm, P.A. has a proven reputation for providing personalized legal counsel to immigrants and their families in the South Florida area, including Fort Lauderdale and Miami. Focusing on Immigration, Nationality, and Asylum law we bring detailed preparation, professionalism, and expertise to every case. Our staff is knowledgeable about the latest immigration news and USCIS policies, and our results have proven successful for countless clients and their families.

attorneys.name: James Adams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Brandon, FL
attorneys.bio:
Personal injury and workers' compensation attorney James ("Jay") M. Adams provides his clients with the knowledge, support and counsel they need to make informed decisions about their cases. Over the past 30 years Mr. Adams has focused his practice on protecting the legal rights of those who have been injured as a result of the negligence and wrongful conduct of others and because of injuries they sustained in the workplace. Through his aggressive representation, he has recovered millions of dollars on behalf of his clients to compensate them for their losses and damages.

Attorney James M. Adams has always represented the injured and has never worked for the insurance companies. He provides his clients with the knowledge, support, and counsel they need to make informed decisions about their cases. Mr. Adams has an in-depth knowledge of criminal defense, personal injury, and workers' compensation law and the experience to be suitably aggressive when the situation calls for it.

Mr. Adams handles all matters related to claims for damages when injuries have been caused by the wrongful acts of others. We are the liaison with insurers, working to minimize the risk of delay or denial. We prepare and file all necessary documentation and act on your behalf in all hearings or proceedings.

We will help you seek full and fair compensation for all your losses, including wages and income, medical expenses, and physical pain and suffering, and we will fight to get you the resources to pay for essential needs like medical supplies, a wheelchair, vehicle adaptation, handicap accessible housing and personal assistance.

Attorney James Adams has also spent a large portion of his career representing those who have been wrongfully accused of wrongdoing by our criminal justice system ensuring that their legal and constitutional rights are protected through his skill and experience.

Mr. Adams's focus is on client satisfaction. Every case receives equal attention, no matter how large or small, complex or simple. Mr. Adams fights hard to make sure that the individuals he represents receive what they are entitled to under the law.

attorneys.name: Scott C. Adams Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Adams received his Juris Doctorate from the Shepard Broad Law Center, Nova Southeastern University, graduating in the top 5% of his class. In law school, Mr. Adams was a member of Law Review, as well as, the Chief Advocate for the Moot Court Honor Society. He attended law school as a Dean Fellow Scholarship recipient. Prior to seeking higher education, Mr. Adams served in the United States Army and the New Jersey Army National Guard. He is a veteran of the Persian Gulf War, where he received an accommodation for Valor for Action in Combat. He ended his military career at the rank of Sergeant.

"The things that come to those that wait are the things left behind by those that hustle."

Following law school, Mr. Adams was awarded a prestigious Judicial Law Clerk position with the Honorable Melanie May of Florida's Fourth District Court of Appeals. Since completing his Judicial Clerkship, Mr. Adams has focused his practice exclusively on civil litigation. His experience includes employment law (Fair Labor Standards Act, COBRA claims, worker's compensation & nonpayment of wages), general civil liability (UM, PIP & Bad Faith), and appellate practice. Mr. Adams is a member of the firm's employment law and personal injury law sections.

attorneys.name: Jason R. Adamsky
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jason Adamsky is a Senior Associate in the firm's Fort Lauderdale office, where he assists partners in a variety of complex commercial litigation matters. He takes great pride in his ability to expertly guide his clients through even the most difficult situations, using sophisticated and nuanced methods that he has perfected over many years of working in the legal field.

Throughout his legal career and prior to joining the firm, Jason worked on behalf of some of the largest insurance companies, defending their policyholders in various complex and high-stakes personal injury matters. He brings this invaluable experience to every case, ensuring his clients receive the best possible representation.

Mr. Adamsky's primary area of practice is commercial litigation, where he provides exceptional legal representation to businesses and individuals in various disputes. With his extensive knowledge and experience in this field, Jason is committed to achieving the best possible outcomes for his clients, using his unique problem-solving approach and unwavering dedication to their success. His clients can trust that they have a skilled and experienced attorney on their side who will work tirelessly to protect their rights and interests.

In his free time, Jason indulges his passion for all things automotive, particularly American muscle cars. Although a Florida Native, he enjoys traveling and exploring new places. With his exceptional legal skills and dedication to his clients, Jason Adamsky is a force to be reckoned with in the legal world.

Ms. Adelson is a Florida Supreme Court Certified Civil Circuit, Appellate, County and Federal Court Certified mediator, Florida Supreme Court Qualified Arbitrator, specializing in such areas as employment disputes, disability, discrimination and retaliation, civil rights, contract, and complex business disputes.

Ms. Adelson is especially effective with hostile and litigious parties because of her more than 25 years of litigation and trial experience, as a lawyer handling employment law, discrimination, civil rights, and business dispute cases. She is a creative thinker and has a proven track record of negotiating and resolving these types of cases.

attorneys.name: Dana L. Ahmad
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Innovative and dynamic, Attorney Dana L. Ahmad is a strong problem solver and creative thinker who consistently embraces challenges and generates positive results across a variety of legal settings.

Born in Los Angeles, California and raised in Orlando, Florida, Ms. Ahmad takes pride in her Central Florida upbringing. She received her Bachelors of Science in Psychology degree from the University of Central Florida and went on to graduate with her Juris Doctorate from Barry University, Dwayne O'Andreas School of Law in 2019.

While pursuing her undergraduate degree, Ms. Ahmad volunteered her time mentoring and building college plans for at-risk high school students and was awarded the "Providing the Light" mentor award by the Orange County Superintendent for her work in the mentorship program.

In 2012, Ms. Ahmad was awarded with the "Arab American Artist of the Year" award and was featured on the Lebanese American Chamber of Commerce's Next Generation Profile for her work in raising Arab American awareness and promoting international relations, civil rights, and advocacy. Ms. Ahmad is also bilingual, speaking both English and Arabic fluently.

While in law school, she interned and advocated for clients affected by hate crimes, employment discrimination, and civil rights violations at a nationwide non-profit organization. She then interned at a prominent Central Florida law firm for one year where she focused on advocating for clients who did not have a voice of their own. She was then selected to fill one of only eight spots at her law school's Immigration Clinic, where she fought for indigent clients and assisted with their immigration needs.

Prior to joining Morgan and Morgan, Ms. Ahmad advocated for clients at another prominent law firm handling class action lawsuits ranging from unfair business practices to consumer rights.

With a strong passion for defending those who can not adequately defend themselves, Ms. Ahmad uses her valuable experience and insight to fight for her clients who have been injured at no fault of their own.

On her free time, Ms. Ahmad enjoys cruising the Caribbean, traveling internationally, and spending quality time with her family.

In 2012, Ms. Ahmad was awarded with the "Arab American Artist of the Year" award and was featured on the Lebanese American Chamber of Commerce's Next Generation Profile for her work in raising Arab American awareness and promoting international relations, civil rights, and advocacy. Ms. Ahmad is also bilingual, speaking both English and Arabic fluently.

While in law school, she interned and advocated for clients affected by hate crimes, employment discrimination, and civil rights violations at a nationwide non-profit organization. She then interned at a prominent Central Florida law firm for one year where she focused on advocating for clients who did not have a voice of their own. She was then selected to fill one of only eight spots at her law school's Immigration Clinic, where she fought for indigent clients and assisted with their immigration needs.

Prior to joining Morgan and Morgan, Ms. Ahmad advocated for clients at another prominent law firm handling class action lawsuits ranging from unfair business practices to consumer rights.

With a strong passion for defending those who can not adequately defend themselves, Ms. Ahmad uses her valuable experience and insight to fight for her clients who have been injured at no fault of their own.

On her free time, Ms. Ahmad enjoys cruising the Caribbean, traveling internationally, and spending quality time with her family.

attorneys.name: Peter D. Aiken
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
I am a fourth generation native Floridian. My undergraduate degree is in accounting from the University of South Carolina. After graduation, I served in the United States Treasury Department as a special agent with the Intelligence Divisions. The enforcement training regimen consisted of basic training in Federal Criminal Investigation, which included techniques of interrogation, surveillance, photography, forensics and report writing. Specialized training included investigating and prosecuting Federal Criminal Tax Violations. Formal legal training included a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Miami. After joining the Department of Justice, I served for several years as a trial attorney in the US Attorney's Office in Miami, Florida handling a wide range of Federal violations including tax prosecutions, drug prosecutions, firearms prosecutions, and other Federal violations. I left the United States Attorney's Office to join the firm of Cohen and Hogan then located on South Beach. At the time, Cohen and Hogan was one of the best known criminal defense firms in Miami, specializing in complex Federal criminal litigation involving wiretaps, racketeering, and major fraud cases.

In 1974, I moved my practice from Miami, Florida to Ft. Lauderdale, Florida where as a sole practitioner expanded my practice to include State criminal defense. I practiced in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida from 1974 to 2002. During that period of time, I developed one of the largest Federal criminal practices in Broward County and represented people throughout the United States in various Federal venues. Many of these cases were complex multi-defendant conspiracies. My Federal Trial experience includes jury trials in Los Angeles; Salt Lake City; New York City; Cleveland, Ohio; Florence, South Carolina; Georgia; Virginia and North Carolina and handled relating proceedings in other states, including Mississippi; Michigan; Illinois and Massachusetts. My admissions to the Appellate venues include the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, the 4th Circuit Court of Appeals, the 5th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals, as well as the United States Supreme Court. I am at this time a member of the bar of four (4) states including Florida, Colorado, Wyoming and Montana. In terms of trial experience, I have participated in approximately 200 jury trials encompassing almost every conceivable type of criminal violation, including homicide, drug violations, conspiracy, racketeering, firearms violation, securities violation, wire and mail fraud, wildlife violations, income tax fraud, sales tax fraud, employment tax fraud, high seas violations, explosives violations, embezzlement, theft, counterfeiting and forgery, labor law and racketeering violations, bribery and smuggling. Over the years, my clients have included a congressman, a number of judges, politicians, and people from every walk of life from the clergy to the homeless. As a Federal criminal practitioner, I have also extensively represented witnesses and targets before Federal grand juries and in that capacity, over the years, represented numerous organized crime figures involved in gambling, extortion, prostitution, loan sharking, and racketeering.

In 2002, I expanded my practice to include the Southwest Coast of Florida and formed a partnership with Sean C. O'Halloran, a former State Prosecutor in both Charlotte and Lee County. Mr. O'Halloran is the son of a prominent lawyer and a native Fort Myers resident. The combination of my 30 years of experience and his local knowledge and reputation culminated in the expansion of our practice to Sarasota County and Charlotte County. We now maintain offices in all three counties.

attorneys.name: Sherrille D. Akin
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in DeLand, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sherrille “Sherri” D. Bailey Akin, a DeLand native and esteemed attorney, is renowned for her skills as a “fixer” and a “finder.” Over her 35-year career, she has consistently delivered results for her clients, specializing in estate planning, probate, contested estates and guardianships, and family law cases.

From a young age, Sherri was inspired to pursue a legal career, influenced by her father, T. Wayne Bailey, a prominent Stetson professor and community leader. At just 14, she began working in the law office of Bill Sherman, a respected local attorney, where she learned the fundamentals of legal practice and client relations. This early exposure solidified her commitment to the legal field, and she continued to gain experience as a paralegal in college and a clerk in law school.

After completing her education at Stetson University, Stetson University College of Law, and the University of Florida, Sherri further honed her skills clerking for the U.S. Tax Court in Washington, D.C. Despite a brief relocation prompted by personal commitments, Sherri maintained her legal practice in Florida, focusing on estate planning, guardianship, care planning, and fiduciary litigation. Her expertise as a Florida attorney is particularly valued by clients with ties to Ohio, where she is also licensed.

Sherri is adept in complex estate planning and tax law, emphasizing high net worth individuals and asset protection planning. Her Ohio licensure enhances the firm's ability to assist Florida residents with matters related to Ohio.

Sherri holds a J.D., cum laude, from Stetson University College of Law, an advanced tax degree, LL.M., from the University of Florida College of Law, and a B.A. in Political Science from Stetson University. Her father's legacy as the founder of Stetson's Department of Political Science continues to inspire her dedication to the legal profession.

attorneys.bio:
Eliana Aklepi is a litigation attorney handling passenger personal injury, sexual assault, and crewmember cases. Eliana prioritizes working closely with clients, ensuring their stories are heard. Eliana’s undergraduate degree from Drexel University allowed her to work with artists, helping them avoid exploitative contracts. This work sparked her desire to fight corporations with abusive labor practices.

Eliana received her law degree from the Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law. In law school, she focused her studies on international law and labor. Her interest in maritime law stems from her work in Cardozo Law School’s Human Rights and Atrocity Prevention Clinic, the only law student-run clinic in the U.S. working on international human rights matters. In this clinic, she was able to target a multinational mining corporation committing human rights abuses against native tribes in Brazil and report them to the S.E.C. with a petition to cease funding. During law school, Eliana conducted an independent study on seafarers’ rights.

Currently, Eliana is a New York City Bar Association’s International Human Rights Committee member. In her free time, Eliana likes to visit parks and museums.

attorneys.name: Pete V. Albanis
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Panagiotis "Pete" V. Albanis is a partner in the Fort Myers office of Morgan & Morgan. He has been a member of the firm's national Complex Litigation Group since 2009. Prior to joining the firm, Pete practiced in Chicago at a large defense firm where he primarily represented corporate defendants in intellectual property, securities, and breach of contract disputes.

From 2009 through the present, Pete has handled mass torts, products liability, construction defect, and consumer protection matters for the firm nationwide. Pete has been appointed to and has served on numerous committees in several national Multi-District Litigations ("MDLs"), including: Chinese Drywall (MDL 2047, Plaintiffs' Steering Committee); Windsor Wood Clad Windows; (MDL 2688, Plaintiffs' Steering Committee); and Taxotere/Docetaxel (MDL 2740, Bellwether Committee).

Pete has been an integral member of the firm's Chinese Drywall Team, representing hundreds of property owners from 2009 through the present. In 2019, he was a member of the leadership team that represented thousands of homeowners during negotiations with the Taishan Defendants that led to the historic Taishan settlement.

In addition to his construction defect litigation practice, Pete handles other mass tort matters nationwide involving defective products, gross negligence, and strict products liability.

Finally, Pete is honored to represent intellectual property owners in copyright, patent, trademark, and trade secret infringement disputes throughout the country. Pete assists small businesses and individuals in the enforcement of their IP rights. Representative cases include: Vinson v. Nike, Inc., Case No. 09-721 (Western District of Wisconsin) (representing plaintiff in reverse confusion trademark infringement matter); Byrne et al. v. Crist et al., Case No. 10-1187 (Middle District of Florida) (representing Charlie Crist in copyright infringement case brought by musician David Byrne).

Pete is an AV-Preeminent® rated attorney on Martindale-Hubbell. He has been a member in good standing of the Illinois Bar since 2002 and the Florida Bar since 2010. Pete graduated from the University of Chicago with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1999 and from DePaul University College of Law with his Juris Doctor in 2002.

attorneys.name: Stephanie Alcalde
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Stephanie Alcalde is a longtime resident of Central Florida with a passion for law that began in middle school. To help pursue her career goals early on, she attended the Law Magnet Program at Boone High School before earning her Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies with a minor in Criminal Justice from the University of Central Florida. She went on to obtain her Juris Doctor from Florida A&M University College of Law in 2014.

While in law school, Stephanie was actively involved in leadership and student organizations, serving on the Executive Board of both the Student Bar Association and the Hispanic American Law Student Association.

Stephanie has practiced family law in the Central Florida area for over a decade. After being admitted to The Florida Bar, she joined a family law firm before opening her own practice in 2016. Her experience includes handling contested and uncontested divorces, paternity actions, custody disputes, child support, alimony, modifications, domestic violence injunctions, and prenuptial and postnuptial agreements.

Stephanie is deeply committed to her community. Since high school, she has been involved with the Orange County Teen Court program, where she has served from a Jury Adviser and guest Judge. Professionally, Stephanie is an active member of multiple legal organizations. She has served on the Orange County Bar Association Young Lawyers Section (OCBA YLS) Board from 2016 to 2024, including a term as President from 2022 to 2023. Since 2022, she has served on the Orange County Bar Association Executive Council. She is also a member of the Central Florida Family Law Inn of Court, a member of the Central Florida Association for Women Lawyers, and the Hispanic Bar Association of Central Florida.

Stephanie has been recognized as a Rising Star by Super Lawyers every year since 2020 and holds an AV® Distinguished™ Peer Review Rating from Martindale-Hubbell® for her legal professionalism and ethics.

attorneys.name: Kenyetta N. Alexander Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Alexander is a partner in the firm. Kenyetta worked as a law clerk with Mr. Osherow while in law school and then as an associate attorney in the firm for 8 years, and rejoined the firm in 2020.

Ms. Alexander received her Juris Doctorate (JD) in December, 2006 from Nova Southeastern University in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida. She graduated from LaGrange College, Lagrange Georgia, in 1999, with a B.A. in Political Science, magna cum laude, May, 1999, and also received an A.A. degree in Criminal Justice,. She i s a member of The Florida Bar since April 2007, and a member of the Bar of the State of Georgia, since February 2018. She is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, 2007 (including Bankruptcy Court), and the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, 2008 (including Bankruptcy Court).

Ms. Alexander has managed numerous complex cases in state and federal courts including cases in bankruptcy courts, in the areas of business and commercial litigation, consumer finance, condominium and homeowner association law, securities law and labor and employment law from inception through trial. She has handled and participated in all phases of cases, including successfully representing clients at trial as first and second chair in both jury and non-jury trials, as well as arbitrations. Ms. Alexander also has significant experience handling appeals including researching and writing briefs and participating in oral arguments.

Ms. Alexander's work includes, claimants against brokers and broker-dealers for breach of contract and violations of the Securities Act of 1933; partners in actions against partnerships arising under breach of partnership agreement; corporations in actions arising under breach of employment/non-compete and non-solicitation agreements, including obtaining temporary and permanent injunctions against former employees prohibiting competing with and soliciting the corporation’s clients; complex litigation cases in state and federal courts, including plaintiffs in the Multi-District Litigation in the Southern District of New York against Standard Chartered, Fairfield Sentry Limited Fund, et al. (the feeder fund for Bernard L. Madoff Investments Securities, LLC) for breach of contract and violations of the Securities Act of 1933; creditors In re Rothstein, Rosenfeldt, Alder, P.A. (Case No.: 09-34791) and In re Banyon 1030-32, LLC (Case No.: 10-33691) to recover monies absconded by Scott Rothstein; former employees against employers for violations of the FLSA.; employers in actions arising under Title VII; actions before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, as well as other administrative hearings.

Ms. Alexander also has had experience conducting mediations and arbitrations before the American Arbitration Association and FINRA, including prosecuting claims against Morgan Keegan and . defending claims against Allstate Financial Services, LLC. Ms. Alexander also assisted in the handling and successful resolution of a class action lawsuit against Buy Owner, Inc., et al. for violations of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act in the Fifteenth Judicial Circuit in and for Palm Beach County (Case No.: 50 2006 CA 011489MB).

attorneys.name: D. Christopher Alfonso
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
D. Christopher Alfonso is an attorney at the firm D. Christopher Alfonso, P.L., in Tampa, Florida. He takes on cases such as estate planning, probate and trust administration, guardianships, premarital agreements, and estate disputes. He is a qualified Florida attorney and a fourth-generation Tampa native who has spent the past two decades helping individuals, families, and business owners with a wide range of estate planning, probate, and guardianship concerns. He is licensed to practice in Florida.

In addition to his work with local clients, Mr. Alfonso also acts as counsel for a midtown Atlanta family office in assisting their clients with Florida-specific estate planning, business, and real estate endeavors. His experience in wealth planning for a global bank includes consulting on extensive estate and financial plans for high-net-worth clients before he went into solo practice. He has also interned with a federal judge in Florida's Middle District and clerked with a prestigious West Palm Beach probate litigation firm.

Mr. Alfonso earned his law degree from Houston's South Texas College of Law with honors and completed a year of postgraduate tax work in the LL.M. program at the University of Florida. His lovely wife Amy is a fellow attorney, and he takes great pride in being a stepfather to her two adorable children. Finally, he is a devoted Gator alumnus who loves SEC football, Tampa Bay sports, and Texas-style BBQ.

attorneys.bio:
Ala Alikhani graduated from Florida Atlantic University in 2007, with a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Management. He subsequently attended Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad Law School and obtained his Juris Doctor degree in 2011.

Throughout his professional career, Mr. Alikhani has specialized exclusively in defending injured employees in workers compensation cases. Mr. Alikhani has handled all kinds of issues encountered throughout the course of a workers compensation claim. He has attended a countless number of Hearings, Mediations and Depositions throughout the litigation process of different claims. His goal in handling workers compensation claims is that his clients receive the benefits they are entitled to under the law, as well as utilizing a wide variety of negotiating tactics to seek to recover the highest settlement amount.

Mr. Alikhani makes himself readily available to handle all aspects of the claim. If clients are looking for advice on different issues that may arise throughout the course of a workers compensation claim, Mr. Alikhani makes an emphasis on personally being there for his clients.

Applying his knowledge to the workers compensation law, Mr. Alikhani offers his insight and zealous advocacy to represent you in your fight for medical and wage benefits.

There are no out of pocket expenses unless a recovery is made on your behalf. We also offer a free consultation. Contact us to find out how we may assist with your claim.

attorneys.name: Frank J. Aloia Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Frank J. Aloia, Jr., is a senior partner at Aloia Roland, which he co-founded in 2004. The son of a successful Fort Myers attorney, Aloia, chose to make his own way in the legal profession, first as an Assistant State Attorney, and then later as a business and corporate attorney who quickly gained a reputation as a fierce litigator. This skill, combined with an extensive working knowledge of the real estate industry, led Aloia to increasingly focus his practice on multivariate real estate litigation, commercial real estate law, and corporate transactional law.

In addition to bringing his substantive commercial and real estate legal acumen to bear on behalf of his clients, Aloia also offers perspectives and insights that can only come from being a successful entrepreneur.

Aloia and his fellow partners have grown their firm rapidly: from a two-attorney/two-staff operation in 2004 to the twelve-attorney/40+ staff firm of today. Over the past several years, Aloia and his fellow partners have heavily reinvested in their firm to offer the full range of legal services demanded by multifaceted clients. This expansive skill base and resource depth have assisted many of Aloia’s clients to not only protect their business interests but to also achieve consistent and positive momentum.

Involvement & Education

Aloia is President of Atlas Title of S.W. FL, Inc., a title agent for The FUND/Old Republic National Title Insurance Company, a member of the Lee County Bar Association, The Southwest Florida Chapter of the Federal Bar Association, Lee County Real Estate Council, and is a past member of the Attorney’s Title Fund Services Circuit Advisory Council and the Calusa Chapter of Inns of Court.

Within the community, Aloia serves on numerous boards as a director or trustee:

The Bobby-Nichols-Fiddlesticks Charity Foundation

The Thomas Edison & Henry Ford Winter Estates, Inc. (for which he served as Chairman of the Board from 2019-2023)

Board of Directors for Community Cooperative a/k/a “The Soup Kitchen”

School Board for Bishop Verot Catholic High School (alumni class of 1989)

Board of Directors of the Bishop Verot Athletic Boosters

Active parishioner at The Church of the Resurrection of Our Lord Catholic Church.

Aloia was conferred a Juris Doctor at the Florida State University College of Law (1996) and holds a Bachelor of Science from Florida State University (Cum Laude, 1993).

attorneys.name: America Alvarez
attorneys.practice_type: Foreclosure Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
America Alvarez has been an attorney at the Corona Law Firm, P.A. for more than nine (9) years and graduated from the University of Miami Law School in 1987. Although she has practiced in various departments at the law firm, her fields of concentration are bankruptcy and foreclosure. She represents individuals that have fallen into difficult financial times and are trying to have a new fresh start. She also works with homeowners who are trying to save their homes.

In 1987, Ms. Alvarez began her legal career as an attorney-advisor with the United States Department of Labor, Office of Administrative Law Judges. She worked for an Administrative Law Judge assisting with cases and the drafting of opinions. During this time, she not only worked on labor cases but on Black Lung cases which dealt with coal miners, and it was a great honor to work on a project to assist individuals who had worked under very rough conditions for many years.

From 1990 to 2010, she was employed by American division of an international publishing company. During these years, she concentrated on the drafting of contracts, licensing of works, copyright law in different countries, and litigation support for collection, contract breaches, and copyright. In addition, she was very involved with the everyday business operations of the corporations.

Ms. Alvarez was afterward employed for a law firm whose focus was discrimination law in the fields of housing and disabilities. During these years, she was involved in cases against the school board, hospitals and other establishments for failure to accommodate persons with disabilities including deaf individuals and individuals with learning disabilities. In addition, she was also involved with the investigation of large housing organizations who discriminated against individuals based on race, religion, origin, gender, sexual preference, and marital status.

At the end of this year, Ms. Alvarez will have been an attorney for 34 years. During these years, her focus has always been to help her client and give the best legal advice possible. However, law is a field that is always evolving from new laws or statutes to new technology changing it. Therefore, Ms. Alvarez is always learning and will always be learning in the field of law.

attorneys.name: Annalie Alvarez
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Doral, FL
attorneys.bio:
Since 2007, when she began her legal practice in Florida, Attorney Annalie Alvarez has focused on helping clients resolve issues, not complicating them further.

Attorney Alvarez takes an individualized approach to each case, rejecting the impersonal factory approach to the practice of law so pervasive in today’s legal market. She develops a quality relationship with her clients from the first consultation, through the conclusion of their legal case.

Prior to opening her own boutique law firm, Annalie Alvarez interned for the Honorable James Lawrence King, Federal Chief Judge for the Southern District of Florida.

Thereafter, Attorney Alvarez expanded her legal background by working at a law firm which represented international clients against large corporations in the area of personal injury.

For the over 15 years, Annalie Alvarez has expanded her practice in the areas of Estate Planning, Probate, Divorce, Paternity, Child support, and all areas of Family Law including Domestic Violence and Property Insurance Claims.

attorneys.name: Anabel Alvarez
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Sandra Echevarria, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Raised in Miami, Florida, Ms. Alvarez began pursuing her legal career to become a first generation attorney. While in law school, Ms. Alvarez worked diligently to achieve academic success, including earning performance based scholarships and making the Dean's List. Her dedication to her academic goals allowed her to become first a member of the Greenbook Journal and later rise to Editor of the Greenbook Journal.

During her time in law school, Ms. Alvarez focused her studies on issues concerning international law and human rights, ultimately achieving an International Law Concentration. Her focus on these international issues naturally led her to focus on a career in Immigration Law.

Following law school, Ms. Alvarez joined the Law Offices of Sandra Echevarria, and began providing deportation defense to the community. Ms. Alvarez worked defending immigrant rights, defending individuals placed in removal proceedings, individuals facing deportation, families adjusting status, victims of crimes, victims of domestic violence, various waivers and pardons, as well as litigating before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), and filing appeals to the Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA). Ms. Alvarez has proved to be a highly distinguished attorney, frequently arguing and winning cases before EOIR, as well as cases and appeals before USCIS.

attorneys.name: Nicole Alvarez
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Nicole Alvarez P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
As a lifelong Miami, Florida resident, Nicole Alvarez has over a decade of courtroom experience. She received her B.A. from the University of South Florida before graduating from Stetson University's College of Law in 2005. Immediately after finishing law school, she became a prosecutor for the Broward State Attorney's Office. She tried more than 50 jury trials as lead counsel with numerous misdemeanors, differing degrees of felonies, and capital sex battery cases. In the last three years with that office, she was a sex crimes prosecutor.

Nicole then moved on to a private practice where she specialized in Foreclosure Law. As a litigation attorney, she defended the rights of financial institutions. She discovered her passion along with success and continued the same practice to another law firm. By this time, she had a combined number of 70 non-jury trials between the two firms. In December 2014, Nicole went to another firm, where she then practiced Insurance Law. She dealt with PIP and defending insurance companies.

After ten years of practicing law and being confident with her experience as an attorney, Nicole decided to open her own practice specializing in criminal defense and immigration. She believes that everyone deserves fair, competent and skilled legal representation when under charges, facing complex family matters, or deportation processes.

Outside of her career, Nicole enjoys giving back to the community and helping others. For many years, she has been involved heavily in several charities and served as chairperson for the Juntos Foundation.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney, Melissa Alzate received her Juris Doctor from Florida Coastal School of Law in May 2017; she earned a Bachelor in Arts in Legal Studies with a Minor in Political Science from the University of Central Florida in December 2014.

During her time at Florida Coastal School of Law, she received a Research, Writing, and Drafting Certificate; Pro Bono Honors Award; and earned a position on the Moot Court Honor Board through her display of exemplary oral advocacy and writing skills. As part of the Honor Board, Mrs. Alzate traveled nationally to compete at the highest levels of appellate advocacy. She represented Florida Coastal School of Law in the Hispanic National Bar Association Moot Court Competition, where she received Best Petitioner Brief Award. As President of the Hispanic American Law Student Association, Mrs. Alzate focused on promoting the professional needs and goals of law students of Hispanic descent. She also served as a Certified Legal Intern with the Florida Coastal Family Law Clinic and Immigration and Human Rights Clinic. Prior to joining the firm, Mrs. Alzate began her legal career representing clients in matters of civil litigation including: foreclosure defense, debt defense, and bankruptcy.

Mrs. Alzate is a passionate animal advocate. During her free time, she volunteers with various dog rescue organizations in Central Florida.

Mrs. Alzate loves her husband and three rescue dogs; Matea, Judge, and Williamsburg.

Attorney Alzate has a strong work ethic driven by her desire to help others. Her results oriented style and habit of looking at cases from all angles makes her an essential part the team. Attorney Alzate speaks Spanish fluently.

attorneys.name: Timothy G. Anderson Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tim Anderson Jr. was born in Tampa, Florida, in 1979. Tim Jr. is a graduate of H.B. Plant High School, and has spent the majority of his life as a Tampa resident, except for the years he spent away as a "Gator" at the University of Florida.

In 2002, Tim Jr. graduated with honors from the University of Florida with a B.A. in political science. Tim continued at UF where he earned his law degree at the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2005.

Aside from being a "Gator football" fan, while at the University of Florida, Tim Jr. became involved in a number of student activities. Tim was actively involved with the Sigma Chi Fraternity, and the U.F. Interfraternity Council, serving as president of both of those organizations.

During Tim's time in law school, he worked in Tampa during the summer months as a law clerk in the personal injury and criminal practice areas. Tim became a Certified Legal Intern at the State Attorney's Office and tried his first jury trial in his third year of law school.

After passing the Florida Bar exam, Tim served for two and a half years as an assistant state attorney for the 13th Judicial Circuit in Hillsborough County. In this position, Tim prosecuted hundreds of criminal cases at the misdemeanor and felony level. While serving as an assistant state attorney, Tim was able prosecute to verdict over 20 jury trials.

In March 2008, Tim Jr. joined his dad and the staff he has grown up around. He is delighted to further his career by helping those injured in truck and auto accidents and individuals accused of criminal wrongdoing.

Tim Jr. is a member of Florida Justice Association, Tampa Bay Trial Lawyers Association, the Hillsborough County Bar Association and has been recognized as one of the "Top 40 Under 40" lawyers in the state of Florida by The National Trial Lawyers.

Tim Jr. is married and practices in the personal injury and criminal defense areas of law.

During his free time, Tim Jr. enjoys boating, snow skiing and "Gator" football games. Tim has also played the piano since age 4, and loves to entertain a crowd with rock-n-roll style piano performances.

attorneys.name: Timothy G. Anderson Sr.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Timothy G. Anderson graduated with honors from Jacksonville University in 1971 and the University of Florida College of Law in 1974. He grew up in a casualty insurance environment, his father being a State Farm Insurance divisional superintendent.

In 1975, after one year of defending insurance companies, he began exclusively representing individuals injured by the negligence of others. His clients included victims of automobile, truck, premises liability, professional negligence and product liability accidents. Mr. Anderson has been lead counsel in hundreds of personal injury trials and has been Board Certified by the Florida Bar in the field of Civil Trial Practice since 1983.

He has been recognized as a Top 100 Lawyer by the invitation-only National Trial Lawyers and selected for inclusion as a Super Lawyer. Tim has been included in Tampa Bay Magazine as one of Tampa Bay's top lawyers and holds the highly prestigious AV preeminent rating* by Martindale Hubbell.

Professional memberships include The Florida Bar, American Association for Justice, Florida Justice Association, Tampa Bay Trial Lawyers Association, Hillsborough County Bar Association and Master of the American Inns of Court. During his career he has always maintained a policy of mentoring younger attorneys.

In addition to his active trial practice, he frequently lectures and provides expert testimony in matters involving personal injury and insurance law. Topics routinely include civil trial certification, premises liability, automobile traffic reconstruction, proving damages, trial tactics and insurance bad faith.

The state of Florida has more than 93,000 lawyers. In 2013, Mr. Anderson was recognized by the Florida Bar as one of only 221 outstanding lawyers who have achieved 30 or more years of continuous board certification. Only 23 of that number call Tampa home.

During his high school years Mr. Anderson was a dedicated athlete playing a variety of sports, including basketball and baseball. He earned a full scholarship to play both of those sports at the collegiate level. That background led to many years of coaching in a variety of youth leagues in the Tampa Bay area. When not participating, he avidly supports the USF Bulls, Tampa Bay Rays and the Tampa Bay Lightning, in addition to his alma mater.

Tim is a member of American Legion Post 273, Madeira Beach, having served in the United States Army before law school. He is also a member of Palma Ceia Lodge 290 F. & A.M. and the Egypt Shrine in Tampa.

Mr. Anderson and his wife of over 36 years, Carole, have one daughter, two sons and three grandchildren. The Andersons are long-time members of Hyde Park United Methodist Church.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.bio:
Brian M. Andino is a skilled personal injury attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., where he diligently represents individuals who have suffered harm due to negligence, defective products, or unsafe conditions. His practice focuses on high-impact cases, including catastrophic injuries, wrongful death, and negligent security, with a commitment to securing meaningful justice and compensation for his clients.

Mr. Andino earned his Juris Doctorate from the University of Miami School of Law, where he was an active member of the Law Trial Team and received recognition from the HOPE Public Interest Resource Center for his outstanding pro bono contributions. As a valued member of Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., Mr. Andino brings integrity, skill, and heartfelt advocacy to every case, continuing to make a positive impact in the lives of those he serves.

attorneys.name: William C. Anderson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dade City, FL
attorneys.bio:
William Clark “Will” Anderson was born in Morton, Mississippi and raised in Gallatin, Tennessee. Mr. Anderson graduated from Hampden-Sydney College with a degree in Psychology.

Following college, Mr. Anderson enlisted in the United States Marine Corps Reserve, while also attending Florida Coastal School of Law. In 2008, Mr. Anderson was deployed to al Anbar, Iraq where he served as a rifleman and radio operator in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom. During his time in the USMC, Mr. Anderson maintained a security clearance, received multiple medals and awards, and worked for the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA.)

After graduating from law school, Mr. Anderson worked as a public defender in Tampa and as a court appointed attorney in Polk County. For several years, Mr. Anderson worked as a private criminal defense attorney throughout Florida. Mr. Anderson has handled, to varying degrees, thousands of criminal cases. Mr. Anderson’s extensive experience includes successfully defending a number of high-profile media cases; alleged sex offenses; drug offenses; violent crimes; juvenile delinquency; and all manner of violent and non-violent criminal offenses.

Mr. Anderson’s work has garnered attention from several local, national, and international news organizations. Mr. Anderson has been called upon to lecture to other attorneys and law students at both the Tampa Office of the Public Defender and Florida Coastal School of Law.

Mr. Anderson has devoted his entire professional life to defending individuals from the government. Mr. Anderson treats each client and their families with the dignity and respect that they deserve. Mr. Anderson aggressively and diligently defends each case.

Mr. Anderson joined Mander Law Group in 2018. He focuses on criminal defense.

attorneys.name: Amanda Annunciata Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Amanda Annunciata works tirelessly for her clients and has over eight years of experience handling work injury claims throughout Tampa and Sarasota.

Amanda Annunciata is originally from New England and moved to Florida where she finished High School. After obtaining her Bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies at Keiser University, she was admitted to Stetson University College of Law, where she graduated cum laude in 2014. While attending law school at night, Mrs. Annunciata worked full time as a paralegal for the Florida Department of Children and Families, gaining significant experience as a child welfare advocate.

After earning her Juris Doctorate, she litigated dependency cases for the Department of Children and Families. She then became Assistant State Attorney in the Twelfth Judicial Circuit, where she litigated criminal cases, including misdemeanor, juvenile, and felony offenses.

Mrs. Annunciata has been able to parlay her passion for helping others as a trusted worker’s compensation attorney at Berlin Law Firm, where she is well respected by her colleagues and clients. Her professionalism, in-depth knowledge of the law, and excellent communication skills have bolstered her reputation as a formidable attorney in all types of work injury claims.

Her peers describe her as detail-oriented, hardworking, and always well-prepared. This high level of respect amongst her peers earned her recognition as an SRQ Magazine “Elite Top Attorney” in workers’ compensation law for multiple years in a row in addition to being awarded an AV Preeminent Rating by Martindale-Hubbell.

Mrs. Annunciata loves coming to work every day, helping clients stand up to uncaring insurance companies. When she is not practicing law, she enjoys spending time with her husband and three children, as well as doing volunteer work for the Sarasota Teen Court. She is an avid football fan and loves being outdoors.

attorneys.name: Pamela Anselmo
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
With over 25 years of experience, Pamela Anselmo is a trusted Florida real estate attorney, title agent, and business lawyer, helping clients across Florida and beyond with real estate closings, property transactions, landlord legal issues, and business disputes. She represents real estate developers, investors, rental property owners, landlords, and business owners, providing practical, results-focused legal counsel.

Pamela handles residential and commercial property closings, including condominiums, subdivisions, mixed-use developments, and investment properties. As a licensed Florida title agent and closing attorney, she helps clients navigate complex closings, clearing title and survey defects, and ensuring smooth, stress-free transactions.

She also works closely with rental property owners and landlords, advising on property management legal matters, rental agreements, and dispute resolution, including evictions, contract enforcement, and liability management.

Pamela regularly counsels private lenders and investors on funding structures for real estate acquisitions, construction projects, and redevelopment, including transactions involving environmentally impacted properties. Her experience helps clients manage risk and streamline projects from acquisition to sale.

In addition to real estate, Pamela advises closely held businesses on corporate law matters, including contract negotiations, profit-sharing structures, succession planning, and business dispute resolution. She also represents clients in general business litigation, offering straightforward, business-minded strategies to resolve conflicts efficiently.

Pamela’s clients value her clear communication, practical guidance, and fast response times. Whether you’re buying your first property, managing rental units, or resolving a contract dispute, Pamela delivers smart, effective legal solutions tailored to your business goals.

attorneys.name: Kimberly De Arcangelis
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kim De Arcangelis (formerly Kim Woods) has national litigation experience and currently represents numerous employees in matters involving wage disputes, misclassification, retaliation and discrimination. Mrs. De Arcangelis has experience litigating these claims in federal and state courts and arbitration. Prior to joining the Employee Rights Group at Morgan & Morgan, Mrs. De Arcangelis represented employers and insurance carriers and she uses that experience to better server her current clients . Mrs. De Arcangelis has both bench trial and federal jury trial experience.

Throughout her career, Mrs. De Arcangelis has successfully obtained unpaid wages and other damages on behalf of thousands of employees throughout the United States in both single plaintiff and class and collective actions. For example, Mrs. De Arcangelis represented a class of NFL Cheerleaders who alleged that they were not paid for practices, various appearances and other time in Pierre-Val, et al. v. Buccaneers Limited Partnership, LLC., d/b/a Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Case No.: 8:14-cv-01182, United States District Court, Middle District of Florida-Tampa Division. She also represented a class of Road Patrol Deputies and Corrections Officers who alleged that they were not paid for mandatory meetings in Ruddell et al. v. Flagler County Sherriff's Office et al., Case No.: 3:14-cv-00873, United States District Court, Middle District of Florida-Jacksonville Division. However, in addition to standing up to corporations on behalf of her clients, Mrs. De Arcangelis also spends her time serving as the Orlando Division President of the Friends of 440 Scholarship Fund, which is a statewide charitable organization that raises scholarship funds for children of injured workers.

Mrs. De Arcangelis is admitted to the Florida Bar (2006) and in U.S. District Courts including the Middle, Northern and Southern Districts of Florida, Southern District of Indiana, Western District of Tennessee, and Northern District of Illinois.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Manny Arce is a civil trial lawyer that practices in personal injury including wrongful death, medical malpractice, premise liability, and defective products. He prides himself in his aggressive and impassioned advocacy and but does his work in a professional and ethical manner. He is an AV Preeminent rated attorney by Martindale-Hubbell, which is its highest possible rating for both ethical standards and legal ability. He was also selected as a Top 40 Under 40 Trial Lawyer by the National Trial Lawyers organization.

He is a native Miamian and second generation Cuban-American. Mr. Arce received his undergraduate degree at the Florida International University where he earned a Bachelor of Arts with a major in political science. While at Florida International University, he was nominated to the Honor Society of Pi Sigma Alpha.

Mr. Arce received his law degree from the University of Miami in Coral Gables. While at the University of Miami, Mr. Arce was an active participant in various organizations. He held an executive position on the school’s Moot Court Board and was a staff editor on the Race and Social Justice Law Review. He was also selected to join the The Spellman-Hoeveler Chapter of the Inns of Court Honor Society. He received Honors Awards in both litigation course taken and received the Marco A. Vazquez Memorial Scholarship for outstanding skill in litigation.

Mr. Arce is currently a member of the American Bar Association, Cuban American Bar Association, Florida Bar, and Dade County Bar Association. He is eligible to practice in the State of Florida and in the United States District Court Southern District of Florida.

Exclusively representing condominium associations, businesses, people, families, estates, and other legal entities against insurance companies for the wrongful denial or delay of all or part of insurance benefits due an insured. Ms. Arkin handles coverage disputes, matters of policy interpretation, cases where the insurance company recommends a contractor, or chooses to repair the property, matters of benefits calculation, amount of loss, and cases involving alleged misrepresentations in an application, or alleged fraud/arson. attorneys.name: Karen L. Arnett
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Santa Rosa Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
A resident of Miramar Beach, Florida, and native of Valparaiso, Indiana, Karen L. Arnett earned her B.A. in History and Government from Luther College in 1969. She graduated and received her J.D. from Valparaiso University School of Law in 1972. While in law school, Karen was a member of the Moot Court team and earned "The Book Award" in UCC: Secured Transactions.

Karen was admitted to the Indiana State Bar in 1972, and the Florida State Bar in 2002, where she earned the top bar exam score on the February 2002, exam. Honored by the Florida Supreme Court for this accomplishment, Karen was chosen to speak on behalf of the candidates at the Ceremony for Induction of Candidates to the Florida Bar in May, 2002.

Throughout her career, Karen has worked on a variety of legal issues. She now concentrates primarily on Estate Planning, Probate and Chapter 7 Individual Bankruptcy.

Karen is an active member of both the Walton County Chamber of Commerce and the Destin Chamber of Commerce. She is also a member of the Florida Bar Association and Okaloosa-Walton Bar Association. She has also served on the Indiana Regional Planning Commission, Porter County Planning Commission in Valparaiso, Indiana. Karen was also a Porter County elected official. She served as a member of the Porter County Board of Commissioners (county's executive body), and as a member of the Porter County Council (county's fiscal body).

Karen is licensed to practice law in the State of Florida, the State of Indiana, all federal district courts for the State of Indiana, the 7th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court.

Karen is an active member in the choir of the Faith Assembly Christian Church in Miramar Beach and the owner and operator of the Arnett's Gulfside Trail Rides in Santa Rosa Beach.

attorneys.name: Barry Aronin
attorneys.practice_type: PIP Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
I joined LaBovick Law Group in 2014 as the Director of Insurance Litigation. As a West Palm Beach PIP lawyer, I have PIP litigation experience representing injured persons and medical providers in their claims against automobile insurance carriers for failure to properly pay PIP benefits. I earned my Juris Doctorate from the Shepard Broad Law Center at Nova Southeastern University after obtaining my Bachelor of Science in Business Administration from Lynn University in Boca Raton, Florida.

In law school, I was an active member of the Sports and Entertainment Law Society. I had the distinction of being included on the Dean’s List at Shepard Broad Law Center for four consecutive semesters. This gave me a unique insight into representing both Plaintiffs and insurance companies alike and the practical manner and application in which Insurance Law is practiced while attending Law School.

My motto is that every medical provider in Florida deserves full and fair PIP reimbursement from the insurance company. I maximize justice for my clients by aggressively fighting for their rights. I became a lawyer to ensure that all medical providers throughout the State of Florida have the necessary resources to continue providing essential medical services. I truly embrace the “fight to win” core value of LaBovick Law Group. I do not shy away from insurance carriers’ denials and I “fight the good fight” on any and all issues/denials.

Similarly, I have represented thousands of injured workers throughout the State of Florida. I aggressively fight to ensure the Workers Compensation carriers provide medical treatment and lost wage benefits.

I like to stay active in my community. In Florida, I have engaged in disaster relief work at the American Red Cross Center in Boca Raton, Florida. In my spare time, I enjoy spending time with my wife and two children, exercising at the gym, and participating in adult basketball leagues.

attorneys.name: Rossana Arteaga
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Rossana Arteaga-Gomez has an active civil litigation and criminal defense trial practice in both federal and state court. She is a firm believer that to truly be a “trial lawyer” a lawyer must actually try cases and seek as many opportunities as possible to argue in court.

Rossana began 2026 by arguing an appeal before the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals involving a foreign country’s assertion of sovereign immunity under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act. In 2025, Rossana was the lead attorney in a federal criminal case involving an employee of a major international company. The Court acquitted her client after her cross-examination of the government’s main witnesses. In 2023, Rossana was one of the lead attorneys who successfully prosecuted a First Amendment retaliation claim against a sitting City of Miami Commissioner, helping the trial team win a $63.5 million judgment for the clients. Notably, during a short break in that seven-week First Amendment retaliation trial, Rossana tried a separate criminal case obtaining an acquittal for her client. In 2019, Rossana was one of the lead attorneys defending the then-largest healthcare fraud case in the nation in a trial that also lasted seven weeks. Rossana developed the theory of defense on the principal count of health care fraud conspiracy. The jury deadlocked, and so her client avoided a conviction on that count.

Rossana honed her trial skills as a Miami-Dade Assistant Public Defender. In that position, she tried a wide variety of cases ranging from first-degree murder, burglary, and insurance fraud to driving under the influence. Rossana also successfully argued a Stand-Your-Ground Motion obtaining the dismissal of an aggravated assault with a deadly weapon charge. Additionally, Rossana successfully argued motions to suppress and for judgment of acquittal, as well as defended clients in pre-trial detention and probation violation hearings.

Rossana served as a Law Clerk to U.S. District Judge Marcia G. Cooke and U.S. Magistrate Judge Edwin G. Torres in the Southern District of Florida. She has worked at boutique and large litigation firms. Rossana also taught legal research and writing for three years at the University of Miami School of Law.

​Rossana is a Miami native and speaks fluent Spanish. She serves on the Board of Directors of the Friendship Circle of Miami.

attorneys.name: Lily Arslanian
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Lily Arslanian earned her B.A. in International Relations with a concentration in Foreign Policy and Security Studies from Boston University in 2021, and received her Juris Doctor from the University of Miami School of Law as a Dean’s Merit Scholar in 2025. While at Miami Law, she gained hands-on legal experience representing indigent clients as a Certified Legal Intern at the Law Offices of the Public Defender for the 11th Judicial Circuit, and through her advocacy work with the University of Miami Human Rights Clinic. She further developed her legal research and policy skills at the United States Institute of Peace, where she contributed to international legal initiatives focused on critical minerals and global governance.

During law school, Lily served as the Business and Managing Editor of the University of Miami Race & Social Justice Law Review and held leadership roles within the International Moot Court Program. She competed with the Moot Court’s International Criminal Court team at The Hague and at the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris, where her team received recognition for excellence. She was awarded the Director’s Award for her top performance in International State Responsibility, and received the HOPE Public Interest Center’s Exemplary Service Award. Lily is fluent in Armenian and French, and is passionate about traveling the world and exploring different cultures and cuisines.

attorneys.name: Richard Asselta
attorneys.practice_type: Education Law Lawyers in Plantation, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Asselta exclusively focuses his practice to the area of education law issues and over the last ten years has helped to shape this new specialty. Mr. Asselta began his career working for a defense firm that exclusively dealt with criminal appeals and post-conviction criminal litigation. Mr. Asselta has prepared briefs and motions concerning major drug trafficking crimes, criminal conspiracy, and financial crimes, to name a few. He is also an experienced litigator, having tried numerous matters. Mr. Asselta has represented clients in Florida and New Jersey and in numerous federal courts of appeals.

Mr. Asselta's education law practice includes representing the interests of students facing expulsion, college and graduate students throughout the United States facing academic integrity or conduct issues, and fighting for Florida school teachers facing action by their districts and the Florida Department of Education.

For nearly ten years Mr. Asselta represented a public school district, giving him great insight into the process and procedures a school utilizes in dealing with student and teacher disciplinary issues. This opportunity has given Mr. Asselta a unique understanding of the challenges that students face and how the school approaches and handles these challenges. Mr. Asselta's extensive involvement in academic integrity and conduct hearings with colleges and universities has given him unique insight and experience that many other practitioners simply do not have. A critical review of documents and meticulous hearing and appeals preparation are but a few of the ways Mr. Asselta ensures that his clients are provided with the level of services and care that each deserves.

Richard grew up in New Jersey and attended college in Washington, D.C. He attended law school in South Florida where he served as an Associate Editor of his school's Law Review. Upon graduation Richard worked for a firm that specialized in federal appellate and post-conviction law. While there, he assisted in the preparation of appellate briefs and motions in federal courts throughout the country. He then worked on a variety of complex civil matters and represented a public school district.

attorneys.name: Mary P. Aspros
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Tallahassee, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mary F. Aspros was born and raised in the small town of Falmouth, Massachusetts, as one of six children. She moved to Florida in 1989 and put herself through school, first attending Fort Myers Community College and then the University of South Florida in Tampa. She moved to Tallahassee in 1994 and has been there ever since. She is married to Steven Aspros, a prominent Dentist in Tallahassee, and has three step-children: Lisi, Natalia and George.

Mary is a proud Seminole, with three degrees from Florida State University. She finished her BA in Psychology in 1995 and earned a Masters of Social Work in 1997 after completing two externships at the Florida Department of Developmental Disabilities as well as the Leon County Guardian Ad Litem Program. She then entered law school at Florida State, graduating in May of 2000.

During her time at FSU law school, she was appointed to the position of University Defender, providing undergraduate and graduate students with representation before the University in student code of conduct disciplinary proceedings.

Mary also worked for the FSU law school's Children's Advocacy Center (now referred to as the Public Interest Law Center) advocating for low income families in matters relating to education law and social security disability law.

Mary practiced in the areas of Labor and Employment Law for ten years at the firm of Meyer, Brooks, Demma, Aspros & Blohm, where she handled both public and private sector employment matters, while focusing the majority of her practice defending educators before state and local disciplinary boards on both employment and licensure matters.

In 2009, Mary opened and became managing partner of the Tallahassee branch of the Nugent Law Firm, handling Social Security Disability and Personal Injury cases. During her time with the Nugent Law Firm, she represented thousands of disabled people at all levels of the Social Security disability process and personally attended hundreds of social security hearings throughout Florida, Georgia and Alabama.

Mary is so happy to now be working for Morgan & Morgan in the firm's Tallahassee office. Her passion for helping people makes her the perfect fit for our growing Social Security practice.
