attorneys.name: Karina Asvolinsque Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Karina Asvolinsque is an Associate Attorney at Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli & Pratt, P.A.

At the beginning of her career, she represented clients in a wide range of immigration matters, including removal defense, asylum, and petitions for survivors of domestic violence and human trafficking. Karina earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Miami School of Law, where she served as a student intern with the Human Rights Clinic. In that role, she contributed to Shpagina v. Russian Federation, a case decided favorably by the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).

She also co-founded and served as Vice President of the Human Rights Society. In addition to her J.D., Karina holds an LL.M. in Intercultural Human Rights from St. Thomas University School of Law, where she was Editor-in-Chief of the Intercultural Human Rights Law Review.

Her commitment to international human rights advocacy includes speaking engagements and collaborations with Brazilian-American non-governmental organizations on anti-human trafficking initiatives aimed at prevention, particularly for vulnerable populations.

Karina previously served as Volunteer Counsel to the Consulate General of Brazil, assisting Brazilian nationals with U.S. immigration matters. Earlier in her career, she worked for the Consulate General of France in Miami in the Press and Public Affairs Division.

She earned her double Bachelor’s degree in International Relations and Political Science, from Florida International University.

Fluent in Portuguese, Spanish, French, and Russian, Karina serves a diverse clientele with empathy and clarity, guided by the belief that justice begins with giving every client a voice.

M.H. Hildebrandt Scholarship, 2019 - 2020

attorneys.name: DeeAnn D. Athan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
DeeAnn Athan received her Juris Doctorate degree from New York Law School, N.Y., N.Y. in 1983, after receiving her Bachelor of Arts Degree in Education from University of South Florida. DeeAnn began her career as a prosecutor with the State Attorney's Office in Hillsborough County, Florida. Upon leaving the Office of the State Attorney, DeeAnn began a general private practice where she litigated many criminal and family law matters over the course of the next nine years. She is not only an experienced trial attorney, but she is also a well versed appellate attorney having represented clients in both state and federal appellate courts in both civil and criminal matters. She is admitted to the practice of law in the State of Florida and in federal courts including the United States Supreme Court.

After nine years of a successful private practice DeeAnn joined the Office of the Public Defender in Hillsborough County where she supervised other lawyers and continued to litigate serious cases. Ultimately, she became a member of the Homicide Division. DeeAnn is well known for her defense of high profile cases. She successfully represented Walter "JJ" Revear, a twelve year old charged with robberies and later, car thefts. She was lead counsel for fifteen year old Valessa Robinson who was accused of murdering her mother. In that successful defense, Valessa avoided life in prison with a lesser conviction for Third Degree Murder and Grand Theft. Both "JJ" and Valessa were targeted by the local and national medias. DeeAnn was ridiculed by many for her zealous and unwavering representation of these children. DeeAnn has appeared on Court T.V. now TruTV, both as a litigant and as an attorney expert, on 48 Hours on CBS, on Dateline NBC, and on American Justice on A&E.

DeeAnn began with the law firm of Escobar, Michaels & Associates, in June of 2003 where she continues to litigate serious criminal matters. In 2010 she decided to return to the roots of her early practice by joining the Family Law group. DeeAnn continues to use her twenty-eight years of legal experience to aggressively litigate divorces, child support matters, child custody issues, termination of parental rights, dependency defense and domestic violence injunctions.

attorneys.name: Scott W. Atherton
attorneys.practice_type: Fraud and Business Litigation Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Scott Atherton, an attorney with Atherton Law Group P.A., is also Of Counsel to Jacobson Law P.A.. Scott focuses his practice on fraud and business litigation cases, as well as high stakes e-discovery disputes.

After graduating summa cum laude (top 1%) from Nova Southeastern University, Scott subsequently joined Akerman Senterfitt where he handled a number of high stakes litigations. See, e.g., State Farm Mut. Auto. Ins. Co. v. Kugler, 2011 WL 4389915 (S.D. Fla. Sept 21, 2011) (prosecution of RICO, fraud, and deceptive trade practice claims on behalf of auto insurance carriers seeking in excess of $35 million in damages against physicians, surgery centers, and medical practice managers relating to certain spinal procedures performed on personal injury claimants); Yueh-Mei Kim Nutter, P.A. v. Schober, 2011 WL 1474864 (S.D. Fla. Feb. 4, 2011) (defense of New York-based law firm's Board of Directors in connection with claims asserted by former equity partners of the firm); Leor Exploration & Production, LLC v. Aguiar, 2010 WL 3782195 (S.D. Fla. Sept. 28, 2010) (obtained order striking plaintiff's claim seeking over $1 billion in economic damages as a sanction for hacking into a co-defendant's email account during discovery); AlphaStaff, Inc. v. McDonie, 2010 WL 7368045 (Fla. 17th Jud. Ct. Sept. 27, 2010) (prosecution of defendant involved in large scale trade secret misappropriation scheme which was confirmed after forensic computer investigation revealed that the defendant used an external hard drive to make unauthorized copies of thousands of files).

Scott has continued his complex litigation practice since establishing the Atherton Law Group, P.A., including his representation of clients in fraud cases. See, e.g.,Retterath v. Homeland Energy Solutions, LLC, 2014 WL 1515522 (S.D. Fla. Apr. 17, 2014) (counsel for publically registered alternative fuel company in defense of hostile takeover attempt by the company's largest unit holder. attorneys.name: Michael A. Atter
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael A. Atter, J.D., an “A.V.-Preeminent” rated attorney, is a graduate of Florida State University (B.A., Magna Cum Laude, English 1976) and the Florida State University College of Law in Tallahassee, FL (J.D. 1979). He is a member of the Florida Bar and Federal Bar-Middle District of Florida. Mr. Atter joined the Firm as an Associate in 1981 and has served as the Managing Partner since 1996, where he has overseen the growth of the Firm. Prior to coming to the Firm, he served as Assistant State Attorney for the Fourth Judicial Circuit, where he prosecuted juvenile, misdemeanor, and felony offenses, from 1979 to 1981. When he left the State Attorney's Office to join the Firm, he was a Circuit Court Division Chief. At Wood, Atter & Wolf, P.A., Mr. Atter has primarily represented Plaintiffs in Personal Injury, Wrongful Death, and Medical Malpractice cases. A veteran of jury trials and high-end injury cases, he has concentrated in the areas of traumatic brain injury, trucking accidents and complex medical negligence cases. Over the years, Mr. Atter has handled numerous cases resulting in seven-figure outcomes. Mr. Atter also represents clients in Family Law and Criminal Law matters. His civic involvement has included: President of Board for Five STAR Veterans’ Center; Board of Directors, Greater Jacksonville Area USO (2007-Present). Jacksonville Jaycees (Jaycee of the Year in 1983); Vice President and President of the Civic Roundtable (1984; 1985), Board of Directors, First Coast Family Center (2000-2002); Board of Visitors, FSU College of Law (2003-2006).

attorneys.name: Debra Auerbach
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law -- Employer Lawyers in Hollywood, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mrs. Auerbach is an employment attorney located in our Hollywood, Florida office. Prior to joining Gallup Auerbach, Mrs. Auerbach spent several years working for one of Florida's largest law firms focusing her practice entirely on representing employers. During this time, Mrs. Auerbach gained extensive experience practicing in both state and federal court as well as before administrative agencies, such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. Additionally, Mrs. Auerbach has extensive experience providing risk management services to employers intended to minimize exposure to potential employment claims.

Mrs. Auerbach joins Gallup Auerbach as a senior associate representing both employees and employers. Mrs. Auerbach represents clients in all aspects of litigation involving the Fair Labor Standards Act, overtime compensation, minimum wages, equal pay, unemployment compensation, discrimination, harassment, workers' compensation retaliation, whistleblower, and wrongful termination, among other employment disputes.

attorneys.name: William N. Avera (1927
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Gainesville, FL
attorneys.bio:
The 2009 loss of William N. (Bill) Avera was acutely felt not only by his family, staff, and professional colleagues of many years, but by so many admiring members of the North Florida community that attendance to his memorial service numbered in excess of 500 people.

Bill Avera was raised in Gainesville, Florida, in a house that is, ironically, now the present location of the Alachua County Judicial Center. After completion of his military service in the United States Navy during WWII, Bill attended the University of Florida where he completed a degree in Law. He spent his entire professional career representing the people of Florida.

His peers say that Bill Avera possessed legendary skill in the courtroom, with his ability to read people giving him a natural advantage in adjusting his advocacy.

Widely known as one of the first lawyers in the State of Florida to devote his practice solely to helping the injured and survivors of personal injury and wrongful death, Bill Avera dedicated his life and career to aiding people in recovering compensation after tragic circumstances struck.

From successfully forcing railroads to install lighted and flashing signs at crossings in the 1960s, to holding Honda accountable for its negligently designed 3-wheel ATV in the 1980s, his career spanned nearly five decades of service to society.

Bill Avera was a member of the Florida Bar, the International Academy of Trial Lawyers, the American College of Trial Lawyers, the American Board of Trial Advocacy, the American Association for Justice and was one of the first presidents of the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers, now known as the Florida Justice Association.

attorneys.name: Jose Avila
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jose Avila’s practice focuses on advising clients in a variety of corporate, finance, and M&A matters, particularly in connection with cross-border transactions. Jose has extensive experience representing lenders and sponsors in project finance transactions related to the development and construction of infrastructure and energy projects throughout Latin America. He also assists domestic and international clients in connection with the acquisition and disposition of renewable and conventional energy projects.

Jose routinely assists start-ups with corporate formation, operational structuring and with establishing their core suite of commercial documents, including service agreements, sales agreements, joint venture agreements, technology contracts, vendor agreements and subcontracting arrangements.

Relying on his extensive knowledge of a wide-range of commercial transactions, Jose has advocated on behalf of companies in a variety of dispute resolution proceedings. He has substantial experience counseling litigants in international investor-state and commercial arbitration proceedings (in English and Spanish) under the auspices of the ICDR, ICSID and ICC in connection with disputes arising from cross-border energy, infrastructure, M&A and other commercial transactions.

Jose is a graduate of Harvard Law School and has over a decade of experience counseling international and domestic clients. Prior to founding Jun Avila, Jose worked at some of the nation’s premier law firms in New York City, Chicago, and Miami. He also served as an in-house counsel for a leading multinational payments company.

attorneys.name: Jodi Avila
attorneys.practice_type: Appeals Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jodi Avila focuses her practice on appellate advocacy and complex commercial litigation. She represents clients in federal and state appellate courts in matters arising out of business disputes, including breach of contract, business tort, antitrust, and civil RICO cases. Jodi is frequently engaged to handle appeals and to advise trial counsel and clients on dispositive motion strategy, issue preservation, and case positioning at critical stages of litigation.

In addition to her appellate practice, Jodi has significant experience litigating complex commercial matters at the trial level. She has represented clients through all phases of litigation, including motion practice, discovery, evidentiary hearings, and trial, in disputes involving breach of contract, business torts, fiduciary relationships, cross-border assets, and contested trust and estate matters.

Jodi represents clients in federal and state courts and regularly serves as counsel in arbitration and mediation. Her appellate experience includes representing clients before the United States Supreme Court and the United States Courts of Appeals for the Eleventh, Federal, and D.C. Circuits. Earlier in her career, she served as a judicial clerk to the Honorable Adalberto Jordan of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit.

Jodi is actively engaged in the legal community and currently serves on the Southern District of Florida’s Magistrate Judge Merit Selection Panel, where she evaluates and recommends candidates for appointment to the federal judiciary. Prior to joining Jun Avila, Jodi was a litigation partner at one of the nation's premier international law firms.

attorneys.name: Bryan Frederick Aylstock
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action Claims Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio: Personal Injury Lawyer Bryan F. Aylstock earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in history from the University of North Florida in 1992 (magna cum laude), and graduated number one in his law school section at the University of Florida in May, 1995. During law school, Mr. Aylstock was both an associate and a senior editor of the Florida Law Review. While on the Review, he published an article on the case of Fabre v. Marin, 623 So.2d 1182 (Fla. 1993), one of most significant cases to affect the area of personal injury law in Florida over the past ten years. Prior to graduation, Mr. Aylstock received the American Jurisprudence Award in Constitutional Law, became a member of The Order of the Coif, worked as a defense counsel for the University of Florida Honor Court , and was installed as a Teaching Fellow. After completing law school, he was accepted as an Honors Intern at the United States Department of Justice, where he worked for the Director of the Federal Tort Claims Act Division on such high profile matters as the Ruby Ridge and Waco cases. Upon completion of his tenure at the Department of Justice, Mr. Aylstock served as a judicial clerk for the Honorable Roger Vinson, Chief Judge for the United States District Court, Northern District of Florida. Mr. Aylstock is presently licensed to practice before all State and Federal Courts in Florida, having passed the Florida Bar with the highest score in Florida 's First Appellate District. He is also licensed to practice before all Alabama and Mississippi State and Federal Courts, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Illinois, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. Mr. Aylstock is a member of the American Inns of Court, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America, and the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers . Mr. Aylstock specializes in pharmaceutical and medical device defects, having successfully handled thousands of fen-phen diet drug and silicone gel breast implant cases over the course of his career. Currently, Mr. Aylstock limits his practice to wrongful death, personal injury, and class action claims, with an emphasis on cases involving the recently withdrawn anti-cholesterol agent Baycol, the diet drugs fen-phen and Redux, the diabetes drug Rezulin, and phenylpropanolamine ("PPA"), Zelnorm Recall , Avandia side effects, Advair lawsuits, Gadolinium side effects, Fosamax and Tequin.

attorneys.name: Adam J. Azoulay
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Sharon L. Azoulay, PA
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Delray Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Adam J. Azoulay got his professional start in the entertainment industry in 2008, working on a variety of film productions. He is an alumnus of the University of Central Florida, where he received a Bachelor of Arts in Film Production and graduating with honors. He went on to attend law school at the University of Florida, graduating in 2015 with a special certificate in Intellectual Property law, and a pro bono certificate for the free legal services he provided to the local business community. He is a member of the Florida Bar in good standing.

In his legal career, he first worked for a music streaming service, and became well versed in the complexities of copyright code as it relates to music, and in general. He clerked at one of Florida's largest firms, where he was subsequently hired on as an associate attorney. There he helped start-up companies with their corporate formation and intellectual property needs, before deciding to leave a big firm and join Sharon L Azoulay PA.

He has years of experience with corporate law, trademark law, trade secrets, contracts, licensing, publishing, and more. After five years of working in the IP sector, he transitioned his contract drafting skills to a practice in wills, trusts, and estates. Because of his many years of contract drafting experience, he is able to bring a unique approach to drafting wills and other estate documents. He enjoys working in a smaller firm because of the personal attention and time that he is able to give to each of his clients.

attorneys.name: Sharon L. Azoulay
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Sharon L. Azoulay, PA
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Delray Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sharon L. Azoulay was born in Miami, Florida and was educated in Florida schools. She graduated from the University of South Florida with a Bachelor of Arts in Special Education and taught in Miami's inner city. After returning from living in Israel for seven years, she attended the University of Miami and received her Juris Doctor in 1989. She has been handling personal injury claims in South Florida ever since.

Sharon is a member of the Florida Bar and a Certified Circuit Court Mediator. During her tenure as president of the South Miami-Kendall Bar Association, she organized a Diversity Workshop for the legal community. She has recently expanded her firm to include Broward and Palm Beach Counties and is a member of the local bar associations in each of these counties.

Sharon believes in giving back to the community, volunteering for local charities. She helped organize the annual fundraising walk for the Crohn's and Colitis Foundation of America over the past eighteen years and raised funds by participating in seven Team Challenge half marathon races for CCFA. She participated in pro bono activities as a member of her local bar association, such as Law Day in local high schools, educating students about the legal profession.

Sharon is dedicated to managing each case personally, always giving special attention to each one of her clients. She always takes the time to explain the claims process to them and keeps them informed during the handling of their case. She is fluent in English and Hebrew, and can accept Spanish-speaking clients. She enjoys the diversity of her practice.

His experience has helped him obtain relief for his clients, avoiding deportation and successfully defending asylum claims. He has helped eligible clients obtain American citizenship.'

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
George M. Bakalar is a seasoned civil trial attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., where he plays a vital role in advocating for clients impacted by personal injury, wrongful death, and premises liability. With decades of courtroom experience and an unwavering dedication to justice, Mr. Bakalar provides strategic legal representation marked by skill, empathy, and results.

As a Florida Bar Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer, Mr. Bakalar has earned one of the highest distinctions within the legal community, affirming his proficiency and experience in handling complex injury cases. His sustained AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell for more than ten years reflects peer-recognized excellence in legal ability and ethical standards.

Mr. Bakalar's legal foundation was built on academic merit and diverse practice areas. He earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Florida, College of Law in 1988, following a Bachelor’s Degree in Criminology from Florida State University. He also brings expertise from commercial litigation and criminal defense, giving him a well-rounded perspective on the intricacies of the legal system.

Admitted to the Florida Bar in 1989, Mr. Bakalar has consistently fought for the rights and recovery of injury victims. His contributions extend beyond the courtroom through active involvement in professional associations including the American Bar Association, the Florida Bar Trial Lawyers Section, and the Palm Beach County Justice Association. He also served on the Florida Bar Grievance Committee, chairing it in 2009, and is a proud lifetime member of the Golden Key National Honor Society.

Mr. Bakalar's multifaceted expertise, ethical leadership, and relentless client advocacy continue to make him a trusted pillar of the Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A. legal team.

Baker is a highly accomplished personal injury attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., known for his relentless representation of plaintiffs harmed by negligence in cases ranging from car accidents and slip-and-falls to negligent security, shootings, and product liability. attorneys.name: Braden K Ball Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Braden K. Ball, Jr. is a highly experienced lawyer with over 24 years of practice in Pensacola, Florida, in various legal areas such as real estate, estate planning, probate, civil litigation, and Association law. Throughout his extensive career, Braden has gained a reputation as a dedicated and skilled attorney, committed to providing high-quality legal services to his clients.

Braden attended Vanderbilt University for his undergraduate studies and subsequently obtained his Juris Doctorate from Stetson University College of Law. He has spent years honing his legal skills and experience, representing clients in various routine and complex matters. Over the years, Braden has represented buyers, sellers, real estate developers, lenders, and realtors in completing successful residential and commercial real estate transactions and many other areas of real estate law. In estate planning, Braden helps clients create customized plans to protect his clients' assets and ensure that there wishes are carried out in the event of their death. He also assists clients with probate and trust administration, helping them navigate the legal process with sensitivity and efficiency.

When clients are in need of representation in court, Braden assists clients in various types of civil disputes, including contract disputes, real property disputes, probate disputes, and many other civil disputes.

In addition, Braden provides counsel to various homeowners and condominium associations to help them navigate the complex legal issues that arise in managing and governing communities.

Braden is a highly respected member of the legal community, known for his integrity, professionalism, and commitment to his clients. When not practicing law, Braden enjoys spending time with his wife and two children, travelling, and boating.

attorneys.bio:
Kiersten was born and raised in The Villages, Florida. She attended the University of Florida for her undergraduate career and obtained her B.S. in Psychology and her B.A. in Political Science while there. During her three years of undergrad at UF, Kiersten was a member, captain, and then coach of the UF Mock Trial Team - the "LitiGators". While attending undergrad, Kiersten also worked as a news clerk for The Villages Daily Sun and then as a forensic psychology assistant at Community Behavioral Services.

Kiersten then attended the University of Florida Levin College of Law on a full academic scholarship. During her law school career, Kiersten was a Dean's Scholar, Ethos of Excellence Scholar, and earned the book award in recognition of earning the highest grade in her Social Science, Crime, and the Law class. Kiersten additionally had the honor of being accepted as a member of the UF Law Trial Team and competed in that capacity for two years while in law school. Kiersten was also a Levin Ambassador and later served as the admissions coordinator for the Levin Ambassador's program.

Before becoming an associate at Folds Walker, Kiersten was a law clerk for the firm. Kiersten focuses her practice in the areas of family and municipal law. When not in the office, Kiersten enjoys playing endless games of fetch with her dogs, Nala and Moose and coaching the UF undergraduate Mock Trial Team.

attorneys.name: Patricia Baloyra
attorneys.firm_name: Damian & Valori LLP | Culmo Trial Attorneys
attorneys.practice_type: Government Relations Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Patricia Baloyra represents developers and property owners through all aspects of project development, entitlement and enforcement processes, including applications, public hearings, and appeals in both Circuit Court and with the Division of Administrative Hearings. She handles all aspects of interaction with local government administration, including planning, zoning, building, public works, environmental resource, and code enforcement officials. Her interaction with municipal and county administrations, boards, and staff has included negotiating a wide range of issues related to entitlements and code interpretations. She has served as an Assistant City Attorney for various municipalities in Broward, Miami-Dade, and Monroe County. In that capacity, her work has included writing ordinances related to land use, zoning, and code enforcement. She has also prepared and responded to requests for proposal and requests for qualifications, as well as objections to such public bidding processes. Additionally, Baloyra has advised municipal boards when seated in their quasi-judicial capacities.

Ms. Baloyra also has extensive experience representing companies and individuals in a variety of complex litigation involving diverse subject matter, including land use, zoning, and environmental issues, as well as complex commercial litigation, including cases involving contractual, partnership, business torts, fraud, RICO, secured transactions, and employment issues. She is a member of the Florida bar and is admitted to practice before the United States District Courts for the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida.

Baloyra is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell, achieving the agency's highest rating for both competency and ethics.

Baloyra is a Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design Accredited Professional (LEED AP) and has the knowledge and skills to facilitate the LEED certification process for her clients.

She has been named by the South Florida Business Journal as both a "Key Partner" and "Heavy Hitter in Commercial Real Estate" for demonstrated success in her field. She has also been listed in Florida Trend magazine's 2011 and 2013 Legal Elite, an honor achieved by less than two percent of the members of the Florida Bar. She has been recognized in 2013-2018 by the top legal guide "The Best Lawyers in America," published by Woodward and White.

attorneys.name: Michael R. Band
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael R. Band is a former chief assistant state attorney (Miami-Dade State Attorneys Office) and served as a federal prosecutor in the Southern District of Florida.

Mr. Band has been called upon to represent a sitting United States Congressman, the elected Public Defender, and numerous other public officials. He has been asked by judges and leading law firms to represent and counsel clients. He has served and continues to serve municipalities, government officials, and the Miami Dade School Board in the representation of institutions and individuals under investigation or to advance their positions before courts or Ethics Commissions.

Michael is known for his tenacity, innovation, and commitment to his clients. Recognized by his peers he has served in leadership positions with the Florida Bar as chair of its Criminal Law Section and three-times chair of its Judicial Nominating and Procedure Committee. Closer to home he has served as chair of the Dade County Bar Association's Criminal Courts Committee and Judicial Poll Committee as well as on its Board of Directors. Michael has served on the boards of Legal Services of Greater Miami, Florida Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys – Miami, and as chair of the Miami Beach Housing Authority and his synagogue.

Michael was appointed by Florida’s governor to the Eleventh Judicial Circuit Nominating Commission. His representation/advocacy has extended internationally to counseling clients and has successful argued to the Commission De Controle Des Fichiers De L’O.I.P. (Interpol) for the removal of a client from Interpol’s Red Notice List. He has counseled and advocated for a host of Fortune 100 corporate clients: from ATT through Waste Management.

Recognizing that victory for his client may come through skillful negotiation before arrest, that is, convincing the prosecutor that the case may lack evidence or the legal support before an indictment is returned, or charges brought forward or after an arrest or the handing up of an indictment at trial. Michael has tried in excess of one-hundred jury trials. In his home district, as a federal prosecutor, he led the trial team in one of the district's longest trials (approximately five and one-half months) returning verdicts of guilty against twelve defendants on charges of RICO, CCE, corruption, drug and homicide counts; and, as a defense attorney in a four month trial where the jury acquitted his client of two murder counts but finding him guilty of conspiracy - later overturned on appeal. He has appeared in courts from Seattle to Key West, New York to Los Angeles and from Chicago to Houston providing aggressive and balanced representation.

attorneys.name: Ken A. Barlow Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Corey I. Cohen & Associates
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Trial Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ken Barlow was born and raised in Charlotte, North Carolina, and attended both The University of the South and Wake Forest University. He received his Bachelor of Arts from the University of the South, also called Sewanee, in 1985. Ken attended the Cumberland School of Law at Samford University, Birmingham, Alabama, and graduated with his Juris Doctor (J.D.) in 1988. He is admitted to the Alabama Bar Association (1989) and the Florida Bar Association (1991) and is designated by the Florida Bar as a Board-Certified Criminal Trial Expert. This designation indicates that the lawyer in question is recognized as having obtained the highest level of expertise recognized by the Florida Bar in the certification area. Board Certification requires both passing a Florida Bar Board Certification exam, and also requires Peer Review with both lawyers that have practiced against an applicant, as well as with Judges before whom the successful applicant has been lead counsel in a specified number of jury trials.

Ken Barlow opened his own law practice in Birmingham, Alabama in 1989. He practiced both criminal and family law and appeared in both State and Federal Courts. He was admitted to the Northern District Court of Alabama in 1989. Ken then moved to Cocoa, Florida, where he worked for the Law Firm of Daniel Ciener. Ken next moved to Orlando, Florida, where he became a State Prosecutor in the Ninth Circuit in Orange County, Florida. While serving the citizens of Orange County as an Assistant State’s Attorney for nine and a half years, Ken prosecuted felony and misdemeanor cases. He served in the Sex Crimes Unit, the Felony Trial Bureau, the Misdemeanor Trial Bureau, the Traffic Trial Bureau, and the Intake Bureau as well. While assigned to the trial divisions at the State Attorney’s Office, Ken was in Court, arguing cases, on a nearly daily basis.

In April of 2001, Ken Barlow left the Ninth Circuit State Attorney’s Office and took a position at the Law Firm of Jaeger & Blankner, P.A., a local law firm that specialized in Criminal Trial Defense. It was during his eight-year tenure at Jaeger & Blankner as a Criminal Trial Lawyer that Ken sat for Board Certification and became a Board-Certified Criminal Trial Expert. At Jaeger & Blankner, Ken appeared in various Felony and Misdemeanor Courts representing clients in the Central Florida area and beyond, and successfully tried many cases during his tenure with the Firm. In Alabama, Ken was admitted to the United States District Court for the Northern District of Alabama and is admitted to the United States Court for the Middle District of Florida.

Ken Barlow was first elected to the County Court Bench in August 2008 and was sworn in to his first term on the Bench in January 2009. During his first term, Ken has served in the criminal division, presiding over criminal jury trials, as well as a two-year stint in a Specialized Division hearing Initial Appearances and related matters at the Orange County Jail. As is the case with all serving Judges in the Ninth Circuit, Ken has also served as the Emergency Duty Judge each year, handling both Felony and Misdemeanor matters.

Ken is happily married and resides in Orange County with his wife Elizabeth and stepson Nicholas.

After leaving the Bench on January 5, 2015, Ken Barlow opened his own law practice, serving clients in State and Federal Courts in criminal law-related matters in Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Volusia, Brevard, Lake, Sumter, Marion, and Flagler Counties in Florida.

On November 1st, 2019 Ken brought his 30-plus years of experience to the Law Firm of Corey Cohen, where he continues to represent criminal Defendants in cases in both State and Federal Courts.

Honors

Florida Bar Board Certified, Criminal Trial Law, 2008 to present

Tendered and Accepted as Expert, Bankruptcy Court, Middle District of Florida

Conducted in excess of 70 jury trials

NCAA Athlete in College, Wrestling

attorneys.name: Brett C. Barner
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
Principal Attorney Brett C. Barner is a native Floridian. Born and raised in Palm Beach Gardens, Brett attended The Benjamin School from kindergarten through 12th grade. After a brief stint at Washington & Lee University in Lexington, Virginia, where he played football, Brett graduated from The University of Florida with a degree in business. Excelling academically, Brett put himself through law school at Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad Law Center. During law school, he supplemented his education by clerking at Freeman Barner & Associates, P.A.

Unlike many attorneys, Brett did not go directly to law school upon completing his undergraduate studies. Instead, he gained extensive sales, management, and leadership experience during his highly successful years spent with Fidelity Federal Bank & Trust (now PNC Bank) and e-Numerate Solutions, Inc. (a software company located in McLean, Virginia). This real-world business experience informs his approach to the practice of law. Brett Barner is well-rounded, immediately at ease with clients, fellow attorneys, and judges. His is a refreshingly pragmatic and transparent approach to client service and legal representation.

Brett concentrates his practice predominately in the areas of estate, trust, guardianship, and fiduciary litigation. He has helped clients obtain fantastic results in the most complicated cases, with some cases involving hundreds of millions of dollars in assets. Brett also represents commercial clients in litigation related to real estate and in other business disputes. Brett Barner has successfully represented clients on appeals before the Fourth District Court of Appeal and in federal court as a member of the US District Court Southern District of Florida.

Brett Barner holds the prestigious AV Preeminent® rating from Martindale-Hubbell. The AV Preeminent® rating evidence his peers’ ranking of him as holding the highest level of professional excellence. An AV Preeminent® rating is Martindale’s highest possible peer review rating and considers the ability and ethics of the lawyer as well as confidential opinions of members of the bar and judiciary. The honor is bestowed upon those lawyers, who exude extraordinary legal capability and adhere to strict ethics.

Brett Barner is a graduate of the prestigious Florida Fellows Institute of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel (ACTEC). He is an active member of the Florida Bar Real Property, Probate, and Trust Law section (RPPTL), participating in the discussion and drafting of new legislation while attending their quarterly meetings around the state. He is a member of the RPPTL’s guardianship committee, probate procedure committee, real property litigation committee, and regularly attends the probate litigation, trust law, and other committee meetings. He has served as the co-chair of the Palm Beach County Bar Association (PBCBA) Estate and Probate CLE Committee and as the co-chair of the Probate Committee of the Bench-Bar Conference, which is an annual conference between attorneys and probate judges. He is also a member of the PBCBA Elder Law and Probate/Guardianship Practice committees.

Brett serves on the Board of Directors for the North County Section of the Palm Beach County Bar Association and is a former member of the esteemed American Inns of Court – The Craig S. Barnard American Inn of Court LIV in West Palm Beach (local chapter). The American Inns of Court are designed to improve the skills, professionalism, and ethics of the bench and bar and have been endorsed by the Conference of Chief Justices and the Judicial Administration Division of the ABA. Members hold professionalism and ethics in the highest regard and strive to promote these ideals throughout our legal community.

Principal Attorney Brett C. Barner stewards Barner & Barner as the living professional legacy of Freeman Warren Barner, Jr.

attorneys.name: Freeman W. Barner Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
The late Freeman Warren Barner, Jr. was a true and consummate southern gentleman. This was a defining characteristic of the man and the attorney. A perfectionist, his fingerprints remain clear on the firm that, today, still bears his name.

Freeman Warren Barner, Jr. was born and grew up in the small town of McKinney, Virginia. After attending Randolph Macon College located in Ashland, Virginia, he entered the military. As a Captain in the U.S. Army, he was stationed at the famed Presidio, a now decommissioned military base in San Francisco. Following service, Freeman used the G.I. Bill to attend law school at the University of Florida. There, he excelled academically, becoming Executive Editor of the University of Florida Law Review, and graduating with honors. He was also named to the Order of the Coif for high attainments in the study of law.

In 1973, Freeman joined the prestigious Cromwell Remsen Firm and was soon the sole litigator and a partner. John D. MacArthur, who founded Palm Beach Gardens, was counted among his many prominent clients. Following Cromwell, he founded Freeman Barner & Associates, P.A. In 2014 the firm name changed to Barner & Barner, P.A. when his son, Brett C. Barner, became his partner.

Outside the practice of law, Mr. Barner assisted in the founding of The Benjamin School, where all his children attended. He served passionately on the school’s board of directors for 25 years. For eleven of those years, he served as the board’s Chairman and President.

Freeman W. Barner, Jr. achieved an AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest possible peer review rating that considers the ability and ethics of the lawyer as well as confidential opinions of members of the bar and judiciary. This singular honor is bestowed upon lawyers who exude extraordinary legal capability and adhere to strict ethics during their practice of law.

Mr. Barner handled cases throughout Florida in state and federal courts. He enjoyed admission to the Florida Bar, all U.S. District Courts within Florida (Southern District, Middle District and Northern District), the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and the United States Supreme Court.

Our firm today is a direct reflection of Freeman W. Barner, Jr.’s commitment to build a law practice defined by excellence and driven by attorneys and a legal staff determined to do their very best by every client entrusted to their care and counsel.

attorneys.name: Scott C. Barnes
attorneys.firm_name: Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
A fierce advocate for his clients, no matter the severity of challenges they face, Scott Barnes fights tooth and nail to get them the compensation they deserve for the injuries they have had to endure due to no fault of their own. From the law office of Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes in Pensacola, Florida, he serves residents throughout the surrounding region in a wide variety of complex legal matters involving mesothelioma/asbestos claims, motor vehicle accidents, medical malpractice, catastrophic injuries and wrongful death, among many others.

Mr. Barnes completed his undergraduate studies in 2003, graduating summa cum laude with his Bachelor of Science degree in criminology from Florida State University. He went on to attend the University of Florida Levin College of Law, where his academic prowess and acumen became evident early on through his inclusion in the dean’s list and as a finalist of the National Civil Rights Trial Competition in New York. He received his Juris Doctor magna cum laude in 2007, and in the same year, he obtained his license to practice law across all Florida state courts. He later became admitted to practice before the United States District Courts for the Northern and Middle Districts of Florida.

A true consummate professional through and through, Mr. Barnes understands the emotional frustration his clients endure on a daily basis. He utilizes his unwavering work ethic and meticulous focus to provide his clients with an opportunity to take back the reins of their lives after having it briefly derailed. He stays actively involved within his legal community, maintaining close affiliations with organizations such as The Florida Bar, the Florida Justice Association, the Escambia-Santa Rosa Bar Association and Multimillion Dollar Advocates Forum.

attorneys.name: Crystal Barranco Garcia Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Miami Lakes, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mrs. Barranco Garcia was born in Cuba and came to the United States at the age of 14. Arriving at this country without speaking English Crystal made it her mission to achieve her dreams. She started learning English in 9th grade at Westland High School, and by her junior year she was earning Cambridge ACE certifications and taking honors classes. She graduated with highest honors from Miami-Dade college with an Associate’s degree in Psychology. She later earned a Bachelor’s degree in Political Science as well as a minor in International Relations at Florida International University where she graduated cum laude. She also recently graduated cum laude from St. Thomas University College of Law with her juris doctor degree. Crystal worked for many years in the insurance field and now uses that knowledge in the personal injury field.

She enjoys philanthropic work such as serving in her local church, fundraising for kids in Cuba and fundraising for assistance after natural disasters. She continues visiting Cuba and helping people in need. She has a passion for teaching others what she has learned and teaching others that their dreams can always become a reality.

Mrs. Barranco Garcia is fluent in English and Spanish and licensed to practice law in the state of Florida.

attorneys.name: José Barreiro
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
SENIOR TRIAL ATTORNEY

Prior to joining MANEY | GORDON Trial Lawyers, José A. Barreiro, founded the José A. Barreiro Law Firm, P.A., and has been a trusted advocate for clients in the Tampa area since 1997. With almost three decades of experience handling a wide range of legal matters from personal injury claims like traffic collisions and workplace injuries to representing individuals facing criminal charges, José has earned a reputation as a fierce trial lawyer. His proven track record of success in court is matched by his unwavering tenacity, expertise, and commitment to his clients’ best interests.

A graduate of Mercer University’s Walter F. George School of Law, José brings an unparalleled combination of legal knowledge, strategic thinking, and courtroom skills to each case. He is admitted to practice before any trial court in the State of Florida, the Supreme Court of Florida, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, and the U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida. In fact, he has been a Florida Supreme Court Mediator since 2006 and Arbitrator since 2019. His credentials, coupled with his recognition as an AV Preeminent® attorney, reflect his standing as one of the top lawyers in the region. He is also a recognized Martindale Hubbell Client Champion Platinum award winner, a testament to his commitment to delivering excellent service and results.

In addition to his legal practice, José is an active member of several prestigious legal organizations, including the American Bar Association, the National Trial Lawyers Association, Florida Bar Association, Florida Justice Association, the Hillsborough County Bar Association, and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

BACKGROUND

José is deeply connected to the Tampa community, being a 4th-generation native of the area with Cuban heritage. His family’s legacy of hard work and dedication informs his approach to law, and he takes great pride in helping his neighbors navigate the legal challenges they face. His ability to speak fluently in Spanish allows him to communicate and serve the Hispanic community as well. Over the years, José has built a diverse client base across the State of Florida.

Outside of his practice, José enjoys spending time with his family. He is married to Martha, a Hillsborough County high school teacher, and they have two daughters and a son. Despite his busy professional life, José makes time with his family for outdoor activities, including boating, biking, and golfing.

HONORS AND AWARDS

Rated AV Preeminent by Martindale Hubbell, the highest rating an attorney can obtain in the areas of legal ability and ethical standards.

Selected for inclusion in The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100. This is an invitation-only organization composed of the premier trial lawyers from each state in the nation who meet stringent qualifications as civil plaintiff and/or criminal defense trial lawyers. Selection is based on a thorough multi-phase process which includes peer nominations combined with third-party research. Membership is extended solely to the select few of the most qualified attorneys from each state who demonstrate superior qualifications of leadership, reputation, influence, stature and public profile.

attorneys.name: Stacey L. Bartlett Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Steven J. Glaros & Associates
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
As a long-term Tampa Bay area resident, Stacey Bartlett attended the University of South Florida where she received a full scholarship and graduated with her B.A. cum laude. She then worked her way through law school and earned her law degree from Stetson University College of Law, which is recognized as one of the top schools in the country for trial advocacy. There she participated in the client counseling team and competed nationally as a member of the dispute resolution team.

After graduating in 2004, Stacey began working for a Fortune 100 company and spent close to a decade practicing in corporate America. She has benefited from numerous leadership, management, and relationship-building courses during her tenure and has been awarded recognition for her performance, collaboration and negotiation skills, and leadership in difficult situations. Stacey’s real-world experience gives her the ability to look outside the box and bring a different perspective to her client’s cases. She is able to combine her knowledge of the criminal justice system with this experience to earn results for her clients.

Since then, Stacey has become a member of the Clearwater Bar Association, the Pasco Bar Association, the Florida Association for Women Lawyers, and has been admitted since 2014 in Florida. In 2017, she opened her own firm where she solely practices criminal defense. Stacey is a full-time wife, mother of two beautiful children, and criminal defense attorney.

“Since I was 8 years old, I have always wanted to be an attorney. I’ve always been passionate about helping others, especially those who have a feeling of helplessness. Fighting for other people is in my DNA. I truly believe in seeking justice in ALL circumstances; this means helping people to understand their rights, fighting to ensure those rights are intact, and making sure that the criminal justice system doesn’t overwhelm my clients. I believe that people deserve second chances, that a mistake shouldn’t define anyone, and that a label such as “criminal” shouldn’t become anyone’s identity. Because of this, I work tirelessly to combine compassion, zeal, and integrity in my practice.”

attorneys.name: Andrew Baskin
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accident Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
With over a decade of experience, Andrew (“Drew”) Baskin has built a reputation as a dedicated and skilled advocate for individuals and families affected by personal injury and wrongful death. He has successfully represented clients in a wide variety of cases, earning respect for his depth of knowledge, compassionate approach, and results-driven strategies.

Interact with your attorney, not some case manager! It’s YOUR case and Mr. Baskin understands this. Mr. Baskin believes in personalized attention, honest communication, and client interaction are all keys to achieving the best possible results. Your primary contact regarding YOUR case will be Mr. Baskin, not some case manager or paralegal.

Let Mr. Baskin’s experience work for you. Mr. Baskin’s experience encompasses a broad range of personal injury, wrongful death and insurance coverage matters, including:

Automobile Accidents - Whether it’s a rear end collision, complex multi-vehicle collision or a pedestrian accidents, Mr. Baskin has helped clients recover compensation for medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering. Once retained, Mr. Baskin moves swiftly to preserve and develop critical case winning evidence which often disappears with the passage of time.

Semi Truck Accidents - Is your attorney familiar with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (“FMCSR”) and how they apply to your case? You better hope they are! Mr. Baskin has successfully handled cases involving semi-truck collisions by applying the FMCSR.

Slip and Fall - Mr. Baskin understands the complexities of premises liability law. Whether your fall happened in a grocery store, parking lot, apartment complex, or workplace, he knows how to build a strong case by moving fast to preserve evidence, consult with medical professionals, and formulate a strategy to secure the compensation you deserve.

Product Liability - Mr. Baskin has taken on major manufacturers and distributors, helping obtain compensation for those harmed by defective or dangerous products.

When not practicing law, Drew enjoys spending time with his wife and three young children.

If you or a loved one has been injured, trust Mr. Baskin to provide experienced, compassionate, and effective representation every step of the way.

attorneys.name: H. Scott Bates
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Scott Bates was born January 19, 1956, in Frankfurt, West Germany. He received his B.A. in 1978 and his J.D. in 1981 from the University of Florida where he was a member of the Alpha Tau Omega fraternity. He is admitted to practice in both the United States District Courts of the Southern and Middle Districts, as well as the U.S. Court of Appeals, 11th Circuit, as well as being admitted to practice in Tennessee since 2000.

Mr. Bates began practice in 1981 with his father, Richard W. Bates, a well-known Central Florida trial lawyer. In 1987 the firm of Bates & Bates merged with Mateer and Harbert, becoming Mateer, Harbert & Bates. From 1987 through 1992, Mr. Bates was practicing almost exclusively medical malpractice defense for Orlando Regional Medical Center. In 1992 Mr. Bates left that firm and joined Morgan & Morgan as one of its four equity partners. Since 1992, Morgan & Morgan has grown from a seven- (7) lawyer plaintiffs' firm to its current size as the state's largest plaintiffs' personal injury firm. The firm has offices in Orlando, Tampa, Jacksonville, Fort Myers, Fort Lauderdale, Daytona Beach, Kissimmee, Winter Haven, St. Petersburg, Sarasota, Lakeland, Naples, Tallahassee, The Villages, Tavares, and West Palm Beach, as well as in Memphis and Nashville, Tennesse; Jackson, Mississippi; Atlanta and Columbus, Georgia; Lexington, Kentucky; and New York City; employs more than 700 attorneys, thousands employees, and is now recognized as the largest plaintiffs firm in the country. He is also Vice President and General Counsel of Legends Sports Management Group, and a certified Players Agent by Major League Baseball. Legends currently represents over 40 professional baseball players, including eight current major leaguers.

In 1989, at the age of 32, he was one of the youngest lawyers in Florida to become a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer. He is also Board Certified as a Civil Trial Lawyer by the National Board of Trial Advocates. In 1989, he was the youngest of 35 trial lawyers selected to become Charter Members of the Central Florida Chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates, a select organization of Plaintiff and Defense Trial Lawyers whose selection process is by substantial trial qualification. Mr. Bates has been an AV rated lawyer by Martindale Hubbell for over 25 years.

Mr. Bates is a recognized and frequent lecturer, both to physicians and attorneys, in the area of medical malpractice litigation, peer-review privileges, and medical records law. He has a well-recognized expertise in the evaluation, litigation, and trial of failure to diagnose cancer cases. He has tried to verdict in excess of 100 medical malpractice cases, and has participated as Appellate counsel in over 15 reported cases, including the often cited Florida Supreme Court decision in Amente v. Newman, M.D. In 1996, he received what was believed to be the largest Plaintiff's medical malpractice verdict in Seminole County's history in the Amente case.

Mr. Bates is also involved in civic activities. From 1995-1999, Mr. Bates was a member of the Board of Directors of the Metro Orlando Unit of the American Cancer Society. In 1996 and 1997, he additionally was the Chairman of the Cancer Society's Income Development Committee, its chief fundraising arm, and in 1997 was their Treasurer as well. In 1996 he founded the Orlando Invitational Team Golf Championship, a charity fundraiser for the Metro Orlando Unit, serving as Tournament Chairman. Mr. Bates currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Florida Sports Hall of Fame and was the Chairman of the 2019 Hall of Fame Induction Gala in Orlando. In 2011, he became a minority owner of Orlando City SC of Major League Soccer.

Mr. Bates was married July 10, 1982, to his wife, Terri. They reside in Orlando with their four children, Rick, Jaclyn, Will and Tori. His sons Rick and Will are also attorneys with Morgan & Morgan. Rick is a Medical Malpractice lawyer while Will works with our Personal Injury team. His daughter, Jaclyn, also works with the firm as a legal assistant.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Richard W. Bates is an Orlando native. After graduating from the University of Richmond in Virginia, Mr. Bates received his juris doctorate from Stetson University's College of Law, an institution that specializes in the grooming of trial lawyers. Mr. Bates began his career at Morgan & Morgan, P.A. pursuing claims ranging from consumer product cases to heavy truck tire and vehicle cases against some of the largest manufacturers both in the United States and abroad. Since then, Mr. Bates has handled premises liability cases, automobile accident cases, and medical device cases, with a current emphasis on medical malpractice cases. Over his years at Morgan & Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Bates' proudest accomplishment as a lawyer is the millions in verdicts and settlements he has obtained on behalf of his clients. In 2016, Mr. Bates became a partner, and is honored to be a part of a firm dedicated to fighting for justice in and out of the courtroom.

Mr. Bates is admitted to practice in every circuit in the State of Florida, as well as the Southern and Middle Districts. He is a member of the Florida Justice Association, the Florida Bar Association, and the American Association for Justice. Mr. Bates currently lives with his wife Leanne, a prosecutor, their son Parker, and their two dogs, Cooper and Ellie.

attorneys.name: Tom Baugher
attorneys.practice_type: Sex Crimes Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
After growing up in Pennsylvania, I attended college at Johns Hopkins University. At Johns Hopkins, I was a member of the Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) and was captain of the football team. Upon graduation, I received a commission as an officer in the Army Reserve and an NCAA postgraduate grant to attend graduate school. Following graduation, I attended the University of Pennsylvania Law school in Philadelphia. During my time at Penn, I concentrated in criminal law and national security law. While in law school, I interned at the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania and for the Pennsylvania Institutional Law Project (a prisoners' rights legal aid nonprofit).

In 1996, I graduated from law school and became a member of the Pennsylvania Bar and New Jersey Bar. I worked for a large Philadelphia law firm before fulfilling my career ambition of becoming an FBI Agent.

After graduating from the FBI Academy, I served in Newark, New Jersey, San Juan, Puerto Rico, Tampa, Florida, Washington D.C., and Sarasota, Florida.

In addition to various supervisory assignments, I was an Assistant Inspector-in-Place, member of the FBI's Shooting Review Group and the FBI's Compliance Inspection Teams, Crisis Management Coordinator, SWAT Senior Team Leader, and Liaison to the Department of Homeland Security.

During my 25-year career with the FBI, I investigated drug trafficking organizations, violent gangs, white collar criminals, corrupt public officials and terrorists.

I have instructed police officers on federal civil rights/color of law matters, and hate crimes. Additionally, I served as a police instructor, firearms instructor, defensive tactics instructor, tactical instructor, medical instructor, and active shooter response instructor for patrol officers.

My last assignment before retirement was as the Supervisor of the Sarasota, Florida office and Program Coordinator for Economic Crimes and Intellectual Property Crimes in the Tampa Division.

In addition to the law, I currently use my skills and experience as a consultant for a non-profit organization. In this capacity, I administer an all-hazards security program that provides consultations, training, threat and vulnerability risk assessments, and threat mitigation.

I am also an Adjunct Professor of cybercrime at the University of South Florida (USF).

attorneys.name: Michael V. Baxter
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Injury Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael V. Baxter is a partner with Lesser, Landy, Smith and Siegel, PLLC who works in the West Palm Beach office and focuses his practice on representing those who have been catastrophically injured due to medical negligence.

Michael began his career as an Assistant State Attorney in Miami-Dade County. During his time as a prosecutor, Michael tried over 70 jury trials and prosecuted some of the county’s most dangerous criminals while serving in the career criminal unit.

Michael then spent the next 16 years defending hospitals and health care providers in medical negligence cases. In 2015, Michael joined a local Plaintiff’s personal injury firm where he headed up the firm’s medical malpractice department representing individuals and families who suffered catastrophic injuries as a result of medical malpractice. In the 10 years he spent as the firm’s lead medical malpractice attorney, Michael obtained the two largest settlements in the firm’s 47-year history. He also obtained a favorable verdict on behalf of every medical malpractice client he represented at trial, including multiple seven-figure verdicts.

Michael has received numerous awards including the National Trial Lawyers Top 100 Lawyers; Florida Super Lawyers; Top Attorney in Medical Malpractice and South Florida Legal Guide’s Top Attorney. He obtained a Top 5 Medical Malpractice Verdict in Florida in 2024. In 2020, Michael obtained the 7th largest medical malpractice in the United States (2nd largest in Florida in 2020). In 2017, he obtained the 20th largest medical malpractice verdict in Florida.

A native of Miami, Florida, Michael attended Florida State University and graduated with a degree in finance. He earned his Juris Doctorate from Nova Southeastern University and was admitted to The Florida Bar in 1996.

Michael is married to his wife of 22 years, Helene, with whom he has identical twin daughters, Madisen and Maysen.

Michael Beane joined Moore Ingram Johnson & Steele in 2015 and is the managing partner of the Jacksonville Office. Mike continues to devote his legal career to defending the rights of Insurance Carriers, Adjusters, and Employers in the area of Workers Compensation Defense.

Mike lives in Jacksonville with his wife and two sons. He enjoys spending time with his family and friends, watching his sons play football, baseball and tennis along with cheering on the Florida Gators.

attorneys.name: Marcos Beaton
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Marcos Beaton, Jr has successfully represented thousands of clients in both federal and state courts across the country. He began his career at the Miami-Dade Public Defender’s Office, after which he went to work with one of the nation’s best criminal defense lawyers, Roy Black, eventually becoming Roy Black’s partner. Mr. Beaton opened his own firm in 2017.

Mr. Beaton is also a highly respected teacher of criminal trial practice. He has been an adjunct professor at the University of Miami School of Law since 2011, where he co-teaches a trial-intensive class with his former law partner, Roy Black. Mr. Beaton is also on the faculty of the National Criminal Defense College, which runs perhaps the nation’s most prestigious and intensive trial skills programs for criminal defense lawyers.

From 2017 to 2018, Mr. Beaton served as the President of the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers — Miami Chapter.

Mr. Beaton has dozens of jury trials and thousands of courtroom hours in both state and federal courts. He has handled complex criminal cases in both federal and state courts. His clients include doctors, lawyers and successful business professionals. His cases have included misdemeanor cases where professional licenses are on the line all the way up to highly complex securities fraud cases, complex tax cases, racketeering cases, and even first-degree murder. He has tried multi-week and multi-month cases in both federal and state court and has participated in many exhaustive, internal, pre-indictment and pre-arraignment investigations. Mr. Beaton has extensive experience in matters involving highly regulated industries and is able to assist individuals and organizations accused of fraud and/or deceptive practices. Because of this experience, Mr. Beaton can also assist and advise on corporate governance and compliance matters, including in the area of anti-money laundering, health care, government contracts, wildlife regulations, firearms manufacturing and sales, and others. He regularly counsels companies from a variety of industries on the adoption and operation of their compliance programs and, in particular, assists companies in the health care industry and companies with overseas operations with internal investigations and ethics issues.

Mr. Beaton is highly respected for his passionate work on behalf of clients. He has a decorated background as a trial lawyer and advocate. He has consistently been recognized by his peers, including recognition as a Top 40 Lawyers Under 40 by the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation, recognition as a “Best Lawyers in America” by Best Lawyers Magazine, recognition as a “Best Lawyers in South Florida” as published in the Wall Street Journal, recognition as a “Top 10 Attorneys in Florida” by Super Lawyers magazine in 2021.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Palm Harbor, FL
attorneys.bio:
WILLIAM H. BECK, born December 28, 1971 in Arcadia, California; Education: National Polytechnic College of Science (1994), Brigham Young University (2004); University of Florida Levin College of Law (2007).

As a youth, Mr. Beck achieved the highest rank in Boy Scouts, the Eagle Scout, and spent two years in Europe where he learned to speak fluent German. After High School, Mr. Beck attended the National Polytechnic College of Science in Los Angeles where he specialized in Hyperbaric Medicine and received a Commercial Diving Certificate with a concentration on Advanced Dive Medicine in 1994.

Mr. Beck worked as a Paramedic in Los Angeles County and served four years as a Fireman in the United States Navy Reserve attached to the Navy Submarine Command in San Diego, California. Mr. Beck has also worked in the construction management industry and for the Public Transportation Department for the Municipality of Anchorage, Alaska.

Mr. Beck returned to college in 2000 and earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Management from Brigham Young University in 2004 and a Juris Doctor from the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2007.

After graduation, Mr. Beck served as a Trial Court Law Clerk and Judicial Staff Attorney for the Fifth Judicial Circuit of Florida. Mr. Beck is also a Florida Supreme Court Certified Family Law Mediator experienced in mediating dissolution and child custody and support issues with great success. Mr. Beck practices primarily Family Law including marriage dissolutions, child custody and adoptions. Mr. Beck lives in Palm Harbor, Florida with his wife and six children.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Achieved Eagle Scout, the highest rank in Boy Scouts of America

Jacky Beda is a native of Miami, Florida.

Mr. Beda earned his undergraduate degree from Yeshiva University where he majored in Political Science and played Division III NCAA Men's Basketball.

After earning his degree, Mr. Beda attended George Washington University Law School. During his time in Washington D.C, he clerked for the Department of Justice and for the Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia. Mr. Beda graduated law school in 2017 with High Honors and received the Thurgood Marshall Scholar distinction.

After law school, Mr. Beda was a prosecutor at the State Attorney's Office for the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit where he gained extensive litigation experience prosecuting felonies from inception through verdict as first-chair trial attorney.

In April of 2021, Mr. Beda joined Zarco Einhorn Salkowski, P.A. His practice focuses on commercial and franchise litigation. Prior to joining the firm, he was an associate at a prominent defense firm, practicing both state and federal civil litigation.

attorneys.bio:
BIOGRAPHY

"I am a 4th generation Miami attorney, born and raised. When we work together I will always be respectful, honest and guide you to the best result possible."

Since 2002, Attorney Justin K. Beckham has exclusively practiced criminal defense in Miami-Dade County. After earning the highest award in the University of Miami Moot Court program during law school, he joined the Office of the Miami-Dade County Public Defender.

He successfully defended thousands of clients at the Juvenile, Misdemeanor, and Felony Levels, both Federal and State, taking nearly 50 cases to trial and earning several acquittals. He began his own law practice in 2006, concentrating only on criminal cases.

ACCOLADES & CREDENTIALS

Justin was selected for inclusion in the Super Lawyers® list in the areas of criminal defense and DUI from 2010 through 2012 and in 2015, an award bestowed to only the top 2.5% of practicing attorneys in the State of Florida. Furthermore, he has also been accepted as a member of The National Advocacy for DUI Defense, LLC (or NAFDD). The exclusive organization is reserved for criminal defense lawyers who are recognized as being the United States' top defense attorneys. He was also selected as one of the top "40 under 40" Trial Lawyers in the country in 2013, and as one of the Top Lawyers in Florida by the Legal Network that same year. In 2022, he was inducted into the prestigious Lawyers of Distinction Network, achieved by only 1% of lawyers in the country. He has over one hundred and fifty (150) 5 STAR Google Reviews and has been rated a "10 out of 10" lawyer by AVVO since 2011.

GENERATIONS OF LEGAL EXPERIENCE

Justin K. Beckham is the only 4th generation trial lawyer in Miami-Dade County history. His great-grandfather, Walter H. Beckham, served as one of the first Juvenile Judges in Miami.

His grandfather, Walter H. Beckham Jr., is a Professor Emeritus at the University of Miami Law School and served as President of the National Judicial College. His father, James K. Beckham, focuses his practice on personal injury litigation in Homestead, Florida. Justin is fully fluent in both written and spoken Spanish.

He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Dade County Bar Association, and the Dade County Trial Lawyers Association. Justin has been interviewed by numerous media outlets about criminal defense-related topics.

attorneys.name: George C. Bedell III
attorneys.practice_type: Federal White Collar Crimes Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
I am a third generation trial lawyer and a fourth generation native Floridian. I have been trying cases since 1983. I have represented people and companies in federal and Florida courts since 2000.

During the sixteen years that I spent as an assistant state attorney in Tampa, I tried over 80 felony jury trials. By preparing and trying cases as a prosecutor, I learned how criminal investigations should be conducted and how evidence should gathered and collected. During my first five years in private practice I worked in a firm that specialized in white collar criminal defense and complex civil litigation. I started my own firm in 2008 and continue to represent individuals and companies in federal and Florida courts in criminal investigations and prosecutions with an emphasis on white collar cases.

In 1989, the Board of Legal Specialization and Education of The Florida Bar awarded me certification in Criminal Trial Law. To become certified, I passed an examination on criminal law, demonstrated that I had substantial involvement in criminal trial law through cases I had tried, and received positive peer review from judges and other lawyers concerning my competence as a lawyer. To maintain certification, I have had to demonstrate that I continue to have substantial involvement in criminal law. My certification has been renewed every five years since it was awarded.

I received my undergraduate degree from UNC – Chapel Hill in 1979. I received my law degree from the FSU College of Law in 1982.

attorneys.name: Alexandra Beitra
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Alexandra Beitra, Esquire is an associate attorney at Jeffrey Law, where she focuses her practice on complex marital and family law litigation, including dissolution of marriage, paternity, equitable distribution, parental responsibility matters, and prenuptial agreements. Ms. Beitra is dedicated to protecting her clients’ interests and guiding them through some of the most challenging times in their lives with clarity, preparation, and a steady approach.

A lifelong Florida resident, Ms. Beitra earned her Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science, magna cum laude, from Florida International University. She went on to receive her Juris Doctor from St. Thomas University School of Law, where she served as an intern with the Federal Public Defender’s Office for the Southern District of Florida, a highly selective position that allowed her to gain valuable federal courtroom experience early in her career, and as a Judicial Intern to the Honorable Milton Hirsch of the Eleventh Judicial Circuit for two semesters. Ms. Beitra was also the recipient of the Book Award in both Conflicts of Law and Pre-Trial Litigation, honoring her for having the best grade in each course.

Ms. Beitra’s legal experience began long before she attended law school. She worked for many years as a legal assistant and paralegal in law firms practicing in a wide range of areas, including civil litigation and union-side labor law. Having served in nearly every role within a law firm, she brings a comprehensive understanding of the legal process and a strong work ethic to her practice. Before focusing her practice exclusively on family law, Ms. Beitra practiced real estate law, representing mortgage servicers in residential and commercial foreclosure litigation.

Outside of her practice, Ms. Beitra enjoys spending time with her husband, a first responder, their son, and her stepchildren. She often spends her weekends at the baseball park or taking advantage of Florida’s outdoor lifestyle.

attorneys.bio:

She was certified as an Elder Law Specialist by the Florida Bar Board of Legal Specialization and Education in 2006. Presently, there are less than 150 attorneys of the approximately 100,000 licensed attorneys in the State of Florida that have met the educational, experience, and professional standards to become designated as an Elder Law Specialist. attorneys.name: Carol Bello
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Lutz, FL
attorneys.bio:
A first generation American and Tampa native, Carol Bello spent most of her childhood in Colombia before migrating to Florida with her family. She is fluent in Spanish. Carol has a passion for helping others and strives to ensure that every client’s question is answered and their needs are met.

After earning her Bachelor’s degree in Social Science from Florida State University in 2017, Ms. Bello was admitted to Western Michigan University Cooley Law School, where she obtained her Juris Doctor and graduated in the top 10% of her class with Honors.

During law school, she served as Associate Editor of the Thomas M. Cooley Law Review, was a Dean’s Fellow, Secretary of the Student Bar Association, and President of the Hispanic Organization of Legal Advocates.

Before attending law school, Ms. Bello worked as a legal assistant at a workers compensation law firm, where she witnessed firsthand the injustices and barriers faced by injured workers navigating the workers’ compensation system. Inspired to advocate more directly for those in need, she decided to attend law school so she could fight for fair treatment and ensure injured workers received the benefits and medical care they deserved.

During law school, Ms. Bello continued working as a legal assistant, gaining valuable practical insight that strengthened her foundation as a future workers’ compensation attorney. Since becoming an attorney, she has handled cases involving treatment denials, delayed care, and disputed benefits, and has secured positive outcomes for her clients through diligent advocacy and strategic case development.

Ms. Bello is committed to serving her community. She volunteers with Bay Area Legal Services, assisting pro se litigants with family law forms and providing translation services for Spanish-speaking individuals seeking legal help. She also dedicates her time to the Humane Society of Tampa Bay, where she assists the veterinary department with translation, walks dogs, and helps animals find their forever homes.

Outside of her professional and volunteer work, Ms. Bello enjoys reading, spending time with her family, and watching reruns of Shark Tank.
