attorneys.name: Michael B. Brehne
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Michael B. Brehne, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accident Lawyers in Altamonte Springs, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael Brehne is a 19-year resident of Florida hailing from East Brunswick, NJ. He is a graduate of the University of Florida and has served this community as a police officer in several capacities. Mr. Brehne began his law enforcement career as a sworn Auxiliary State Trooper with the Florida Highway Patrol while attending the University of Florida. He was primarily assigned to road patrol duties, but served on several special duty assignments such as narcotics interdiction and fugitive apprehension squads that included a canine.

Upon graduation, Mr. Brehne sought full time employment with the Orlando, Florida Police Department where he graduated first in his academy class. Mr. Brehne's first assignment was in road patrol where he received numerous citations and commendations for bravery and for reducing crime within his district. He served as a senior field training officer for new academy graduates and he was a member of the Emergency Response Team and a firearms instructor. After three years, Mr. Brehne was promoted to Detective where he served as an investigator in the Drug Enforcement Division.

In 1994, Mr. Brehne began his legal studies at Mercer University School of Law in Macon, GA. By the end of his first year, Mr. Brehne was selected as a Moot Court team member and competed in national moot court competitions. In addition, Mr. Brehne was selected as a member of the Mercer Law Review and was awarded an academic scholarship in his third year of law school. He graduated in May of 1997, in the top 17th out of a class of 141.

Mr. Brehne is admitted to the Florida Bar and was admitted to the Federal Bar in the Middle District of Florida. He is a member of the Orange County Bar Association, Seminole County Bar, American Association for Justice and the Florida Justice Association formally the Association of Florida Trial Lawyers. He is a civil justice attorney who has litigated hundreds of personal injury, insurance, workers' compensation, false arrest and police misconduct cases.

Mr. Brehne, with a background in law enforcement and a distinguished career as an attorney, is known for his strong sense of justice. He combines his assertive courtroom presence with a compassionate advocacy for his clients. His office actively engages in community support, notably through the Ribbon Rider's Pink Elves program, which aids women battling breast cancer. Additionally, Brehne has been a significant supporter of youth initiatives, being the first private donor to the Nope to Dope Program by the Altamonte Springs police department, providing funding and essential media equipment. Furthermore, he sponsors scholarships for high school JROTC members and student-athletes.

Mr. Brehne has two children. They live in Apopka. Mr. Brehne was an adjunct professor at Florida Metropolitan University in Orlando where he lectured on Legal Writing, Business Law and Criminology. He enjoys the beach, exercising and Florida Gator Football.

attorneys.name: David Brevda
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
David Brevda is a trial attorney focused on nursing home negligence and medical malpractice litigation. Admitted in both Florida and New York, David fights for the rights of injured clients and their families in cases involving nursing home abuse, medical malpractice and wrongful death. David prides himself on treating each case individually and pursuing justice for victims with tenacity.

Mr. Brevda received his Juris Doctorate degree from the New York University School of Law and is well versed in long term care staffing, corporate structuring and tax issues. He graduated cum laude from the University of Florida with a bachelor's degree in accounting and later received a master's degree in accounting from the University of Florida as well. In addition to holding a Master's in accounting, David Brevda has earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in taxation, graduating summa cum laude at the top of his Tax Law program.

Prior to joining Senior Justice Law Firm, David Brevda worked as a lawyer at the international headquarters of Clifford Chance law firm in London, United Kingdom. As an attorney at Clifford Chance, Mr. Brevda advised international investment banks and corporate issuers on equity and debt capital markets transactions, including high-yield bond offerings, high-yield notes analysis in restructuring, and IPOs.

Mr. Brevda has extensive experience with international corporate structures in the medical, long-term care, banking, and telecommunications sectors across Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

A Unique Understanding of Understaffing, Corporate Structures & Asset Location

David Brevda returned to practice law in the U.S. to fight for the rights of those injured by nursing home, long-term care and healthcare corporations.

Particularly with nursing home and assisted living facility corporations, corporate owners insulate themselves from liability by carrying minimal insurance policies and creating shell companies to hide their money. Corporate nursing homes create multi-layered structures in order to minimize assets available to pay damages when they are negligent and hurt their vulnerable residents. Oftentimes, they will also use webs of related entities in order to perpetrate Medicare fraud.

Mr. Brevda uses his vast knowledge of corporate and business structures to help identify the true owners of nursing homes by untangling the complex webs of shell companies created by the owners. This unique legal background in tax law and accounting enables David to analyze long term care facility staff numbers and budget diversions, especially in regards to understaffing, Medicare fraud and qui tam actions.

This in-depth financial and staffing analysis is unique among nursing home abuse law firms. Mr. Brevda's skill sets assist clients in obtaining compensation for the preventable injuries suffered inside these corporate-owned facilities.

attorneys.name: Vanessa Lee Brice
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
VANESSA LEE BRICE was born and raised in Zimbabwe, Africa. She later married her husband, a U.S. Marine who was assigned to the US Embassy in Harare. Ms. Brice later emigrated to the United States after her husband received new orders. Ms. Brice and her husband have a daughter, Nyasha.

Ms. Brice and her family were stationed at Camp LeJeune, North Carolina, and later at Paris Island, South Carolina, where her husband was a Drill Instructor. She worked as a paralegal in personal injury law firms in both North and South Carolina. The military again relocated her husband, this time to Orlando, Florida, where she again worked as a paralegal in a personal injury law firm.

Ms. Brice became a naturalized U.S. citizen in 2000.

As the law firms’ main link to the clients and their families, Ms. Brice came into contact with so many families who were touched by injury or medical malpractice. Knowing she could do more to help those families, Ms. Brice attended undergraduate school at night, graduating in 2006 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Management and Marketing (with honors).

In August 2006, Ms. Brice entered Florida A&M University Law School. She joined the firm as a summer clerk/intern in 2007, and continued to work with the firm throughout the rest of her time at law school. Ms. Brice graduated in May of 2009, and officially joined the firm as an Attorney in August, 2009.

Before receiving her law degree, Ms. Brice worked as a personal injury paralegal for over 15 years where she specialized in litigation and trial support. With this wealth of experience, she brings a unique perspective to her position as an attorney. As the spouse of a veteran, she has a special interest in helping veterans, and is accredited by the Veterans Administration.

While at law school, Ms. Brice participated in mock trial, mediation and arbitration competitions, representing her school at ABA and Florida Bar competitions around the country.

Ms. Brice is admitted to practice in the State of Florida. She is also a Veterans Administration Accredited Agent.

Kevin is recognized by the Florida Bar as a board-certified expert in business litigation. The Florida Bar rigorously evaluates the experience and competency of attorneys to determine board eligibility. There are less than 250 board certified attorneys in business litigation out of over 100,000 members of the Florida Bar.

He was rated as one of the Top 100 "Bet The Company" Litigators in the nation in 2019. He is a former Hillsborough County prosecutor where he took over 100 cases to trial.

Kevin enjoys spending time with his family, playing golf and tennis and cheering on the Bucs and Seminoles. He is a member of Grace Family Church and regularly volunteers his time and efforts to local civic and community organizations and causes.

attorneys.name: Edson R. Briggs Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Claims Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
R. Edson Briggs, Jr. works in the First-Party Insurance Division at the Miami office of Morgan & Morgan, P.A. His practice consists of representing the people of South Florida and Southwest Florida when their insurance company wrongfully denies their claims for insurance coverage. This includes homeowners, automobile, and life insurance, as well as other forms of insurance claims.

Mr. Briggs has been honored with the prestigious "AV rating" by Martindale-Hubbell, the preeminent national publication in the legal field. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law.

Mr. Briggs received an A.B. in History with a Certificate in Latin American Studies from Princeton University in 1990. He then received his J.D. from the University of Florida College of Law in 1993, and an L.L.M. in Interamerican Law from the University of Miami School of Law in 2002. After graduating from law school and before entering private practice, Mr. Briggs served on active duty for four years as an officer in the U.S. Army Military Intelligence Branch with U.S. Southern Command in Panama. He was honorably discharged from active duty with the rank of Captain in 1997. Thereafter, Mr. Briggs has had extensive experience in civil commercial and insurance litigation including property damage, construction defects, personal injury, title insurance, real estate and banking disputes.

Mr. Briggs grew up in South Florida and has worked there during his entire career in private practice. Having studied in Spain and having lived and traveled extensively in Latin America for four years, Mr. Briggs is fully bilingual in English and Spanish. He is married with two sons, and enjoys running and triathlons in his spare time.

attorneys.bio:
Robert "Bo" Briggs is a sixth generation Ocalan. Bo graduated from Belleview High School in its first graduating class. While there, he was a 3-year golf team captain and 2-time Television Production Student of the Year. He went on to graduate from Florida State University with a double major in finance and marketing. He was active in his fraternity, Sigma Alpha Epsilon, was an officer and member of the club water ski team, and participated in various other community, civic, and philanthropic activities. He continued his education at Stetson University College of Law, which, during his time there, was named the number one law school for trial advocacy. Bo received a "Certificate of Concentration" in Advocacy for his intensive skills-based curriculum. He was a member of the Calvin A. Kuenzel Student Bar Association and was Secretary of the Stetson Chapter of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. Since law school he has served on the Florida Justice Association Young Lawyers Division Executive Board, was a founding organizer of the Marion County Justice Association, has volunteered for civil and legal programs, and is an associate in the D.R. Smith Chapter of the American Inns of Court. Bo remains politically active on behalf of the Florida Justice Association and has lobbied and testified in Tallahassee for the protection of victims’ rights. Bo joined his father, Randy, at The Briggs Law Firm in 2005.

Bo and his wife Nadia have been blessed with three beautiful children.

attorneys.name: Randy Briggs
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Ocala, FL
attorneys.bio:
Following graduation from college and two years as a First Lieutenant in the U.S. Army, Randy returned to law school at the University of Florida. After graduating in the top 10% of his law school class in 1975, with several academic honors, Randy accepted a position with the Orlando law firm of McGuire, Voorhis and Wells, P.A. His two years with that firm were spent primarily in the defense of complex medical malpractice claims, various types of insurance defense work, and representation of accident victims.

A fifth-generation Marion County resident, Randy returned to his home of Ocala in 1977 and joined the firm of Ayres, Cluster, Curry, Meffert & McCall, P.A., and was made a partner the following year when the firm was renamed Ayres, Cluster, Curry, McCall & Briggs, P.A. He remained a partner in that firm for 22 years until establishing The Briggs Law Firm. From 1977 to 1983, the majority of his work in the personal injury field was on behalf of insurance companies, defending their insureds throughout Central Florida. In 1983, he completely stopped representing insurance companies and since that time has devoted more than 95% of his work life to representing accident victims.

In opening The Briggs Law Firm, Randy brought to the practice over 25 years of experience, Board Certifications in Civil Trial Law awarded by both the Florida Bar and the National Board of Trial Advocacy, and an "AV" rating by Martindale-Hubbell, its highest peer review ratings for legal ability and ethics. His experience includes jury trials throughout Florida, including Miami, Pensacola, Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, and numerous Central Florida cities. His experience also includes handling, from inception to conclusion, claims involving most every type of accident, as well as nursing home claims, very selective claims of medical malpractice, and complex product liability claims. He has taught trial skills to trial lawyers at seminars and trial schools, has lectured at personal injury seminars sponsored by the Florida Bar throughout the state, and has coached University of Florida Law School Trial Teams for competitions held in Alabama, Georgia and Florida.

attorneys.name: Jason A. Brodie
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Serving as a champion of Florida families for a decade, Jason A. Brodie, Esquire believes family matters are delicate matters. It is a philosophy that is proven time and again, as he advises clients about their marital, parental and children's rights. He works closely with clients to resolve concerns, relieve anxiety, and develop practical solutions to avoid or defend against difficult family-related legal challenges. Demonstrating the understanding, compassion and recognition that each family deserves and his ability to deal with the issues at hand, make him and his partner Joshua K. Friedman unparalleled on a broad range of issues, which include, Family Law, Divorce, Child Custody, Child Support, Timesharing, Alimony & Spousal Support, Domestic Violence, Paternity, and Equitable Distribution (Property Division).

Jason earned his Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration with honors from the University of Florida in 1997 and his J.D. (Juris Doctor) in 2000 from the University of Miami, School of Law. Upon his admittance to the Florida Bar, Jason began his legal career in South Florida with a boutique law firm. Jason took his experiences from this firm and decided that by co-founding a private boutique practice, Brodie & Friedman, P.A., in Boca Raton, it would better afford him the opportunity to give every client the individualized attention they deserve. Jason is a member of the Florida Bar, the Palm Beach County Bar Association and the South Palm Beach County Association. Jason has been recognized by his peers as a 2010 Rising Star and 2013 Super Lawyer by Super Lawyers magazine.

Jason has been featured on local and national media. Jason has shared his family law counsel regarding timely headline news stories on NBC Today, MSNBC, Fox News, Nancy Grace, WPTV NewsChannel 5, WPBF Channel 25 and WPEC Channel 12.

Active in the community, he has served on his community's bylaws committee for two years and now serves on it nominating committee. He is a member of the Greater Boca Raton Chamber of Commerce, and sponsors community events such as the Allianz Championship, a Champions PGA Tour event that benefits Boca Raton Community Hospital, and the Palm Beach County March of Dimes Signature Chefs & Wine Extravaganza. He also supports Stand Among Friends that promotes opportunities for people with disabilities to live a life without limits and experience the highest degree of independence and success in their communities; the Anti-Defamation League, the nation's premier civil rights/human relations agency that fights anti-Semitism and all forms of bigotry, defends democratic ideals and protects civil rights for all, as well as advocacy organizations that provide safe havens for victims of domestic violence such as Women In Distress of Broward County.

A Maryland native, Jason has called Florida home for more than 20 years. He is married to Jaclyn, who is also an attorney. The couple are proud parents of two children.

attorneys.name: Gregory B. Bromley
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Forrest & Forrest, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Bromley is the Senior Associate at Forrest & Forrest and specializes in all family law and divorce matters, including paternity, premarital agreements, domestic violence, enforcement, contempt, alimony, child support, custody, visitation, parenting plans, time-sharing, equitable distribution, property division, restraining orders, as well as post-judgment modifications.

He joined the Law Office of Forrest & Forrest, PLLC in 2020 as an associate attorney, devoting his legal practice entirely to family law cases.

Prior to handling family law matters, Mr. Bromley worked for the State of Florida for 5 years representing and advocating the best interests of abused, abandoned, and neglected children with the Guardian ad Litem Program. The majority of his time with the State of Florida was spent in the courtroom arguing cases on behalf of minor children who had been removed from their parents and needed to be reunified.

He is well-qualified to litigate adoptions, both private and state facilitated.

In private practice, he also uses his experience to represent clients who have temporarily lost custody of their children and are facing allegations made by the Department of Children & Families. He is a graduate of the Palm Beach Atlantic University (B.A., 2012) and Nova Southeastern University School of Law (J.D., 2015).

attorneys.name: Beach A. Brooks III
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Winter Haven, FL
attorneys.bio:
Beach A. Brooks III was born in Winter Haven, Florida. From a very young age, Beach had a competitive spirit. He had to win at everything he did. As a child he played several sports, but as he grew older, his love for baseball outgrew the others. While attending Winter Haven High School, Beach starred on the varsity baseball team and helped lead the team to three straight state championship games.

After graduating from high school, Beach’s hard work and dedication paid off with an opportunity to attend a top-100 business school while also playing Division 1 baseball. He graduated from the University of Cincinnati with a degree in Business Management.

Beach’s Career Start at Brooks Law Group

Upon completion of college and his athletic career, Beach was looking for a career that could fulfill his competitive spirit while also bettering society. Law was a natural choice. His father Beach Jr., uncle Stephen K. Brooks and several other family members were all attorneys.He grew up around the law and saw the positive impact it could have on clients’ lives and the community as a whole.

Beach attended Stetson University College of Law and graduated in May, 2016. While at Stetson he received the highest grade in his class in Criminal Procedure. Beach was drawn to Stetson because of their advocacy program, which is top in the country.

Not only were his father and uncle his mentors, but Beach comes from a family that has served the people. His grandfather Beach Sr. was a longtime doctor in the Central Florida area, while his other grandfather was a colonel in the Air Force. These influences have shown him the joy helping others can bring while also making the community a better place.

Beach is excited to join his next team here at the Brooks Law Group. Beach’s competitive spirit is still there and will drive him to get the best results for his clients.

attorneys.name: Vanessa Brooks Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in DeLand, FL
attorneys.bio:
A Former Prosecutor Now Advocating for Families With Clarity and Peace

Vanessa began her career aiming to be a prosecutor but discovered her true passion was helping people through life’s most challenging moments with clarity and compassion. Early work in an estate planning office showed her how powerful thoughtful planning can be for families. Her time in Dependency Court and prosecution taught her to see the human story behind every case. Today, she uses that experience to guide families through estate planning and probate with honesty, empathy, and clear explanation.

Why Families Trust Vanessa

A calming, thoughtful approach shaped by years in emotionally intense legal settings

Deep commitment to treating clients with dignity, compassion, and clarity

A teacher at heart—she helps clients understand their options, not just sign documents

Ability to see the human story behind every situation

A guiding presence for families facing uncertainty, grief, or indecision

Beyond the Office

A lover of books, theme parks, long walks, and working out, Vanessa finds joy in staying active and exploring new experiences. She has narrated three books on Audible, ran a half-marathon, and hopes to one day take on the world’s toughest race. Her sense of adventure mirrors the energy she brings to helping families move forward with confidence.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Roger Brown is a partner in the Morgan & Morgan Business Trial Group and handles cases throughout South Florida. Mr. Brown handles a wide variety of complex business litigation on a contingency-fee basis, including contract disputes, business torts, real estate, professional malpractice, misrepresentation and fraud claims, shareholder and partnership disputes, and more. He regularly handles matters in both state and federal courts.

In addition to litigating general business matters, Mr. Brown also manages all of Morgan & Morgan's construction cases in South Florida. Notably, Mr. Brown is Board Certified in construction law by the Florida Bar - an honor reserved for lawyers recognized as "experts" in all aspects of construction law and is a distinction bestowed on less than 1% of Florida Bar members. He also serves on the Palm Beach County Bar Association Construction Law Committee.

Mr. Brown's career has been dedicated to representing owners, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers and design professionals in all types of construction disputes, which he does on a contingency-fee basis. He handles claims involving construction defects, nonpayment, schedule delays, payment and performance bonds, lien foreclosures, designer malpractice, and other contract matters. Mr. Brown's ultimate goal is to use his experience and resources to maximize the potential recovery in your case.

Mr. Brown graduated from Boston College and the University of Florida Levin College of Law.

attorneys.bio:
Fort Lauderdale Florida Divorce Lawyer

Prior Legal Experience

Rebekah Brown-Wiseman is an experienced family law litigation attorney. This came from years of prior legal experience amongst which includes being a prior:

Florida State Attorney that represented the Department of Children and Families in child custody and termination of parental rights cases.

State of Florida Guardian ad Litem Program lawyer that represented the best interests of children in child custody cases.

Family law attorney for both a large law firm and a boutique family law firm

The Law Office of Rebekah Brown-Wiseman exclusively handles family law cases. The firm recognizes the importance of being specialized in only family law to keep up-to-date with the current Florida family law statutes, rules and case law to vigorously represent her clients.

Lawyer With Social Work Experience

Florida's child custody statute requires that judges consider the developmental stages and needs of the child and the demonstrated capacity and disposition of each parent to meet the child's developmental needs when making child custody determinations. Ms. Brown-Wiseman has experience in social work, which is unique to the vast majority of family law attorneys which provides her with superior knowledge to litigate issues of child development and family systems in highly contested child custody cases. Amongst Ms. Brown-Wiseman experience includes:

Former child therapist

Master's degree in social work with a concentration in children & families

Bachelor's degree in psychology

Former Court social worker that evaluated malingering in individuals pleading insanity and incompetency defenses to criminal charges

Dedication to Family Law

Ms. Brown-Wiseman's 8th grade yearbook listed the anticipated future professions of each of the graduating students and she was given the prediction to become a family law attorney. This was after she had a personal experience testifying in her parents' divorce case. Ms. Brown-Wiseman had her first opportunity to help family law clients in 1998 when she worked at Harvard Law School's Hale & Dorr Legal Services. Ms. Brown-Wiseman has the determination to zealously advocate for her cases and has both the legal and social work experience to guide her clients step-by-step through the process.

Connections with Community Professionals

Not only do clients need a team effort within the firm, many family law cases need the assistance of additional professionals. Ms. Brown-Wiseman maintains connections with community professionals that already have stellular reputations with the Court. It is an advantage if the judge already is familiar with and trusts your expert witness. It is crucial that you work with expert witnesses who returns your telephone calls promptly, conducts the necessary work timely and maintains a team effort to develop a strong offense and defense for your case. Attorney Brown-Wiseman maintains relationships with psychologists, social workers, forensic accountants, vocational evaluation experts, private investigators, etc., to provide you with a list of recommendations or she can work with an expert witness of your choice.

attorneys.name: Jonathan Brozyna
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan Brozyna is a partner in the Tampa offices of Morgan & Morgan, P.A. Jonathan dedicates his legal practice to representing clients injured in catastrophic automobile and trucking collisions, wrongful death, and general personal injury cases. Jonathan believes that everyone deserves the very best legal representation and prides him in relentlessly seeking justice for his clients.

Over the years, Jonathan has obtained millions of dollars in verdicts and settlements for his clients. Some of Jonathan's most recent verdicts include: a $1.3 million (motor vehicle crash), $3.38 million (truck crash), and $202,000 (slip and fall). In addition to trial victories, Jonathan has recovered millions of dollars in settlements for his deserving clients.

Jonathan attended the University of Arizona where he was a member of the University's Division I Men's Tennis Team, receiving his B.A. in 2002. In 2008, he received his Juris Doctorate Degree from Florida State College of Law. While attending Law School in Tallahassee, he served as a Law Clerk for the Florida Attorney General in the Economic Crimes Division.

Before joining Morgan & Morgan, Jonathan worked at two prestigious Civil Trial Firms located in Tampa, Florida. During the early years of his legal career, he defended numerous large insurance companies/their insureds, a multi-state Supermarket chain, property owners and state entities in a variety of civil claims, including: auto accidents, tractor-trailer accidents, motorcycle accidents, negligent security, slip and fall accidents, pharmacy negligence and wrongful death. Having represented large insurance companies for many years, Jonathan understands how insurance companies defend and evaluate injury cases. He uses his intimate knowledge of the insurance industry to help his clients who have suffered serious personal injuries at the hands of someone else's negligent conduct.

In addition to having years of experience defending cases in State and Federal Court, Jonathan has also prosecuted thousands of personal injury cases, recovering tens of millions of dollars for his clients over the years. Unlike many of his peers, he has successfully tried numerous Civil Jury Trials early on in his legal career and is at home in the courtroom.

Mr. Brozyna is married and has two young daughters.

attorneys.name: Eric D. Bruce
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Bradenton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Eric D. Bruce focuses his practice on wrongful death and serious personal injury cases. He was born in Baltimore, Maryland, and moved to Florida with his family when he was a teenager. Mr. Bruce is a graduate of Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton, Florida, where he earned a Bachelor of Business Administration. He received his Juris Doctorate from the University of Miami, School of Law in Coral Gables, Florida, in 1992.

While at the University of Miami, he was an active participant in service and advocacy activities, earning places on the University's Moot Court Board, Bar and Gavel Honor Society, American Bar Association National Appellate Advocacy Team, and the Attorney General's Office Clinical Placement Program. In his final year at the University of Miami, School of Law, he was awarded the University's Roger Sorino Award and named the outstanding graduating student in service and leadership.

Mr. Bruce was admitted to the Florida Bar in 1992 and moved to the Sarasota-Bradenton area that same year to begin his career as an attorney. During the course of his career, he has been engaged in various aspects of civil practice, including over ten years of service as the Senior Program Attorney for the Manatee County Clerk of Circuit Court's Child Support Enforcement Office, where on occasion he acted in the capacity of a Special Prosecutor on behalf of the State of Florida Department of Revenue in Indirect Criminal Contempt cases. He is a member of the Florida Justice Association, a long-time coach and supporter of the Manatee High School Mock Trial Team program, a continuing legal education lecturer and the 2009-2010 President for the Manatee County Bar Association.

He married University of Miami School of Law classmate Lisbeth Perucki Bruce in 1991 and together they have a son and daughter who are currently attending Manatee County Public Schools.

attorneys.name: Vincent Michael Bruner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Walton Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Vince Bruner, was born in Dothan, Alabama, in 1957. He is a lifelong resident of Okaloosa County. His mother and father, Peggy and Max Bruner, taught school in the Okaloosa County school district for more than 25 years. Max Bruner was school superintendent in Okaloosa County from 1964 to 1984.

Vince Bruner graduated from Choctawhatchee High School in 1975, Florida State University in 1979 and the Cumberland School of Law at Samford University in 1984. He was active in athletics and academics in high school and college where he received a scholarship for football at the University of Kentucky and later finished playing for Bobby Bowden at Florida State University.

Vince worked as an intern at the State Attorneys office while attending Cumberland and worked full time as an assistant state attorney from 1984-1985. In 1986, he entered the private practice of law in Fort Walton Beach as an associate with the firm Smith, Grimsley, Remington & Kessler. In 1987, he was named city attorney for the City of Fort Walton Beach and in 1988, he was named city attorney in the City of Valparaiso. He served as city attorney for the City of Fort Walton Beach for approximately 2 years and in Valparaiso for 5 years.

In 1988, he was elected to the Florida Senate, serving one 4 year term in Senate District 3. His 9 county Senate district was one of the largest geographical districts in Florida, including 9 counties, Bay, Okaloosa, Walton, Gulf, Washington, Calhoun, Franklin, Liberty and Walkulla counties. He was chairman of the Senate committee on Corrections and was voted by his peers as "Most Promising Freshman". After just one term, he returned to the full time private practice of law.

As a member of the Joint Select Committee of Senate and House members which determined claims bills presented against the State of Florida or any of its political subdivisions, Vince developed a special interest in serious accidental injury cases. Since 1992 he has devoted his practice solely to work as a Plaintiff's personal injury lawyer, dedicated to assisting people injured in accidents throughout the Florida panhandle. His education and experience in both law and government and his familiarity with the places and people in the Florida panhandle have assisted him in effectively representing people injured by the careless and negligent acts of others.

He has maintained offices in both Panama City and Fort Walton Beach since 1988. He remains dedicated to helping and assisting victims of accidental injuries and the neglect of others.

Vince has 4 children, Drew, Vincent, Peggy and Jack.

Honors

attorneys.bio:
Victoria was born and raised in the Chicagoland area. She is first-generation American on her mother’s side and second-generation on her father’s. As the daughter and granddaughter of Italian and Argentinian immigrants, Victoria always was always passionate about working with the immigrant community.

Victoria earned her Juris Doctor with a concentration in International Law from the West Virginia University College of Law. In law school, Victoria worked as a clinical law student with the WVU Immigration Legal Clinic where she worked with immigrants from all over the globe with various ethnic and economic backgrounds. It was here where she chose to go into immigration law.

Victoria also worked with the Farmworker and Landscaper Advocacy Project, a non-profit in Illinois, where she created and managed the Immigration Legal Department. Victoria provided full and limited scope representation in various immigration cases, including Asylum and Withholding of Removal, U Visas, Temporary Protected Status, Deferred Action for Labor Enforcement, and Parole in Place.

sections.content:

As the daughter and granddaughter of Italian and Argentinian immigrants, Victoria always was always passionate about working with the immigrant community.

Victoria earned her Juris Doctor with a concentration in International Law from the West Virginia University College of Law. In law school, Victoria worked as a clinical law student with the WVU Immigration Legal Clinic where she worked with immigrants from all over the globe with various ethnic and economic backgrounds. It was here where she chose to go into immigration law.

Victoria also worked with the Farmworker and Landscaper Advocacy Project, a non-profit in Illinois, where she created and managed the Immigration Legal Department. Victoria provided full and limited scope representation in various immigration cases, including Asylum and Withholding of Removal, U Visas, Temporary Protected Status, Deferred Action for Labor Enforcement, and Parole in Place.

attorneys.name: Bjorn E. Brunvand
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Lawyers in Clearwater, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Brunvand has concentrated his legal practice in the area of federal and Florida state criminal defense from the investigative stages through motions, resolution negotiations, trials and sentencing if necessary.

Born in Stavanger, Norway, Bjorn has a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the University of South Florida and a law degree from Stetson University College of Law. While attending Stetson, he was a founding member of the Stetson Intramural Law Journal and handled several jury trials in the Public Defender Clinic. Upon graduation from Stetson, he became an Assistant Public Defender in the Sixth Judicial Circuit, and served in that capacity from 1989 to 1992. As an Assistant Public Defender, he tried more jury trials than most attorneys try in a lifetime. In 1991 he had the opportunity to attend and graduate from the National Criminal Defense College, in Macon, Georgia. In December 1992, he entered private practice, in the Tampa Bay Area (Florida).

While in private practice, Bjorn has been fortunate to successfully represent individuals and corporations that faced serious criminal charges in Federal and State Courts. The fraud cases range from government fraud cases involving Medicare, Medicaid, Defense Contracting, Mortgage and Banking. His practice includes the representation of individuals charged as participants in major international drug trafficking ventures whether they choose to defend their case via a jury trial or through negotiations to avoid lengthy prison sentences. Other cases handled by his office include but are not limited to the following: murder, manslaughter, child pornography, burglary, grand theft, embezzlement, organized crime, DUI and other criminal traffic offenses.

Bjorn is a member of the Florida Bar, the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. He is recognized both as a Florida Board Certified Criminal Trial Attorney and a Nationally Board Certified Criminal Trial Lawyer. He was voted as a Super Lawyer in 2008 and 2009 and continues to be AV® Preeminent™ Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell.

Bjorn is the former President of and remains active in the Pinellas County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and the Pinellas County Trial Lawyers Association. He has served as an active member of the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Barney Masterson Inn of Court, the Federal Bar Association, Clearwater and St. Petersburg Bar Associations, the Criminal Law Section of the Florida Bar and the National Organization for Reform of Marijuana Laws (N.O.R.M.L.)

attorneys.name: Joseph R. Bryant
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Joseph R. Bryant is third generation Tampa native. He graduated Jesuit High School in 1977, received his undergraduate degree from Florida State University in 1982, and received his law degree from the University of Mississippi in 1985. He was admitted to the Florida Bar, U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Eleventh Circuit, in 1986.

From 1986-1991, he was a senior Assistant Attorney General, handling criminal appeals and collateral petitions on behalf of the State of Florida in capital and non-capital cases. From 1991-1996, he was employed as a Senior Trial Attorney by Allstate Insurance Company. From 1997-1998, he was an Associate with the insurance defense firm of Mckendree, Driscol & Silver. In 1999, he started his own plaintiffs personal injury practice, Joseph R. Bryant, P. A. During that time he litigated the following types of cases in both state and federal court: personal injury and wrongful death, breach of fiduciary, breach of privacy, products liability, premises liability, toxic torts, railroad accidents, defamation, breach of contract and warranty, first and third party insurance bad faith claims, suits for declaratory judgment, suits against the sovereign, petitions for writ of certiorari, true bills of discovery and for injunctive relief.

Mr. Bryant is a Board Certified in Civil Trial by the Florida Bar, and has over 253 written appellate opinions in cases he has handled. He is A-V Rated by Martindale Hubbell, is a Florida "Super Lawyer," and has testified in court as an expert witness.

attorneys.name: R. Kellen Bryant Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Berg Bryant Elder Law Group, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kellen is a partner and co-founder of Berg Bryant Elder Law Group after having spent 7 years building his own practice from scratch. Kellen started his solo practice at 26 years old during the 2009 recession, with no contacts and no prior legal experience in elder law. Kellen has since built a practice that has served over 1500 families and supports a full office staff to help serve all client needs. Kellen is a Jacksonville, Florida native, having attended Sandalwood High School and his close family still lives in Jacksonville. Like many of his clients, Kellen has been financially on his own since age 18.

Kellen is one of approximately 100 attorneys that the Florida Bar has certified as an expert in elder law. There are approximately 70,000 licensed attorneys in Florida, thus, the board certification makes Kellen uniquely qualified to help caregivers and elderly clients.

Due to the poor economy in 2009, traditional opportunities to work under experienced attorneys was not available to Kellen and he has spent nearly $100,000 (and counting) on seminars and trainings all over the country in pursuit of trying to become the best elder law attorney for his clients and their caregivers. Of course, lawyers cannot say that they are the best attorney, but the goal is to continually try to be the best.

attorneys.practice_type: Tax Law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Christin M. Bucci focuses her practice on the successful resolution of federal and state tax controversies. She has over 20 years of extensive experience in representing individuals and corporations in tax matters before all levels of the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Tax Court and Federal District Court, offering an unparalleled level of services and insight into the most challenging tax disputes. Christin M. Bucci has also counseled corporate and individual clients in numerous tax planning strategies and transaction matters, both domestic and international. She holds a Master of Taxation (LL.M.) and a Master of International & Comparative Law (LL.M.) from Georgetown University, and is also a Certified Public Accountant (CPA).

Prior to founding Bucci Law Offices, Christin M. Bucci was an attorney at PricewaterhouseCoopers. With more than 20 years of experience, she has received many distinguished awards such as a 2015 Super Lawyer, and Avvo’s 10 Top Tax Award and Client’s Choice Award. Christin has also been “AV Preeminent” rated 5.0 out of 5.0 (2010-2015) by her professional peers through Martindale-Hubbell © Peer Review System. The “AV” Rating of “Preeminent” legal ability is the highest rating awarded, and a testament from peer legal professionals of the highest level of professional excellence and unquestionable ethics.

Christin M. Bucci is licensed to practice law in Florida, Ohio, and the District of Columbia, as well as before the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida, the U.S. Tax Court and the Supreme Court of the United States.

Mr. Buckler started his career representing numerous insurance carriers in State and Federal courts. Three years later he was a named partner in a high profile firm in Tampa and began representing injured consumers. In 1996 he took a position with the firm and has risen to Managing Partner in the Tampa office while also having input into all the firms out of state offices. Mr. Buckler has also been active in the community with numerous organizations.

Mr. Buckler has been honored with the prestigious "AV Rating" by Martindale-Hubbell, the preeminent national publication in the legal field. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law. It is a distinction reserved for a select few in the legal community.

attorneys.bio:
Charles Buist is an accomplished personal injury and wrongful death attorney working out of Orlando, Florida. He is admitted to practice law in Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina. He has a proven track record of success in obtaining justice for his clients in a variety of practice areas including car accidents, dental malpractice, wrongful death, truck accidents, and premises liability.

Charles earned his law degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law, where he graduated cum laude. He also holds a master's in environmental law and policy from Vermont Law School and a master's in business administration from the University of South Carolina Darla Moore School of Business.

After law school, Charles clerked for two different federal judges. First, he clerked with the Honorable Joseph F. Anderson, Jr. at the United States District Court for the District of South Carolina. Thereafter, he clerked for the Honorable David R. Duncan at the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of South Carolina. When Charles finished his clerkships, he entered into private practice.

To schedule your FREE consultation with the Orlando Personal Injury Attorney, visit online or call 321-265-4934.

attorneys.name: Hector R. Buigas Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
"Hector Buigas is an attorney in Morgan & Morgan's Medical Malpractice Department where he focuses on the representation of victims of medical negligence and their families.

Mr. Buigas was born in Miami, FL, the youngest of nine children of immigrant parents. As an undergraduate, Mr. Buigas attended Florida International University while working a full-time job to finance his studies and graduated with honors with a degree in English and American Literature. He earned a full scholarship to law school and attended the University of Florida Levin College of Law, graduating in 1998.

Following his graduation, Mr. Buigas returned to South Florida where he began his career representing physicians, physician extenders, nurses, pharmacists, nursing homes and healthcare facilities in medical negligence claims. For over 20 years Mr. Buigas handled hundreds of cases ranging across all medical specialties, several of which were the focus of both local and national media attention. Over his career he has brought over 30 medical malpractice jury trials to verdict, in addition to the jury trials involving other complex legal matters. He is now focused on using his well-earned knowledge and experience to benefit victims of medical negligence and their families.

Mr. Buigas is AV-Preeminent Rated by Martindale Hubbell and is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, an invitation-only group of experienced trial lawyers and judges dedicated to protecting the right to civil jury trials. When he is not pursuing justice for his clients, Mr. Buigas can be found spending time with his family, coaching soccer, or attending one of his children's many activities. His guiding principle is, ""If you wish to be good, do good.""

Mr. Buigas is a native Spanish speaker."

attorneys.name: Gareth Howard Bullock
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration & Naturalization Law Lawyers in Davie, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Gareth H. Bullock is the founder and managing partner of the 441 Legal Group, Inc., located in South Florida. He is an experienced legal professional who is committed to the practice of law and is passionate in his fight for justice. He is a general practitioner who concentrates his practice in the following areas of law, immigration and nationality law, family law, estate planning and general corporate law. Attorney Bullock is dedicated to providing legal services with conviction; caring and compassion and his ethics and professionalism are beyond reproach.

Attorney Gareth. H. Bullock has been dedicated to helping others since his adolescence and began working in the legal field as an intern in 1994. He gained admission to the Florida bar in 1997 after obtaining his Juris Doctor from the New York Law School in 1996. He completed his undergraduate course study by earning a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Psychology from the Florida International University in 1992. Attorney Bullock is committed to his field and remains engaged in increasing his knowledge of law by participating in ongoing training through the Florida continuing legal education program. He is also a proud member of several legal and professional organizations including, the American Immigration Lawyers Association, Broward County Bar Association, Cornwall College Alumni Association, the Rotary and the Caribbean Bar Association.

Attorney Bullock serves an international clientele from every walk of life. He represents institutions, wealthy individuals, the middle class and even those who are unable to afford legal services through his pro-bono work. He is a firm believer that he is blessed with his talents to help others and knows that to whom much has been given, from him, much is expected. He has earned an international reputation as a competent attorney who cares enough to go the distance. Attorney Bullock will stop at nothing to ensure that his client benefits from the most favorable interpretation of the law. With respect to his philosophy as an attorney, Bullock has this to say, "When I accept a case, I will do whatever is needed for us to win, as long as it is in my client’s best interest. If we don’t win, I take it personally, and my natural instinct is to dissect the decision and find out how I can have it amended." He says that he has never been one to take no for an answer and does not intend to start now.

attorneys.name: Baylee Bunyard
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Baylee Bunyard joined Cobb Cole in 2021 as a Law Clerk for the Estate Planning Department and is now an associate for the firm. He was born in Gulf Breeze, Florida and is currently residing in South Daytona.

Mr. Bunyard is a first-generation college graduate and completed his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science at the University of Florida with a Certificate in International Relations and a Certificate in Public Affairs. He then enrolled in Law School at the Charleston School of Law in 2019 and was recognized on the Dean's List Fall of 2019 and Spring of 2020. While at Charleston, he also received a CALI Excellence for the Future Award in his Legal Research, Analysis, and Writing class, an award designated for the highest grade in the class. Mr. Bunyard transferred to the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2020 where he completed his Juris Doctor and was the sole recipient of the Estate Planning Certificate in his graduating class.

Working actively in the legal industry since 2015, Mr. Bunyard has interned with the Regional Conflict Counsel in Pensacola, was a member of a litigation team that represented plaintiffs across the country in the Proton-Pump Inhibitor Multidistrict Litigation, clerked in Real Estate and Title Law, and recently collaborated with Florida Legal Services on the 2022 Fair Housing Symposium.

Mr. Bunyard is a member of the Volusia Bar Association and the Florida Bar Association. His practice is predominately focused on estate planning needs for Volusia County residents.

attorneys.name: Geannina Burgos
attorneys.bio:
Since joining Dabdoub Law Firm as an associate attorney, Geannina Burgos has focused on providing skilled representation for those who have claims for disability benefits both short and long term. She is able to take her clients through the entire process, from filing the initial individual or group disability claims, handling pre-suit appeals, and litigating benefits that were wrongfully denied or terminated by insurance companies in federal and state court. Her clients are entitled to receive disability insurance policy benefits under a private, or individual, insurance policy or via a long-term disability policy through their employer. A majority of the cases that Nina handles fall under ERISA, or the Employee Retirement Income Security Act. This is a federal law that governs most long-term disability benefits claims.

Nina earned several fellowships from a number of organizations, including the Young Lawyers’ Division of the Florida Bar, the American Society of Public Administrators, the Florida Association of Women Lawyers, and the Ruden McClosky Foundation. During her time in law school, she had a summer judicial clerkship under the Honorable Judge Barbara Lagoa in the Third District Court of Appeal. She also participated in her law school’s Community Development Clinic, and received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award in Mediation.

A classically trained ballet and modern dancer, Nina managed a multi-site nonprofit arts education organization for several years prior to becoming an attorney. She is an active member of the non-profit arts community, sitting on the board of multiple culture-driven organizations and has volunteered as a grant panelist for several cultural institutions.

Nina holds an MBA in Entrepreneurship and is fluent in English and Spanish.

attorneys.name: Ryan S. Burke Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Litigation Lawyers in Saint Petersburg, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ryan S. Burke grew up in Jensen Beach, Martin County, Florida. He attended Florida State University earning a Bachelor’s degree in History and Social Sciences. After graduating Florida State University, Mr. Burke attended and is a graduate of Stetson University College of Law in Gulfport, Florida.

While attending law school, Mr. Burke was an active member of the Moot Court Board. Mr. Burke competed in Moot Court competitions in Florida, Delaware and Vienna, Austria. He was also chosen for internship with a prominent Hillsborough County Circuit Court Judge and a U.S. District Court Magistrate.

Upon being admitted to the Florida Bar in 2005, Mr. Burke was a litigator with a prominent St. Petersburg, Florida law firm focusing his practice on property insurance coverage disputes, sinkholes claims, hurricanes claims, and other catastrophic weather events, including water damage claims, mold claims, theft claims, and fire loss claims.

In 2013, Mr. Burke took a position with a national firm and represented large insurance companies in cases involving complex insurance coverage disputes, including surplus lines and excess lines coverage disputes. In addition, Mr. Burke represented insureds in cases involving insurance agency negligence, premises liability, construction defects, personal injury, negligence, products liability, motor vehicle accidents, and other claims.

In 2017, Mr. Burke and Mr. Dicus co-founded Dicus Burke & Lewis, PLLC, where their primary focus is representing individuals and business owners in claims against their insurance companies, as well as claims against at-fault, negligent parties and the criminally accused. Together they handle a variety of cases including but not limited to commercial and residential property insurance claim dispute litigation, personal injury and premises liability (slip and fall), insurance agency negligence, products liability, motor vehicle accidents and criminal defense. Mr. Burke also handles complex personal injury litigation. Dicus Burke & Lewis, PLLC is regularly engaged by other law firms as co-counsel in disputed insurance claim trial cases. Dicus Burke & Lewis, PLLC has recovered millions of dollars in settlement proceeds and jury verdicts for its clientele.

attorneys.name: Howard Butler
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Howard Butler is the founding senior partner of the Butler Law Group, specializing in wrongful death and serious accident cases.

Mr. Butler is a Nationally Board-Certified Civil Trial Lawyer (National Board of Trial Advocacy) and is AV-rated (highest possible rating) by Martindale-Hubble. Mr. Butler has been repeatedly selected for inclusion in “The Best Lawyers In America” and named a Super Lawyer (Florida) which is limited to the top 5% of lawyers in a state.

Howard Butler and his law firm are included in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers.

Mr. Butler is a graduate of Stetson University (B.B.A. 1982) and the Stetson College of Law (J.D. 1985). Mr. Butler successfully completed ATLA’s National College of Advocacy at Harvard University.

He is a member of Multi-Million Dollar Advocates, American Association for Justice, Florida Justice Association (EAGLE member) and the Attorneys Information Exchange Group (AIEG) and Trial Lawyers for Public Justice.

Mr. Butler served as Corporate Counsel for John Travolta, JTP Films, Inc., Constellation Productions and has represented Kelly Preston, Cal Ripken Jr., Gregory Harrison, and many others. He has been listed among Who’s Who and America’s Registry of Outstanding Professionals and featured on Forbes Best Lawyers Tribute by Forbes Radio. During the course of his 25+ year career, Mr. Butler has represented hundreds of cases involving wrongful death, serious accidents, and personal injury.

attorneys.name: Melinda H. Butler
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Butler has an extensive financial education and regulatory experience in both the public and private sectors. Therefore, Ms. Butler is uniquely qualified to assess a business’s current compliance with Florida regulatory law and is able to recommend efficient and effective modifications to a business for the purpose of enhancing profitability, along with future compliance.

Public Sector

Over the last 14 years, Ms. Butler has administratively prosecuted disciplinary actions and defended license denials.

· At the Florida Office of Financial Regulation (“OFR”) Ms. Butler was a Chief Counsel for over two years and Lead Attorney for over seven years. In her role at OFR she was regularly involved with:

· Assessing the compliance of Money Services Business, Consumer Finance Company, Mortgage Lender, Broker, and Loan Originator licensees and the qualifications of such license applicants.

· Regularly training consumer finance staff in the legal complexities of consumer finance law, including the fundamentals of how to best perform and analyze money services businesses examinations.

· From 2010 to 2013, Ms. Butler represented the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation’s Division of Alcohol and Tobacco, and the Florida Department of Financial Services’ Division of Insurance Agents and Agencies.

· Assessing the compliance of Liquor, Catering, and Restaurant Alcoholic Beverage licensees and the qualification of such license applicants, and Tobacco Permittees and the qualifications of their permit applicants.

· Assessing the compliance of Insurance Agency and Agent licensees and the qualifications of such license applicants.

As an administrative attorney and supervisor, Ms. Butler regularly coordinated with Florida Assistant State Attorneys to assist them in their criminal prosecution of agency respondents.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Ms. Butler, was the technical aide to the Commissioner/Chairman of the Florida Public Service Commission, regularly performing reviews and providing recommendations for the resolution of all cases brought before the Commission.

Private Sector

Upon admission to the Florida Bar in 2009, Ms. Butler went into the private practice of criminal law.

Before moving to Florida, Ms. Butler served as the Vice President - Regulatory of Union Telephone Company and the President of the New Hampshire Telephone Association (“NHTA”).

· As the Vice President of the telephone company, Ms. Butler was the company’s liaison to the New Hampshire Public Utilities Commission and the Federal Communications Commission.

· As the President of the NHTA, Ms. Butler was the Chairman of the NHTA’s Legislative Committee, which developed and implemented the association’s legislative initiatives.

attorneys.name: Sarah S. Butters
attorneys.practice_type: Probate, Estate Planning and Administration Lawyers in Tallahassee, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Butters is a shareholder at Ausley McMullen and has extensive experience in estate, trust and related litigation; the preparation of wills, trusts and sophisticated estate planning techniques; and the administration of probates and trusts. She frequently serves as an expert witness and consultant on high stakes disputes.

Sarah represents personal representatives, trustees, corporate fiduciaries, beneficiaries and numerous national charities in all aspects of trust and estate administration. She has extensive litigation experience in elective shares, spousal rights, undue influence, incapacity and breach of fiduciary duty cases.

Sarah regularly testifies before the Florida House and Senate on legislation impacting the law of wills, trusts and guardianships.

Sarah is the Chair of the Real Property, Probate and Trust Law Section of The Florida Bar and a Fellow of the American College of Trusts and Estates Counsel. She is an Adjunct Professor at Florida State University's College of Law where she teaches law of wills and trusts and is also a Past President of the Tallahassee Regional Estate Planning Council.

attorneys.name: Nicholas Bykowsky Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Nicholas Bykowsky has been practicing law in Florida for over twenty years, primarily focusing on business litigation. He has represented the Florida Department of Revenue in tax controversies, the state securities regulator, as well as private businesses in both corporate matters and health care law. Nicholas has extensive knowledge of the Florida court system, giving him the skills to facilitate the best possible outcome for his clients.

He graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a B.A. degree having a double major in Economics as well as Political Science and was awarded his Doctor of Jurisprudence degree from the Oklahoma City University School of Law. He has appeared as lead trial counsel in Florida circuit courts in every major metropolitan area of the State of Florida and as appellate counsel on behalf of the State of Florida in the District Courts of Appeal and the Florida Supreme Court.

Nicholas was born and raised in northern New Jersey and has been a resident of Florida since 1996. Nicholas has a love of music and has performed as a member of local concert bands, orchestras, and jazz bands throughout his entire life. He is an accomplished professional-level trombonist. In 1994 he completed his first - and last - marathon run in just under five hours. In his spare time, he likes to compose music and work on completing his first novel. He thoroughly enjoys outdoor activities and travels out west for hiking in the mountains of Wyoming. Football season beckons every fall, and having lived and worked in Green Bay for nearly eight years he continues to support and follow both the Wisconsin Badgers and the Green Bay Packers.

attorneys.name: Maddison Cacciatore
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury – Plaintiff Lawyers in Melbourne, FL
attorneys.bio:
Maddison Cacciatore-Straus, raised in Brevard County, pursued a legal career due to the inspiration and admiration she felt for her father and grandfather. Following in their footsteps, Ms. Cacciatore began her career by helping fight the big tobacco companies in Engle progeny cases while working at Abrahamson & Uiterwyk’s Mass Tort Division. Here, she was mentored by the trial legend, Hendrik Uiterwyk, and Anna Frederiksen-Cherry, who taught her the importance of professionalism and communication within the legal field. After gaining valuable experience, she could not pass up an offer to move home to Brevard County and begin working alongside her father and grandfather at Nance Cacciatore.

To complete her J.D., Maddison attended Stetson University College of Law. She says that she did not go to law school only so she could negotiate with insurance adjusters. Instead, she wanted to gain important legal knowledge that she could then pass to the people of her community through her legal representation and counsel.

Recently, Maddison became Guardian ad Litem in Brevard County. In this role, she is assigned to a child within the dependency system and her role is to be an independent, third-party, volunteer who advocates for the best interests of the child. She takes pride in being able to become another trusted adult in a child’s life when that child might be going through one of the most difficult times they will ever face. She describes this opportunity as “eye-opening” and appreciates the way it further connects her to the community she loves.

attorneys.name: Sammy M Cacciatore
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Melbourne, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sam Cacciatore, a native to Melbourne, joined the firm in 1998 following several years as an assistant state attorney in Brevard County. He prosecuted crimes and tried numerous jury trials, obtaining extensive courtroom experience.

In addition to his law degree, Mr. Cacciatore received a master’s degree in health sciences from the University of Florida. His education and experience in this field provide a unique and valuable perspective in understanding the vocational rehabilitation needs of injured people. It also provides a background and understanding of the adjustment that is required for one to cope with new injuries. This is extremely important in evaluating what it takes to help injured individuals recover after a serious accident.

In 2003, Mr. Cacciatore was elected by the membership of the Florida Justice Association to serve on its Board of Directors. In the past, he has also served on the Board of Governors for the Young Lawyers Division of the Florida Bar, the Board of Directors for the Brevard County Bar Association and the Leadership Council for the Take Stock in Children Program of the Brevard County Schools Foundation. Mr. Cacciatore has also served on the Board of Directors of the Brevard Bar Foundation and is a member of the Coastal Conservation Association.

attorneys.name: Sammy Cacciatore
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Melbourne, FL
attorneys.bio:
After a long, successful career, Sammy recently retired to spend more time with his family.

In addition to obtaining numerous multimillion-dollar verdicts and settlements for people injured in auto accidents or victims of medical or professional malpractice, Sammy Cacciatore helped rewrite legal history in 1973.

His pioneering efforts in the case Hoffman v. Jones established comparative negligence as the standard in Florida, which ultimately led to the change to this standard throughout America. He stood off more than 400 corporations in America and changed the way in which injured people are compensated.

In the early 1970s, if defendants could prove that an accident victim was even 1% at fault for the accident, the victim would receive nothing. This legal argument, which unfairly protected big corporations, was called contributory negligence. Sammy argued that contributory negligence was unfair and benefited the wrongdoers who caused accidents. Hoffman v. Jones established comparative negligence as the fairway to rule in personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits. Today, courts and juries determine the degree of fault of all involved and then award damages accordingly.

Born and raised in central Florida, Sammy attended undergraduate and law school at Stetson University. He moved to his wife’s hometown, Melbourne, joining Jim Nance one of the founding members of the Inner Circle of Advocates in August 1967. In addition to his heavy trial practice, Sammy has served on the Board of Directors of the Florida Justice Association for more than 20 years, serving as its president from 1984 to 1985. He was also elected by his colleagues in the Eighteenth Judicial Circuit to represent them on the Board of Governors of the Florida Bar.

Sammy is one of the few lawyers board certified in Civil Trial Law by the Florida Bar and in the specialty of medical malpractice by the American Board of Professional Liability Attorneys. He has handled many medical malpractice cases throughout Central Florida.

Here at home, Sammy has always been involved in the community in some way or another. He is an active member of the Holy Name of Jesus Catholic Church, the Coastal Conservation Association, and the Back Country Fly Fishing Association. When his children were growing up, he was involved in their schools.

attorneys.name: Courtney N. Caddeo
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Palm Harbor, FL
attorneys.bio:
Courtney Caddeo is an experienced Florida divorce and child custody attorney. Ms. Caddeo has worked in the family law arena for many years, including several before actually becoming an attorney. As an attorney, Courtney truly enjoys helping people in tough situations and prides herself on working hard to gain her clients good outcomes. She is both a skilled negotiator and a skilled litigator. When settlement cannot be reached, Courtney is thoroughly prepared to take the matter to court. To her, the greatest satisfaction is obtaining just and fair results.

Courtney attended St. Petersburg College and received her Bachelor’s Degree in Paralegal Studies in 2012. While in college, she gained her first experience in the family law world, working in various non-attorney roles. She quickly realized that family law was the career she was meant to pursue. Prior to law school, she worked her way up from being a receptionist, to becoming a paralegal. After college, she elected to advance her skill set further by going to law school. Courtney obtained her Juris Doctorate degree from Thomas M. Cooley Law School in 2016 and was sworn in as member of the Florida Bar in 2017. Since then, she has dedicated her career exclusively to practicing as a family law attorney.

Over the course of her practice, Courtney has handled all aspects of both simple and complex cases involving divorce, time sharing, child support, alimony, equitable distribution, custodial rights of non-parents, adoptions, dependency, domestic violence injunctions, and many other family law matters. She has developed extreme attention to detail in handling financial aspects of family law cases, and also has been involved in highly litigated time sharing and custody cases.

Courtney was born and raised in Dunedin, Florida and is a rare Pinellas County native. She has practiced primarily in Hillsborough, Pasco, and Pinellas Counties, as well as the surrounding counties of Polk, Hernando, Sarasota, and Manatee.

In her spare time, Courtney enjoys spending time with her family, her 3 Corgis, and rooting for the Tampa Bay Lightning. Contact us online to schedule an appointment with Ms. Caddeo.

Call us today, at (727) 361-2413, or contact us online to schedule a consultation session with Courtney Caddeo.

attorneys.name: Gina Marie Cadogan
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Law Lawyers in Plantation, FL
attorneys.bio:
GINA M. CADOGAN of Cadogan Law located in Plantation, Florida, practices labor employment law counseling and litigation. Prior to owning her law firm, Ms. Cadogan primarily represented Fortune 500 Companies, municipalities, non-profits and hospital systems in employment and commercial litigation at large National and International firms. Presently, she represents individual employees and companies in all aspects of employment and labor claims, including but not limited to discrimination, harassment and retaliation, non-compete agreements, wrongful discharge, workers’ compensation retaliation, unpaid wage claims, overtime claims, negligent hiring/retention, and medical leave violations. Gina also provides advice about a full range of employment matters, including personnel practices and policies, investigation of discrimination, harassment and retaliation claims, medical leave issues, as well as hiring and termination decisions.

Gina frequently speaks on these topics both locally and nationally at legal conferences and to her corporate clients. She recently received recognition for securing a “Top Florida Verdicts of 2014” in a federal disability discrimination case, which was upheld on appeal to the Eleventh Circuit. She has also been honored as “The National Black Lawyers- Top 100” and “Top 100 Attorneys” and “Top 40 Under 40” by both The National Black Lawyers and Legacy Magazine.

Gina received her law degree from Emory University School of Law in 1999 and served on the Moot Court Board and was a recipient of the Order of the Advocates. She graduated from the University of Florida in 1996, with dual degrees and high honors (magna cum laude) and was inducted as a member of the Phi Beta Kappa and Golden Key Honor Societies. She is admitted to the Florida Bar, Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals and the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida. Gina is active in the Federal Bar Association, Caribbean Bar Association and Broward County Bar Association. She also gives back to the legal community by serving as a Board Member for The Federal Bar Association–Broward Chapter, volunteering with the Legal Aid Society, and providing legal assistance to veterans through Mission United Veterans Pro Bono Project. She also volunteers with community outreach organizations, including serving on the Board of E.A.S.E. Foundation, which provides assistance to low income families struggling to make ends meet. Most importantly, Gina loves spending quality time with her two children and husband.

attorneys.bio:
People often ask me why I dedicate my professional life to defending "criminals."

First, the vast majority of my clients are not "criminals." They are honest, decent, and hard-working people, who for a number of different reasons, have made poor life choices and are dealing with the aftermath of those poor life choices. In my experience, the poor life choices that they made are the end result of personal and professional difficulties that they have been dealing with for a long time. They come to my office confused, embarrassed and under a great deal of stress at carrying around the label of someone who has been arrested or accused of committing a crime. I help them navigate the intimidating world of courthouses, judges and prosecutors. With proper representation, they can return to the productive lives that they led before they made the poor life choices that caused them to come to my office.

Second, the general public does not understand that the police quite often get it wrong. Unfounded, false or mistaken charges are sometimes made by family members, domestic partners, friends, employers and police officers. I pride myself on fighting back against those false or mistaken charges made against my clients to allow them to return to their communities and the productive lives that they led with their freedom and reputations intact.

Last, I enjoy taking on the unlimited resources and power of the government, police officers and prosecutors. It is truly a battle between David and Goliath but I relish the challenge.

I pride myself on winning cases for clients, not just "handling" cases. I scrutinize each case to determine if the facts fit the charge and whether the police violated the law in the manner in which they conducted a search or questioned a client for example.

Attorney Caldarone graduated from Pepperdine University (B.A., 1993 and M.A., 1999) in Malibu, California and received his legal degree from Northeastern University School of Law (J.D., 2002) in Boston, Massachusetts.

After graduating from law school, attorney Caldarone was appointed as an Assistant State Attorney for the Miami-Dade County State Attorney's Office. As a prosecutor, Attorney Caldarone has successfully tried as lead counsel and handled hundreds of misdemeanor and felony cases. That intensive experience taught him how police and prosecutors build criminal cases and how to expose the weaknesses in those cases.

Attorney Caldarone is licensed to practice in all state and federal courts in Florida, the Supreme Court of the United States and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Attorney Caldarone is a member of the American Bar Association, National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Collier County Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Greater Naples Chamber of Commerce.

In addition to fighting for his clients, attorney Caldarone prides himself on his involvement in the community. Toward that end, he volunteers his time with the Teen Court of Collier County program and accepts pro bono cases with the Guardian ad Litem office in Collier County, Florida.

attorneys.name: Lawrence C. Callaway III
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Ocala, FL
attorneys.bio:
Lawrence C. Callaway, III, is a transactional, real estate and probate attorney who also handles real estate related litigation matters. He represents both individuals and institutions and also serves as counsel to the Marion County Industrial Development Authority.

Mr. Callaway received his BBA (cum laude) from Stetson University in 1976, and received his JD (cum laude) from that university in 1979. While an undergraduate, he received numerous awards for leadership and scholarship, including being named to Omicron Delta Kappa, the national leadership honorary. In law school, Mr. Callaway served as a teaching assistant and research assistant in the area of commercial law and was honored as a Dana Scholar.

A third generation Floridian, Mr. Callaway was born and raised in West Palm Beach. He moved to Fort Lauderdale after graduating from law school. After practicing in South Florida for almost two decades, Mr. Callaway moved to Ocala to join the firm of Ayres, Cluster, Curry, McCall & Briggs in 1999. In 2008, he joined Randy Klein and Fred Roberts, Jr. at Klein & Klein, LLC.

Mr. Callaway's civic involvement includes serving on the local Board of Directors of the March of Dimes Birth Defects Foundation and acting as Scoutmaster for Troop 100 of the Boy Scouts of America. He has also served as a Board Member and President of the Marion County Public Education Foundation.

Mr. Callaway has been married to his wife, Loxi, for twenty three years. He and his wife have two college age children, Caitlin and Corey.
