attorneys.name: David M. Goldberg
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Thank you for visiting my firm's website, I would tell you that a website may give you an overview of what you may be looking for in an attorney, however, when choosing an attorney you are committing to what could be a prolonged business relationship that in some cases can last years. Thus, I encourage you, that if you are in need of a seasoned litigation attorney that you make an appointment so we can meet face to face in my office to discuss your legal needs. I offer free consultations, and in my firm, you will be meeting with me, not a case manager, paralegal, associate or some other glorified assistance. I handle every case personally for my clients. I have worked in the "large firms" and have chosen to take a different route opening a "boutique" law firm with one on one handling of my clients claims. I am a second generation attorney in Southwest Florida and I have spent my entire career representing the people of my home town of Ft. Myers, Fl and its surrounding areas.

After graduating Highschool from Ft. Myers High School, I attended Tulane University in New Orleans, where I majored in Political Science and where I was inducted into the prestigious Honor Society of Kappa Delta Phi. After graduating with a B.A. I attended Law School at Cumberland School of Law at the Samford University, in Birmingham, Alabama, where I obtained a Juris Doctorate Degree. I then returned to my hometown of Ft. Myers, and began working as a Prosecutor in the 20th Judicial Circuit in Lee County Florida. I obtained my license to practice law in 1995, and continued to prosecute criminals in Lee County, until 1998. I left the State Attorney's Office when I was offered a job at Goldstein, Buckley, Cechman Rice and Purtz where I started practicing in the field of Personal Injury Law. I stayed with GBCRP as a litigation attorney until 2001, when I began work as a senior associate with Geraghty Dougherty and Edwards, PA, where I quickly obtained Partner status. After five years as a partner in the Geraghty firm, I then decided it was time to do things my way and opened my own firm in December of 2005.

I have diligently been practicing personal injury law since 1998. I have been active in the field of criminal defense work, as a former prosecutor, I found a love for the courtroom and practicing criminal defense allows me to hone my litigation skills with constant court appearances.

I am member of the Lee County Bar, as well as the Florida Bar and a member of the Middle District of Florida, United States District Court.

I am also an Eagle Member of the Florida Justice Association formerly the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers, an organization dedicated to protecting the rights of individuals and consumers in the State of Florida.

I have been working in the Court Rooms of Lee County for 16 years vigorously protecting the rights of my clients. I look forward to representing you when you are in need of zealous representation to protect your rights for your legal claims.

As an attorney that has worked in government offices, large offices and mid size offices, I have found that having a solo practice gives me the flexibility to represent my clients on a one on one basis ensuring that each claim is handled with the utmost attention to detail with a personal touch that can not be achieved in large scale firms.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born and Raised in New York, with a background as a school psychologist and Special Education instructor, Mr. Golden has been practicing law since 1977. During the last 40 years as a Miami-Dade County probate lawyer, he has been focusing on the areas of Probate, Guardianship and Trust litigation and administration.

Mr. Golden wrote the guidelines for the Probate Court for Cuban Blocked Estates and has a license from the U.S Treasury Department to travel to Cuba to represent Cuban National Beneficiaries of Florida estates. As Chairman of the Internal Procedures Committee, Mr. Golden works closely with the four Miami-Dade County Probate Judges and with Probate and Guardianship attorneys and practitioners to enhance operation of the probate court.

Mr. Golden has served as Chairman of the Dade County Probate & Guardianship Committee and has served the Bar on the following committees:

Mr. Golden is licensed to practice law before the Federal and State Courts of Florida, the United States Tax Court, and the United States Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit . Mr. Golden graduated from the University of Florida with a bachelors degree in Business Administration majoring in finance. After graduating Mr. Golden worked for an analytics company which provided advanced statistical information to both the NCAA and NBA. Mr. Golden continued to work in analytics throughout law school in addition to clerking at a law firm and graduated early from the Shepard Broad Law School at Nova Southeastern University in 2016. Mr. Golden went on to obtain his LL.M. degree in Taxation from the University of Miami School of Law in 2017. Mr. Golden has assisted in the production and publication of articles in national legal journals in the areas of tax law.

As an active member of the community Mr. Golden volunteers his time to lecture and provide assistance through various organizations which focus on both legal assistance and education to the less fortunate. Mr. Golden looks to align himself with any person or organization seeking to further beneficial community efforts and invites those like-minded individuals to contact him with their cause. Mr. Golden enjoys yoga, animals, reading, puzzle games, the NBA, and college football.

attorneys.name: Matthew Goldkind
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Matthew is a litigator known for developing thoughtful case strategies from the outset, communicating with clients empathetically, and advocating zealously in the courtroom. Prior to joining AXS LAW, Matthew worked for three years at the Miami-Dade Public Defender's Office, where he litigated five trials to verdict and upwards of a dozen evidentiary hearings.

Matthew earned his Juris Doctor magna cum laude from Harvard Law School in 2022. In law school, Matthew sought extensive clinical experience—drafting appellate amicus briefs, representing indigent criminal defendants, and conducting mediations. He also served on the editorial board of the Civil Rights-Civil Liberties Law Review and was a member of the Board of Student Advisers.

Prior to law school, Matthew worked for nearly two years at Treacy & Company, a management consulting firm. He graduated from Washington University in St. Louis with a B.A. In 2019. Outside of work, Matthew enjoys visiting national parks, running, and singing.

attorneys.name: John Golding
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
John Golding is a seasoned Trial Attorney with more than 25 years of courtroom experience arguing cases involving automobile, motorcycle and boating negligence, defective products and hazardous conditions. Having ridden motorcycles since age 10, and having operated boats since his teens, John understands the dynamics and mechanics of automobile, motorcycle and boating accidents. He possesses the experience and knowledge necessary to evaluate product crashworthiness, to assess driver/operator error, and to maximize the recovery for victims of roadway, off-road and waterway negligence.

BACKGROUND

John grew up in Southwest Virginia, graduated cum laude from Bluefield State College in 1983, and obtained his law degree from the University of Louisville in 1986. Upon graduation, John's love for the water prompted him to move to Tampa. Shortly thereafter, John began devoting his practice to exclusively personal injury matters. He is a veteran trial lawyer who has established a reputation for skilled advocacy. John is licensed to practice throughout Florida State and Federal Courts, and the US Supreme Court. John has obtained an AV rating from Martindale Hubbell, the highest rating an attorney can achieve for legal ability and ethics.

attorneys.name: Mitchell Scott Goldman
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Lawyers in Cocoa, FL
attorneys.bio:
I am a native of Florida and Brevard County, and grew up in Melbourne Beach. For college, I went to Washington University in St. Louis, where I graduated magna cum laude with a degree in economics. Law school followed, at Washington University in St. Louis when I graduated in 1984.

It has been my honor to represent many different lenders and bankers during my forty plus years of practice. I conducted loan closings for national banks, insurance companies, regional banks, local banks, credit unions, CDFIs, private and out-of-state lenders. Working with so many fine and caring bankers throughout my career, some in excess of thirty years, has been an amazing and meaningful experience. We closed, and continue to close loans for a myriad of borrowers, including: (a) manufacturing companies; (b) hotels; (c) gas stations; (d) mobile home parks; and, (e) strip centers. The types of loans include conventional loans for purchases and refinances, construction loans, owner financing, and SBA (7)(a) and 504 loans.

In addition to commercial lending, I handle other types of real estate transactions including, 1031 exchanges, drafting sales contracts, leases, and easements, title insurance matters, residential closings, and assisting buyers with their due diligence. I handle commercial and residential real estate matters throughout Florida.

Supporting the community where I was raised and where I practice is of critical importance to me. In 1993, I became a charter member of the Rockledge Rotary Club, I was its third president, and remain a member. Also, I was a past president of the Central Brevard Sharing Center, Central Brevard Chapter of the American Cancer Society, Brevard County Legal Aid Society, and Crosswinds Youth Services (twice). I had the privilege of serving as legal counsel for the Cocoa Beach Area Chamber of Commerce, and also served on the Board of Directors for the Eastern Florida State College Foundation.

When not working, I love to spend time with my wife, Cindy, and our dog, Morty, working out and going for long walks. Watching my favorite sports teams is most enjoyable, go Cardinals, Gators, Celtics and Jets! Reading is also a passion, and I am working on a book with the tentative title of "Real, Real Estate."

Working with my valued staff to help our clients reach their goals and realize their dreams is truly gratifying.

attorneys.bio:
Richard J. Goldman has been duly licensed to practice law by the Supreme Court of the State of Florida since 1988, by the Supreme Court of the United States of America since 1991, and by the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida since 1996. Mr. Goldman has been a member of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America since 1988.

After obtaining his Juris Doctorate at Nova University in 1988, Mr. Goldman worked exclusively in insurance defense where he was responsible for defending insurance carriers, self-insureds, school districts, hospital districts, and cities, in all insurance-related claims in Circuit Court.

After practicing Personal Injury and Workers’ Compensation law from 1992 through 2004 as a partner with the Law Firm of Grossman & Goldman, P.A., Mr. Goldman opened his own practice, devoting his time solely to representing persons injured in work-related accidents, Personal Injury cases, Medical Malpractice, Product Liability as well as Construction Litigation.

Although he practices principally in Palm Beach and Broward Counties, Mr. Goldman has also tried numerous cases in several other Counties throughout Florida in Circuit Courts and Workers’ Compensation Courts. He has also tried several Federal District Court cases in the Southern District of Florida and has been involved in multi-district litigation cases as co-counsel.

Mr. Goldman is Board eligible and has yet to seek certification from the Florida Bar as a specialist in Workers’ Compensation. He has previously lectured on several topics dealing with Workers’ Compensation.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
BRIAN GONZALEZ PROFILE

Tampa Criminal Defense Attorney Brian E. Gonzalez's polished trial skills and professional demeanor have earned him the respect of clients, peers, prosecutors and judges throughout Florida. He has successfully tried important high stakes cases that were broadcast beginning to end on Court TV, earning praise from other commentators and legal experts.

Brian received his Juris Doctorate degree from South Texas College of Law in 1984. Before attending law school, he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science from the University of Florida in 1981. He was a scholarship baseball player while at UF, his teams winning Southeastern Conference Championships in 1980 and 1981.

Brian has been a member of several legal organizations such as the American Bar Association, the Florida Bar Criminal Section, the Hillsborough County Bar Association, the Hillsborough County Criminal Defense Lawyer's Association and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

He began his legal career in 1985 in Tampa, where his family has lived for over 100 years as an Associate with the respected criminal firm of Ferlita, Nutter and Rosello, P.A. In 1989, he opened the Law Offices of Brian E. Gonzalez, P.A. and was soon well known for his defense of high profile cases in Hillsborough County. Brian represented Jon Whispel, whose case garnered national attention after he and Adam Davis participated in the murder of Vickie Robinson, the mother of teenager and co-defendant Valessa Robinson. He also, at one time, represented infamous serial killer Oscar Ray Bolin. Other high profile cases include representation of Robert Brim, known as the Hyde Park Rapist, whose defense included the first successful pretrial attack on the admissibility of DNA evidence in a criminal case and Joshua Rosa, whose first degree murder trial was televised gavel to gavel nationally by Court TV.

For in excess of 29 years, Brian Gonzalez has committed himself to only defending criminal cases. He has personally handled over 7,000 criminal cases to conclusion in numerous Florida counties, every Florida Federal District Court and in multiple states. He has diligently represented criminal defendants in over 220 trials with clients charged with everything from first degree murder, drug trafficking, robbery and rape to theft, violation of probation and DUI.

Winning a case depends not only on the circumstances of your charges but upon how well it is presented to a judge, a jury or a prosecutor. You need experience on your side. You need a strong reputation on your side. You need an attorney who has had continued success in the courtroom by concentrating on only one area of the law - criminal law.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Jorge L. Gonzalez, PA
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Doral, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Miami, Florida, Diego Gonzalez is a 2nd generation attorney who realized at a young age that he wanted to pursue a career that involves helping the people of his home community. Diego used to spend his summers observing and assisting his father, Jorge Luis Gonzalez, in his family law practice that has served hundreds of clients for more than 30 years. He would see how his father would alleviate the concerns of people at the lowest points of their lives through careful and respectful discussion, before watching him zealously advocate for his clients in the courtroom through arguments that were fierce as they were shrewd and diplomatic. It was through these experiences that Diego recognized his calling to help others in need.

After graduating from Florida State University in 2018 with Cum Laude honors and a B.S. in International Affairs, Diego immediately began his legal journey at Saint Thomas University College of Law in Miami Gardens, Florida. It was there that Diego gained a deep knowledge and appreciation for Criminal Procedure, in which he earned the CALI Book Award for the highest grade in his class. Diego was then admitted into Saint Thomas’s award-winning Trial Team, where he sharpened his trial advocacy skills in a program renowned for their consistently high-level performances in competitions across Florida and the country.

In 2021, after graduating from law school and passing the Florida Bar, Diego’s combined appreciations for criminal procedure and trial advocacy led him to becoming an Assistant Public Defender for the Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida in Miami-Dade county. In his two years there, Diego successfully defended several hundreds of indigent clients at the Misdemeanor and Felony Levels, including drafting/arguing several substantive motions and taking multiple cases to jury trial.

Today, Diego is once again working alongside his father Jorge - except now, as an associate attorney with the valuable legal experience necessary to effectively serve the citizens of South Florida. Diego now remains focused in zealously defending people accused of crimes and also increasing his proficiency in family law, all while continuing to defend hundreds of civil infractions across the state. If you seek an attorney within these practice areas that is eager to listen and fight for your rights, call 305-703-7459 or 786-474-6444 to schedule your free consultation.

attorneys.name: Anthony Gonzalez Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Foreclosure Defense Lawyers in Plantation, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Gonzalez has legal experience representing clients with their consumer financial services and other civil litigation issues. As a Plantation Florida Lawyer some of Mr. Gonzalez’s areas of practice involve: defense against Home Owner Association’s (HOA’s), Foreclose Defense, Credit Card Debt Defense, defending individuals who were being sued for Deficiency Judgments, Contract Disputes, representing clients in Federal Bankruptcy Court in the Southern District of Florida.

LEADERSHIP, MEMBERSHIP & HONORS

Mr. Gonzalez is a proven leader with a passion for providing service to his community. While enrolled at TAMIU, Mr. Gonzalez served as a member of Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity and served as their President in 2007-08. During Mr. Gonzalez’s undergraduate studies, he became familiar with all different aspects of the criminal justice system; specifically, by partaking in unpaid internships at both the Laredo Police Department and at the Federal Public Defenders Office.

Mr. Gonzalez’s observed the criminal justice system first hand at the Laredo Police Department where he participated in ride along with police officers and observed the police departments normal interactions with citizens. On occasion he even viewed arrests and bookings for criminal violations. Mr. Gonzalez’s experience interning at the Federal Public Defenders Office allowed him to see what it was like for individuals who had already been incarcerated and were awaiting to speak with their attorney and/or were awaiting trial. These experiences allowed Mr. Gonzalez have benefited him as a Plantation Florida Lawyer. He has gained profound respect and admiration for the legislative branch (creates the laws), executive branch (includes our criminal justice system and those who enforce the laws), and the judicial system (most commonly comprised of the judges, attorneys, and jurors who make sure that the laws are properly enforced against an individual and/or entity).

SERVICE TO THE COMMUNITY

Mr. Gonzalez was told throughout his childhood by his loving mother that, “it is more important to give a gift then to receive a gift.” Mr. Gonzalez was taught at a young age the importance of always lending a helping hand to the individuals in his community. To instill this principal, Mr. Gonzalez partook in the annual family tradition of volunteering at many community events as a young man which stemmed from feeding the homeless on Thanksgiving Day to cleaning up around his city.

After moving to South Florida to begin his career as a lawyer, Mr. Gonzalez always remembered the importance of assisting those in his community. Mr. Gonzalez has regularly volunteered at Feeding South Florida and at Jubilee Center of South Broward.

FEEDING SOUTH FLORIDA

Mr. Gonzalez’s volunteer work and efforts have served nearly 800,000 food insecure individuals in the quad-county service area. Mr. Gonzalez played a vital part in the daily operations by helping sort through donated food to ensure that it was safe to go back out to the community for consumption. Much of what of what is done at Feeding South Florida (“FSF”) is dependent on volunteer help in the warehouse. In addition, food donated from food drives, supermarkets and other food industry companies must be sorted, checked, and repackaged. Volunteers process the bulk of the food in salvage creating a constant need for individuals in that department. Without volunteers, FSF would not be able to sustain the more than 40 million pounds of food and grocery product that comes through their doors annually. Mr. Gonzalez’s efforts at FSF have been described by a Volunteer Coordinator as follows: Mr. Gonzalez was always willing to stay late, do the dirty work, and help ensure that the job gets done. We truly appreciated all of his work, dedication, and extra time donated to our organization.”

JUBILEE CENTER OF SOUTH BROWARD

Mr. Gonzalez has also volunteered regularly at Jubilee Center of South Broward (“JCSB”). The mission of JCSB is to provide emergency resources and relief from huger and despair by serving individuals and families through various programs, including their Soup Kitchen, Food Pantry, hygiene kits, clothing, and by providing these individuals information and referrals to other agencies throughout the County which may be able to assist them in their time of despair. The services that JCSB provides to the community are always free of charge. An office administrator of JCSB has stated the following about Mr. Gonzalez’s community service at the JCSB:[Mr. Gonzalez] has helped us with various tasks including prepping and serving lunch, stocking the pantry, cleaning and whatever projects needed to be done. We are glad to have had [Mr. Gonzalez] with us, he has gone above and beyond our expectations for a volunteer. Anthony has gained the love and respect of our entire staff and our clients. We are truly grateful for all of his hard work and dedication….

Mr. Gonzalez’s care for his South Florida community has resulted in over 195 hours of combined community service rendered at Feeding South Florida and the Jubilee Center of South Broward. As a Manager-Member of Light & Gonzalez, PLLC, Mr. Gonzalez continues to serve and give back to the South Florida community.

attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Gina Gonzalez is a trial and litigation attorney, concentrating her practice on representing individuals injured as a result of the negligence of others. Gina firmly believes in accountability, and justice for those burdened by the weight of fighting against large insurance companies with seemingly endless resources.

Born and raised outside Ft. Lauderdale, Gina has always been a Florida native. She is a proud double Gator, graduating cum laude from the University of Florida College of Business, majoring in Business Administration with a minor in Entrepreneurship. She also graduated cum laude from the University of Florida Levin College of Law, where she was an executive board member of the Florida Moot Court Team.

While working part-time in law school, Gina quickly learned it was her desire to concentrate her legal career in the practice of personal injury law. She received the book award in Medical Malpractice, and was recruited immediately out of law school to join Morgan & Morgan. Throughout her time at the firm, Gina has been able to put her litigation skills to the test and truly fight for the justice that our clients deserve.

Gina works out of the Tampa office and handles cases in the greater Tampa Bay area, but she remains true to her hometown as a loyal fan to the Miami Dolphins.

attorneys.name: Orlando Gonzalez
attorneys.practice_type: Drug Charges Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Orlando Gonzalez is a trial lawyer with over sixteen years of litigation experience in both the criminal and family law. Mr. Gonzalez’s trial experience includes a wide variety of jury trials ranging from DUI to attempted 1st degree murder. In addition, Mr. Gonzalez has successfully represented clients in family law actions involving, divorce, child custody, child support, petition for relocation and paternity matters. Mr. Gonzalez provides representation in all Florida Courts and in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

In addition, Mr. Gonzalez represents the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office with litigation in forfeiture matters. Forfeiture matters involve the seizure of property, e.g. US currency, automobile and/or boats by law enforcement officers, when a person is accused or a violation of law (committing a crime).

Mr. Gonzalez attended Eastern Michigan University, Ypsilanti, MI on a full athletic scholarship. Mr. Gonzalez was selected to the Michigan All-State baseball first team as a junior and senior at Bishop Gallagher High School in Harper Woods, Michigan. After attending E.M.U. Mr. Gonzalez joined the West Palm Beach Police Department where he worked as a road patrolman and as a detective in the Special Operations Division. In 1993 Mr. Gonzalez attended Stetson University College of Law and has been in practice since 1996. Mr. Gonzalez’s police experience provides a tremendous advantage to his clients charged with violations of Florida and/or Federal laws.

He founded the Premises Liability Department for the firm's Central Florida offices, and then led Florida's Fire Litigation Practice, which specializes in wrongful death cases caused by fire. A large portion of his practice is devoted to litigating crashes involving interstate/intrastate trucking companies.

Mr. Gonzalez has represented professional athletes from the NBA and PGA Tour, and has given lectures on personal injury law to hundreds of attorneys across the country. He has also been featured on numerous national and local media outlets, and can be frequently seen on the Firm's television commercials.

Since joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Gonzalez has effectively and successfully represented individuals and families throughout the country, where he has achieved substantial verdicts and settlements for multi-millions of dollars. While some cases may be settled without the need for trial, he firmly believes in aggressively representing his clients and will pursue litigation whenever it is necessary. To date, he has litigated hundreds of cases against the largest corporations and insurance companies in the world. His primary goal is to make sure his clients receive the personal attention and justice they deserve.

attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Claims Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
James "Jim" Goodnow was born and raised in upstate New York. He graduated with honors from the State University of New York at Oswego and attended law school in his hometown at Syracuse University College of Law.

Following law school, Mr. Goodnow moved to Florida and began his legal career as an Assistant State Attorney in Pasco County, where he tried numerous cases. He often prosecuted the office's toughest cases involving the most serious crimes and worst criminals, earning a reputation as an aggressive trial attorney who fought hard for justice on behalf of the victims of crimes.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Goodnow was a partner in a large Florida insurance defense law firm where he successfully defended multiple Florida insurance carriers throughout the State of Florida in various types of homeowner and commercial insurance claims by their insureds, including losses caused by water, mold, wind, hail and fire. His success includes the defense of these insurance carriers at Trial and the verdicts he obtained in their favor on a variety of insurance claims.

After years of defending insurance companies and watching how they worked to deny and underpay valid claims by their insureds, Mr. Goodnow now exclusively represents insured policyholders and homeowners who have had their insurance claims wrongfully denied or underpaid by their insurance company. If you need help with your insurance claim, contact Morgan & Morgan so Mr. Goodnow can help you.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
James "Jim" Goodnow was born and raised in upstate New York. He graduated with honors from the State University of New York at Oswego and attended law school in his hometown at Syracuse University College of Law.

Following law school, Mr. Goodnow moved to Florida and began his legal career as an Assistant State Attorney in Pasco County, where he tried numerous cases. He often prosecuted the office's toughest cases involving the most serious crimes and worst criminals, earning a reputation as an aggressive trial attorney who fought hard for justice on behalf of the victims of crimes.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Goodnow was a partner in a large Florida insurance defense law firm where he successfully defended multiple Florida insurance carriers throughout the State of Florida in various types of homeowner and commercial insurance claims by their insureds, including losses caused by water, mold, wind, hail and fire. His success includes the defense of these insurance carriers at Trial and the verdicts he obtained in their favor on a variety of insurance claims.

After years of defending insurance companies and watching how they worked to deny and underpay valid claims by their insureds, Mr. Goodnow now exclusively represents insured policyholders and homeowners who have had their insurance claims wrongfully denied or underpaid by their insurance company. If you need help with your insurance claim, contact Morgan & Morgan so Mr. Goodnow can help you.

attorneys.name: Matthew Goodwin
attorneys.practice_type: Estate law (Real Estate, Estate Planning & Administration) Lawyers in NAPLES, FL
attorneys.bio:
Real Estate Lawyer, Closings and Escrow, Probate, serving Collier and Lee Counties, Florida. The firm handles trust and estate planning for simple and complex estates, as well as real estate closings and escrow services to buyers and sellers of real estate, and probate and trust administration.

Matt has built relationships with a number of trusted realtors and advisors who are available to aid his clients in their real estate needs and the estate planning process ensuring his client always have a comprehensive plan in place and a trusted professional to rely on.

In today's age of technology, our society relies so heavily on computers to make decisions for us. However, when it comes to legal issues, there is no substitute for an attorney's judgment. Computers are good for completing routine tasks, and for processing large amounts of data, but neither a computer nor a computer generated form you can download from the Internet is a genuine substitute for a lawyer's individual judgment and counsel.

Matt realizes that there are many estate planning options out there, and you can now purchase a form will or even a trust on the internet at a substantial discount. However, what those documents lack are the judgment, counsel, and integrity of a real person.

Matt has worked in the service industry for more than 10 years. He has extensive experience working with people and enjoys solving complex problems. On the weekends, Matt enjoys spending time with his family, spending time outdoors, running and bike riding. He currently resides in the City of Naples with his wife Nancy, his son Justin, and their dog Max.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey F. Gordon P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey F. Gordon joined the team at Lesser, Lesser, Landy and Smith, PLLC in 2018, following a 30-year career at the law firm of Board and Cassel.

Jeff was born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania in 1961. He attended Emory University in Atlanta,Georgia where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Philosophy and Political Science. Jeff then attended the University of Florida School of Law earning his J.D. degree. While in law school, he served as Chief Defense Counsel for the University of Florida Honor Court, was a legal research and writing teaching assistant, and served as a certified legal intern with the Public Defender's Office, where he tried numerous criminal cases. Upon graduation in 1986, he began work as a criminal defense attorney in Miami, where he received extensive trial experience.

In 1987, Jeff joined the law firm of Broad and Cassel. He became an equity partner in 1994. He served as the firm's sole personal injury attorney, handling cases throughout Florida and in numerous other states.

Jeff has been a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer since 1993, and is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates.

Jeff is very active in his community. He has been a licensed foster parent since 2010. He is Chairman of the

Board of Champions Empowering Champions, an organization that supports former foster youth at Florida Atlantic University. He served as Chairman of the Palm Beach Advisory Group with the foster care agency

Kids in Distress, and he is a proud Board Member of Friends of Foster Children, a foster support group in

West Palm Beach. Jeff has coached over 50 different youth sports teams in Boca Raton.

Outside of work, Jeff enjoys playing basketball in several leagues and in Masters Basketball tournaments

throughout the country. He is also a guitarist in The Fast Crowd, a classic rock band that plays locally in

Boca Raton. Since 1994, Jeff has taught as an Adjunct Professor at Florida Atlantic University, teaching at

least one class per semester in Civil Litigation, Criminal Law and Personal Injury.

Jeff's practice focuses on personal injury and wrongful death litigation. He has successfully handled

numerous claims in excess of one million dollars. He has litigated all types of personal injury and wrongful

death claims, including automobile liability, medical malpractice, premises liability, and products liability.

He has extensive experience in highway construction site and commercial trucking accident cases.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey "Jack" Gordon
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey “Jack” Gordon is a highly skilled trial attorney who has been profiled among the Top Lawyers© in the Bay Area by Tampa Bay Magazine and has twice been selected a Leading Attorney of the Southeastern United States in Forbes magazine. For over a decade, he has been selected for inclusion among Florida Trend's Legal Elite, most recently inducted into the Florida Trend's Legal Elite Hall of Fame, and recognized as one of the Top 100 SuperLawyers® in the state of Florida along with one of the Top 50 SuperLawyers® of Tampa Bay.

As managing partner, Mr. Gordon concentrates on prosecuting claims of medical negligence and was voted by his peers as Tampa Magazine’s Top Lawyer® since 2016 in Medical Malpractice (Plaintiffs).

Five times Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by The Florida Bar, Mr. Gordon is also twice certified by The National Board of Trial Advocacy as an expert in both Civil Trial Law and Civil Pre-trial Litigation. He is AV® rated Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell.

In 2017, Mr. Gordon earned National Board Certification as an expert in Medical Malpractice law by the American Board of Professional Liability Attorneys. He is 1 of merely 17 lawyers in the State of Florida to have achieved this distinction.

Mr. Gordon is a Fellow of the Litigation Counsel of America, Trial Lawyer Honorary Society, and serves as a member of both the Trial Law Institute and the Diversity Law Institute.

Mr. Gordon garnered a 2014 and 2015 National Litigator Award from the Trial Lawyers Board of Regents and is a Lifetime Member of The Million Dollar Advocates Forum having achieved multiple seven-figure jury verdicts and settlements.

Mr. Gordon was honored in Florida Top Verdicts for having obtained the largest award in a lawsuit against a Dram Shop in 2011 (8.25 Million Dollars). Mr. Gordon prosecutes these claims individually and continues to serve as co-counsel throughout Florida for the purpose of assisting fellow lawyers to represent individuals injured as a result of the improper service of alcohol by bars, stores and restaurants.

In December of 2017, he obtained the largest award in a lawsuit involving a motorcycle accident (14.95 Million Dollars). After jury selection and merely four days of testimony in what was expected to be a 10-day trial, GEICO executives at the corporate headquarters in Maryland authorized consent judgment before verdict.

Mr. Gordon has been elected to membership in the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA) and is listed in The Best Lawyers in America (2020 Edition).

Mr. Gordon has also achieved national recognition for his efforts in seeking to overcome tribal sovereign immunity on behalf of critically injured clients in multiple lawsuits filed against the Seminole Tribe of Florida.

Mr. Gordon remains committed to representing individuals who have been injured, and families of relatives who have been killed, as a result of medical malpractice, motor vehicle negligence, and dram shop violations. Mr. Gordon is admitted to practice law in the state of Florida and in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, and has tried and argued cases in jurisdictions throughout the United States.

Since 1992, Mr. Gordon has combined his passion for helping others with his precision advocacy and has represented victims of negligence in cases ranging from catastrophic vehicular accidents to boat explosions to surgical errors to failed hospital equipment. In addition to representing families who have lost members due to wrongful death, Jack has represented clients who have suffered a myriad of injuries including spinal perforations, silicone induced fibromyalgia, brain traumas, loss of limbs, paralysis, and organ loss.

BACKGROUND

With a strong work ethic, established by his family and forged by a father who worked as a brick mason, Jack has been driven to succeed in all aspects of his life — from excelling in school to winning in the courtroom today. While earning his Bachelor’s degree in English at Tulane University, Jack played lacrosse and minored in physiology. At Tulane University School of Law, he combined his passions for health and scholarship, and in 1988 introduced to the Louisiana legislature a proposal forcing pharmacies to provide enhanced disclosure on consumer prescriptions.

Out of law school, Jack clerked for Judge Edward Barfield in the First District Court of Appeal and then received the appointment as Special Assistant Public Defender for the Appellate Division of Dade County, Florida. In 1990, he became the youngest certified Circuit Court Arbitrator in Palm Beach County. Entering private practice in 1992, Jack served as legal counsel to U.S. Total Health and Fitness and Gold’s Gym, and still found time to earn APFC, IPFA and ACE certifications as a personal trainer.

It is this background that naturally led Jack to represent plaintiffs suffering from injuries as a result of negligence and medical malpractice. In 1994, Jack established his reputation by successfully representing more than 120 women injured as a result of silicone breast implants in cases against the pharmaceutical manufacturers.

attorneys.bio:
Pamela M. Gordon, Esq. is a litigation attorney with over twenty years of legal experience. She has a Bachelor of Science in Communications, from Florida State University, and a Juris Doctor, from University of Miami. Ms. Gordon is the founding Partner of the Law Office of Pamela M. Gordon, P.A., in Hollywood, Florida. In June 2017 in recognition of her exhibition of the highest degree of professionalism, Ms. Gordon received the Broward County Bar Association’s Joseph J. Carter Professionalism Award. Ms. Gordon has experience practicing in the areas of marital and family law, commercial litigation, foreclosure defense, bankruptcy and appeals. She has a Fourth District Court of Appeal opinion which is a precedent in the State of Florida, as it relates to Parenting Plans and Timesharing. Ms. Gordon is also a trained collaborative law attorney and a marital and family law mediator.

In addition, Ms. Gordon is passionate about giving back to her Caribbean American Community and her Community at large. attorneys.name: Michael A. Gottlieb
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense State and Federal Court Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael A. Gottlieb is AV peer-review rated through Martindale-Hubbell, which is the highest rating a lawyer can obtain. Mr. Gottlieb began his career in the legal justice system working for the Broward Sheriff's office in the legal department. Following that job, he became an Assistant Broward County Public Defender; he has practiced criminal defense for 30 years. He attended Nova Southeastern University Law School and The George Washington University where he obtained a Bachelor of Science in political science.

As a criminal defense lawyer in Broward County, Florida, Mr. Gottlieb has handled thousands of cases and tried more than 150 criminal jury trials to verdict. Mr. Gottlieb has attained acquittals in Murder in the First Degree, Attempted Murder in the First Degree of a Law Enforcement Officer, State Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon, DUI Manslaughter cases, as well as many lesser charges.

Mr. Gottlieb has also successfully had many cases dismissed by pre-trial motion such as Perjury, Trafficking in Oxycodone and Possession of Cocaine among numerous others. A vigorous motion practice helps Mr. Gottlieb maintain many dismissals without subjecting clients to expense and anxiety of trial.

Michael Gottlieb is experienced in vigorously seeking out critical deficiencies that weaken the prosecution's case against you and possibly avoiding a trial altogether.

Call Mr. Gottlieb today for a free case evaluation.

attorneys.name: Jessica Gow
attorneys.practice_type: Land Use & Zoning Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jessica Gow was born and raised in Ocala, Florida, and attended the University of West Florida after graduating from Belleview High School. After graduating Magna Cum Laude and as an Honors Scholar with the University of West Florida, Mrs. Gow attended the Florida State University College of Law. While in law school, Mrs. Gow served as the President of the Environmental Law Society, Associate Editor of the Journal of Land Use and Environmental Law, and Notes and Comments Editor for the Florida State University Law Review. Mrs. Gow also volunteered as a Peer Mentor for the law school, and acted as a student ambassador throughout her time there.

Throughout her law school career, Mrs. Gow worked with various environmental nonprofits, including Save the Manatee Club, Surfrider Foundation, the Florida Coastal and Ocean Coalition, and Earthjustice, the nonprofit law firm. Mrs. Gow also worked in real property and land use matters at Gunster Law Firm, located in Tallahassee, Florida, and worked alongside University professors as a research assistant in the areas of Torts, Tax law, Environmental law, and Administrative law. Mrs. Gow graduated Magna Cum Laude, with a certificate in Environmental and Land Use law.

Mrs. Gow focuses her practice in the fields of environmental and land use law, assisting in the redevelopment of real property through the Florida Brownfield Program and assisting in all aspects of the regulatory and permitting review process for development projects.

Mrs. Gow currently serves on the executive board of the Volusia County Association for Responsible Development (VCARD), and is an appointed board member of the Volusia Forever Advisory Committee and the Environmental and Natural Resources Advisory Committee. Mrs. Gow is also closely involved in Homes Bring Hope, an organized dedicated to eradicating homelessness in Volusia County, along with being a member of the Florida Brownfields Association.

In her free time, Jessica enjoys playing board games, enjoying Florida's coast, and going hiking with her husband, Jeramie, and their two dogs.

attorneys.name: Dillon Graham
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Trial Law Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
A respected Florida foreclosure lawyer, Miami-based Dillon Graham is the founder and managing attorney of Graham Legal, P.A., which is located in Coral Gables (Miami), Florida.

With more than 30 years of legal experience, he possesses a unique dedication to helping victims pursue justice in cases related to foreclosure defense and personal injury.

"I don't know of anything more satisfying," reflects Dillon, "than to be able to help someone during what may be one of the hardest times in their life. I really count myself lucky because I can use my knowledge and skill as a foreclosure lawyer to help people when they face a foreclosure on their home. We can't undo the past, but I can certainly help them look toward a brighter future, and that means a lot to me."

Mr. Graham is an experienced civil trial attorney and is admitted to practice before the U.S. Supreme Court, the U.S. Court of Appeals, local U.S. District Courts, and in all Florida state courts.

He has obtained the highest available peer-review rating of "A-V" by Martindale-Hubbell.* He is a proud member of the Florida Justice Association. Furthermore, he is a member of the American Justice Association, the Miami-Dade County Bar Association, and the Miami-Dade County Justice Association.

Martindale-Hubbell provides the most widely recognized ratings of lawyers, and has been doing so for over 100 years. There are two categories of ratings. "Legal Ability Ratings" range from "C" (for Good to High), "B" (for High to Very High), and "A" (for Very High to Preeminent). The "General Ethical Standards Rating" is "V" (Very High).

attorneys.name: Jennifer Grant
attorneys.practice_type: Estate & Trust Litigation Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
The founder of her own law firm since 2009, Jennifer Grant focuses her practice primarily on complex trust, estate, and guardianship litigation. Her firm assists families, fiduciaries and beneficiaries in cases involving will contests, fiduciary removal and defense, the appointment of guardians, trust and estate administration, elder exploitation and similar matters. Prior to focusing on these areas, Jennifer was a commercial litigator representing both plaintiffs and defendants in all types of business disputes involving contract breaches, fraud, and shareholder and partnership disputes among other issues. This experience providers her the skill set needed to pursue whatever rights her clients have in these areas including when an estate or trust holds disputed business interests. Jennifer has received recognition from her clients and fellow attorneys alike for her successful track record, dedication to helping clients make the right decision for them, and swift action towards resolution. Jennifer also prides herself on being accessible and available to her clients during these stressful times.

Jennifer attended the University of Florida for both her undergraduate degree in Broadcast Journalism and graduate degree, her Juris Doctor. Jennifer obtained her LLM (masters of law) in estate planning from the University of Miami, Heckerling Institute. Prior to Jennifer having her own firm, Jennifer worked at prominent, large Florida law firms, where she gained significant experience in complex civil litigation cases involving shareholder and partner disputes, professional negligence, intellectual property issues, and business torts. There, she also received training in probate and trust administration before starting her own firm in December 2009.

Ms. Grant is a member in good standing of The Florida Bar and thus is admitted to practice before all Florida state courts. She is also admitted to practice before the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida. A member of several professional organizations and an avid community volunteer, Ms. Grant also presently sits on the board of directors for the American Cancer Society.

attorneys.name: Frederick "Fritz" Gray
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Fritz Gray, of counsel, has been a practicing attorney in Tampa for more than 30 years. He is AV-rated by Martindale Hubbell with extensive experience in complex civil trials focusing on medical malpractice, general negligence, wrongful death, automobile accidents and premises liability. Mr. Gray has been a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer since 1989 by the Florida Bar and is also certified as a Civil Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy since 1986. In addition, Mr. Gray has been selected by his peers as a Florida Super Lawyer from 2007 through 2017. In 1997, Mr. Gray was invited for membership to the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA). Mr. Gray is a member of the American Association of Justice since 1982 and Florida Justice Association since 1984, Board of Directors, 1994-1998.

Mr. Gray has been admitted to practice law in Florida since 1984. Mr. Gray is also admitted to practice before the United States Supreme Court, The Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States District Court, Middle District of Florida.

Mr. Gray has received multiple million dollar verdicts and settlements in medical malpractice, wrongful death and premise liability cases. Mr. Gray has lectured about medical malpractice issues to medical students at the University of South Florida School of Medicine as well as attorneys. Mr. Gray has spent much of his career in handling spinal cord, brain, and amputation injuries that resulted from medical malpractice and automobile negligence.

BACKGROUND

Mr. Gray grew up in Iowa and attended the University of Wyoming in 1973. He received his B.A. in Business Administration and Theatrical Arts, 1977. During the summer months of 1974 & 1975, Mr. Gray toured the Rocky Mountain States performing summer stock. Mr. Gray graduated from Drake University Law School in 1980. From 1981 to the present, Mr. Gray has consistently represented the interests of injured persons in cases of personal injury and wrongful death from medical malpractice, automobile accidents, and premises liability.

attorneys.name: Terry Gray
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Terry A. C. Gray graduated with Honors from the University of Virginia's exclusive Political Honors Program, and also served as President of the University's Student Council and Student Body. Following graduation, Mr. Gray was awarded a Henry Luce Fellowship which he spent in Thailand in the arena of local political development.

He is a graduate of Stanford Law School where he was a member of both the Stanford Law Review and the Stanford Law & Policy Review. During law school, Mr. Gray worked for a fair housing law firm as well as the NAACP Legal Defense and Education Fund during the summer. After graduation, he clerked for the Hon. Thelton E. Henderson in the Northern District of California. Prior to joining Farrell & Patel, Mr. Gray was an Associate at Wilmer Cutler & Pickering (now Wilmer Hale) in Washington, D.C., and Counsel at Boies, Schiller, and Flexner where he served on a special litigation team for David Boies.

Mr. Gray is proficient in spoken Thai and is published author on topics ranging from fair housing issues, to the Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill, to text-book tort liability issues.

He has substantive experience in the areas of Complex Class Actions; Mass Tort; Entertainment litigation; Various state and federal statutory matters; Partnership Disputes; Complex accounting and reporting of sophisticated multinational foreign exchange and currency related investment transactions; Federal and Blue Sky securities requirements; National and international institutional banking regulations; Antitrust litigation; Government contracts; Human and environmental toxic tort related areas; Bio-Pharmaceutical vaccine litigation; Federal Criminal law involving weapons and explosives; Civil Rights law and Affirmative Action; and Landlord-Tenant issues. Mr. Gray also has substantial experience in massive volume Electronic Discovery issues.

Terry Gray is admitted to practice in Florida and Washington D.C. He is admitted to the M.D. of Fla., S.D. of Fla., and 5th Cir. Fed. Ct. of Appeals. He has won numerous awards and honors including the Distinguished Speakers' Award, and the Gray-Carrington Award for personal integrity, achievement, leadership and humility.

attorneys.name: Tyler L. Gray
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tyler Gray devotes his practice exclusively to representing injured workers in the State of Florida. A majority of his cases involve clients injured in work-related accidents in the Pensacola District, which encompasses the counties of Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa. In his practice, Mr. Gray works hard to preserve the principles on which he was raised: to put others' interests before his and to maintain his integrity.

Born and raised in Cantonment, Florida, Mr. Gray is no stranger to the Pensacola area and the local community that makes it great. Following his graduation from J.M. Tate High School, he earned his Bachelor of Science degree in Finance from Florida State University. After a brief stint in the financial field, Mr. Gray returned to Tallahassee where he earned his Juris Doctorate in 2007 from the Florida State University College of Law.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Gray worked on both sides of the table. For approximately three years, he represented insurance companies and employers with a state-wide defense firm. Thereafter, he was employed by a local Pensacola firm, where he represented clients in regard to their workers' compensation, employment, and Social Security matters. This valuable experience assists Mr. Gray in the handling of his clients' claims, as he is able to analyze a claim from different vantage points to ensure his clients are afforded the benefits they are entitled to and deserve.

In addition to being a member of the Florida Bar, Mr. Gray is also a member of the United States District Court for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida.

Mr. Green practiced with a large civil litigation firm in Birmingham, Alabama before he and his family relocated to his wife's hometown of Naples, Florida in 1998. He has also served as a Florida Supreme Court Certified Circuit Civil Mediator since 2007.

When not working, Mr. Green enjoys hunting, fishing, making music with his friends and spending quality time with his family.

attorneys.name: Edwin A. Green III
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Ocala, FL
attorneys.bio:
Trip Green was born and raised in Tallahassee, Florida. Following his graduation from Leon High School in 1987, he served in the U.S. Army and was honorably discharged in 1989.

Mr. Green used the GI Bill and Army College Fund to pay his way through school and graduated from the University of Florida in 1994 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History.

While he was a student at the University of Florida, Mr. Green was a member of Alpha Tau Omega fraternity and served as President of the Interfraternity Council in 1993. He was inducted into the prestigious Florida Blue Key Leadership Honorary in 1994.

Mr. Green graduated from law school in May, 2000 and has been working for the firm since December, 2001. He has been a partner with the firm since July, 2006.

Mr. Green is a trial lawyer who practices primarily personal injury, medical malpractice and employment/labor law. He regularly tries cases in Central and North Florida in both Federal and State Court.

Mr. Green has obtained large verdicts and settlements for his clients. Mr. Green recently obtained a jury verdict in favor of a client that exceeded $450,000. He has also successfully negotiated several million and multimillion dollar Plaintiffs' lawsuits in both the State of Florida and Louisiana.

Mr. Green is a member of the Florida Bar, the Florida Justice Association, and is admitted to practice before the Federal District Court in the Middle and Northern Districts of Florida.

Mr. Green currently serves as a Director of the Florida Children's Brain Tumor Foundation and is a member of the Church Council and Staff Parish Committee for First United Methodist Church in Ocala.

attorneys.name: Kevin A. Gregg
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kevin A. Gregg is a partner with Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli & Pratt, P.A., practicing in all areas of immigration law, including removal defense, appellate advocacy, federal court litigation, and USCIS representation. Kevin loves immigration law, and advises each client like he would his own family. He believes strongly that with the proper focus and creative legal argument, even the trickiest immigration problems can be solved. Kevin is admitted to the State Bars of California and Florida, and the host of the weekly immigration case law podcast: Immigration Review, available on the KKTP website and all podcast platforms, including Apple Podcasts and Spotify.

Kevin has practiced in the realm of immigration law and litigation for nearly a decade and, due to his years working “behind the bench” for judges, he is uniquely qualified to represent clients in court. Prior to joining KKTP, he served a one-year Judicial Clerkship with the Honorable Beth F. Bloom in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida. Before that, he served for two years as a Judicial Law Clerk and Attorney Advisor in the San Diego Immigration Court, Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), through the Attorney General’s Honors Program. Kevin now applies the skills he developed working for judges to represent clients at all stages of immigration proceedings.

Kevin is a graduate of Boston University School of Law and the University of Florida.

attorneys.bio:
Casey Gregory grew up in New Jersey prior to relocating to Florida to attend college. Casey earned her Bachelor’s Degree in psychology, with a minor in criminal justice from the University of Tampa. While at the University of Tampa, Casey was a member of the University’s Honor’s Program, and graduated cum laude.

Casey earned her Juris Doctor from Western Michigan University Thomas M. Cooley Law School, where she received a full scholarship due to her academic success. During law school, Casey consistently made the Dean’s List and Honor Roll, competed in Moot Court, and graduated Cum Laude.

Casey has been with the Law Offices of Steven Glaros and Associates for two years, and has over three years of experience in the area of family law. Before being admitted to the Florida Bar, Casey worked alongside Mr. Glaros as a law clerk, giving her an extensive knowledge in all aspects of family law matters. Casey is also a member of the Young Lawyer’s Division.

In her spare time, Casey enjoys spending time with her fiancée and two American Pit-Bulls. She enjoys golfing, spending time with her friends, watching movies, and trying new restaurants in the Tampa Bay Area.

attorneys.name: Don Greiwe
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accidents Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tampa personal injury attorney Don Greiwe is AV-rated by Martindale-Hubbell. Mr. Greiwe's practice areas include medical malpractice, general negligence, auto accidents, premises liability, products liability, and mass torts (unsafe pharmaceuticals and defective medical products). As a Tampa injury attorney, Mr. Greiwe is a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer and is certified as a Civil Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. Mr. Greiwe is a Board Certified Circuit Court Mediator and continues to mediate cases involving personal injury and medical malpractice on a regular basis. Mr. Greiwe was admitted to the Florida Bar in 1976 and is also admitted to the U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida, and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Fifth and Eleventh Circuits. Mr. Greiwe received his law degree from the University of Miami and graduated from the University of Notre Dame in 1973.

Tampa medical malpractice attorney Mr. Greiwe has been selected annually since 2007 as one of the best medical malpractice attorneys in America by the Best Lawyers in America, the oldest and most respected peer-review publication in the legal profession. Currently, Mr. Greiwe is recognized in three specialty categories - Medical Malpractice Law, Personal Injury Litigation, and Mass Tort Litigation/Class Actions. Mr. Greiwe was honored with the distinction of 2013 "Lawyer of the Year" by Best Lawyers in the area of Tampa Plaintiff Medical Malpractice Law. He was also named 2017 "Lawyer of the Year" in Tampa Personal Injury Litigation.

Mr. Greiwe once again has the distinction of being selected by Super Lawyers as one of Florida's top trial attorneys for the 2016 edition. Mr. Greiwe has been selected for inclusion in Super Lawyers for consecutive years since 2006 for his legal experience and professional achievements.

attorneys.name: Joy E. Greyer
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Each year, thousands of Americans file claims for social security disability and supplemental security income. And each year, thousands of these same claims are denied for one reason or another. When this happens people secure the assistance of a social security attorney.

Social security is a basic right of every American citizen, and benefits should be made available when a person becomes disabled or is no longer capable of working.

Joy E. Greyer is a lawyer to whom many have turned for help in social security and supplemental security income disability claims. She is a trial attorney with twenty years of experience. Greyer is a Board Certified Social Security Disability Advocate through the National Board of Legal Specialty Certification and the State of Florida. She is one of only 10 lawyers who have achieved certification in the state of Florida, and one of 56 attorneys in the United States who have been certified by the National Board of Social Security Disability Advocates.

Greyer is a part of the legal team of Rosenthal, Levy, Simon & Sosa taking the lead in the social security disability department together with a panel of experienced Palm Beach lawyers. She has successfully represented clients at hearings in front of administrative law judges.

Many people ask what makes Greyer so effective in Social Security claims. Greyer has made her name in the field simply because she believes in the entitlement of the injured. Her many years of work as a solo-practitioner paved the way to make her a valuable addition to Rosenthal, Levy, Simon & Sosa.

Greyer considers her work as more than a profession, it is her personal passion. She is a West Palm Beach attorney fueled to serve and defend the injured and disabled by ensuring that they receive proper compensation. She finds fulfillment in defending those who are not capable of defending themselves. She states, “Millions of Americans suffer from disabilities and impairments resulting from disease, accidents or congenital defects. As a social security disability attorney, my passion is advocating for these individuals and working to see they receive every benefit to which they are entitled.”

Joy E. Greyer is an exceptional lawyer who uses her passion and years of experience to her advantage. While her strength lies in the field of social security disability benefits, she is also well versed in workers’ compensation litigation and appellate practice.

She has been a member of the Florida Bar since 1994 and is licensed to practice in the United States District Court, Southern District of Florida.

*Offers Free Initial Consultation

attorneys.name: Michael J. Griffith
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Admitted to practice law in 1974, Michael J. Griffith has been representing criminal defendants and accident victims for more than 35 years. He is a dedicated lawyer who puts his clients' interests first, and who only represents individuals - not government or big business.

Born in Pennsylvania, Michael J. Griffith attended college at the University of West Florida in Pensacola, and he earned his law degree at the University of Mississippi School of Law in Oxford. After a stint with the Office of the State Attorney, 20th Judicial Circuit of Florida in the mid-1970s, he then represented clients as a Shareholder in the firm of Levin, Middlebrooks et al. until 1990. Today, he is the owner of Michael J. Griffith, P.A., serving individuals charged with crimes and injured in motorcycle and automobile accidents throughout the Southeastern United States. He is also an experienced family lawyer, working closely with high-net worth individuals, military service men and women, same-sex partners, and other individuals to complete their divorces and deal with child-related issues. Read more about Michael's practice areas.

A Reputation for Excellence and Client Service

Michael J. Griffith is a Life Member of both the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL) and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (FACDL). He is also a member of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America (ATLA), and has been named to the Top 100 Lawyers in Florida. Other attorneys describe Michael as, "a highly skilled attorney who may be counted upon to render a thorough and innovative defense," and "a nationally known criminal defense lawyer with a reputation for aggressively defending his clients." Clients call Michael a "fighter" and an "excellent lawyer" who "knows the law and is on your side."

A Rider Dedicated to Helping Motorcycle Accident Victims

When he is not practicing law, you will probably find Michael J. Griffith out on his motorcycle. Michael has been riding for more than 50 years, and has ridden his bike across the country. He is a member of the Harley Owners Group (HOG), the BMW Owners Group, the American Motorcycle Association, and ABATE.

Contact Pensacola Attorney Michael J. Griffith

If you are looking for aggressive representation that gets results, contact Michael J. Griffith today. Located in Pensacola, Michael J. Griffith P.A. fights for injury victims throughout Florida, and represents criminal defendants across the entire Southeastern United States.

Paul Gross is a third-generation Floridian and was born and raised in the Tampa Bay Area. Mr. Gross obtained his undergraduate degree in Political Science from Florida State University in 2001. After graduating from law school, Mr. Gross went to work as an assistant public defender in the Sixth Judicial Circuit of Florida. attorneys.name: Jorge L. Guerra Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
For over 30 years Jorge L. Guerra has stewarded clients through the litigation process, helping them achieve their desired results. Having been a banker before becoming an attorney, Mr. Guerra brings a businessman's perspective to his practice, analyzing litigation risks and providing strategic advice to clients who appreciate his understanding of the consequences of decisions made before and during litigation.

Jorge has represented clients as varied as the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the largest South American distributor of cellphones (Samsung and Nokia). He has represented the Blank family office since 2005, as well as national and regional banks, individual bank officers and directors, South Florida real estate developers, foreign investors and private lenders, large Florida agricultural interests, and small family businesses. Jorge's areas of expertise include banking and insurance-related matters, shareholder and partnership disputes, business torts, breaches of contract, creditors' and debtors' rights, and receiverships. He has also handled professional liability matters on both sides of the aisle, securities claims, disputes over intellectual property rights and antitrust cases.

Beyond his legal training, Jorge has a degree in finance and economics and worked as a commercial lending officer at the largest regional bank in the 1980s. Whether he's formulating and executing winning litigation strategy, negotiating to avoid unfavorable litigation, or providing general business guidance, Jorge's analytical skills and his dogged determination make him a pre-eminent businessman's lawyer.

Jorge has tried cases before juries, judges, domestic and international arbitrators, and administrative agencies. He has numerous million-dollar-plus verdicts and awards and has argued appeals in both state and federal courts across the country. He has been a Director of the Dade County Trial Lawyers' Association and was the first Chairman of its Commercial Litigation Section, where he co-authored the "Operating Statement for Business Court Pilot Program, 11th Judicial Circuit, Dade County, Florida," the first set of operational rules and procedures for an experimental program that, in 2006, became the 11th Circuit's Complex Business Litigation Division. Jorge graduated from the University of Miami (B.B.A. Finance, 1983; J.D. 1986), where he was a member of the Law Review and the Moot Court Board. He was admitted to The Florida Bar in 1986 and is also a member of the Bar of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, the Miami-Dade and Cuban-American Bar Associations, and the Florida Bar Business Law Section.

attorneys.name: Joseph Lafayette Gufford III
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Stuart, FL
attorneys.bio:
Possessing an extensive history in law and business, attorney Joseph Gufford III currently serves clients from The Gufford Law Firm in Martin County, Florida. The former Chairman of the Martin County Bar Association's Family Law Committee, Gufford concentrates on family law and its subsections including divorce, child custody, guardianship law, visitation rights, paternity, prenuptial agreements, child support enforcement actions and spousal support. Family Law practice is very document intensive and requires a close examination of each party's assets and income. Joe Gufford has an extensive staff of experienced paralegals that give him the ability to maximize his efforts on behalf of each and every client. In many cases, the opposing party will intentionally hide assets or attempt to reduce their income to lessen their exposure to child support, alimony and equitable distribution. Thus, having an experienced staff to sift through bank statements, Financial Affidavits and Tax Returns is essential. Additionally, in some cases, it is necessary to have the right experts to consult with in order to achieve the client's goals. Whether it is a custody evaluator, a forensic accountant or a vocational assessment, knowing the right experts to call upon if often the key to success in complicated matters.

Other areas Joe Gufford, III practices in range from civil litigation, probate, landlord/tenant disputes, business organizations and estate and probate law.

Before starting his professional life as a lawyer, Joseph Gufford attended the University of Florida and majored in Political Science and History. During this period, Gufford acquired a commission as a Second Lieutenant after graduating from the U.S. Army Airborne School. Subsequently, he enrolled at Stetson University College of Law and commenced his career as a Clerk with Justin C. Johnston and Associates PA. In his first trial, he was successful at assisting his client in obtaining a multi-million dollar judgment against a manufacturer of a defective heater.

Following the receipt of his Juris Doctor, Joe Gufford became an Associate Litigation Attorney with O'Brien & Hooper, PA. At the personal injury firm, he litigated against Cellular One in one of the nation's first AIDS discrimination suits. Joe's vast experience has enabled him to represent clients in civil suits, family law, and business litigation.

The holder of a “Superb” rating from Avvo.com, Gufford has written and presented on legal issues, such as changes to Florida statutes that affect custody and equitable distribution. Covered by the Martin County Bar Association (MCBA) for his pro bono work, Gufford has also obtained Pro Bono Service Awards from MCBA and Florida Rural Legal Services on multiple occasions. Pro Bono work is important to Joe Gufford and he does as much of it as possible. All Pro Bono cases that Mr. Gufford handles are referred to him through Florida Rural Legal Services.

attorneys.name: Michael F. Guilford
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Guilford was born and raised in Coral Gables, Florida and is a third generation Miamian. Mr. Guilford enjoys outdoor activities including motorcycle riding, offshore fishing, scuba diving and hiking. Mr. Guilford attended the prestigious Ransom preparatory school and graduated from Florida State University with a double undergraduate major in Finance and Economics. Thereafter, Mr. Guilford attended the University of Miami School of Law where he was a member of the Student Senate and was president of the Student Bar Association. Mr. Guilford is a member of Iron Arrow, the "Highest Honor Attained" at the University of Miami.

From 1985 to 1991 Mr. Guilford was a member of the Law Firm of Patton & Kanner where he defended ship-owners, charterers and cruise lines in crew member litigation including Jones Act, Unseaworthiness and Maintenance and Cure claims and passenger personal injury claims.

From 1991 to 1997 Mr. Guilford was Vice President and assistant General Counsel of Scandinavian Marine Claims Office, the North American arm of Scandinavian Underwriters Association. In this position he was working directly for underwriters/insurers both actively handling and overseeing outside counsel on crew member, passenger, personal injury and physical damage/Hull & Machinery claims.

From 1997 to the present Mr. Guilford has been the founding partner of Michael F. Guilford, P. A. and during this period was also a founding partner of Guilford & Rash, P. A. where he has focused his practice primarily on representing injured crew members and passengers against the major cruise lines and ship owners throughout Florida and the United States.

Mr. Guilford is one of a very few admiralty trial lawyers who has worked for a defense firm representing cruise lines and in house for the cruise lines' insurers and therefore knows from the inside how cruise lines and their insurance companies handle these claims and uses that knowledge to obtain the very best results for his clients.

Mr. Guilford is rated AV Preeminent by Martindale, a rating acquired by only 5% of all attorneys. The rating indicates he has reached the height of professional experience and is recognized by his peers for the highest levels of skill and integrity. Mr. Guilford has been a member of The American Association for Justice since 1999, is a member of the Florida Justice Association, and the Southeastern Admiralty Law Institute, has been the vice chair of the ABA Admiralty Committee and is currently a member of the Florida Bar Admiralty Committee. Mr. Guilford has been a frequent guest lecturer on seaman's rights, including at both the University of Miami and the Direccion General De La Marina Mercante De Honduras.

In addition to Mr. Guilford's professional activities he is a member of the University of Miami Citizens Board, a past member of the University of Miami Law School Alumni Association Board of Directors, an adult advisor to Boy Scout Troop 457 and is a member of the Board of Directors of the Alma Jennings Foundation.

Mr. Guilford is a member of the Florida Bar, The United States District Courts for the Southern, Middle and Northern District of Florida and has appeared before the District Courts of the Southern District of New York and the Western District of Washington as well as the Florida District Courts of Appeal and the Federal Circuit Courts of Appeals for the 2nd, 9th, and 11th Circuits.

attorneys.bio:
As a graduate of the University of Florida with a degree in Criminal Justice, Matthew Gunter developed a passion for the legal field and decided to pursue a career in the law. In 2009, Mr. Gunter graduated from Barry University-Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law in Orlando, Florida and began a career in criminal law.

Mr. Gunter worked as an Assistant State Attorney in the 18th Judicial Circuit for Seminole County. While working for the State, he focused on prosecuting thousands of cases including Grand Theft, DUI, Possession of Cannabis, and Domestic Violence Battery. His time with the State Attorney's Office allowed him to evaluate cases and hone his skills as a trial lawyer.

After the State Attorney's Office, Mr. Gunter was an associate with Katz & Phillips, P.A. There, he used the skills he learned as a prosecutor to defend clients and find weaknesses in the State's case while advocating zealously for his client's rights. While with Katz & Phillips, P.A., Mr. Gunter handled hundreds of misdemeanors and felony cases ranging from simple drug offenses to armed robbery charges.

Now as an associate with Morgan and Morgan, P.A., Mr. Gunter's experience in and out of the courtroom proves to be a valuable asset in seeking justice for the people.
