attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Elaine A. Humphreys is Senior Counsel at Block & Scarpa and is a member of the Estate Planning and Probate Department. Prior to joining Block & Scarpa, Elaine had her own law firm, Elaine A. Humphreys, P.A., based in West Palm Beach, Florida.

After working for many years in the public sector as a government attorney for the N.C. Attorney General's Office and later as the City Attorney for Lake Worth, Florida, Elaine obtained her L.L.M. in Taxation from the University of Florida, Levin College of Law, in Gainesville, Florida. Her practice now focuses on helping families with their estate planning and asset protection needs, and through the probate, trust administration and guardianship processes. In addition to her estate planning, probate and trust administration practice, Elaine also helps local businesses with their legal needs in their operational matters, contracts and commercial leases; and she advises municipalities on various aspects of municipal law, contracts and ordinances.

Elaine serves on the Philanthropic Advisory Council of the Community Foundation of Palm Beach and Martin Counties, and is a Member of the Real Estate, Wills and Probate and Tax Sections of the Florida Bar Association. She is also a Member of the Probate and Guardianship Committee and the Estate and Probate CLE Committee of the Palm Beach County Bar Association. Elaine is also a member of the North Carolina State Bar. Outside of the office, Elaine enjoys biking, yoga, traveling, and reading mystery novels.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey J. Humphries
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Protection Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey J. Humphries is from Helen, Georgia. He received his Bachelor of Science Degree in Criminology from North Georgia College and State University in 1999. While at North Georgia, Mr. Humphries participated in the ROTC program and graduated Summa Cum Laude. While attending North Georgia, Mr. Humphries worked as a deputy sheriff for Hall County, Georgia.

Mr. Humphries then attended Florida Coastal School of Law on a full scholarship where he graduated at the top of his class in December 2003. While he attended law school, he was a Case Note editor for the law review and a member of the moot court honor board. He also had the privilege of being an intern for Justice Peggy Quince of the Florida Supreme Court.

Mr. Humphries then joined the insurance defense firm of O'Hara Halvorsen Humphries, PA, in October 2003. He started as an associate and eventually became president and co-owner of the firm. Mr. Humphries spent 11 years defending major insurance companies and its insureds. He was the lead trial lawyer at the firm having tried over 50 cases to jury verdict, including wrongful death, legal malpractice, breach of insurance contracts, trucking accidents, slip and fall, negligent security (shooting), and a variety of other types of cases. In 2013, Mr. Humphries was invited to join the prestigious Claims and Litigation Management Alliance (CLM), which is an invitation-only national organization created by the claims and litigation management industries.

Mr. Humphries was selected by his peers to join the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA), a national association of experienced trial lawyers and judges dedicated to the preservation and promotion of the civil jury trial and elevating the standards of integrity, honor, ethics, civility, and courtesy in the legal profession.

No matter how much experience a lawyer may have in civil trial, only board certified civil trial lawyers are allowed to identify themselves as specialists or experts in this area of law.

Mr. Humphries is also a board member of the Jacksonville chapter of Hope Worldwide, an international charity that providers volunteer services to the poor, sick, and suffering, throughout the world.

Mr. Humphries is licensed to practice in both federal and state courts in Florida and Georgia. He handles personal injury and consumer protection cases at Morgan & Morgan.

attorneys.name: John Iannarelli
attorneys.practice_type: Sex Crimes Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
John Iannarelli served as an FBI Special Agent for 20 years, during which he was a SWAT team member and participated in the investigations of the Oklahoma City bombing, the 9/11 attack, the shooting of Congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords, and the Sony hack. Among his many FBI assignments, John served as the FBI's National Spokesperson, on the Cyber Division Executive staff, and was as an Assistant Special Agent in Charge overseeing all Criminal, Cyber and Counterintelligence investigations. He was recognized with the FBI's Director Award for Distinguished Service.

A former San Diego Police Officer and attorney with international studies at Oxford England, John is admitted to the practice of law in California, Maryland, and Washington DC. In addition, he is the recipient of an Honorary Doctor of Computer Science in recognition of his contributions to the field of cyber investigations. John was also an NFL Security Representative responsible for ensuring public safety throughout the football season and the Super Bowl.

John is the author of five books, including Why Teens Fail and What to Fix, a parents' guide to protecting their children on the Internet and other dangers, and How to Spot a Terrorist Before It's Too Late. His just released 5th book, Disorderly Conduct, examines the lighter side of law enforcement and the humorous moments during his FBI career.

John is a frequent on-air contributor for the national news media and has been profiled in Forbes. He provided live on-scene coverage from Las Vegas of the Mandalay Bay mass shooting attack as it occurred. An engaging and entertaining keynote speaker, John is a National Speakers Association Certified Speaking Professional (CSP®) known for sharing his intriguing insights combined with his superb sense of humor. He has presented to Fortune 500 companies, domestic and international audiences, the United Nations, and the Vatican, where he has personally met on several occasions with Pope Francis.

Awards and Honors

Honors

FBI’s Director Award for Distinguished Service

attorneys.bio:
Jason Imler is a Tampa Bay Area native that has a passion for law. He graduated cum laude from Western Michigan University – Thomas M. Cooley Law School. Since graduating from law school, Jason has held positions as an administrative specialist with the Guardian Ad Litem Office in Pinellas County, legal administrator for the Home Shopping Network, and practiced plaintiff’s side employment law as a partner in a Tampa firm.

Since 2017, Mr. Imler has counseled individuals in all manners of employment law matters including Discrimination Litigation, Retaliation Litigation, Employee Compensation Rights, Non-Compete Agreements, FMLA compliance, Sexual Harassment Litigation, FLSA compliance and more.

Jason is active with the HCBA YLD, and currently serves as Treasurer. Previously, Jason served as a member of the YLD event committee, a liaison for the YLD Board to both the 5k pro-bono run and Hillsborough County Bar Foundation. In addition to his positions with the HCBA YLD, Jason also has Board of Directors experience as a director of his neighborhood’s HOA, spent numerous years as a director for the Land O' Lakes Little League, and is an associate member of the Ferguson White Inn of Court.

Outside of his professional life, Jason is a husband and father of three. Jason takes an active role volunteering with AAU basketball, coaching multiple recreational sports, participating in Cub Scouts and being a #girldad.

attorneys.name: Timothy M. Ingram
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Accidents – Plaintiff Lawyers in Clearwater, FL
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, Tim Ingram has represented only injured persons and their family members in personal injury cases. Mr. Ingram's area of practice includes representing injured persons in automobile accidents, motorcycle accidents, motor vehicle accidents, slip and fall and trip and fall accidents, and dog bite cases.

Mr. Ingram has represented thousands of injured persons throughout the state of Florida over the past 20 years. He has handled, negotiated, litigated, settled, and mediated thousands of cases. He has successfully recovered millions of dollars from insurance companies over the past 20 years. He has obtained numerous six figure verdicts and judgments on behalf of his clients.

Mr. Ingram has represented injured persons in both State and Federal Courts throughout Florida. He has represented injured persons on appeal in state and federal trial appellate courts throughout Florida.

Mr. Ingram has appeared, argued, and won before the Florida Supreme Court.

Mr. Ingram is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the Florida Bar. Less than 2% of Florida Bar Members are Board Certified in Civil Trial Law. He is also Board Certified in Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. Less than 1% of Florida Bar members are Board Certified by the National Board of Trial Advocacy.

Mr. Ingram is an AV rated attorney by Martindale-Hubbell National Law Directory. An AV rating is Martindale-Hubbell's highest rating given. An AV rating signifies that the recipient's legal abilities are of the very highest standard and that his professional ethics and conduct are beyond question.

Mr. Ingram is admitted to practice in the United States Supreme Court, the US Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, the US District Court for the Southern District, the US District Court for the Middle District, the Florida Supreme Court and all Florida State Courts.

Mr. Ingram is an EAGLE member of the Florida Justice Association and a member of the American Association for Justice. These two organizations are dedicated to serving the interests of plaintiffs, injured persons, and their families in litigation.

Mr. Ingram was born in Louisville, Kentucky, on February 29, 1960. He was raised in Omaha, Nebraska. He obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Kentucky, in Lexington, Kentucky, in 1982. He graduated in the top 10% of his class and earned his degree with High Distinction. He was selected to the Phi Beta Kappa National Honor Society.

While attending the University of Kentucky, Mr. Ingram was a walk on on the University of Kentucky Men's Varsity Basketball Team from 1978 to 1980.

Following graduation from the University of Kentucky, Mr. Ingram attended the University of Florida College of Law in Gainesville, Florida. While at the University of Florida College of Law, Mr. Ingram entered the open writing competition for the University of Florida Law Review. Mr. Ingram was selected to the University of Florida Law Review in 1983 and served as a Board Member of the University of Florida Law Review through 1985. Mr. Ingram received his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Florida College of Law in 1985.

Mr. Ingram's hobbies include basketball, both playing and coaching. Mr. Ingram has been married for 27 years and has 4 teenage children. He teaches and coaches his children, their friends, and their classmates in the Countryside Recreation Center Youth Basketball League and AAU Youth Basketball.

He has successfully recovered millions of dollars from insurance companies over the past 20 years. He has obtained numerous six figure verdicts and judgments on behalf of his clients.

Mr. Ingram has represented injured persons in both State and Federal Courts throughout Florida. He has represented injured persons on appeal in state and federal trial appellate courts throughout Florida.

Mr. Ingram has appeared, argued, and won before the Florida Supreme Court.

Mr. Ingram is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the Florida Bar. Less than 2% of Florida Bar Members are Board Certified in Civil Trial Law. He is also Board Certified in Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. Less than 1% of Florida Bar members are Board Certified by the National Board of Trial Advocacy.

Mr. Ingram is an AV rated attorney by Martindale-Hubbell National Law Directory. An AV rating is Martindale-Hubbell's highest rating given. An AV rating signifies that the recipient's legal abilities are of the very highest standard and that his professional ethics and conduct are beyond question.

Mr. Ingram is admitted to practice in the United States Supreme Court, the US Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, the US District Court for the Southern District, the US District Court for the Middle District, the Florida Supreme Court and all Florida State Courts.

Mr. Ingram is an EAGLE member of the Florida Justice Association and a member of the American Association for Justice. These two organizations are dedicated to serving the interests of plaintiffs, injured persons, and their families in litigation.

Mr. Ingram was born in Louisville, Kentucky, on February 29, 1960. He was raised in Omaha, Nebraska. He obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Kentucky, in Lexington, Kentucky, in 1982. He graduated in the top 10% of his class and earned his degree with High Distinction. He was selected to the Phi Beta Kappa National Honor Society.

While attending the University of Kentucky, Mr. Ingram was a walk on on the University of Kentucky Men's Varsity Basketball Team from 1978 to 1980.

Following graduation from the University of Kentucky, Mr. Ingram attended the University of Florida College of Law in Gainesville, Florida. While at the University of Florida College of Law, Mr. Ingram entered the open writing competition for the University of Florida Law Review. Mr. Ingram was selected to the University of Florida Law Review in 1983 and served as a Board Member of the University of Florida Law Review through 1985. Mr. Ingram received his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Florida College of Law in 1985.

Mr. Ingram's hobbies include basketball, both playing and coaching. Mr. Ingram has been married for 27 years and has 4 teenage children. He teaches and coaches his children, their friends, and their classmates in the Countryside Recreation Center Youth Basketball League and AAU Youth Basketball.

He is a former President and Board Member of the Eighth Judicial Circuit Bar Association, a past President of the Gainesville Jaycees, and is an active member of the Florida Law Network.

attorneys.name: Monica Ishak Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Monica Ishak, Esq., is a first-generation American and South Florida native. She is based in West Palm Beach, Florida, and is licensed to practice law in Federal and Florida courts. She is the founding partner and CEO of The Ishak Law Firm, P.A. Monica began her career trying cases as a certified legal intern in law school at the Public Defender’s Office in Miami.

Upon graduating from law school in 2019, she started as an Assistant Public Defender in Palm Beach County, where she tried numerous misdemeanor cases. During her time at the Public Defender’s Office, jury trials ceased due to COVID-19. During this time, Monica filed numerous Motions to suppress and Stand Your Ground motions that ultimately resulted in the dismissal of nearly 30 cases during a two to three-month time span. Monica also received the award for having the most jury trial experience in misdemeanor court at that time.

As jury trials started to pick up again, she continued her trial experience as she was promoted to handle felony and serious cases while providing her clients with favorable results. After her time at the Public Defender’s Office, Monica continued her legal career as an associate at the renowned law firm, Kubicki Draper, where she represented insurance companies in first-party property and personal injury cases. Monica tried her first civil jury trial at Kubicki Draper. However, Monica decided to return to private criminal defense, where she continued her experience as a criminal trial lawyer representing people with various charges and successfully handled a first-degree murder jury trial.

Monica continued her legal career as a civil litigator and trial lawyer as in-house counsel for a homeowner’s insurance company, where she was on the trial team. While there, she tried numerous civil jury trials throughout the tri-county area. Monica’s passion lies in criminal justice reform and ultimately providing quality representation to those she knows she can help. She is a successful advocate and knows how to achieve favorable results for her clients.

attorneys.name: Adam H. Itzkowitz Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lutz, FL
attorneys.bio:
Adam Itzkowitz moved to the Tampa Bay area from New York to pursue one of his life goals, becoming a restaurateur. Since that time, he has owned, managed and operated multiple restaurants throughout Florida which led him to starting a restaurant management-consulting group.

Adam attended law school at Stetson University College of Law, where he graduated cum laude. Adam has interned for judges at the Sixth Judicial Circuit Family Division, as well as at the Sixth Judicial Circuit Criminal Division. Adam’s in-depth knowledge of the laws led him to a teaching assistant position for the Federal Rules of Evidence. Adam has also authored a chapter on the topic of Evidence Bias in a publication titled “Ethical Issues, Bias and Other Challenges in Forensic Evidence Management.”

Since he began practicing law, Adam has practiced in several disciplines of law, including business litigation, hospitality and tourism law, family law and personal injury law. Adam takes great pride in taking the life lessons he has learned in his many years in the hospitality sector and applying them to the way his firm treats their clients. Adam is regularly asked to speak on topics relating to hospitality law and is often a guest lecturer at American University Washington College of Law in Washington D.C. teaching hospitality and business law principles to the attendees.

Adam has a passion for involvement in the community. He gives back by hosting various organizations at his and his client’s restaurants. Adam was previously a board member of the Westchase Charitable Foundation and a Law and Science Fellow for the National Clearinghouse for Science, Technology and the Law.

At home, Adam is happily married and a new father to his first child whom the couple welcomed in January 2020. In his spare time, he enjoys spending time with his friends and family, watching football, and playing golf.

attorneys.bio:
Jessica Ann Israileff was born and raised in the Chicagoland area and moved to Florida in 2014 to attend Stetson University where she obtained a Bachelor's Degree in Human Health Science.

Upon completion of her undergraduate studies, Jessica moved back to Chicago and began working at a law firm that specialized in condominium and community development law. More specifically, Jessica worked in the department responsible for the consummation of deconversion transactions - the process of selling an entire condominium property to a third party for the subsequent conversion to rental apartments. This experience ignited Jessica's passion for real estate and ultimately influenced her decision to attend law school. Although her law school experience was anything but ordinary due to the covid-19 pandemic, Jessica took major advantage of the flexibility that online learning offered and spent a significant amount of time in Sarasota where she worked part-time at GKW as a law clerk. As a law clerk Jessica performed legal research, drafted legal documents, and assisted with the closing of real estate transactions.

Jessica earned her Juris Doctorate Degree in 2022 from the University of Florida Levin College of Law. While attending UF, she successfully completed the Environmental, Land Use, and Real Estate Law Program and earned a certificate of the same. Jessica was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2022.

Jessica earned her Juris Doctorate Degree in 2022 from the University of Florida Levin College of Law. While attending UF, she successfully completed the Environmental, Land Use, and Real Estate Law Program and earned a certificate of the same. Jessica was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2022.

attorneys.bio:
Lance C. Ivey is recognized as a top civil litigation attorney in the area of products liability. His practice includes cases involving automotive design and manufacturing defects including insufficient roof strength, handling and stability defects, defective airbags and defective seat belts. Lance has handled defective product cases all over the country and has obtained numerous multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements for firm clients in cases against virtually every international automotive and tire manufacturer.

As a result of his work, Lance has played an integral role in improving vehicle safety for consumers. After he settled a large, confidential case involving a defective seat belt, one major automotive manufacturer recalled over 300,000 vehicles. Lance is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by The Florida Bar. Certification is the highest level of evaluation by The Florida Bar of an attorney's competency and experience.

attorneys.name: Amanda R. Jacobson Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Jacobson, Chmelir & Ferwerda Attorneys At Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Winter Springs, FL
attorneys.bio:
Amanda R. Jacobson has been an attorney for 26 years, practicing in the areas of criminal law and family law. After graduating from Rollins College in Winter Park, Florida, Ms. Jacobson attended the University of Miami School of Law, where she successfully competed in trial team events as a member of the Moot Court Board. While in law school, Ms. Jacobson interned at the Office of the State Attorney in Orange County, Florida, the office that she later joined as an attorney when she graduated in 1996. As an Assistant State Attorney, Ms. Jacobson spent the following three years prosecuting all criminal cases, from DUIs and traffic matters, misdemeanors, drug cases and juvenile matters to serious felonies and violent crime.

In 1999, Ms. Jacobson, along with her three partners, left the Office of the State Attorney to form the law offices of Jacobson, Chmelir & Ferwerda. Since that time, she has defended numerous criminal cases in the Central Florida area, focusing with her clients on personal attention and jury trial practice. In addition to her work in criminal state court cases, Ms. Jacobson also represents clients in federal court in the Middle District of Florida on all charges, including conspiracy, drug trafficking and tax evasion.

In 2000, the firm expanded its services to include a family law section, providing legal support to clients with domestic cases. Ms. Jacobson has represented many family law clients in matters ranging from divorce, child support and custody to adoptions and name changes. She litigates all types of cases, including simple uncontested dissolution of marriage, complex custody actions, and divorces involving business valuations.

Ms. Jacobson is also a Certified Family Law Mediator who can assist you in resolving all family law matters prior to, during or after court proceedings. Mediation is an essential tool in negotiating a settlement that the clients can control once they have reached an agreement.

Collaborative divorce is often the best solution for families going through a dissolution of marriage. Ms. Jacobson is collaboratively trained and welcomes the opportunity to offer collaboration as a path for your dissolution resolution.

attorneys.name: Martin J. Jaffe
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Deland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Martin Jaffe was born in Bayonne, New Jersey in 1965. He graduated from Florida State University in 1987, then worked for several years as a claims adjuster for a national insurance company and as well as a parole officer. Mr. Jaffe graduated from the University of Akron School of Law in 1998. While in law school he was a national finalist two years in a row in the ATLA National Trial Tournament, and named best advocate in the NITA Tournament of Champions Trial Competition. He was also an Associate Editor of the Akron Law Review.

After law school, Mr. Jaffe moved to Florida and was a partner in one of Florida's leading defense firms defending catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases nationwide for large corporations before joining Morgan & Morgan. Mr. Jaffe now represents victims of serious personal injury and wrongful death cases, product defects, as well as carbon monoxide poisoning events. He has been lead trial counsel to verdict in cases at both state and federal court levels, and is admitted to practice in all Florida state and federal courts.

Recently he has obtained verdicts of $2.9 million (motor vehicle crash), $951,000 (motor vehicle crash), $534,000 (pedestrian struck by vehicle), $2.54 million (carbon monoxide poisoning), as well as settlements for his clients in the amounts of $7.25 million (gypsum stack liner failure), $5.5 million (tire failure), $1.8 million (fuel tank rupture), $1.3 million (carbon monoxide poisoning), $1.3 million (airbag defect), $1.25 million (pedestrian struck by motor vehicle), $1.1 million (electrical component failure and fire), $1.2 million (tire failure), $800,000 (tire failure), $750,000 (tire failure), $550,000 (smoke detector failure), $520,000 (metallurgical component failure), $417,500 (motor vehicle crash) and $380,000 (motor vehicle crash). Mr. Jaffe has also been retained as counsel on cases in Tennessee, Mississippi, Georgia, Colorado, Arkansas, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

Mr. Jaffe was selected by Florida Trend Magazine's Legal Elite Civil Trial Law in 2016 and has earned the AV® Peer Review Rating by Martindale-Hubbell, the preeminent national publication in the legal field every year since 2005. According to Martindale-Hubbell, "An AV rating is a significant accomplishment - a testament to the fact that a lawyer's peers rank him or her at the highest level of professional excellence. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law. It is a distinction reserved for a select few in the legal community." Further, Mr. Jaffe has been rated AV in the Martindale-Hubbell Judicial Edition 2017 and selected as one of Orlando Life Magazine's Top Lawyers in Orlando for 2012 and 2013.

Mr. Jaffe stays active in the community through coaching basketball, and as a board member of several non-profit organizations.

While in law school he was a national finalist two years in a row in the ATLA National Trial Tournament, and named best advocate in the NITA Tournament of Champions Trial Competition. He was also an Associate Editor of the Akron Law Review.

After law school, Mr. Jaffe moved to Florida and was a partner in one of Florida's leading defense firms defending catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases nationwide for large corporations before joining Morgan & Morgan. Mr. Jaffe now represents victims of serious personal injury and wrongful death cases, product defects, as well as carbon monoxide poisoning events. He has been lead trial counsel to verdict in cases at both state and federal court levels, and is admitted to practice in all Florida state and federal courts.

Recently he has obtained verdicts of $2.9 million (motor vehicle crash), $951,000 (motor vehicle crash), $534,000 (pedestrian struck by vehicle), $2.54 million (carbon monoxide poisoning), as well as settlements for his clients in the amounts of $7.25 million (gypsum stack liner failure), $5.5 million (tire failure), $1.8 million (fuel tank rupture), $1.3 million (carbon monoxide poisoning), $1.3 million (airbag defect), $1.25 million (pedestrian struck by motor vehicle), $1.1 million (electrical component failure and fire), $1.2 million (tire failure), $800,000 (tire failure), $750,000 (tire failure), $550,000 (smoke detector failure), $520,000 (metallurgical component failure), $417,500 (motor vehicle crash) and $380,000 (motor vehicle crash). Mr. Jaffe has also been retained as counsel on cases in Tennessee, Mississippi, Georgia, Colorado, Arkansas, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

Mr. Jaffe was selected by Florida Trend Magazine's Legal Elite Civil Trial Law in 2016 and has earned the AV® Peer Review Rating by Martindale-Hubbell, the preeminent national publication in the legal field every year since 2005. According to Martindale-Hubbell, "An AV rating is a significant accomplishment - a testament to the fact that a lawyer's peers rank him or her at the highest level of professional excellence. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law. It is a distinction reserved for a select few in the legal community." Further, Mr. Jaffe has been rated AV in the Martindale-Hubbell Judicial Edition 2017 and selected as one of Orlando Life Magazine's Top Lawyers in Orlando for 2012 and 2013.

Mr. Jaffe stays active in the community through coaching basketball, and as a board member of several non-profit organizations.

attorneys.name: Veronica Jattan
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Veronica Jattan is a dedicated immigration attorney raised in Central Florida. She laid the foundation for her career at the University of Central Florida, where she earned a Bachelor's degree in Cultural Anthropology, honing her skills in ethnographic research and cross-cultural competency. This background proved invaluable as she pursued her Juris Doctor at Loyola University New Orleans College of Law.

Upon graduating, Attorney Jattan immersed herself in immigration law, starting as a Staff Attorney at Catholic Charities Diocese of Baton Rouge. There, she provided critical legal representation to clients in immigration detention centers across Louisiana. Her passion for representing immigrant families led her to become a CLINIC Reunited Families Fellow, where she advocated for families separated under the "Zero Tolerance" policy at the southern border.

Returning to her home state, Attorney Jattan continued her impactful work at Catholic Charities of Central Florida. She rapidly progressed from Staff Attorney to Supervising Attorney, overseeing comprehensive immigration assistance for families throughout Florida.

Currently, Veronica Jattan serves as a Managing Partner at Vedder & Jattan, P.A., leverages her extensive experience to guide clients through the intricate maze of immigration law. Her unwavering commitment to immigrant rights and family reunification has solidified her reputation as a trusted advocate in the field.

Awards and Honors

Gillis Long Poverty Law Center Public Service Award

attorneys.name: Emily C. Jeffcott
attorneys.practice_type: Mass Torts Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Emily Jeffcott joined Morgan & Morgan's Pensacola office in 2019 as a trial attorney. She is licensed to practice law in Florida, Louisiana, Texas, New York and the District of Columbia. Her practice areas extend primarily to product liability multi-district litigation, focusing on depositions, science & expert development, trial practice, and law & briefing. Ms. Jeffcott is a member of the Plaintiffs Steering Committee for In re: Juul Labs, Inc. Marketing, Sales Practices & Products Liability Litigation. In addition, Ms. Jeffcott is a member of the trial team and Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for In re: Taxotere Products Liability Litigation, serving on as co-chair for the law & briefing committee and a member of the science committee. Ms. Jeffcott is also a member of Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for In re: Valsartan (NDMA) Contamination Products Liability Litigation, serving on both the law & briefing committee and the science committee. Ms. Jeffcott's past multi-district litigation experience includes In re: Xarelto. Products Liability Litigation, where she served as trial counsel in all bellwether trials, in addition to In re: Zofran Products Liability Litigation, In re: FEMA Trailer Products Liability Litigation, and In re: Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill.

Ms. Jeffcott has also represented whistleblowers across the country. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Jeffcott was lead counsel for Relators in a $125 million qui tam settlement against Bechtel for alleged false claims related to the Hanford Nuclear Waste Treatment Plant in Washington. Ms. Jeffcott has also litigated cases involving Medicare fraud.

A 2009 graduate of St. Mary's University School of Law, Ms. Jeffcott received numerous accolades for her oral advocacy skills and brief writing, including being named the ABA's third-best advocate in the United States. An avid reader and writer, Ms. Jeffcott publishes regularly in legal journals and magazines distributed worldwide.

Mrs. Jeffreys is a former adjunct Professor of Law at Seton Hall University, School of Law. Mrs. Jeffreys is a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and formerly served on its Board of Directors. Mrs. Jeffreys has been distinguished as a Fellow of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys. Mrs. Jeffreys is a former Vice-Chair of the American Bar Association's Individual Rights and Responsibilities Elder Law Committee. Mrs. Jeffreys is an active member of the Special Needs Alliance, a national network of lawyers dedicated to serving families of persons with disabilities. Mrs. Jeffreys has been chosen as a New Jersey SuperLawyer by her peers every year since 2008. She frequently lectures on Elder Law topics at both the State and National level. She is a member of the Florida Bar Association, the Collier County Bar Association, and the Collier County Woman's Bar Association.

She is the co-author of Representing the Elderly Client- Law and Practice, Panel Publishers 1999, now Wolters Kluwer. Mrs. Jeffreys graduated from Boston College and received her Juris Doctor degree from Seton Hall University School of Law.

attorneys.name: Robert Stone Jeffrey Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Robert Stone Jeffrey, Esquire, focuses his practice on litigation, including domestic and international divorce, marital and family law disputes, as well as civil and family law appeals. Robert has also represented clients relative to a wide array of civil and business disputes, including residential and commercial foreclosures, non-compete and non-solicitation litigation, competition law, shareholder derivative actions, and disputes between business owners. Robert is admitted to the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States, as well as the United States District Courts in and for the Middle and Southern districts of Florida. Robert prides himself on offering his clients straight-forward, comprehensive and personalized solutions, and in giving each and every client his complete and undivided attention. Robert was peer rated "AV" by Martindale-Hubbell for the "Highest Level of Professional Excellence," and has achieved a perfect 10/10 rating on Avvo.

Prior to establishing his own law practice in April of 2017, Robert was a partner at a boutique commercial and family law litigation firm in Miami, Florida, which represented clients in high-profile, complex, and celebrity litigation. Robert graduated from law school magna cum laude, in the top 4% of his class, and was awarded a Dean's Merit Scholarship. Robert's academic achievements allowed him to become an editor of the Florida Coastal Law Review, where he was named Editor of the Year in 2010, as well as Best Editor for a number of individual volumes. While completing his studies, Robert also worked for numerous professors, either as a teaching or research assistant, and interned for a United States District Court Judge.

Robert obtained his undergraduate degree from the University of Central Florida, where he majored in International and Comparative Politics and minored in Spanish, was involved in organizing a number of charitable and philanthropic activities, and served as a Student Government Association Elections Commissioner. While in college, Robert was also the president of his fraternity, Lambda Chi Alpha.

attorneys.practice_type: Dog Bite & Animal Attacks Lawyers in Plantation, FL
attorneys.bio:
"Tom Jerla is an attorney with Morgan & Morgan in the firm's premises liability division located in Plantation, Florida. He joined the firm in June of 2021. His practice is dedicated to representing clients suffering from injuries due to the negligence of individuals and corporations including but not limited to shopping centers, malls, and grocery stores. Tom has dedicated his practice to representing injured individuals since 2012.

After graduating law school, Mr. Jerla worked as an Assistant State Attorney in the Miami-Dade County State Attorney's Office where he tried more than forty cases to verdict. Prior to leaving the Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office in 2007, he was assigned to the Economic Crimes Division where he was responsible for the investigation and prosecution of investment fraud, insurance fraud, mortgage fraud, healthcare fraud, embezzlement and identity theft.

Following his career as an Assistant State Attorney, Tom handled hundreds of cases on behalf of a national janitorial service company. As a result, he understands how these corporations evaluate liability and claims in premises cases and can utilize his knowledge to aggressively conduct discovery and hold these businesses and individuals accountable for their wrongdoing.

In his free time, Tom enjoys spending time with his wife and son. In addition, Tom serves on the Board of Directors for The 22 Project is a non-profit organization dedicated to helping military veterans suffering from PTSD and Traumatic Brain Injuries."

Approachable, relationship-focused planning

Experience in both medical and legal decision-making

Deep commitment to helping families avoid crisis-driven decisions

Clear communication without legal overwhelm

A strong track record serving Central Florida families for over a decade

attorneys.name: Sheryl C. Johansen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Sheryl C. Johansen is a seasoned criminal defense attorney with nearly fifteen years of criminal courtroom experience and a proven track record of winning difficult cases. As an Assistant Public Defender, she tried over fifty criminal cases to verdict - ranging from homicide cases to kidnapping, trafficking, and complex financial crime cases - while managing high-volume dockets of up to 180 cases at a time.

Known for her meticulous case preparation and strategic advocacy, Ms. Johansen has secured dismissals through well-crafted motions and obtained critical post-conviction relief, including a granted Writ of Habeas Corpus in Perosino v. Gualtieri, 277 So. 3d 84 (Fla. 2d. DCA 2019). She is equally skilled at developing mitigation, negotiating favorable plea agreements, and communicating clearly and compassionately with clients facing the most serious consequences.

Ms. Johansen’s perspective is informed by experience on both sides of the courtroom. Before becoming a public defender, she served in the State Attorney’s Office as a certified legal intern, where she participated in charging decisions, pretrial motion practice, and trial work, and at the United States Attorney’s Office, where she conducted research and drafted motions in both the criminal and civil divisions, including providing pretrial support for white-collar criminal trials.

Ms. Johansen’s courtroom success is rooted in a strong academic foundation. Ms. Johansen earned her Juris Doctor from Barry University School of Law, graduating in the top 6% of her class (10th of 156). While in law school, she served on Law Review as the Business Editor, received multiple book (for receiving the highest grade in her class) awards, won the Best Legal Brief Award, and earned an Honors Certificate in Trial Advocacy. She was a standout member of Barry Law’s Trial Advocacy Team, reaching the Final Four at the AAJ Trial Advocacy Competition, winning a National Championship at the Quinnipiac ABA Trial Advocacy Competition, and finishing as runner-up at the Florida Bar Competition.

Before her legal career, Ms. Johansen worked in the financial services industry in Portland, Maine, an experience that sharpened her strategic thinking and acumen. Ms. Johansen holds a Bachelor of Arts in Media Studies and Communications from the University of Southern Maine. She is an active member of the Goldburg-Cacciatore Criminal Law Inn of Court, the Pinellas Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Baylor Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Baylor Johnson is a Shareholder of Urban Thier & Federer, P.A. He is based out of the Orlando office. Mr. Johnson's practice focuses primarily on civil litigation, including personal injury, contract disputes, and property claims. He also has extensive experience and knowledge practicing criminal defense, litigating probate disputes, and drafting wills, trusts, and related estate planning documents.

Mr. Johnson began his career as an Assistant Public Defender for the 9th Judicial Circuit in Orange County, Florida, where he represented hundreds of clients from arrest through disposition. During his time as a Public Defender, he conducted multiple trials and evidentiary hearings on behalf of his clients. Mr. Johnson has extensive trial experience, including first and second chair jury and bench trials.

Subsequently, he joined one of the largest insurance defense firms in Florida. With over twenty offices throughout the United States and the U.S. Virgin Islands, Mr. Johnson had the opportunity to expand his litigation experience to civil and administrative cases, including personal injury and wrongful death claims.

Having spent much of his career defending legal claims, Mr. Johnson brings a new perspective to Urban Thier & Federer, P.A. He is a member of the Florida Bar.

attorneys.bio:
Brock Hjalma Johnson is a native Floridian who has lived in the Tampa Bay area nearly his entire life. Brock was born and raised in Dade City, Florida. He graduated from Tampa Preparatory School in 2003 and received his undergraduate degree from the University of Florida in 2007.

Following his graduation from UF, Mr. Johnson worked on Capitol Hill in Washington D.C. as a member of the legislative staff for U.S. Senator Mel Martinez. His time in D.C. confirmed his desire to pursue a law degree and he moved back to Florida to attend Stetson University College of Law.

While at Stetson, Mr. Johnson was a member of the nationally recognized Stetson Trial Team. His aspiration to become a trial attorney was solidified after being part of a three-person team that won the 2010 National Trial Competition. He graduated from Stetson and was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2011.

Brock Johnson began his legal career at Banker Lopez Gassler P.A., practicing in the field of civil defense litigation. He has tried multiple cases arising out of auto accident and premises liability claims. Florida SuperLawyers named him a "Rising Star" in 2013, 2014 and 2015.

Mr. Johnson joined Morgan & Morgan in 2015 so that he could put his litigation and trial skills to work for the people of Florida.

attorneys.name: Samantha Johnson
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Corey I. Cohen & Associates
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Samantha Johnson has been practicing law for 10 years. Even before attending law school, Samantha Johnson began her work in the field of criminal law. While at the University of Central Florida, Samantha Johnson worked with victim advocates as an intern in the Victim Services Unit.

Following her graduation from the University of Central Florida, she began working with the Office of the Public Defender, Eleventh Circuit, in Miami Florida as a paralegal in the early representation. After attending and graduating from Barry University, School of Law, Samantha began working with the Office of the State Attorney as a Victim Advocate.

To date, her unique experience has allowed her to work on both sides of the table and gain a more complete understanding of the practice of criminal law. It was shortly after that Attorney Johnson became an Assistant Public Defender at the Office of the Public Defender in Orlando. After some years with the Public Defender's Office, Samantha went out on her own in 2009 and has been working in the practice of criminal defense in many counties across Central and South Florida. Those counties included, Palm Beach, St. Lucie, Lee, Hendry, Lake, Polk, Volusia, Osceola, Seminole and Orange County. This experience has familiarized her with a number of different judges and prosecutors and has established a good working relationship with many.

Samantha Johnson has now teamed up with attorney Corey Cohen. With both of their extensive knowledge and experience, together, they both look forward to working with you in helping you to fight your case.

attorneys.name: Ronald Wayne Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law - Federal (White Collar Crime) Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Since graduating from the University of Florida, College of Law In Florida in 1973, Ronald W. Johnson has practiced criminal law. His expertise and accomplishments have earned him a Martindale-Hubbell AV rating and lead him to be named as a Florida criminal Law Super Lawyer. Mr. Johnson started his career as an Assistant Public Defender, and then worked for 10 years as an Assistant State Attorney, six of which were spent as the Chief Assistant State Attorney handling major criminal prosecutions. He was also involved in the prosecution and interrogation of mass murderer Theodore Robert Bundy, Jr. after his arrest in Pensacola, Florida. In 1974, Mr. Johnson entered the private practice of law and limits his practice to criminal trials and appeals. During his career, Mr. Johnson has attended numerous CLE courses, including the National Institute for Trial Advocacy Advanced program, and the National Institute for Trial Advocacy Training Trial Advocacy Workshop at Harvard Law School. Mr. Johnson taught annually for 10 years at the Public Defender's/Prosecutor training program at Stetson University College of Law and the University of Florida College of Law. He has served as a member of the executive counsel of the Criminal Law Section of the Florida Bar and has served on numerous Florida Bar Criminal Law Section committees, including the Certification Committee, the Florida Supreme Court Criminal Procedures Rules Committee, the Education Committee, the Ethics Committee, the Federal Practice Committee, the Substantial Assistance and Drug Trafficking Committee, and served as chairman of the Florida Bar Criminal Law Section Narcotic Practice Committee. Mr. Johnson has been a Board-Certified Criminal Trial Lawyer by the Florida Bar since 1984. Mr. Johnson limits his practice to criminal trials and appeals and practices throughout the South Eastern United States.

attorneys.bio:
William A. Johnson, founder of William A. Johnson, P.A., is a graduate of the University of Florida Liberal Arts and Sciences College, where he received his Bachelor of Arts Degree in Political Science. Mr. Johnson received his Juris Doctor in 1990 from the University of Florida College Of Law and was admitted to the Florida Bar in 1991. He has been Florida Bar Board Certified in the area of Elder Law since 2004, and practices predominantly in the fields of estate planning, Medicaid planning, long-term care planning, guardianship, incapacity planning, will and trust, and probate. He is a two-time winner of the Elder Law Section Member of the Year award.

Mr. Johnson is the Substantive Law Vice Chair of the Elder Law Section of the Florida Bar and the President of the Space Coast Chapter of the Florida State Guardianship Association. He serves as a member of the Florida Bar (Elder Law Section; Real Property, Probate & Trust Law Section), the American Bar Association (Real Property, Probate & Trust Law Section) and the Brevard County Bar Association. He is also a member of the Florida Bar Elder Law Executive Committee and The ELS/AFELA Task Force. In addition, Mr. Johnson belongs to the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys, the Academy of Florida Elder Law Attorneys, the Space Coast Guardianship Association, and the Space Coast Chapter of the Florida State Guardianship Association. He served on the board of directors and as Chairman for the Brevard Alzheimer's Foundation and was the 2006 president of the Brevard Association of Human Services. Mr. Johnson was born in London, England in 1965.

attorneys.name: Brigitte Jolliet
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Brigitte Jolliet is a personal injury litigation attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., where she advocates passionately for accident victims throughout Florida. A South Florida native, Ms. Jolliet combines rigorous legal training with real-world experience to deliver results with compassion, precision, and integrity.

Ms. Jolliet earned her Juris Doctor from Georgetown University Law Center, graduating as a distinguished Blume Public Interest Scholar. Prior to law school, she completed her undergraduate studies magna cum laude at the Honors College of Florida International University and gained practical experience as a personal injury case manager—an early testament to her commitment to justice and client service.

Her advocacy journey began with impactful work at Kristi House Children’s Advocacy Center, supporting survivors of exploitation and collaborating with the Miami Children’s Courthouse child trafficking division. In recognition of her contributions, she received the 2020 Champion for Children Award from the Child Welfare League of America.

While at Georgetown, Ms. Jolliet developed policy expertise through clerkships and internships with the U.S. Senate Small Business Committee and U.S. Senator Marco Rubio’s office, where she later served as a legal policy advisor. In this role, she addressed critical issues ranging from criminal justice reform to constitutional law.

Her legal insight further expanded at the National Governors Association, where she served as a legal policy analyst. There, she helped lead federal grant initiatives focused on juvenile justice reform and deflection-based alternatives to incarceration.

Today, at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., Ms. Jolliet blends her multidisciplinary background in advocacy, policy, and litigation to guide clients through complex personal injury matters. Her dedication to meaningful legal service and community impact continues to distinguish her as a trusted voice for justice.

Awards and Honors

Brittany Johnstone is one of the Associate Attorneys at the Law Offices of Forrest & Forrest, with exclusive practice in Marital and Family Law. Ms. Johnstone’s areas of practice include Divorce (High Net Worth Divorce, Uncontested, Same-Sex, etc.), Prenuptial and Postnuptial Agreements, Alimony/Spousal Support, Child Support, Custody/Parental Responsibility, Time-Sharing, Relocation, Post-Judgment Modifications, Enforcement and Contempt, Paternity, Domestic Violence, Dependency, Adoption, Termination of Parental Rights, and much more.

During her time at Nova Southeastern University, Ms. Johnstone developed her passion for Family Law and advocating for clients through her membership and various leadership roles in student organizations, as well as through her employment with the Law Offices of Forrest & Forrest as a Law Clerk. Ms. Johnstone obtained valuable Family Law Litigation experience for over a year through this position as a Law Clerk before gaining admission to the Florida Bar in September of 2023.

attorneys.name: Velma Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Velma Lozano Jones was born in San Benito, Texas as a second-generation Mexican-American and is fluent in Spanish. She lived in Corpus Christi, San Antonio, Laredo, Brownsville, Del Rio, and the Rio Grande Valley. As her parents were not able to finish school because they had to work in agriculture to help support their families, they were strong advocates for getting a post-graduate education. After high school, she attended and graduated from Del Mar College earning an Associate's Degree in Arts-Mid Management with the Ruben Bonilla Sr. Memorial Scholarship. She proceeded to Texas A&M-Corpus Christi earning a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration-Marketing. She diligently worked full-time all during college to pay for her education. She became an active and initiated member of the co-ed Delta Sigma Pi Professional Business Fraternity where she served as chapter secretary and senior vice president to help fellow business students in their business studies, post-graduate job search, and ethical practices in business enterprise.

Velma moved to Orlando, Florida and proudly joined Morgan & Morgan in 2000 where she worked as a personal injury pre-suit paralegal for eight years. It was during this time that she was admitted to and attended Florida A&M University-College of Law in 2004. She continued to work full-time at Morgan & Morgan while attending law school at night. She graduated in May 2008 and was admitted to the Florida Bar on September 30, 2008, and to the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida on April 12, 2012. She gratefully accepted John Morgan's invitation to join his legal team in 2009 and worked at the Morgan & Morgan Kissimmee Office until 2014 and Orlando downtown office until 2015. She tried cases in Florida and Federal courts and fought for injured clients who had suffered losses in auto crashes, slip and fall and negligent security injuries.

Since 2015, Velma has been fighting for her clients to win their claims for Social Security Disability Insurance and Supplemental Security Income at the Morgan & Morgan Social Security Disability Office in Orlando.

attorneys.name: Arthenia L. Joyner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Senator Arthenia L. Joyner is a dynamic individual whose personal life reads like a chronicle of the struggle for equal justice. She has not just lived history, she made it. Senator Joyner is Of Counsel at Swope, Rodante P.A. in Tampa, FL, practicing in the area of personal injury. Born in Lakeland FL and reared in Tampa, she grew up in a time of segregation and has always been determined to end it. Senator Joyner began her long march for equality as a high school student in Tampa protesting for change as a participant in the Woolworth lunch counter demonstrations. That journey took her to jail cells in Tallahassee during her undergraduate years at Florida A&M University when she was twice arrested for demonstrating against segregation and spent 14 days in the Leon County, FL jail. When president of the National Bar Association, she was arrested for protesting apartheid outside of the South African Embassy in Washington, D.C. in 1985.

Joyner entered politics in the early ‘70s when she chaired in Tampa the Shirley Chisholm’s presidential campaign, Jesse Jackson’s 1984 and 1988 presidential campaigns, and co-coordinator of Lawton Chiles’ 1990 gubernatorial campaign, and Bill Clinton’s 1992 presidential campaign.

A graduate of Florida A&M University College of Law, she was Florida’s fifth Black female lawyer, the first Black female lawyer in Hillsborough County, the first Black lawyer in Polk County, the first Black female lawyer to serve on the board of the Hillsborough County Bar Association, the first Black attorney appointed by Governor Lawton Chiles to the Hillsborough County Aviation Authority, the first Black female appointed to the Board of Directors of the Greater Tampa Chamber of Commerce, the first Black female State Representative and State Senator elected from Tampa, the first Black female Minority Leader in the Florida Senate. Senator Joyner has practiced law for fifty-three (53) years – longer than any Black woman in the history of Florida.

Her most prestigious appointments came from President Clinton, including the U.S. Delegation to the International Population Development Conference in Cairo, Egypt (1994) and the U.S. Delegation to the United Nations 4th World Conference on Women in Beijing, China (1995). She is widely recognized for her leadership on women’s and human rights issues and her relentless passion for justice, truth, and equal rights. The Board of County Commissioners and the Tampa-Hillsborough Library Board in 2018 celebrated her many contributions to Florida and the community by naming its new $9.3 million library in her honor.

attorneys.name: William M. Julien
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of William M. Julien, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Boynton Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Florida employment lawyer William M. Julien has focused on employment law issues since 1994. He opened his own law firm to protect employees' rights in 2002. He earned his law degree from the University of San Francisco. In college, he was named Outstanding Student-Athlete of the Year as an NCAA wrestler at Wright State University in Ohio. He brings that same wrestler's toughness, tenacity, and will to win to your employment law claim.

While many of my law firm's employment law clients come from communities between West Palm Beach and Fort Lauderdale, we have handled workers' rights cases all over Florida. There's never a charge for an initial consultation. We handle most claims on a contingent fee basis, so you won't be charged for legal fees until your case is resolved in your favor. Many laws covering employee rights claims also require your employer to pay your attorney's fees if you win.

attorneys.name: Lydia Jung
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lydia Jung is a licensed attorney in Georgia, specializing in family-based immigration, consular processing, and humanitarian relief. She possesses experience in navigating various facets of immigration law, including adjustment of status, citizenship, waivers, U visa applications, and asylum cases.

A graduate of Georgia State University College of Law, Attorney Jung holds a Juris Doctor degree and is an active member of the State Bar of Georgia. She distinguished herself as a cum laude graduate of the University of Florida, where she earned her Bachelor of Arts in Criminology & Law.

Attorney Jung's personal background as a Korean American imbues her with a deep empathy for the immigrant community. Fluent in both English and Korean, she is committed to providing compassionate and effective legal representation to clients from diverse cultural backgrounds.

attorneys.name: Andrew Jun
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Jun focuses on assisting clients in various commercial matters, including corporate, finance, and M&A matters. Andrew has a wealth of experience working with financial institutions, investment advisers and investment funds, including private equity funds. He routinely serves domestic and international clients, including in cross-border transactions.

Andrew also frequently advises on all aspects of establishing a startup business, including the tax and legal structuring, service and other operational agreements, as well as any required legal and regulatory filings.

Andrew has a depth of experience assisting clients with their regulatory compliance obligations. Some of the regulatory areas that he has assisted clients in include securities regulation, anti-money laundering, as well as various business licensing requirements. Andrew has represented clients before government regulators and self-regulatory organizations, and often provided advice on how businesses should structure their internal operations for consistency with the applicable regulatory obligations.

Andrew graduated from Harvard Law School and has advised a large number of domestic and international clients. Prior to founding Jun Avila, Andrew worked at the Toronto offices of top-tier Canadian national law firms.

attorneys.name: Paul Jun
attorneys.practice_type: Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Paul Jun’s practice focuses on advising clients in a variety of M&A, securities law, finance and general corporate matters, particularly in connection with cross-border transactions. Fluent in Japanese and with over a decade of experience working in Tokyo, he has particular expertise advising Japanese clients in corporate transactions involving the U.S.

A small sample of Paul’s broad transactional experience includes advising:

the acquiror in the largest private equity deal in Japan to date,

a consumer goods manufacturer in the divestiture of multiple business units,

a Japanese company in the sale of its Brazilian subsidiary,

a biotech company in its strategic partnership with a major U.S. food processing company,

utility companies in their minority investments in a combined-cycle power plant project in Ohio,

developers and lenders in multiple large solar power projects in Japan and India, and

numerous Japanese companies on U.S. securities law compliance matters in M&A transactions and in other contexts.

In addition to advising on all aspects of M&A and securities law matters, Paul is also available to advise on finance and general corporate matters, including secured and unsecured loan agreements, sales and supply agreements, manufacturing agreements, license agreements, and non-disclosure agreements, among others.

Paul is a graduate of Harvard Law School. Prior to joining Jun Avila, Paul worked at the Tokyo offices of top tier international law firms.

attorneys.name: Kevin F. Jursinski B.C.S.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Jursinski & Murphy, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kevin F. Jursinski is recognized as one of Southwest Florida's premier attorneys. He has concentrated more than 30 years of practice in the area of real estate, business and construction law in Naples and Fort Myers.

What makes Jursinski unique is that he is Florida Bar Board Certificated in three areas of practice: Real Estate Law, Construction Law and Business Litigation. He is the only attorney (out of more than 96,000 attorneys) in the entire state of Florida who has ever received certification in these three practice areas simultaneously. Certification is The Florida Bar’s highest level of evaluation of the competency and experience of attorneys by the Supreme Court of Florida. The Florida Bar recognizes Kevin as a Board Certified Specialist and expert in Real Estate Law, Construction Law and Business Litigation.

Additionally, he is one of only a handful of Florida Board Certified Real Estate Attorneys in Fort Myers, Florida who is also skilled as a commercial litigator. He has successfully tried numerous cases, by both bench and jury trials, as well as effectively arbitrated business and real estate-related matters. When disputes arise, he is fully prepared to negotiate, mediate, arbitrate or litigate to reach a resolution that is in his clients' best interests.

Kevin's skill and experience has earned him many accolades. He is rated AV Preeminent®, which is the highest ranking level of professional excellence, skill and integrity under the Martindale Hubbell® Peer Review Rating(TM) system. He has also earned a perfect 10.0 score on AVVO.com, a lawyer rating and referral website. For several consecutive years, Kevin has been named a Florida Super Lawyer by Super Lawyers Magazine.

Clients rely on Kevin to handle business and real estate contracts from the initial stages of negotiation and drafting through the actual closing of the transaction. Because of his significant litigation knowledge and experience, Kevin takes a proactive view toward contract drafting and negotiation with the aim of avoiding litigation.

Kevin is a graduate of Kent State University (B.A. Criminal Justice) and graduated in the top 15 percent of his class at Ohio Northern University Pettit College of Law (J.D. 1980). He is admitted to practice in all Florida state courts and the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida. He is a certified circuit court mediator as well as a state-qualified arbitrator, handling only real estate, construction and business-related issues. In addition, he is regarded as one of the top attorneys in the State of Florida in the field of gaming and entertainment law as it relates to the use of video games, arcade amusement centers and game promotions

Kevin is a member of The Florida Bar's sections on: Real Property, Probate and Trust; Business Law; Entertainment, Arts and Sports Law; and City, County and Local Government Law. He is a 30-year member and agent of Attorneys Title Insurance Fund and a Florida licensed real estate salesman for the past 30 years.

The Law Office of Kevin F. Jursinski & Associates is composed of experienced, proven and successful attorneys. Real estate, foreclosure, business litigation, and construction law matters are the law firm's exclusive areas of concentration. Each member of our firm has extensive experience in complex legal real estate matters. For expert assistance in your legal affairs, contact The Law Office of Kevin F. Jursinski & Associates.

attorneys.name: Matthew R. Kachergus
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Matthew R. Kachergus is a lifelong resident of Jacksonville, Florida, attending both elementary and high school in the area. After graduating from Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia, Mr. Kachergus decided to follow in the footsteps of his father and become an attorney. After working for the Office of the Public Defender, Fourth Judicial Circuit, in the Office’s Investigations Division, Mr. Kachergus attended the University of Florida Levin College of Law, where he graduated in 1999. While at law school, Mr. Kachergus received book awards for contracts and international business transactions.After graduating from law school, Mr. Kachergus went to work at Sheppard, White, Kachergus & DeMaggio, P.A. Over his twenty-year career, Mr. Kachergus has successfully represented a wide variety of clients facing an array of criminal charges, including individuals whose Constitutional rights have been violated as well as individuals in civil litigation matters and appeals.

Mr. Kachergus’ tenacious representation and devotion to clients has led to inclusions in Best Lawyers in America in White Collar and Non-White Collar Criminal Defense, Civil Rights, and Appellate Practice. Additionally, Mr. Kachergus has been named as a Super Lawyer in the field of criminal defense. Mr. Kachergus is a member of both the National and Florida Associations of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Mr. Kachergus focuses on representing clients in criminal and civil rights cases. He has specific experience in cases involving police misconduct, police dog bites, excessive force, taser use, and false arrests.

He is admitted to The Florida Bar and is a member of the Supreme Court of the United States of America, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit and Federal Circuit, the United States District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida, as well as the District of Columbia. Mr. Kachergus was a Barrister in the Chester Bedell Inn of Court from 2009 – 2012 and from 2017 - 2020 a member of the First District Court of Appeal Inn of Court.

attorneys.name: Anna Kaminska
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Anna Kaminska is a litigation partner with extensive experience in both criminal and civil matters. She counsels public and private companies and their executives in a wide variety of cases ranging from high-stakes business disputes to investigations involving federal and state law enforcement and regulatory agencies. With over two decades of experience—as an appellate attorney, defense counsel in criminal and civil litigation, and veteran federal prosecutor specializing in financial fraud—Anna brings broad perspective to every single case and knows how to focus immediately on what matters most.

Before joining AXS, Anna spent nearly 13 years as a federal prosecutor in Washington, D.C., most recently serving as the Chief of the Market Integrity and Major Frauds Unit in the Fraud Section at the Department of Justice, where she oversaw more than 200 criminal investigations and led a team of trial attorneys and deputy supervisors in complex fraud investigations involving securities, commodities, cryptocurrency, financial instruments, government procurement, and federal programs. She also served as Senior Counsel to the Assistant Attorney General for the Criminal Division, working with senior leadership at the Department of Justice on a wide range of law-enforcement priorities, including trade fraud and consumer fraud.

As a trial lawyer, Anna prosecuted cases involving multimillion-dollar accounting fraud, cross‑border investment and telemarketing scams, pandemic‑relief schemes, foreign bribery, false statements, and money laundering, among others, serving as lead counsel in numerous multi-week trials and reaching corporate resolutions with criminal fines exceeding $2 billion. Her work earned her several awards, including the Assistant Attorney General’s Award for Exceptional Service and commendations from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Drug Enforcement Agency for investigative excellence. As a supervisor, Anna helped to shape law-enforcement priorities and oversaw significant data-driven initiatives involving the detection of executive insider trading, market manipulation, and fraud in government contracting.

Earlier in her career, Anna practiced in a multinational law firm in New York, where she represented clients in complex federal criminal matters, major civil disputes, and appellate litigation, including in the United States Supreme Court. In her first criminal trial as CJA counsel at the firm, she helped secure a mid-trial acquittal for her client in the Southern District of New York, and her work on a petition for certiorari in the Supreme Court challenging an unconstitutional sentence led to the immediate release of another client from prison. Anna clerked for senior judges in both the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and the New York State Supreme Court, Appellate Division.

attorneys.name: Ramil A. Kaminsky Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Complex business litigation Lawyers in Lakeland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ramil Kaminsky is the Founder and Managing Partner of RAK Law, where he leads a highly skilled team experienced in all aspects of pre-suit and post-litigation matters. With extensive experience, Mr. Kaminsky has managed over 600 cases, consistently achieving favorable outcomes for his clients in areas such as complex business litigation, first-party property disputes, and construction law. He has also handled appeals on these issues, leveraging the appellate process to create influential case law and shape legal precedent.

As a first-generation American, Mr. Kaminsky is the son of Jewish Uzbek immigrants who fled the Soviet Union to escape religious persecution. Raised in Brighton Beach, NY—nicknamed “Little Moscow”—he learned firsthand the value of freedom and the American dream. Unlike many Jewish parents at the time who primarily encouraged their children to pursue careers in medicine, Mr. Kaminsky’s parents gave him the freedom to choose between becoming a doctor, lawyer, or accountant.

Mr. Kaminsky moved to Tampa, Florida, during high school and graduated from Freedom High School. He continued his education locally, attending the Honors College at the University of South Florida (USF), where he earned dual degrees in Psychology and Biomedical Sciences. He then pursued his legal education at Stetson University College of Law, where he earned his Juris Doctor. During his time at Stetson, Mr. Kaminsky was deeply involved in student leadership, serving as President of the Calvin A. Kuenzel Student Bar Association and the Jewish Law Student Association. He also gained valuable experience as a certified legal intern for the Office of the State’s Attorney, a law clerk, and through internships with the Florida Attorney General’s Office and other organizations.

In 2013, after graduating from law school, Mr. Kaminsky began his legal career at QBWB, where he defended nursing homes against claims of abuse and neglect. A few years later, he received a rare opportunity to work in-house at Avatar Insurance, where he helped establish their in-house counsel department. During his time there, Mr. Kaminsky developed processes to streamline claims, managed all active litigation, and oversaw the company’s contracts and litigation department.

He later moved to Orlando to work in-house for a statewide roofing and restoration company, where he played a key role in developing, growing, and streamlining their first-party claims. In addition to managing legal matters, he oversaw various aspects of the business and contributed to its growth. Tragically, the company owner and Mr. Kaminsky’s close friend passed away, which led him to establish RAK Law in 2019. Since then, contractors, roofers, and business owners have consistently sought him out for general counsel.

His firm has since grown, and he regularly educates his clients and their teams on legal compliance. A strong believer in honesty and transparency, which is why he believes the law is best practiced when clients understand all their options—“the good, the bad, and the ugly.” His motto, “I’m not here to sell you dreams but to provide the reality,” reflects his commitment to providing candid advice. As both a licensed attorney and small business owner, Mr. Kaminsky brings a unique perspective that allows him to truly understand the needs of his clients.

During his time there, Mr. Kaminsky developed processes to streamline claims, managed all active litigation, and oversaw the company’s contracts and litigation department.

He later moved to Orlando to work in-house for a statewide roofing and restoration company, where he played a key role in developing, growing, and streamlining their first-party claims. In addition to managing legal matters, he oversaw various aspects of the business and contributed to its growth. Tragically, the company owner and Mr. Kaminsky’s close friend passed away, which led him to establish RAK Law in 2019. Since then, contractors, roofers, and business owners have consistently sought him out for general counsel.

His firm has since grown, and he regularly educates his clients and their teams on legal compliance. A strong believer in honesty and transparency, which is why he believes the law is best practiced when clients understand all their options—“the good, the bad, and the ugly.” His motto, “I’m not here to sell you dreams but to provide the reality,” reflects his commitment to providing candid advice. As both a licensed attorney and small business owner, Mr. Kaminsky brings a unique perspective that allows him to truly understand the needs of his clients.

attorneys.name: Eric S. Kane Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Probate Administration Lawyers in Aventura, FL
attorneys.bio:
Eric S. Kane, Esq. is a member of the Florida Bar who has been practicing law for over fifteen years. His main office is located in Aventura, Florida, where he practices in the areas of estate planning, probate, and trust administration.

Mr. Kane was recently recognized as the American Cancer Society (ACS) National Professional Advisor of the Year for his services as a volunteer member of the ACS's Nationwide Gift Planning Advisory Council. He currently serves as the Council's Chairperson.

In 2018, the University of Miami presented Mr. Kane with an award in appreciation for his service to the University of Miami Planned Giving Board. Mr. Kane has also been recognized by the following organizations: Super Lawyers, "Top Rated Estate Planning and Probate Attorney, South-Florida," Super Lawyers-Rising Stars, "Top Rated Estate Planning and Probate Attorney, South-Florida," and The National Advocates, "Top 100 Lawyers, Wills, Trusts, and Estates, Florida." In addition, Mr. Kane has a perfect 10.0 rating from attorney rating and referral service AVVO.

Mr. Kane frequently lectures on the topics of estate planning, probate administration, and healthcare related matters. Mr. Kane recently presented at the Florida Society for Post-Acute and Long-Term Care Medicine (FMDA) 2021 Annual Conference on the topic of Medical Ethics and the Covid Pandemic. Mr. Kane was also a faculty presenter at the National Association of Directors of Nursing Administration in Long Term Care (NADONA) 2020 Annual Conference and a faculty presenter at the Florida Society for Post-Acute and Long-Term Care Medicine (FMDA) 2019 Annual Conference where he lectured on the legal and ethical implications involving the use of Advanced Directives.

Mr. Kane has also authored a section in a course manual on revocable trusts, estate tax planning, and use of irrevocable trusts in Florida entitled "New Era of Estate Planning in Florida" for Lorman Educational Services.

Mr. Kane is a current or a past member of the following organizations: American Cancer Society Nationwide Gift Planning Advisory Council (Chair); Professional Advisory Board for the University of Miami Office of Planned Giving; Professional Advisory Committee of the Greater Miami Jewish Federation; Miami-Dade Israel Bond Board; Estate Planning Council of Greater Miami; Franklin and Marshall College Alumni Board of Directors; and Florida International University College of Nursing Advisory Board.

Mr. Kane has previously been appointed as a Special Magistrate, Court Appointed Receiver, and Guardian/Attorney/Administrator Ad Litem in the Eleventh Judicial Circuit Court in and for Miami-Dade County.

Mr. Kane is a graduate of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel Florida Fellows Institute and graduated cum laude with a J.D. and L.LM from the University of Miami School of Law in Coral Gables, Florida. He received his B.A. in Government and Latin American Studies cum laude from Franklin and Marshall College in Lancaster, Pennsylvania.
