attorneys.name: Justin J. Klatsky Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Administration Lawyers in Valrico, FL
attorneys.bio:
Justin J. Klatsky is a Partner in the Valrico Law Group practicing in the areas of estate planning and administration, general business and corporate law, and tax law. Over the past eight years, he has developed a comprehensive law practice in those areas, focusing on finding tailored solutions to help clients grow and protect their wealth. Justin earned both his Juris Doctor (J.D.) with honors and his Master of Laws (LL.M.) in Taxation from the University of Florida College of Law. He is a member of the Florida Bar and is admitted to practice before the United States Tax Court.

As an attorney practicing in the area of estate planning, Justin employs wills, trusts, and other devices to protect his clients' assets, interests, and legacy. He believes that in estates and trusts law, asset protection starts with proper planning for both death and incapacity. Justin's estate planning practice is further informed by his experience involved in the administration of trusts and estates; so, Justin does not just plan and implement estate planning for those living, but he has experience with seeing the results of planning (or lack thereof) for those that have passed. He has experience with formal, summary, and ancillary administration, trust and will disputes, and reformation and modification of trusts.

Further, because Justin is also a tax attorney, he advises clients on tax issues of estate planning and administration. For those that have concerns about transfer taxes, such as estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer taxes, and income tax concerns, Justin helps to protect his clients' assets, interests, and legacy by using various advanced planning techniques, such as ILITs, FLPs, QTIPs. Also, as a tax attorney, Justin has experience preparing gift and estate tax returns.

Justin assists business owners at the various stages of the lives of their businesses. At the "birth" of a new enterprise or idea, he counsels entrepreneurs on both how to select the proper entity for their business and how to form their business, with an eye on both tax and liability concerns. During the "life" of the business, Justin advises clients on topics such as asset and stock sales and purchases, shareholder or member buyouts and redemptions, mergers, other reorganizations, and the various conversions of entities from one form to another. Justin has experience with drafting, review, revision, and conflicts involving numerous business agreements. Because of his experience in estate planning and taxation, Justin also assists business owners with developing and implementing customized business succession plans that address the many questions involved in what may happen to a business once the primary operators or owners are no longer involved. In addition to his experience in providing counsel to owners of for-profit enterprises, Justin also has similar experience working with nonprofits and their founders.

There are few situations as stressful as getting a notice, letter, or a visit from the IRS. As a tax attorney, Justin represents individuals, businesses, and organizations in federal tax matters. He has experience assisting clients that have unpaid or unfiled taxes, have received a notice from the IRS, or are subject to a lien or levy (garnishment of wages, other income, or from a bank account). To resolve these issues, Justin provides representation at all levels of the administrative process, including audit (IRS examination), appeal (IRS Appeals), and collections, as well as at the judicial level of the U.S. Tax Court. He also has experience with international tax issues relating to foreign assets and offshore accounts, whether under audit, involving the disclosure procedures, or the planning involved in such ownership.

Justin Klatsky earned his B.A with honors from the Johns Hopkins University, where he was elected to Phi Beta Kappa. He earned his Juris Doctor (J.D.) with honors from the University of Florida College of Law, serving as Student Works Editor of the University of Florida Journal of Law and Public Policy and earning a Certificate in Estates and Trusts Practice. Justin also earned his Master of Laws (LL.M.) in Taxation from the University of Florida, where he served as graduate assistant to Professor Steven Willis.

Justin Klatsky served as Co-Chairman of the Tax Law Section of the Hillsborough County Bar Association for eight years, and he is currently a member of the Tax Law and Real Property, Probate, and Trust Law Sections of the Florida and Hillsborough County Bar Associations. Justin is also a member of the Tampa Bay Estate Planning Council. He has served as a lecturer for Florida Bar approved continuing legal education courses for his peers, authored numerous articles, and presented to professional and community groups on various topics in his areas of practice.

When not assisting his clients, Justin Klatsky enjoys participating in the sport of Schutzhund with his two working line German Shepherds (Bianka and Cade), relaxing with a good book, or traveling the back roads of Florida on the hunt for antiques with his wife, Lily. He and Lily are members of Westminster Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Brandon, Florida.

attorneys.name: Jessica L. Klein
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Civil and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jessica L. Klein is a partner with Mathis Law Group, having previously served as an associate and senior associate with the firm since 2021. With over 15 years of litigation experience, Jessica is versed in complex civil and commercial litigation including business disputes, automobile liability claims, insurance defense and coverage disputes, construction lien enforcement, commercial debt collection, labor and employment law, as well as the prosecution and defense of cargo and PACA claims. Through her practice, Jessica strives to exceed expectations by maximizing client recovery and outcomes, while minimizing client exposure and associated costs. Jessica provides a practical approach to litigation and will develop a case strategy tailored to each client’s specific business needs.

Prior to joining Mathis Law Group, Jessica spent her career representing both businesses and individuals in a wide variety of transactional and litigation matters. She has an extensive background in subrogation and negligence claims, insurance defense, creditors’ rights, healthcare and commercial litigation. Jessica has successfully litigated numerous cases from inception through trial, including receipt of a favorable trial judgment in excess of $2 million. In addition, Jessica has achieved favorable outcomes for her clients through arbitration proceedings and appeals.

Jessica is an avid animal lover and spent a year working with her local humane society to develop community outreach initiatives and advance animal welfare legislation and public policies, including local restrictions on the sale of cats and dogs from puppy and kitten mills. Jessica enjoys hiking and kayaking with her husband, who is a busy aerospace engineer, as well as spending time at home gardening and with her pets.

attorneys.bio:
H. Randolph Klein is a transaction attorney focusing on real property, probate and commercial matters. He is an approved agent for Attorney’s Title Insurance Fund, First American Title Insurance Company and Commonwealth Land Title Insurance Company.

Mr. Klein received his BBA (cum laude) from Stetson University in 1973, and received his JD (with honors) from the University of Florida in 1976. While at the University of Florida he was invited to become a member of the Law Review and is a member of the Order of the Coif. Mr. Klein is a U.S. Army veteran.

Mr. Klein was born and raised in Miami, Florida. His father, Harvey R. Klein, moved to Ocala in 1962 and he joined his father in the full time practice of law in 1976. He and his father practiced together for over twenty-six years until his father’s death in 2003.

Mr. Klein's civic involvement includes service on the Board of Directors of the United Way, Junior Achievement, Munroe Hospital Foundation, Ocala Airport Advisory Board and Heart of Florida Health Center, Inc., to name a few. He is a past president of the Marion County Bar Association.

Mr. Klein has been married to his wife, Susie, for seventeen years. He and his wife have three daughters, Lilly, Laura and Julia.

During both of his summers as a law student, Mr. Knox interned for Nicholas Panagakis, an attorney at Morgan and Morgan in Orlando. Mr. Knox's experience working for the firm gave him the drive to pursue a career in litigation, representing people who have been injured.

Mr. Knox was the President of the Trial Team while attending the University of Florida Fredric G. Levin College of Law. During his competitive run, Mr. Knox won National Championships at the 2018 ABA National Criminal Justice Trial Advocacy Competition in Chicago, and the 2018 Puerto Rico Trial Advocacy Competition. Mr. Knox was recognized with the Best Advocate Award at The Florida Bar Chester Bedell Memorial Mock Trial Competition. Mr. Knox is also a member of the Order of the Barristers, an honor society for law school graduates who demonstrate exceptional skill in trial advocacy, oral advocacy, and brief writing.

Mr. Knox lives in Orlando, Florida, and is the oldest of three brothers.

attorneys.name: Stephen J. Knox
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Stephen Knox was born in St. Petersburg Florida in 1961. He graduated from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Science in Finance before attending the University of Florida College of Law and graduating in 1986 with a Juris Doctor degree. For the past 28 years, Mr. Knox has been litigating, settling and trying Medical Malpractice cases throughout the State of Florida.

Mr. Knox has been rated as an "A" lawyer by his peers through Martindale Hubbell as well as recognized as having the highest ethical standards. Due to his standing among his fellow attorneys, he has been listed in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers. The Florida Bar has recognized Mr. Knox as a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer and he is a member of the Florida Justice Association.

As a practicing Florida lawyer, Mr. Knox has had the privilege of obtaining multiple million and multimillion dollar trial verdicts for his clients over the last 28 years. One of his early medical malpractice trial verdicts was the first million dollar verdict in the history of Morgan & Morgan. He practices throughout Florida and he has had jury trials in Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Polk, Marion, Lake, Brevard, Volusia, Pasco, Manatee, Sarasota, Martin and Leon Counties. His experience in the courtroom is well known to insurance companies and he is regularly successful in settling cases without the need for trial.

Mr. Knox lives in Central Florida with his wife of 25 years and his 3 children.

attorneys.name: John S. Koda Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
John S. Koda received his B.A. from Purdue University in 1984 and J.D. from the University of Florida College of Law in 1989. John is a member of the Florida Bar and is a charter member and Past-President of the Venice-Englewood Bar Association (now the South County Division of the Sarasota County Bar Association).

John's practice areas include general civil litigation in the areas of business, corporate, real estate, construction, and consumer protection. With more than three decades of experience, he has practiced at all levels of Florida courts including appellate courts, administrative hearings and arbitration.

For over 20 years, John was lead litigation counsel for south Sarasota county's oldest law firm, and he also served as senior staff counsel for Florida's Division of Consumer Services and litigated consumer protection cases statewide.

John litigates business, corporate, real estate and consumer matters, specifically related to Florida's Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act (FDUPTA). John works in both the Firm's St. Petersburg and Sarasota offices.

Mr. Koda's community activities have included board memberships with the American Heart Association; Venice Area Beautification, Inc.; Sertoma Club, and the School Advisory Council for Pine View School for the Gifted. He is a two-time past president of Big Brothers Big Sisters of the Sun Coast. He is also a recipient of a national award for community volunteerism from the National Down Syndrome Society. John speaks Hungarian.

attorneys.name: Lauren P. Kohl
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Lauren Kohl's practice area is heavily concentrated in the world of real estate transactions including the representation of buyers and sellers in the purchase and sale of residential and commercial properties, including new construction. In addition to handling real estate closings, Lauren prepares and reviews deeds and mortgage loan documents for her clients and reviews condominium and homeowner's association documents and financial statements. She has been a title insurance agent since 1999 and has conducted over 20,000 closings.

Having earned her Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Magna Cum Laude, from the University of Connecticut in 1988, Lauren went on to obtain her Juris Doctorate Degree, Magna Cum Laude, from the Florida State University College of Law in 1998. She was admitted to the Florida Bar that same year.

Prior to becoming a lawyer, Ms. Kohl enjoyed a successful career in real estate sales which she supplemented with real estate investment. She was the top producer in her Sarasota real estate office for five consecutive years and taught first time home buyer seminars in conjunction with several local and national mortgage lenders. In 2021 and 2022, she was designated an "Elite Top Attorney" by SRQ Magazine. An Elite Lawyer must demonstrate a high degree of skill and success in his or her career, be peer recognized, have exceptional experience, and be active in their community.

Lauren is a member of the Sarasota County Bar Association, the Florida Bar Association, and the Real Property, Probate and Trust Law Section of the Florida Bar. She is also a member of the Realtors Association of Sarasota/Manatee, where she maintains relationships with area realtors as well as keeps abreast of current news and trends in the real estate arena. Over the years, Lauren has served as Board Member for the Sarasota County YMCA, the Venice Aviation Society, and the Big Cat Habitat & Gulf Coast Sanctuary. She enjoys giving back to the community and presently serves on the Board of Directors for CORESRQ, a local non-profit serving families and seniors, as well as sponsors several youth sports teams and maintains a corporate sponsorship at Big Cat Habitat & Gulf Coast Sanctuary.

The combined experience in all aspects of real estate from that of realtor to investor to closing attorney, in addition to her substantial education and expertise in real estate law, makes Lauren the perfect choice for those seeking representation in a real estate transaction.

When not at work, you may find Lauren out on the water, enjoying the sights of our beautiful coast from her bicycle, or relaxing with a good book. Lauren is married to Captain Jon R. Fahs, Jr., US Navy, Retired who is an attorney practicing estate planning for his second act. They have five children.

attorneys.name: Darryl B. Kogan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Darryl B. Kogan – Florida Personal Injury Lawyer and Board-Certified Civil Trial Advocate

With more than 40 years of courtroom experience, Darryl B. Kogan is one of Florida’s most accomplished and respected personal injury attorneys. As a Board-Certified Civil Trial Lawyer and co-founder of Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., he is widely known for his ability to handle complex cases involving serious injuries, wrongful death, and catastrophic losses. Clients across South Florida and beyond turn to Mr. Kogan for his legal knowledge, ethical integrity, and unwavering dedication to justice.

Since founding the firm, he has built a team of skilled litigators who share his commitment to excellence and client-focused advocacy. Whether he’s litigating in state court, federal court, or handling high-stakes negotiations, Mr. Kogan's goal is always the same: to get the maximum possible compensation for those who have suffered because of someone else’s negligence.

Areas of Practice

Darryl B. Kogan represents clients in a wide variety of personal injury and wrongful death cases. His practice areas include:

Auto Accidents

He represents clients injured in car crashes, rideshare (Uber/Lyft) accidents, drunk driving incidents, and distracted driving collisions. He also helps clients deal with insurance companies, manage medical bills, and secure fair settlements. If you’re searching for a Boca Raton car accident attorney or a West Palm Beach auto injury lawyer, Mr. Kogan is a trusted choice.

Truck and Commercial Vehicle Accidents

Truck accidents often involve catastrophic injuries and multiple parties. Mr. Kogan is experienced in handling cases involving semi-trucks, delivery vehicles, and commercial fleet accidents across Florida highways, including I-95, I-75, and the Florida Turnpike.

Motorcycle Accidents

Motorcyclists are often the most vulnerable people on the road. Mr. Kogan fights aggressively to protect the rights of injured riders and recover damages for medical expenses, lost wages, and long-term disability.

Slip and Fall / Trip and Fall Injuries

As a seasoned premises liability attorney, Mr. Kogan helps clients injured on unsafe or poorly maintained properties, including grocery stores, shopping malls, apartment complexes, and parking lots.

Wrongful Death

Losing a loved one is devastating. Mr. Kogan works with families to file wrongful death claims and pursue justice in cases involving fatal accidents, medical errors, workplace negligence, and more.

Catastrophic Injuries

He represents individuals who have suffered life-changing injuries, such as spinal cord damage, traumatic brain injury (TBI), paralysis, and severe burns.

Mass Torts and Product Liability

Mr. Kogan is actively involved in mass tort litigation and dangerous product lawsuits. He helps clients harmed by defective medical devices, pharmaceutical drugs, and toxic exposure incidents.

A Career Built on Legal Excellence

From the beginning of his legal journey, Mr. Kogan has prioritized academic and professional excellence. He earned his Juris Doctor cum laude from the University of Miami School of Law in 1983 and also holds advanced business degrees: an MBA from the University of Denver and a BBA from Florida Atlantic University.

He has been Board-Certified in Civil Trial Law since 1994, a distinction held by fewer than 2% of attorneys in the state. He is licensed to practice in all Florida state courts, multiple federal courts, and the United States Supreme Court. He has also been granted pro hac vice admission in several other states, including California, New York, Virginia, Michigan, and Colorado.

Bar Admissions and Certifications

Florida State Courts

U.S. District Courts – Southern & Middle Districts of Florida

U.S. Court of Appeals – Eleventh Circuit

U.S. Supreme Court

Pro Hac Vice: New York, California, Virginia, Michigan, South Dakota, Colorado

Board-Certified Civil Trial Lawyer – Since 1994 (recertified through 2024)

Legal Leadership and Community Involvement

Mr. Kogan’s dedication to the legal profession goes beyond the courtroom. He has served in several leadership positions:

President, South Palm Beach County Bar Association

Chair, Florida Bar Grievance Committee (multiple years)

Board Member, Palm Beach County Bar Association

Treasurer, Ruth & Norman Rales Jewish Family Services

His community involvement includes mentoring law students and young attorneys, supporting pro bono legal services, and volunteering in programs that promote access to justice.

Awards and Honors

Mr. Kogan’s excellence has been consistently recognized:

AV Preeminent® Rating from Martindale-Hubbell (1998–2024)

Super Lawyers (2006–2025)

Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum

Top 100 Trial Lawyers, National Trial Lawyers (2021–2025)

Avvo Clients’ Choice Award

Silver Eagle Award, Florida Justice Association

Pro Bono Award, Legal Aid Society of Palm Beach County

Case Results (Representative)

$2.8M – Pedestrian struck by delivery truck in Palm Beach County

$1.4M – Apartment complex security failure resulting in injury

$875K – Slip and fall injury at retail store

$1.2M – Motorcycle accident settlement after complex liability dispute

These outcomes reflect the legal skill and trial strategy Mr. Kogan brings to each case. Results vary by circumstances.

Client-Centered Philosophy

Mr. Kogan believes that successful legal representation begins with compassionate, transparent communication. He and his team keep clients informed every step of the way and work to ease the burden during difficult times. His clients often describe him as honest, approachable, and fiercely committed to their success.

Bilingual Legal Services – English & Spanish

Kogan & DiSalvo serves a diverse population across Florida and offers bilingual services. Mr. Kogan ensures that Spanish-speaking clients receive the same level of advocacy and communication as any other client.

Florida Office Locations

Kogan & DiSalvo has multiple offices to serve clients across the state:

Boca Raton – 7900 Glades Rd, Suite 630

Boynton Beach – 3615 W Boynton Beach Blvd

Delray Beach – 258 SE 6th Ave, Suite 15

Stuart – 6341 S Kanner Hwy

North Miami Beach – 633 167th St, Suite 812

Tampa – 1725 W Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd, Suite 106

Frequently Asked Questions

What does it cost to hire Mr. Kogan?

You pay nothing upfront. Mr. Kogan works on a contingency fee basis—no fees unless compensation is recovered.

How long do I have to file a personal injury lawsuit in Florida?

The standard statute of limitations is two years from the date of the injury. However, exceptions exist. Early legal advice is critical.

How long will my case take?

Every case is different. Some settle within months; others may take longer, especially if litigation is required.

Can I speak with someone in Spanish?

Yes. Kogan & DiSalvo offers bilingual representation in both English and Spanish.

Ready to Talk to a Personal Injury Attorney?

If you or a loved one has been injured in an accident in Boca Raton, Palm Beach County, or anywhere in Florida, contact Darryl B. Kogan for a free consultation. You have no obligation and no legal fees unless your case is successfully resolved.

Every case is different. Some settle within months; others may take longer, especially if litigation is required.

Can I speak with someone in Spanish?

Yes. Kogan & DiSalvo offers bilingual representation in both English and Spanish.

If you or a loved one has been injured in an accident in Boca Raton, Palm Beach County, or anywhere in Florida, contact Darryl B. Kogan for a free consultation. You have no obligation and no legal fees unless your case is successfully resolved.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Roberta Kohn, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Family and Real Estate Lawyers in Wesley Chapel, FL
attorneys.bio:
Roberta Kohn has over thirty (30) years of legal experience and has worked in both the public and private sectors. Ms. Kohn’s civil and quasi civil experience includes divorce, modification of custody and visitation, family law, child support enforcement, paternity establishment, real estate litigation, actions on contracts, FDCPA, TILA, RESPA, FDUTPA, fraud, quiet title actions, torts, insurance defense, bankruptcy and creditor’s rights in the State of Florida.

Ms. Kohn handles all legal matters involved in corporate, real estate and bankruptcy litigation. Ms. Kohn has an extensive background in real estate law, including six years in the title industry, where she was Office Manager of a title and escrow agency. Ms. Kohn has substantial experience in litigation, including representation as an Assistant Attorney General and a Special Assistant United States Attorney. While working for the government, Ms. Kohn tried over 500 cases, including complex tax and bankruptcy matters, real estate matters, tort issues, injunctions and criminal matters. Prior to focusing on family law, Ms. Kohn was the managing attorney for a firm with offices in Tampa, Florida concentrating on litigation of foreclosure and bankruptcy issues for creditors.

Ms. Kohn has handled numerous appeals, including appeals in the 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals and the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals on the Federal level, Bankruptcy Appeals in the Bankruptcy Courts in the State of Florida and in the State of Florida Appellate Court in criminal, tort, bankruptcy, real estate and complex litigation involving constitutional questions.

Ms. Kohn was most recently employed at a boutique law firm in Tampa, Florida, devoted to family and divorce law and is currently concentrating her practice on providing service in the areas of family, divorce, and real estate law for the Tampa Bay Area. The law office is conveniently located in Wesley Chapel, just on the border of Pasco and Hillsborough counties halfway between Tampa and Dade City. The firm is located off of Interstate 75 and State Route 56 making it easily accessible from surrounding counties, including Pinellas, Hernando, Citrus, Manatee and Sarasota Counties.

attorneys.name: Denitsa Kolev
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Denitsa Kolev moved from her home state of Pennsylvania to pursue her undergraduate degree at The Florida State University. After obtaining her Bachelors of Science, Denitsa became a “Double Nole,” and obtained her Juris Doctorate at The Florida State University College of Law. Upon graduation, she began her career as a criminal defense attorney in Tampa as an Assistant Public Defender.

Denitsa started her career as an Assistant Public Defender, where she represented clients in hundreds of cases, counseled people charged with juvenile, misdemeanor, and felony crimes, and led both bench and jury trials in front of Hillsborough County circuit and county judges. Denitsa then joined Escobar, Michaels & Associates where she has since expanded her practice in criminal law and represents clients in counties across the state of Florida. She is a zealous advocate and represents cases thoroughly and aggressively while providing open and empathetic communication with her clients. Denitsa has been successful in arguing motion issues, such as “Stand Your Ground,” motions to suppress evidence, motions to modify and terminate probation, bond motions, and motions to dismiss. She has also successfully defended juvenile, misdemeanor, and felony charges, resulting in dismissals, acquittals, and reduced charges. She has represented clients in high profile cases, and has been featured on Court TV in the Florida vs. Michael Keetley double homicide trial. She also worked closely on the Florida vs. Curtis Reeves case, a self-defense case which ended in an acquittal after a month-long jury trial.

She is admitted to practice in all Florida State County and Circuit Courts as well as the United States Middle District of Florida.

Denitsa speaks Spanish and is also fluent in Bulgarian. She enjoys her free time by traveling and spending time with her family and friends.

attorneys.name: Emily McAlhaney Konicek
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
At Konicek Law, PLLC, I tailor my legal services to your particular case and circumstances. With me, you will not be dealing with paralegals and support staff. I will be personally handling your case from start to finish. I will keep you informed of the progress of your case in a timely manner and will thoroughly work on your case until final resolution. Every case is different and requires a unique approach. My experience allows me to tailor my approach to meet your individual needs. My ultimate goal is to settle your case to get the best resolution for you and to avoid excessive legal fees. This is often done through the mediation process, and the majority of cases settle in mediation. If settlement is not possible, I will proceed to trial or hearing and will diligently prepare your case for court.

My philosophy is to provide a straight forward approach to your particular case. I will tell you the pros and cons of your case and the potential legal ramifications if you were to proceed to a hearing or trial. I believe it is my duty is to give you not only give you not only the best case scenario, but also your worst case scenario if you proceed to court. This will allow you to make informed decisions on how you wish to proceed in your case, as the ultimate decision is in your hands.

I understand that family law cases involve highly sensitive issues that often deal with children. I handle cases in a compassionate, yet practical manner while keeping the sensitive issues in mind throughout the case. If your case involves children, the children will most likely will be the most important aspect of your case and I always keep their best interest in mind when dealing with your particular situation. I have been practicing family law since 2006 and have handled hundreds of family law cases including divorces, paternity, child custody, relocation, and modifications. I have also handled contempt cases, department of revenue child support cases, domestic violence injunctions, as well as various other family law issues. I have practiced in several different counties across the Central Florida area including Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Polk, and Volusia. I have been in front of many different Judges and General Magistrates over the years and have gained knowledge and experience in many different family law realms.

I attended University of Florida in Gainesville, Florida where I obtained by undergraduate dual business degree in Marketing and Management and minor in Economics. I attend law school at Stetson University in St. Petersburg, Florida and graduated with a dual degree in law and Masters in Business Administration. I worked for the State Attorney's Office in Orange and Osceola counties when I first graduated from law school where I prosecuted hundreds of misdemeanor and felony cases. In my experience at the State Attorney's Office, I handled many jury trials and gained extensive trial experience. I was also a DUI/Domestic Violence Specialist in which I was responsible for handling serious DUI cases and charging Domestic Violence cases. I have been practicing family law since I left the State Attorney's Office and opened my own law firm.

I am a member of the Orange County Bar Association and the Central Florida Association of Women Lawyers. I am also an active member of the Junior League of Greater Orlando and have been recognized as a Junior League Volunteer of Distinction.

The hiring of an attorney for your particular situation is one of the most important decisions you will ever make and one of the most expensive decisions you will ever make. I understand how important this process is and it is my goal to handle your case in a practical, cost effective manner. I encourage you to call my office to set up a free consultation. I will be happy to discuss your case and inform you of all of your potential options for proceeding.

attorneys.name: Joseph Anthony Kopacz
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injury Lawyers in Palm Harbor, FL
attorneys.bio:
Joe Kopacz was raised in Pensacola, Florida, and attended St. Leo University where he was a member of the Men's Soccer Team on an athletic scholarship. In 2007, Mr. Kopacz received his Juris Doctorate Degree from the University of Toledo College of Law. Before entering law school, Mr. Kopacz received a Master's Degree in Business Administration (MBA) from the University of West Florida.

Before joining Morgan & Morgan, he worked at two prestigious Civil Trial Firms located in Pensacola, Florida, and Tampa, Florida. During the early years of his legal career, he defended numerous large insurance companies and those they insured in a variety of civil claims, including: auto accidents, tractor-trailer accidents, motorcycle accidents, negligent security, slip and fall accidents, wrongful death, construction site accidents, and construction defect litigation. Having represented large insurance companies for many years, Mr. Kopacz understands how insurance companies defend and evaluate injury cases. He uses his intimate knowledge of the insurance industry to help his clients who suffered serious personal injuries at the hands of someone else's negligent conduct.

Mr. Kopacz has tried many cases in front of juries across the State of Florida and has several published appellate decisions. He has argued in front of the First District Court of Appeal, Second District Court of Appeal, Fourth District Court of Appeal and the Fifth District Court of Appeal.

Mr. Kopacz has been honored with the prestigious "AV Rating" by Martindale-Hubbell, the preeminent national publication in the legal field. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law. It is a distinction reserved for a select few in the legal community. Mr. Kopacz is also Board Certified in Construction Law.

Mr. Kopacz and his wife Andrea have one child - Kate - and reside in Tarpon Springs, Florida.

Ryan has dedicated his entire career to the practice of immigration law solving complex immigration matters, providing strategic advice to professionals, investors, businesses, and their families. Attorney Kosobucki represents numerous clients from diverse industries, including education, healthcare, IT, construction, engineering, hospitality, entertainment, and equine. He also focuses on self-petitions and employment-based visas for individuals of extraordinary ability, including musicians, scientists, actors, entertainers, and athletes. He also devotes a portion of his practice to EB-5 immigration and represents developers seeking financing options other than those from traditional banks and individual investors, as well as to individuals seeking to invest into the United States.

Ryan graduated with honors from Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad College of Law and was a member of Nova Law Review. Ryan is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA). He previously served on AILA's National Board of Publications and chaired the South Florida chapter's Unlicensed Practice of Immigration Law Committee. Ryan is a member of the Florida Bar and has authored or co-authored published immigration law articles in Construction INK! Magazine and the Daily Business Review.

attorneys.name: Traci L. Koster Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Marital and Family Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Traci L. Koster, PLLC is an experienced litigator and keen negotiator focusing her practice exclusively on marital & family law matters. Prior to narrowing her practice to marital & family law in 2016, Traci practiced general civil litigation for several years at a private Tampa law firm. Though Traci's litigation experience makes her adept in the courtroom, she understands most favorable outcomes come through negotiation and alternative dispute resolutions.

Traci is an active member of the Florida Bar and has been intricately involved with the Hillsborough County Bar Association since 2010. Traci was the President for the Hillsborough County Bar Association's Young Lawyers' Division for the 2019-2020 Bar year and currently serves in her third term on the Executive Council for the Hillsborough County Bar Association Family Law Section. Traci is a former member of the Stann Givens Family Law American Inn of Court and a former inaugural member of the William Reece Smith Jr. American Inn of court.

Outside of her legal career, Traci was also part of the Leadership Pinellas graduating class of 2015 and served on the organization's board of directors in 2015-2016. She graduated from Tampa Connection in 2018 and served a two-year term on the Tampa Connection board of directors. These organizations gave Traci a unique, behind-the-scenes understanding of the Pinellas and Hillsborough communities, so she can better represent her clients' needs.

In 2020, Traci was elected to serve in the Florida House of Representatives for District 64, covering parts of Hillsborough and Pinellas Counties. Through her service in the Florida Legislature, Traci takes her passion for helping Florida's families to a statewide platform.

To give back to her community, Traci co-founded the Tampa Bay Pro Bono Partners, which brings attorneys and businesses together to provide pro bono legal services to those in need. Traci has also served as attorney ad litem for children in the foster care system through Crossroads for Florida Kids. In addition, Traci served for three years as a mentor through the Hillsborough Education Foundation's Take Stock in Children Program, and she keeps in touch with her mentee regularly now that she's graduated high school!

In 2016, Traci proudly received the Outstanding Pro Bono Service by a Young Lawyer Award from the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit. In 2019, Traci received the Florida Bar Young Lawyer's Division's Lynn Futch Most Productive Young Lawyer Award, and in 2020, Traci received the Hillsborough County Bar Association's Young Lawyer's Division's Outstanding Young Lawyer Award.

Traci attended the University of Central Florida for her undergraduate degree and was an active member of the Burnett Honors College and the PHI ALPHA DELTA Law Fraternity. Traci graduated Magna Cum Laude with her Bachelor of Science Degree in Legal Studies. After her time at UCF, Traci attended Stetson University College of Law, where she served as an Articles and Symposium Editor for the Stetson Law Review and a research assistant for Professor Louis Virelli. Traci also served two terms as a judicial intern for the Honorable U.S. District Judge Elizabeth Kovachevich - more intimately known as Judge K.

After graduating number two in her law school class, Traci Joined Bush Ross, P.A. as part of their commercial litigation department. During her six years at Bush Ross, Traci gained valuable litigation experience and handled a wide variety of commercial and corporate litigation matters, including marital and family law matters, before leaving the firm to devote her practice exclusively to marital and family law in 2016.

Traci was born in Greensboro, North Carolina, but moved to Florida as a child. She was raised in Palm Harbor, FL and now resides in Tampa with her two children, Colton and Sadie. When she's not working, Traci enjoys spending time with her kids and getting lost in a good book.

Traci is rated AV Preeminent by Martindale Hubbell, has been selected as a Super Lawyer Rising Star eight consecutive years in a row, and is recognized as a Florida Trends Legal Elite Up & Comer. She has also received recognition by Tampa Bay Magazine's list of Top Attorneys: Tampa Bay's Outstanding Young Lawyers since 2014 and has a Superb rating with Avvo. The Tampa Bay Business Journal recognized Traci as People to Know in Law in 2021.

attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in North Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly M. Kostun has twenty-five years of experience as a dedicated litigation attorney at her former firm, Hinman, Howard & Kattell, LLP. Kimberly recently became a partner at Guffey & Kostun Law Group, LLP that was formerly the Peter Feaman Law Group. Kimberly manages the Firm’s Pennsylvania branch office maintaining a general litigation practice. Kimberly has built a reputation for providing effective legal representation across a broad range of practice areas. She focuses on general litigation, complex banking and commercial litigation, construction litigation, motor vehicle injury claims, premises liability, animal bite cases and commercial and residential landlord tenant dispute cases.

In addition, Kimberly has extensive experience in mortgage foreclosure, debt collection, and creditors’ rights, helping clients navigate financial disputes with strategic solutions. As a Florida Supreme Court Certified Circuit & County Mediator, she brings valuable insight into alternative dispute resolution, working to achieve favorable outcomes both in and out of the courtroom.

Licensed to practice in Florida, Pennsylvania, and New York, Kimberly has successfully represented individuals, businesses, and financial institutions in high-stakes cases. Whether handling complex commercial disputes or personal injury claims, she is known for her strategic thinking, attention to detail, and commitment to client success.

attorneys.name: Mark J. Kovack
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mark J. Kovack is a Senior Attorney with Urban Thier & Federer, P.A. He is based out of the Connecticut office.

Mr. Kovack's practice focuses primarily on civil litigation including commercial and business litigation, construction litigation, personal injury law, products liability, real estate litigation, employment law, alternative dispute resolution (including arbitration and mediation), landlord-tenant/housing litigation (commercial and residential), probate litigation, and appeals.

Mr. Kovack is a member of the Connecticut Bar, the New York Bar, the federal United States Second Circuit Court of Appeals, and the bar of the United States District Court for the District of Connecticut. Mr. Kovack serves as a court appointed "Special Master" to mediate disputes in litigation and offers alternative dispute resolution (ADR) services as an arbitrator and mediator. Mr. Kovack has extensive arbitration training with the International Institute for Conflict Prevention and Resolution and is able to serve as an arbitrator and mediator for domestic and international matters.

He has been added as of October 2016 to the list of court appointed animal advocates as part of Connecticut's new law (effective 10/1/16) permitting superior court judges to appoint volunteers to act as advocates for the interest of justice in certain proceedings involving animals.

He is a member of the Connecticut Trial Lawyers Association, a group of trial lawyers representing plaintiffs in personal injury, product liability and malpractice actions. Mr. Kovack is also a Board Member, Executive Committee member and the Secretary of the Danbury Westerners Baseball Club, Inc., a 501 (c)(3) corporation which operates the Danbury Westerners collegiate baseball team in the New England Collegiate Baseball League.

attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Kravitz is Board Certified in Construction Law by the Florida Bar. He has received an “AV Preeminent” rating by Martindale-Hubbell by achieving the highest level of professional excellence rating available. He has also received a “Superb” rating by Avvo.com, the highest rating Avvo awards.

Mr. Kravitz received his Juris Doctorate Summa Cum Laude from Nova Southeastern University, where he was a member of the Law Review and Moot Court Honor Society. He received his Bachelor of Science degree in Biology from Florida State University in 1992, as well as his Master of Science Degree in Psychology from Nova Southeastern University in 1997. Mr. Kravitz has been a resident of the South Florida area since 1978, and currently resides in Parkland with his wife Dawn, and their children Madyson and Braeden.

Mr. Kravitz is admitted to practice in all Florida state and federal courts, as well as the First and Eleventh Circuit Courts of Appeals and the District of Columbia Court of Appeals. He is a member of the Broward County Bar Association and its Construction Law Committee, the American Bar Association, and the Florida Bar Construction Law Committee.

Mr. Kravitz concentrates his practice primarily in commercial and construction law including litigation, arbitration, mediation and negotiation of construction matters including construction lien claims and defense, payment and performance bond claims and defense, bid protests, construction contract preparation and negotiation and construction defect claims and defense. He also has a wide array of experience in contract, tort, corporate, and Americans with Disabilities Act issues. Mr. Kravitz is also qualified in many areas of alternative dispute resolution. He is a Florida Supreme Court Certified Circuit Court Mediator, a Florida Supreme Court Qualified Arbitrator, as well as a Qualified Trial Resolution Judge. Mr. Kravitz is available to serve in any such capacities, in addition to his litigation practice.

Mr. Kravitz is on the 2012 list of “Super Lawyers,” and can be found in the 2012 “Best Lawyers in Florida” publication, 2013 “Best Lawyers in America” and Martindale-Hubbell’s “Top Rated Lawyers” magazine for 2012.

Personal injury lawyer Douglass Kreis Mr. Kreis received his B.A. from Mercer University in Political Science where he attended under a four year academic/athletic scholarship. Following his undergraduate studies, Mr. Kreis attended the Cumberland School of Law where he received his J.D. in 1997. While in law school, Mr. Kreis earned the highest grade in his class in Constitutional Law and the distinction as Cumberland's 1997 Environmental Law Representative to participate in the National Environmental Law Conference in Washington, D.C. Mr. Kreis gained significant trial advocacy experience through the school's Moot Court Competition and received the honor of working with the Honorable Judge Micheal Bolin, Probate Judge for the Probate Division in and for Jefferson County, Alabama as an assistant by way of judicial externship.

Mr. Kreis is admitted to all Florida State Courts and all United States District Courts of Florida. Mr. Kreis is a member of the American Bar Association and the Association of Trial Lawyers of America. Mr. Kreis is an experienced Pensacola personal injury lawyer who was originally from a diverse general practice background before his transition into his present position within the firm's pharmaceutical litigation department. There, Mr. Kreis' work has been primarily focused on claims involving injury arising out the use of the diet drug Fen Phen. Mr. Kreis has jointly provided representation and advisement to thousands of diet drug clients. Other cases

Mr. Kreis is handling include injuries from the ingestion of the withdrawn drugs/products Baycol (anti-cholesterol drug) and Ephedra (dietary and work-out related supplement) as well as consumer fraud and class action cases involving Florida Dry cleaning Litigation, Shell/Texaco Bad Gasoline Litigation and Ford Truck and SUV Defective Door Latch Litigation and wrongful death.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Claims & Lawsuits Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Darrell W. Kropog, Jr., is a recognized personal injury attorney in our Tampa office. He obtained his undergraduate degree from Louisiana State University (LSU) and was a member of the LSU Lacrosse team playing defense and defensive midfielder. After graduating from LSU, Mr. Kropog accepted an academic scholarship to attend the Thomas M. Cooley Law School (now Cooley Law School at Western Michigan University). During his last year in law school, he completed an externship as a law clerk for the prominent Baton Rouge law firm of Manasseh, Gill & Knipe.

attorneys.name: Jack Andreas Krumbein
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jack Andreas Krumbein, Esquire has recovered millions of dollars for his clients litigating personal injury. Prior to becoming an attorney, Mr. Krumbein was a Financial Advisor for Morgan Stanley Private Client Services, International Marketing Manager for a Public-Private Partnership known as the Global Trade Center of the Inland Empire, and a classical and recording musician in Los Angeles, California. During his time working in Los Angeles, he worked on projects for Sting, David Campbell, Avril Lavigne, Ali Helnwein, Josh Groban, Disney, 20th Century Fox, Priceline, Independent Feature Film, Clay Aiken, Ben Moody, Walter Mathau, MC Lite, Monica, Dave Mathews Band at the 2010 Grammy Awards, among many others.

Some highlights of his music career involved productions at the American Embassy in Israel, Jordan's Jerash International Music Festival, Egypt's Royal Opera House, Canada's Calgary Stampede, New York City's Carnegie Hall, among many others. Due to his background, he has traveled to 29 countries and speaks fluent Spanish and English with conversational German. Mr. Krumbein was born in Hamburg, Germany and immigrated to the United States when he was twelve (12) years of age.

In 1998, Mr. Krumbein obtained his Bachelor of Music Performance from Pacific Union College, and in 2004, a Master's in Business Administration (MBA) from La Sierra University. After years of business experience, Mr. Krumbein decided to attend Barry University School of Law. During law school, he was a Deans Fellow, a clinician in the immigration clinic, and obtained the highest grades for his class in Criminal Law, and Contracts Drafting. Mr. Krumbein opened his practice in April 2013.

Mr. Krumbein has taken cases to both jury and bench trial and has been very successful in alternative dispute resolution. He has fought for those who cannot fight for themselves and taken cases so far as to having appealed to the Board of Immigration Appeals, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and to the Supreme Court of the United States. He is admitted to practice law in all the courts within the State of Florida, the Northern District of Florida, the Middle District of Florida, the Southern District of Florida, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and most recently to the Supreme Court of the United States.

During his rare moments away from work, he enjoys playing the violin, soccer, chess, and spending as much quality time with his wife and children as possible.

attorneys.name: Frank C. Kruppenbacher
attorneys.practice_type: Children’s Rights Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Frank Kruppenbacher is an attorney practicing in Orlando, Florida. He attended Mount Saint Mary's University in Emmitsburg, Maryland and graduated magna cum laude; and New York Law School where he graduated cum laude. He subsequently attended the Harvard Graduate School of Education program on public engagement. He has clerked for the Honorable Arnold Fraimon, New York Supreme Court, Manhattan and Honorable Stanley Lesser, United States Bankruptcy Judge, Southern District of New York.

In October, 2008, Mr. Kruppenbacher was appointed to the Florida Commission on Ethics by then Florida House Speaker, now U.S. Senator, Marco Rubio. He previously served on The Florida Commission on Sales Tax Reform as an appointee of Governor Jeb Bush. He currently serves as a gubernatorial appointment on the Orlando Aviation Authority and Board Member of A Gift for Teaching and The Florida Virtual School/Pearson joint venture. He together with Dr. David Moser, M.D., founded the charity "For The Children" to meet with unfunded needs of children.

He currently appears weekly with Attorney John Morgan on the television show "The Agenda" on Central Florida's News 13's "The Advocates."

Mr. Kruppenbacher served as President of the Greater Orlando Chamber of Commerce; was a member of the Orange County Ethics & Campaign Finance Reform Task Force appointed by the Chief Judge of the Ninth Judicial Circuit of Florida; Orange County Oversight Committee; the first Orange County Charter Commission; Central Florida Zoological Board; Orange County Convention & Visitor Bureau Board and Orange County Sheriff Departments Oversight Board. In 2007 he was awarded the Special Service Award from the Florida High Schools Interscholastic Athletics Administrators Association.

Mr. Kruppenbacher lives in Orlando, Florida with his wife Patsy and has three children, Amy, Matthew and Michael and one grandson, Ryan David. He handles government action cases and cases involving children's rights.

attorneys.name: John David Kuchta
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
John David Kuchta is a retired FBI Supervisory Special Agent, former Federal Prosecutor and U.S. Diplomat. Kuchta was awarded the FBI Medal of Valor and the Attorney General's Award for Heroism in recognition of exceptional heroism and voluntary risk of life in the face of criminal adversaries; the FBI Star for split second decision making under fire while suffering grievous injury; the Attorney General's Award for Excellence in furthering National Security Investigations; two United States Attorney's Office Law Enforcement Officer of the Year awards; Florida 20th Judicial Circuit Lee County 100 Law Officer of the Year Award, Anti-Defamation Shield Award in recognition of law enforcement's significant contributions toward protecting America from hate crimes, extremism and international terrorism; and the FBI Combat Theatre Ribbon in recognition of conducting investigations of National importance in a war zone.

Kuchta earned his undergraduate degree with honors from the University of Pittsburgh. Kuchta worked full time while attending night law school at Duquesne University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. He is a retired member of the Pennsylvania Bar and a member of the Florida Bar in good standing. Upon graduation from law school, he clerked for the late Honorable Patrick J. Tamilia for the Superior Court of Pennsylvania. As a federal prosecutor in the Alexandria Division of the Eastern District of Virginia (The Rocket Docket) Kuchta prosecuted all manner of felony and misdemeanor crimes to include drug trafficking, weapons violations, crimes against children, crimes on federal reservations and white-collar crimes.

In 1991 Kuchta became an FBI Special Agent Attorney and an FBI Legal Advisor in 1993. After graduating from the FBI Academy, Kuchta served in Washington, D. C., the FBI Tampa Division, Bagram Air Base, Afghanistan, and as an FBI Assistant Legal Attaché at the U.S. Embassy in London, England. During his 27-year career in the FBI, he conducted investigation which resulted in criminal convictions of drug trafficking organizations, violent gangs, white collar criminals, money launderers, corrupt public officials, terrorists and corporations involved in violating the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.

After retiring from the FBI, Kuchta worked in the corporate sector conducting international ethics and compliance investigations for a Fortune 50 Corporation on behalf of the General Counsel.

Over 30 years ago John swore an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution of these United States. He retired in 2018 after 27 years of service as one of the most highly decorated living FBI Special Agents. You'll need the experience and knowledge of the inner workings of the FBI and the Department of Justice If you find yourself on the wrong end of a federal investigation. And you can be assured he will fight to uphold your rights and ensure that the government meets its heavy burden placed on it by our Constitution. Whether you are a private citizen or corporation criminally or civilly charged; had your security clearance revoked, discriminated against in an employment setting due to your religious, political beliefs or skin color; or fear retaliation for blowing the whistle on cover-up and corruption; know that he will fight for you in the halls of justice.

attorneys.name: Scott A. Kuhn
attorneys.practice_type: Foreclosure & Alternatives Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
A person's experience is vital to understanding the needs of others. And Attorney Scott Kuhn has a lot of experience, in a variety of different worlds.

Before becoming an attorney, for example, Scott Kuhn worked as a firefighter/paramedic, which helps him understand the needs of car accident victims and their families. Working his way through college, while supporting a wife in law school and their child, built understanding for those struggling to make ends meet. As an executive at General Electric, he gained the knowledge to help those building and growing businesses. And while earning both a Masters in Science and a Masters in Business, he became empathetic for those trying to build better lives for themselves and their families.

After earning his law degree, Scott entered yet another world, one in which he could use his empathy and new advocacy skills to help people to a greater degree than ever before. For a time he helped clients meet their goals at his first law firm, Baker and McKenzie in Moscow, Russia. But he eventually realized the large law firm wasn't offering the level of personalized service he felt compelled to provide.

That's why he opened his own law firm in 2006. Among other legal services, he helps those injured by negligent drivers get the money they deserve. For Scott Kuhn, it's all about immediacy: as a first responder, he pulled his own parents out of the wreckage of their car after an accident caused by a careless driver. And while his parents survived that accident, he is one of the few attorneys who have actually seen first-hand the devastating effect negligent driving can have on families, and how quickly they need to be made whole. Scott has also seen the catastrophic financial effects poor estate planning, real estate and other business law dealings can have on those who need to be protected the most.

All these experiences drive him to do his very best to fulfill his ultimate mission: to protect people financially and to educate them about all their legal options. His goal is to help them get the most from all their family and business dealings. Scott offers free consultation and document review for estate planning and probate, and works on a contingency basis for personal injury. He treats his real estate and business law clients in a similarly flexible manner.

Although he holds a bachelor's degree, and two master's degrees in addition to his law degree, Scott feels it is his "empathy, advocacy and immediacy" that differentiates himself from other attorneys - not his advanced education, as comprehensive as it is.

He brings that same sense of urgency and passion to all his practice areas. For Scott Kuhn, there are no routine legal matters. He knows his clients count on him to do the right - and smart - thing every time, on every matter that affects them. He feels privileged to be a part of their lives, oftentimes at moments of their greatest vulnerability. From initial call to the last stage of the appeal process (if it comes to that), Scott is intimately involved.

Scott's commitment to helping people doesn't stop at the door of his law office: He is a Fire Commissioner for the Iona-McGregor Fire District and active in the Greater Ft. Myers Chamber of Commerce. He is also an active Shriner and serves as the Donor Relations Chairman for Shriner's Hospital For Children and attorney for the Araba Shrine Center. He has lived in Ft. Myers with his three children for the past13 years.

All these experiences drive him to do his very best to fulfill his ultimate mission: to protect people financially and to educate them about all their legal options. His goal is to help them get the most from all their family and business dealings. Scott offers free consultation and document review for estate planning and probate, and works on a contingency basis for personal injury. He treats his real estate and business law clients in a similarly flexible manner.

Although he holds a bachelor's degree, and two master's degrees in addition to his law degree, Scott feels it is his "empathy, advocacy and immediacy" that differentiates himself from other attorneys - not his advanced education, as comprehensive as it is.

He brings that same sense of urgency and passion to all his practice areas. For Scott Kuhn, there are no routine legal matters. He knows his clients count on him to do the right - and smart - thing every time, on every matter that affects them. He feels privileged to be a part of their lives, oftentimes at moments of their greatest vulnerability. From initial call to the last stage of the appeal process (if it comes to that), Scott is intimately involved.

Scott's commitment to helping people doesn't stop at the door of his law office: He is a Fire Commissioner for the Iona-McGregor Fire District and active in the Greater Ft. Myers Chamber of Commerce. He is also an active Shriner and serves as the Donor Relations Chairman for Shriner's Hospital For Children and attorney for the Araba Shrine Center. He has lived in Ft. Myers with his three children for the past13 years.

attorneys.name: Ira J. Kurzban Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Naturalization Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Kurzban holds J.D. and M.A. Degrees from the University of California, Berkeley and a B.A. with honors from Syracuse University where he graduated Phi Beta Kappa. He is also an honorary fellow of the University of Pennsylvania School of Law where he was honored for his exemplified signal service to every aspect of the legal profession. He is also the recipient of the Wasserstein Fellowship at Harvard University Law School and was named the 2020 Recipient of the Leonard J. Theberge Award for Private International Law. Mr. Kurzban has been a founding partner in the Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli & Pratt, P.A., Florida for over 40 years and is the chair of the firm's immigration department.

Mr. Kurzban is a past-national President and former General Counsel of the American Immigration Lawyers Association. He has received national recognition for his work in the immigration field. He has been named by the National Law Journal as one of the top twenty immigration lawyers in the United States; he has been listed for over a quarter century in the Best Lawyers in America for his work in immigration and employment law; and he has been listed repeatedly in Law dragon as one of the top 500 lawyers in the United States. Mr. Kurzban was the first recipient of the Tobias Simon Pro Bono Award presented by the Chief Justice of the Florida Supreme Court. He is also the recipient of the Lawyers of the Americas Award for his work on behalf of human rights in this hemisphere given by the University of Miami, the Jack Wasserman Award for excellence in federal litigation and the Edith Lowenstein Memorial Award for excellence in the advancement of immigration law given by the American Immigration Lawyers Association, and the Carol King Award for his efforts in immigration law given by the National Lawyers Guild. In 1986 Mr. Kurzban was selected by Newsweek Magazine in their commemorative issue on the hundredth anniversary of the Statue of Liberty as one of 100 American heroes for his work on behalf of immigrants. He was also selected by Esquire Magazine as part of America's New Leadership Class. Mr. Kurzban has also been named to Who's Who in America, Who's Who in American Law and Who's Who in the World. He was also named as one of the world's twenty three most highly regarded corporate immigration lawyers in the International Who's Who of Corporate Immigration Lawyers and praised as a legend in the field who has written the definitive book on U.S. immigration law. Mr. Kurzban and the firm have been listed in Chambers as first tier lawyers in immigration law in 2021. For the past several years Mr. Kurzban has received Chambers highest ranking as a “star individual.”

Mr. Kurzban has also litigated over 100 federal cases concerning the rights of aliens, including Jean v. Nelson, Commissioner v. Jean, and McNary v Haitian Refugee Center, Inc., all of which he argued before the United States Supreme Court. He has also litigated numerous cases under the Alien Tort Claims Act and the Torture Victim Protection Act, including obtaining a $500 million judgment against Jean-Claude Duvalier, the former dictator Haiti.

Mr. Kurzban was also one of the founders of the Berkeley Law Foundation, a non-profit organization providing scholarships for law students and law graduates engaged in significant legal assistance programs throughout the United States. He is also one of the founders of Immigrants' List, the first pro-immigrant political action committee in the United States.

Mr. Kurzban is an adjunct faculty member in Immigration and Nationality Law at the University of Miami School of Law and has lectured and published extensively in the field of immigration law, including articles in the Harvard Law Review, Columbia University Press, the San Diego Law Review and other publications. He is the author of Kurzban's Immigration Law Sourcebook, the most widely used one-volume immigration source in the United States.

attorneys.name: Grant A. Kuvin
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Grant Kuvin was born in Coral Gables, Florida in 1976. He graduated from Florida State University in 1998 with a degree in Finance and worked as a financial analyst for a local bank in Miami until 2000 when he decided that he wanted to pursue his dream and go to law school. He graduated from Stetson University College of Law in 2003, moved to Orlando, Florida and worked for a large firm representing doctors, hospitals, nurses and insurance companies in medical malpractice and other types of more general trial work. Mr. Kuvin continued on this course until 2008 when he decided to use his past experience to represent the rights of the people of Florida in their personal injury and medical malpractice actions.

Mr. Kuvin worked in Morgan & Morgan's Orlando office until 2014 when he moved to Jacksonville to manage the Medical Malpractice Department for all of North Florida. Since moving to North Florida he and his family have become active members of the local community, regularly delivering meals to the elderly and books to children.

Having tried Malpractice cases throughout the entire state of Florida, Mr. Kuvin understands the time and attention that these complex cases require. In addition, he knows it's important to never lose sight of the emotional toll they can take on the families. But having a voice in a daunting healthcare industry can change not only one client's life, but can potentially help save the lives of many future patients - and that can make a world of difference to us all.

attorneys.name: Jed Kurzban Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
I have been an attorney at Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli & Pratt, P.A., since 1995 and was made an equity partner in 2013. I am the managing partner in an established 40 plus year law firm with a stellar reputation. We pride ourselves in representing our clients with the expertise and dedication that each case deserves. I am a trial attorney and the verdicts and settlements I have obtained on behalf of my clients demonstrate the dedication and perseverance that I invest to make sure that our clients receive the maximum compensation and justice they are entitled to.

I graduated from the University of Alabama in 1992, where I was on both the Dean's List and the President's List (4.0 grade point average). While at the University of Alabama, I was a brother in the Zeta Beta Tau fraternity. I received my Juris Doctor degree from the University of Miami School of Law in 1995 and was admitted to the bar in the State of Florida, the United States District for the Southern District of Florida, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. In 2015, 1 was admitted to the Hawaii Bar and the Hawaii State Bar Association and I am of Counsel with the prestigious law firm of Damon Key Leong Kupchak Hastert.

I have successfully represented my clients as lead trial counsel in all areas of tort. However, the bulk of my practice concentrates on medical malpractice, product liability and personal injury on behalf of plaintiffs. While my main office is in Miami, I have successfully litigated cases throughout Florida and the United States. My nationwide practice emphasizes cases involving the misdiagnosis or improper treatment of kidney disease. As lead counsel and co-counsel in several major cases I have obtained exceptionally favorable verdicts for my clients to obtain the justice they deserve.

I have served as vice-chair of the Dade County Bar Association Trial Section (2001), and on the Board of Directors for the Florida Justice Association (2004). 1 have been to Tallahassee, Florida several times in connection with the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers to lobby and construct litigation aimed at protecting injured victims. I have also directed and participated in courses to implement a permanent attorney ethics and responsibility curriculum in conjunction with the University of Miami School of Law. In the fall of 2014, I was hired to teach a pre-trial civil litigation course at the University of Miami School of Law.

I am currently a member of the Dade County Bar, the Florida Bar, the Hawaii Bar, the American Association of Justice, the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers, the American Bar Association, and the American Constitution Society. I am also AV rated by Martindale-Hubbell and have been named a Distinguished Lawyer, a Super Lawyer, Lawyer of Distinction, and one of the 10 best Attorneys in South Florida.

I am the proud father of Elspeth and Ailsa and the loving husband of Lorna Kurzban.

attorneys.name: Monique L'Italien
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Monique L’Italien was born in Neptune, New Jersey. She graduated, cum laude, with a bachelor’s degree in psychology from Trinity College in Washington D.C. and earned her law degree from Vermont Law School with a particular emphasis in environmental law.

Ms. L’Italien is a seasoned attorney who practiced environmental law and land use in both Washington D.C. and Florida for several years. She then became as Assistant Attorney General for the State of Florida practicing in the Criminal Appeals Division. Ms. L’Italien has argued before the Fourth District Court of Appeal, the Florida Supreme Court, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, and the United States District Court for the Eleventh Circuit.

In 2007, Ms. L’Italien shifted her focus to civil litigation, first for a private firm in Miami then as an Assistant Attorney General in the Civil Litigation Division for the State of Florida where she represented the State in personal injury, civil rights and prisoner cases as well as practiced administrative law.

Ms. L’Italien joined the firm of Rosen Switkes & Entin P.L., in February 2009, where she currently practices in the areas of labor/employment law, civil rights litigation, and commercial litigation.

A member of the Florida Bar, Ms. L’Italien is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

Ms. L’Italien is passionate about volunteerism and presently serves as the Chair of the Animal Law Committee of the Florida Bar and is also an active member of the Junior League of the Palm Beaches.

attorneys.name: Jesus La Rosa Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami Lakes, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Cuba and raised in Miami, attorney Jesus La Rosa began his career at the University of Iowa, College of Law, where he earned a full-tuition scholarship. While at Iowa Law, he distinguished himself through academic excellence and legal writing, earning the Dean’s Award for Academic Excellence in Legal Analysis, Writing and Research, and serving as Associate Editor for the school’s journal on Transnational Law and Contemporary Problems.

After early exposure to immigration law during law school, Mr. La Rosa expanded his practice into corporate and commercial litigation, where he has developed extensive experience representing businesses of all sizes. He regularly advises and advocates for small and midsize companies, while also litigating complex disputes against major publicly traded corporations. His litigation experience spans business owner disputes, shareholder conflicts, banking and private equity matters, and allegations of fraud.

Known for being solutions-driven and fearless in addressing high-stakes challenges, Mr. La Rosa approaches every case with the determination to secure meaningful results for his clients. In addition to his litigation practice, he remains passionate about helping entrepreneurs and business owners with entity formation, tax planning, and strategic business guidance.

Beyond the Law

While Jesus is serious about the courtroom, he’s equally as passionate about life outside of it. Whether he’s mentoring young entrepreneurs, engaging with his community or spending time with his family, Jesus believes in building meaningful connections and giving back.

When he isn’t working, Jesus enjoys traveling, fitness, and exploring new cultures and cuisines. He’s also passionate about classic cars, motorsports and music, interests that keep him grounded and give clients a glimpse of the approachable person behind the attorney title.

Why It Matters

When prospective clients search for Jesus La Rosa, they should find more than just a name they should find a story. This page is not only a reflection of his professional accomplishments but also of his vision for La Rosa Law: to stand as a long-term partner for clients, protecting what they’ve built and empowering their future growth.

attorneys.name: Esther Uria LaBovick Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
Esther Uria LaBovick, Esq., was born on October 13, 1965, in Orlando, FL. Mrs. LaBovick graduated Duke University in Durham, N.C., in 1987 with a Bachelor of Arts. She graduated from University of Miami School of Law in 1990 with a Juris Doctorate. Mrs. LaBovick was admitted to the Florida and Federal Bar in 1990. Her first job was Assistant State Attorney for the Dade County State Attorney's Office under Janet Reno. At that time, Mrs. LaBovick prosecuted drunk drivers. For over 18 months she was trained as part of the special DUI prosecution unit in Dade County.

Early in her career, Mrs. LaBovick learned every aspect of how a DUI criminal can change the life of an innocent victim. In her three years with the State Attorney's Office she had the invaluable experience of countless jury trials. In 1994, when Janet Reno was appointed United States Attorney General, Mrs. LaBovick decided to leave the State Attorney's Office to practice in the private sector. She began overseeing a national caseload prosecuting insurance fraud with the National Counsel on Compensation Insurance (NCCI). This experience allowed her to see the inside of a large group of defense attorneys working to protect the insurance company.

After the firm of Brian F. LaBovick, PA., moved to Jupiter, FL in Palm Beach County, Mrs. LaBovick joined the firm as a Partner. The firm became known as LaBovick and LaBovick, P.A. and began to specialize in the following areas: personal injury, medical malpractice, nursing home abuse, products liability injuries, and pharmaceutical drug injuries.

Mrs. LaBovick is very active in the community. She is currently a member of FAWL (Florida Association of Women Lawyers) and is on the Board for the Junior League of the Palm Beaches. In 1998-1999 she was the Chairperson for the Palm Beach County Eye and Ear Alert Program. She is also very active in fundraising and chairing committees for the Quantum House and The Benjamin School.

attorneys.name: Nathan Ryan LaBar Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. LaBar has had the opportunity to effect real change in his clients’ lives. He only represents individuals and families whose rights have been infringed upon by employers, insurance companies or governmental agencies. His cases can range from simple to complex, including litigating against local companies on behalf of the working-class single parent, to representing groups of people in multi-plaintiff (collective actions) against large scale powerful corporations. He has had the privilege of representing these clients from the beginning stages of litigation through trial and verdict. His experience includes having tried cases in front of hearing officers, administrators, judges, and of course juries ranging from six to twelve-members. He has represented clients in administrative actions, arbitrations, state courts, and in federal court.

As a member of his community, Mr. LaBar is honored to participate in social service institutions whose goal is also to improve the lives of the members of the community. Recently, he has served as the Co-Chairman of the Orange County Bar Association’s Labor and Employment Committee. In addition, he served on the board of a local non-profit educational institution for children. He also enjoys volunteering at Orange County Public Schools events with his family.
