attorneys.name: Brian LaBovick Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
Brian F. LaBovick was born in Pittsburgh, PA, on October 7, 1964. He was admitted to the Florida Bar; the Federal Bar in 1990; the U.S. District Court Southern District of Florida in 1993 and the U.S. District Court Middle District of Florida in 1993.

Mr. LaBovick obtained a Bachelor of Philosophy degree at Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, in 1987, and a Juris Doctorate at the University of Miami School of Law in Florida in 1990. He began his legal career in the prestigious Honors Graduate Program as the United States Department of Justice as a prosecutor in 1990. At that time he was hired to prosecute criminal aliens throughout Florida.

In 1992, Mr. LaBovick founded Brian F. LaBovick, P.A., a sole practice, initially handling civil, commercial and criminal cases, including securities litigation, bankruptcy, dissolution of marriage, and criminal defense. In 1993 the practice moved from Coral Gables to Jupiter, FL in Palm Beach County. After the firm moved to Jupiter, the firm changed its name to LaBovick and LaBovick, P.A. and began to specialize in the following areas: personal injury, medical malpractice, nursing home abuse, products liability injuries, and pharmaceutical drug injuries.

Over the years, Mr. LaBovick has represented thousands of injured people and workers from all walks of life. He has negotiated claims from the most basic automobile accident to the most detailed cases such as medical malpractice, wrongful death or catastrophic injury cases. Prior experience as a licensed insurance agent has provided Mr. LaBovick insight into how insurance companies handle and settle cases.

In addition to his active trial practice, Mr. LaBovick has managed to serve in leadership positions in many professional organizations. Mr. LaBovick served as president of the North Palm Beach County Bar Association, as well as a director of the Palm Beach County Trial Lawyer's Association. He is currently an Eagle Sponsor of the Florida Academy of Trial Attorneys and the American Trial Lawyers Association. The honor was bestowed upon him to serve as a member of the Florida Bar Family Rules Committee by special appointment.

Over the years, Mr. LaBovick has managed to serve in leadership positions and be actively involved in several local charities including: North Palm Beach County Section of the American Cancer Society (Director), Temple Beth Am in Jupiter, FL. (Treasurer), The Benjamin School of Palm Beach (Board Member) and The Quantum House of Palm Beach.

Mr. LaBovick has an “AV” rating from Martindale- Hubbell. He is a member of the National “ Belli Society”, a charitable organization of trial attorneys that promote the study of law through legal research and lectures. Mr. LaBovick is also a member of ACIA, Academy of Catastrophic Injury Attorneys, an organization of the nation’s leading plaintiff’s personal injury litigators.

Mr. LaFrance currently is a member of the Florida Bar and the Hillsborough County Bar Associations.

attorneys.bio:
Dana Laganella Gerling has been nominated again in 2024 as a Super Lawyer; this is the tenth year she has been on the Florida Super Lawyers Magazine list. Only 2.5 % of lawyers in Florida receive such designation. She has also been voted as Legal Elite for a eleventh year in Florida Trend Magazine. Affordable Attorney, Gerling Law Group has won People’s Choice Award from the Bradenton Herald for Favorite Attorney for ten years. Dana is a dedicated community leader who primarily practices in areas of law that include: Estate Planning, Probate, Trust Administration and Elder Law.

Dana is originally from a suburb of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. She attended law school at Quinnipiac University School of Law in Hamden, Connecticut and graduated Cum Laude. She was awarded the Best Advocate of the Northeast Region and was voted Best Attorney in East Manatee County by Living Out East Magazine. It is Dana’s commitment to providing quality, affordable legal services that has won her respect and acclaim from both her peers and her clients. She truly enjoys her work. Her passion for helping people in her community is evident in her dedication to providing education on important topics, including Wills, Trusts, Durable Power of Attorney’s and Health Care Surrogates. Further, as a founding partner of Affordable Attorney, Gerling Law Group Chartered, Dana’s commitment to protecting the interests of her clients has become the focus of this client centered firm.

She is currently President of the Manatee County Florida Association of Women Lawyers and has also served on the Board of Directors with the Sarasota County Florida Association of Women Lawyers. Dana is a member of both the Manatee County and Sarasota County Bar Associations. She formerly served on the Board of the Sarasota County Humane Society, Manatee County Animal Control Advisory Board, and the advisory Board of the Pinellas Animal Foundation.

She earned her undergraduate degree in Business Finance from Bloomsburg University in Pennsylvania, graduating with honors. Dana is a mother of two girls as well as being an animal lover, providing a loving home for two dogs and two bunnies of her own. She is a strong supporter of all animal related organizations in the community.

She serves the following areas: Bradenton, Manatee County, East Manatee County, Palmetto, Ellenton, Parrish, Sarasota, Sarasota County, Florida.

attorneys.name: Roger W. LaJoie
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Roger graduated from the University of Notre Dame, B.A., 1974, M.B.A., 1976, and Nova University School of Law, J.D., 1979. He was admitted to The Florida Bar and the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida in 1979.

He became a partner in the law firm of Sullivan, Stone, Sullivan, LaJoie & Thacker shortly after moving to Vero Beach in 1981. He was Of Counsel with Robin A. Lloyd, Sr. & Associates, P.A., remaining as such until 2009 when he established the law firm of Roger W. LaJoie, P.A.

Roger's practice now primarily focuses on matters relating to business, corporate, real estate, and probate law, including estate planning as well as assisting in the administration of probate estates. He is an attorney title agent for First American Title Insurance Company.

A current member and past President of the Indian River County Bar Association, he is a past Chairman of The Florida Bar Grievance Committee, 19th Circuit. Having a deep commitment to serving the legal needs of the community, he was Pro Bono Attorney of the Year 2000 for the 19th Judicial Circuit.

A Fourth Degree Knight of Columbus, he is a Past Grand Knight of the Holy Cross Council Knights of Columbus. Active in his church, Roger serves as a Eucharistic Minister and Lector at Holy Cross Catholic Church. He has served on the Board of Directors, and is a past President of, Sun-Up of Indian River, Inc., and is a past Board member of Indian River County Habitat for Humanity. He still enjoys volunteering with Habitat for Humanity by swinging a hammer on many Saturday mornings.

Married to Patricia, he has 3 sons, Christopher, Travis and Byron, two stepdaughters, Allison and Whitney, and two grandchildren, Anya and Laurel.

attorneys.name: Sheila M Lake
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in St Petersburg, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sheila first gained legal experience as a Legal Advocate in Vancouver, Washington where she helped victims of domestic violence find legal help. She then moved her then family of seven (now nine!) all the way down to St. Petersburg, Florida. Sheila went on to become the Firm Administrator of a firm in downtown St. Petersburg within her first year. Over the course of the next 15 years, she adopted her two young nephews, earned a Bachelors in American Studies with a concentration in Political Science from Eckerd College, and earned her Juris Doctorate with a concentration in Constitutional Law at WMU Cooley Law School, where she finished 9th in her class and was unanimously selected to be the Valedictory Speaker. She went on to become an associate attorney at a firm in Largo, before heading out on her own and opening Lake Law Firm, P.A. in July 2019 to build her dreams and continue advocating for equality and justice for all.

Sheila is also a pillar of the community, currently serving as a board member and a mentor for I Support Youth, a program helping young children succeed in the professional world. She served as the Vice President of the WMU Straight and Gay Alliance in 2017, and the Director of Professional Public Relations for the WMU Cooley chapter of Help Save the Next Girl, a program dedicated to fighting human trafficking. During her time at WMU Cooley Law School, Sheila was the Managing Editor of the WMU Cooley Journal of Practical and Clinical Law and a Senior Associate Editor of WMU Cooley Law Review. Sheila has remained actively involved in her Alma Mater, WMU Cooley Law School, currently serving as the Committee Chair of the Alumni Outreach Program with the WMU Cooley Law School Alumni Association, Founder of the Alumni Mentoring Program for bar takers and new attorneys, and adjunct professor of law, currently teaching Law Firm Management.

While being a full-time attorney, employer, business owner, law school professor and community servant, Sheila is also a full time Matriarch, with five sons, two daughters, and seven grandchildren! On what little downtime she has, Sheila enjoys the beach, the sunshine, and all the chocolate in the world.

attorneys.name: Christina LaMaida
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Dade City, FL
attorneys.bio:
Christina LaMaida attended Lock Haven University in Pennsylvania for her undergraduate degree in Political Science. After receiving many of the top grades in the department, she was asked to tutor for one of the Department Chairs, which she did for two years. In addition to her studies, she worked three different jobs, held a scholarship, and participated in a national sorority. After completing Lock Haven, she moved to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where she started in sales and was able to perfect her negotiation tactics that became useful in today’s practice. Christina started her legal career in 2005, working as a legal assistant in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, ultimately working her way up to managing partner of this firm.

Christina graduated from Barry University Law School where she was a night student and worked a full- time job during the day at a law office. Not only was she successful in maintaining her job and receiving accolades in school, she was invited to the George C. Young Inns of Court as a law student, received a focus in Children and Families Concentration Program, and completed an internship with the Juvenile Delinquency Law Clinic. During that time, Christina also volunteered for several different organizations including Guardian Ad Litem and GoodWill’s youth mentorship program. Due to the opportunities that were available to her in undergraduate and in law school, she was able to obtain skills and knowledge that exceeds all expectations.

Christina became an attorney because from an early age she was taught to “be a voice, not an echo.” She believes that phrase has resonated with her and helped encourage her to become the attorney she is today. She quickly realized that not everyone could stand up and speak for themselves, let alone be heard at times where it really matters. This gave Christina a new purpose and goal to not let voices go unheard. From that point forward, Christina made a promise that she would put all efforts into those that needed her – her client’s would always be heard.

Christina chose to become a criminal attorney because she felt she could make the most impact in the criminal field. She started with the Public Defender’s Office, here in Dade City, where she learned what it was truly like to defend those during their worst moments and let them know that someone will always be on their side. Working at the Public Defender’s Office taught her how to defend her clients with a passion and she gained invaluable experience that other’s don’t have. During her tenure at the Public Defender’s Office, she had two orders published in Florida Law Weekly, won Pasco County Attorney of the Year for the Public Defender’s Office, and received an Award from the Criminal Section of the Florida Bar Association at the State Attorney/Public Defender yearly conference.

Christina’s current focus is Criminal Defense – State Level, State Appeals and Post Conviction Motions. Christina is currently has bar admission to the State of Florida, U.S. Court of Appeals, 11 th Circuit, U.S. District Court – Middle District of Florida, and U.S. District Court – Southern District of Florida. She is currently a licensed notary and has recently been selected as “Rising Star – SuperLawyers 2023”.

Ben handles each case with honesty, diligence, and a personal investment in helping his clients move forward. His goal isn’t just to resolve cases—it’s to restore peace of mind and hope in the people he represents.

Her advocacy included protecting the rights of the elderly in Guardianship and Adult Protective Services cases. Ms. Lancaster is also proud of her work protecting the rights of parents in Dependency cases.

attorneys.name: Meranda Landes
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Hello, I'm Meranda Landes. Thank you for taking the time to read my biography. I'm a second generation native Floridian, born and raised in Tampa. I attended the University of South Florida where I obtained my Bachelors of Science degree in Health Science, becoming the first in my family to graduate from college. Before joining Morgan & Morgan, I worked for one of the largest personal injury firms in Central Florida. I knew that in order to best help injured victims, I needed to become an attorney. I attended law school at FAMU College of Law right here in Downtown Orlando while working full-time, graduating early. I started my career in personal injury, working at one of the largest auto insurance companies in the nation. I saw firsthand what big insurance companies do to try and devalue the cases of injured, innocent people.

Outside of work I have always loved giving back to the community and helping others. I had the privilege of being a member of Junior League of Lakeland and Orlando. I also served on the board of the directors for Pace Center for Girls, Orange for four years, co-chairing their Believing in Girls Breakfast in 2022, raising over $85,000 for at-risk girls in Central Florida. I served as an Advisory Committee Member for Central Florida Urban League as part of their Community Policing Forum sponsored by the Office of the Attorney General. In 2021 I completed the Central Florida Political Leadership Institute (PLI) sponsored by Orlando Economic Partnership.

I use my years of experience in personal injury litigation and of the auto insurance companies to fight to get you the compensation you deserve. I will always treat you like family and take the time to explain the legal process to you. Together we can take a unfortunate situation and make it better. Thank you for choosing Morgan & Morgan and I look forward to working with you.

attorneys.practice_type: Community Associations Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
"I enjoy obtaining successful outcomes for my clients but what I enjoy most is educating them. "

Samuel Landol concentrates his practice in the areas of community association representation. After receiving his undergraduate degree from the University of Central Florida, Sam obtained his law degree from Suffolk University Law School in Boston, Massachusetts. In an effort to sharpen his understanding of business, Sam obtained a Master’s Degree in Business and Entrepreneurship from the University of Florida in 2011 and is a member of Beta Gamma Sigma, an international honor society for business school graduates.

Mr. Landol was admitted to the Florida Bar and the Federal District Court for the Southern District of Florida in 2003. He began his legal career representing individual bankruptcy debtors filing Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcies in Miami, Ft Lauderdale, and Palm Beach. Since 2005, Sam has been representing Condominium and Homeowner Associations throughout the state of Florida and assists them with collections, foreclosures, contract review, drafting and amending governing documents, covenant enforcement, drafting legal opinions and assisting his association clients with the daily operation and administration of their communities. Sam speaks English, Spanish and limited Portuguese.

attorneys.bio:
Nanci Landy is a seasoned attorney, Arbitrator, and Florida Supreme Court Certified Circuit Court Mediator with more than 37 years of experience in complex litigation and dispute resolution. Throughout her legal career, she has represented clients in commercial litigation, insurance defense, and securities matters, developing a reputation for thoughtful analysis and strategic problem solving in high-stakes disputes.

In addition to her litigation background, Ms. Landy has served as a FINRA arbitrator for more than 15 years, presiding over securities industry disputes and gaining extensive experience evaluating complex financial and regulatory issues. Her work in arbitration has further strengthened her ability to assess cases objectively and guide parties toward fair and practical outcomes.

Ms. Landy also brings substantial business leadership experience to her mediation practice. As the head of a multimillion-dollar company, she gained firsthand insight into the operational, financial, and strategic challenges faced by business leaders. This combination of legal, arbitration, and executive experience enables her to approach mediation with both legal depth and real-world business perspective.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Ormond Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Cynthia Lane handles marital and family law cases for Mara Law, P.A. Ms. Lane is experienced with highly contested cases involving extensive litigation, as well as facilitating alternative dispute resolution and the drafting of detailed uncontested matters. Ms. Lane has experience in a variety of family law actions including dissolution of marriage, child custody disputes, adoptions, marital agreements, paternity cases, domestic violence injunctions, foster care and DCF cases and post-judgment modifications. Ms. Lane is also appointed as a Guardian ad Litem in high conflict litigation cases to assist parties and the Court while advancing the best interest of children.

Ms. Lane graduated from the University of Florida in Gainesville, FL where she received a B.A. in Political Science and St. Thomas University School of Law in Miami, FL where she received her J.D., cum laude. While attending law school, Ms. Lane served as an intern for the Office of the Attorney General for the 17th Judicial Circuit and began working with the Florida Statewide Guardian ad Litem Program. Ms. Lane was an editor on law review and employed as a research assistant for law professors focusing on administrative law and constitutional issues. Upon admittance to the Florida Bar, Ms. Lane served as counsel for Children’s Legal Services, representing the State of Florida in juvenile dependency and termination of parental rights cases.

attorneys.name: Andrew Lannon
attorneys.firm_name: Lannon Land Litigation Local Law, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Business/Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Oviedo, FL
attorneys.bio:
My great grandfather, Eugene Malone, started a law firm in Central Illinois which my father, Richard James "Jim" Lannon, Jr., managed prior to being appointed Judge on the 13th Judicial Circuit, in and for LaSalle County, Illinois. My Aunt, M. Catherine Lannon, was the head of the Administrative Law Division of the Florida Attorney General's Office for 33 years after clerking at the 1st DCA. My cousin, Laura C. Lannon, served as a prosecutor for Cook County, Illinois (i.e., the Chicago metropolitan area) prior to her untimely and unfortunate death. You could say that being an attorney is in my blood.

Born in LaSalle, Illinois in 1974, my family moved to Dedham, Massachusetts when my parents divorced in 1984. I attended school in Massachusetts from 4th grade to my senior year of college, having graduated from The College of the Holy Cross in Worcester in 1996. For the next 4 years, I worked as a sales representative for BellSouth Advertising & Publishing Corporation in Tucker, Georgia, a suburb of Atlanta. Being a sales representative prepared me for being an attorney, for it is far more difficult to sell a product or service to an unwilling buyer than it is to demonstrate to a jury or a judge why your client's position in the lawsuit is meritorious, or why your client deserves to win, and why your client deserves to be compensated (i.e., paid damages).

I attended law school at The Catholic University of America, Columbus School of Law in Washington, D.C. from 2000 to 2003. During this time, I was invited onto the Journal of Contemporary Health Law & Policy (this journal is reserved for students in the top 10% of their class) and (2) Moot Court. My Comment, "Let Him Die with Dignity or Hope for a Cure, the Consequences of Modern Medicine", was printed in the Winter 2002 edition. I have also held the prestigious honor of serving as the Note and Comment Editor for the Journal.

After graduation from law school, I clerked for The Honorable Peggy A. Quince at the Florida Supreme Court for 2 years. I then worked at the 8th largest law firm in the world at the time in its Central Florida Litigation Practice Group handling commercial litigation and appeals. I left that Am Law 100 firm to work at an intellectual property litigation boutique before serving as the Deputy City Attorney in Palm Bay, Florida for 2.5 years. When the City Attorney was terminated, I was promoted to City Attorney, a position that I held for 7 years. In 2018, I joined the 10th largest law firm in Orlando and worked in its Commercial Practice Group before starting my own firm.

attorneys.name: Raquel Y. Lao
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Lao was born in Chicago, Illinois. She is of Chinese-Filipino descent. In 1996, Ms. Lao relocated to the outskirts of Tampa, Florida where she helped run a family-owned cattle and goat ranch.

In 2004, Ms. Lao graduated from Florida State University receiving her Bachelor's Degree in both Finance and Real Estate. Ms. Lao continued her education at Saint Thomas University School of Law, receiving her Juris Doctorate in 2007. Ms. Lao was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2008. Ms. Lao was also admitted to the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida and to the U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida in 2009 and 2010, respectively.

Ms. Lao joined the law firm of Friedman, Rodman & Frank, P.A. as an associate specializing in the area of personal injury law. Ms. Lao has worked diligently in assisting clients to obtain the best result possible. Ms. Lao has represented clients in cases involving rotator cuff tears, ACL tears, and hip fractures as a result of slip and falls at popular supermarkets; loss of vision in one eye as a result of the negligent supervision of minors; permanent scarring from dog bites; severe injuries due to construction accidents; wrongful death claims; battery claims; and bad faith claims handling by insurance companies.

Notably, Ms. Lao has helped a mother, daughter and son obtain a $1.1 million dollar settlement in a claim against a local university for its inadequate security. The loving family had been brutally attacked by a mob on the university's campus which ended in the son surviving a bullet that had entered millimeters away from his heart.

Mr. Lark currently works as a mediator in residential foreclosures, divorce, paternity, general civil and appellate matters. Additionally, he is a member of the Executive Committee of the St. Petersburg Bar Association, the Executive Director of the Barney Masterson Inn of Court, a hearing officer for the St. Petersburg Housing Authority, a board member for the Community Law Program, and a board member of Bayfront Medical Center's Institutional Review Board. During 2010-2011, he helped organize and present three mortgage foreclosure forums to assist homeowners through the mortgage foreclosure crisis. He actively participates with Nokumbaya, a medical mission group, that travels to international locations to provide medical care. Prior to becoming a lawyer, Mr. Lark worked as a Paramedic/EMT, Registered Nurse and National Ski Patroller. He spent his childhood in Vermont and his adult life here in Tampa Bay.

attorneys.name: Christopher Larmoyeux
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Chris Larmoyeux, Of Counsel at BillBone Law Group

Attorney Chris Larmoyeux serves as Of Counsel at BillBone Law Group. He is also a partner with the personal injury law firm of Larmoyeux & Bone, P.L.

Prior to forming Larmoyeux & Bone, Mr. Larmoyeux was a partner with the firm of Montgomery & Larmoyeux. Before that, he was a partner with Montgomery, Searcy & Denney from 1985 to 1989, and with Montgomery, Lytal, Reiter, Denney & Searcy, P.A., in West Palm Beach, Florida, from 1983 to 1985, where he began his legal career in 1979.

Mr. Larmoyeux graduated magna cum laude from the University of Florida (B.A., 1976) and earned his Juris Doctorate from the University of Notre Dame in 1979. While a law student, he studied at Notre Dame London Center of Law and at the University of London, Kings College (1978–1979).

He is admitted to the Florida and Colorado State Bars, the U.S. District Court, Southern District, and the U.S. Court of Appeals, Fifth and Eleventh Circuits. He is Board Certified as a specialist in Civil Trial Practice: Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice, and Wrongful Death. Mr. Larmoyeux is also a member of the Palm Beach County Bar Association, the American Bar Association, The Florida Justice Association, and The American Association for Justice.

His professional recognition includes listings in Best Lawyers in America (Medical Malpractice, Personal Injury & Wrongful Death – Woodward & White), being named among Florida’s “Legal Elite” by Florida Trend Magazine, and being recognized as one of Florida’s “Super Lawyers.” Additionally, Martindale-Hubbell has consistently awarded him its highest rating in Legal Ability and General Ethical Standards.

Mr. Larmoyeux is a frequent lecturer on personal injury cases and has achieved more than sixty-five verdicts and settlements in excess of $1,000,000. Beyond his legal work, he is deeply committed to his community, having served as Chairman of the Palm Beach County Cultural Council and as a member of the Florida Arts Council (appointed by the Florida Secretary of State). He has also served on the boards of numerous charities.

attorneys.bio:
Louis N. Larsen was born in Frankfurt, West Germany and moved to Pennsylvania as a child where he attended public and private high schools. He earned a B.A. in psychology from Rollins College in Winter Park, FL and then his J.D. from the University of Miami School of Law in 1991.

While in law school, Mr. Larsen completed internships at the Dade County Public Defender’s Office in Miami and was on the mock trial team. In addition to course concentration in litigation subjects, he completed a variety of courses in all sections of the legal curriculum to ensure a broad-based legal education.

After graduation, Mr. Larsen began his career representing those who were wrongfully injured through no fault of their own. Twenty-seven years later, Lou Larsen has joined the Schiller Kessler Group as a litigation attorney. He brings extensive experience in all types of personal injury and wrongful death cases in courts throughout Florida.

For the past 14 years, Mr. Larsen has maintained the distinction of board certification which requires extensive documented trial experience, professionalism and ethics.

Lou Larsen is admitted to practice law in six states (FL, NY, DC, PA, IL, MD), and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

attorneys.name: Armando T. Lauritano
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
As the eldest son of a so-called "old school" general surgeon, Armando Lauritano has witnessed firsthand the unfortunate changes in our medical system. The days of house calls, weekend post surgical follow up, and personalized patient service have long since passed as medicine has transformed itself into a managed care corporate megastructure.

Our current medical system has supplanted the time honored mottos of " Patients First" and the Hippocratic Oath with an overriding importance on the financial bottom line. The tragic consequences of this Healthcare evolution have been borne out by the citizens of our country. While admittedly medicine is not an exact science and some undesirable outcomes are unavoidable, those familial tragedies occasioned by neglect, inexperience, and incompetence are not, and the wrong must be rectified.

Our legislature, buttressed by the financial lobbying efforts of the Medical and Insurance Industries has made it increasingly difficult for all victims of our profit driven Healthcare system. Experience and commitment count in avoiding the traps and potential pitfalls of our Medical Malpractice system.

As a practicing attorney Mr Lauritano has devoted the past 14 years solely to the specialty of Medical Malpractice. He is admitted to practice in both New York and Florida and have been lead counsel in numerous medical malpractice trials across this state.

Mr Lauritano is proud to represent and successfully redress the interests of those that have been injured.

attorneys.name: Richard Lavery
attorneys.practice_type: Dog Bite & Animal Attacks Lawyers in Titusville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Richard A. Lavery is an attorney in Morgan & Morgan, P.A.'s Melbourne, Florida office. Born and raised in Pittsburgh, PA, he completed his undergraduate degree with a Bachelor of Arts graduating summa cum laude from the University of Pittsburgh. Following his graduation from college Richard moved to Florida where he attended Florida State University College of Law.

Since graduating law school Richard's primary focus has been in the Personal Injury field as he has a passion for being the voice of those in need. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan he worked for two notable Personal Injury law firms. He has worked on cases in both the pre-litigation and litigation departments handling multiple types of claims including, but not limited to: motor vehicle accidents, dog bites, and slip and fall claims. Additionally, Richard has worked in the Administrative Law arena assisting in litigating Workers' Compensation and Social Security Disability claims from inception through Final Hearing. His vast experience in the Personal Injury field has allowed him to develop a deep understanding of different injuries and illnesses that one can suffer, and the impacts those injuries have on a person's quality of life. Richard understands that Personal Injury claims require zealous advocacy and skill both in and out of the courtroom to obtain favorable results for his clients.

In addition to the experience notated above, while employed at Michles & Booth, P.A, in Pensacola, Florida Richard assisted in litigating a high-profile class action lawsuit, which settled for over 17 million dollars. The class action lawsuit revolved around an explosion at the Escambia County jail.

In January 2021, Richard joined the civil trial litigation team where he continues to protect the legal rights of injured victims. In his spare time Richard enjoys rooting for his Pittsburgh sport teams (Pirates, Steelers, and Penguins) and running.

When faced with an injury, you need the type of experience that can manage all aspects of your legal claim and put your mind at ease. For over 90 years, the Bar Register has been a unique guide to the legal community's most eminent professionals. attorneys.name: Paul Lazaro
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Paul Lazaro is a litigation attorney with Morgan and Morgan. Paul handles all facets of personal injury litigation including depositions, court appearances, and trial.

Prior to joining Morgan and Morgan, Paul commenced his personal injury practice at a closely held law firm in West Tampa. In his time with the firm, Paul handled all facets of litigation including court appearances, depositions, and trial. Most importantly, Paul learned the importance of quality customer service, and further developed his professionalism.

In 2015, Paul was admitted to practice law in the state of Florida. The day after he was sworn as an attorney, Paul was hired by the Law Office of Julianne M. Holt, Public Defender for the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit. As an Assistant Public Defender Paul proudly served Hillsborough County's indigent community, completing multiple jury trials and ninety-six bench trials to verdict.

Paul earned his law degree from the University of Illinois College of Law in Champaign, Illinois. While at Illinois, Paul was President and Events Coordinator for the Federalist Society, Scholarship Chair for the Latina/o Law Students Association, and represented indigent litigants in federal court as a member of the University of Illinois Federal Civil Rights Clinic.

In 2011, Paul graduated from Saint Peter's University, Summa Cum Laude. While at Saint Peter's, Paul was a member of their Division I track and field team receiving All-Academic Conference Honors and was the Opinions Editor for the College newspaper. As a senior Paul was awarded the Pauw Wow Journalism Award and was appointed to the Jesuit Honor Society, Alpha Sigma Nu.

A native of Tampa, Florida, Paul attended Jesuit High School, where he served as vice-president of the school pep band and captained the wrestling team, placing in the state wrestling tournament as a senior.

In his free time, Paul enjoys spending time with his family, golfing, attending theme parks with friends, and researching criminal justice issues.

attorneys.name: G. William Lazenby IV
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Will Lazenby was born in Clearwater, FL, in 1973. He graduated from Admiral Farragut Academy in St. Petersburg, FL, in 1991. During his senior year at Admiral Farragut Will was Battalion Commander, the highest ranking cadet at the school.

Will followed in his father's footsteps and attended undergraduate school at Davidson College in Davidson, NC. He graduated with a B.A. in English Literature in 1995. After spending a semester in Florence, Italy, on a program run by Florida State University, Will started law school at Stetson University College of Law. He graduated from Stetson with honors in 1998. While at Stetson Will was a member of the school's nationally ranked mock trial team and also served as a trial advocacy teaching assistant for two semesters. Will competed in numerous mock trial and moot court competitions during his time at Stetson.

After law school Will spent the first 14 years of his career defending healthcare providers in malpractice lawsuits. At his last defense firm, where he worked for 11 years, Will became a partner in the Tampa office. After leaving that large insurance defense firm Will started working at a small, four attorney firm where he represented victims of medical malpractice. During the seven years Will worked there he settled multiple medical practice cases, several in excess of one million dollars and one case in excess of ten million dollars.

Will joined Morgan & Morgan in order to continue the passionate work of representing victims of medical negligence and their families. He is a dedicated, aggressive, compassionate attorney who strives to achieve the best possible results for his clients, whether that occurs through negotiations with defense counsel, or winning the case at trial.

Will's family is still in Clearwater and he has lived in Tampa since 2000. It's his honor and pleasure to serve clients in the Tampa Bay Area who have suffered at the hands of negligent healthcare providers. Will is a member of the Tampa Bay Trial Lawyers Association and the Florida Justice Association.

attorneys.name: Michael D. Leader
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael D. Leader started his career as an attorney in the Courtroom as an Assistant State Attorney in Broward County, Florida where he was responsible for thousands of files including TRAFFIC CRIMINAL OFFENSES, DUI's, MISDEMEANORS and FELONY charges. He supervised and trained other lawyers and often provided instruction to police officers on various legal issues. While working in the Felony Trial Unit, he was recruited from the State Attorney's Office by the law firm of Essen & Essen, et al where he successfully defended most of the firm's clients in Dade and Monroe Counties.

He has prosecuted and defended thousands of DUI and other criminal matters, has been involved in well over one hundred jury trials and has personally tried over sixty to verdict. Mr. Leader believes in aggressively attacking the government's case against his clients. Although he is a skilled trial attorney, he works to have his client's cases thrown out of court before trial, whenever possible, in order to avoid subjecting his client's to the risks and costs associated with the trial process. He successfully utilizes his background and experience to identify and attack various issues such as destruction of evidence, police error and/or misconduct, unlawful search, seizures and stops, invalid or unreliable breath, blood or urine samples and various other reasons they may apply in a given case. In addition to his success in the courtroom, Mr. Leader has obtained great results in the administrative arena effectively having many of his client's driver license(s) promptly returned to them by having their suspensions invalidated. He has lectured and participated in numerous DUI seminars over his career.

Mr. Leader has dedicated himself to the art of winning in the detailed and technical arena of DUI defense but his experience is in no way limited to the area of DUI. He routinely handles most criminal charges including serious felonies. Mr. Leader handles non-jury trials, evidentiary hearings, violations of probation, administrative hearings and represents individuals during criminal investigations before an arrest has been made or charges have been filed in an effort to avoid an arrest/charge all together. Mr. Leader is regularly in Court in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach County but is also available to represent clients in and out of the Florida in State and Federal Court.

Also notable, Mr. Leader was recognized in 2006 and 2007 as a "Up & Coming Legal Elite" by Florida Trend magazine. The list only includes the top up and coming lawyers who have earned the trust and confidence of other lawyers, those who know their work the best.

attorneys.name: Albert H. Lechner
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in St Augustine, FL
attorneys.bio:
Since the third grade, Albert knew he wanted to be a trial attorney. The son of German-Austrian immigrants, he was taught early the value of hard honest work and brings the highest standards to every case, no matter how big or small.

With over 90 trials under his belt, Albert is a highly experienced courtroom litigator. He has obtained numerous jury verdicts in excess of $1 million, with most verdicts substantially exceeding the defendant's final settlement offer.

He is regularly sought out by other attorneys to serve as co-counsel in trials throughout the Southeast and teaches trial techniques to other lawyers in continuing education programs. Albert is a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer, the highest ranking given by the Florida Bar and a designation bestowed on less than 6% of all active lawyers. He also holds an AV rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest rating available by this national attorney peer review rating service signifying recognition by his peers for the highest ethical standards and legal ability.

He believes trials are the purest form of democracy where citizens who have never met come together for a common purpose, requiring the ultimate in integrity to prevail and provide justice.

A Maryland native, Albert graduated from the University of Maryland and cum laude from University of Baltimore Law School, where he served as editor of the School's Law Review, an honor reserved for the top 10% of the class. After law school, he completed a judicial clerkship for four circuit court trial judges and became a partner at a prestigious plaintiff's personal injury law firm in Maryland before relocating to Jacksonville Beach in 2007.

Outside the courtroom, Albert enjoys golf, fishing, wing shooting and surfing, activities he often shares with his two children. Please contact Albert directly at (904) 417-4158 or lechner@forthepeople.com.

attorneys.name: Mark A. Lee
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Suffering an injury can leave people with serious concerns about their future. Mark A. Lee advocates on behalf of the injured and disabled in the Tampa Bay area – ranging from as far North as Citrus County – South to Sarasota County. He began his legal career working as a paralegal assisting on injury cases from 2004 through 2011. During that time, he earned his Bachelor’s Degree in Public Health from the University of South Florida. He attended the University of Tulsa College of Law where he earned a Juris Doctor and a Health Law Certificate, by focusing his education on areas germane to Health Care. He has been practicing since 2014 and has earned a reputation for aggressive, yet compassionate and thorough representation. He has earned the following distinctions:

Named a Super Lawyers Rising Star 2016 – 2024

Million Dollar Advocates Forum®, Member, The Top Trial Lawyers in America®

Avvo “Excellent” rating

Florida Trend’s Legal Elite 2021

Mr. Lee takes the time to understand a client’s circumstances before creating a customized strategy to secure benefits, dispute a denial or appear in a hearing. Additionally, he is available to clients to answer their questions and provide advice when they need it the most.

One of the reasons Mr. Lee is able to provide exceptional service is because of his commitment to his practice. A resourceful attorney, he benefits from his memberships with groups such as The Florida Workers Advocates, Florida Bar’s Workers’ Compensation Section, and the National Organization of Social Security Claimant Representatives (NOSSCR). He has served as an at-large board member for the Florida Workers’ Advocates since 2015. He is active in the local Tampa Bay Workers’ Compensation Inns of Court.

Mr. Lee is also dedicated to volunteering his time to serve the community. In the past, he has volunteered with Iron Gate of Tulsa, Volunteers of America, Metropolitan Ministries, and Big Brothers Big Sisters of Tampa Bay. He is currently a regular volunteer judge with the Hillsborough County Teen Court program.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Patricia M. Lee is a Senior Attorney with Urban Thier & Federer, P.A. She is based out of the Orlando office.

Ms. Lee's practice focuses primarily on family and estate law with concentration on child custody disputes, child support assessment and enforcement, alimony, equitable distribution, fee awards, relocation, as well as post-judgment modification and enforcement proceedings, including at the appellate court level. Patricia Lee has over 25 years of experience.

Furthermore, Ms. Lee is a referral attorney and mentor for the U.S. Department of State, Office of Children's Issues, the United States implementing agency for the Hague Convention, and is experienced in the international aspects of child abduction, the federal Parental Kidnapping Prevention Act, the Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act, international and national relocation issues, the impact of immigration laws upon dissolution of marriage, the domestication, modification and enforcement of foreign custody and support orders, and other bi-national divorce issues.

Ms. Lee is a member of the Florida Bar. She proficient in Spanish and German, which she uses regularly when representing clients.

attorneys.name: Corey Leifer Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Corey Leifer was born in Queens, New York and grew up on Long Island. He attended college at the University of South Florida ("USF") in Tampa, Florida, where he received a degree in Criminal Justice. Mr. Leifer was a member of the Dean's List at USF and was the recipient of the prestigious Honors Convocation Award during his senior year. He earned his law degree at Western Michigan University Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan.

Mr. Leifer began his legal career as a Prosecutor at the Broward County State Attorney's Office, where he served as lead counsel in over 50 trials. As a Prosecutor, Mr. Leifer prosecuted thousands of cases including DUI's, Battery, Theft and numerous Drug related offenses. After leaving the State Attorney's Office, Mr. Leifer returned to New York and accepted a position as an executive with the National Basketball Association at NBA Entertainment in Secaucus, New Jersey. In 2002, Mr. Leifer moved back to Florida and established the Leifer Law Firm, which concentrates solely on Personal Injury matters such as auto accidents, wrongful death cases and premises liability. Mr. Leifer is also is involved with nationwide Mass Tort Litigation involving those injured by bad drugs and defective medical devices. Mr. Leifer has successfully recovered millions of dollars for accident victims throughout the state of Florida.

Mr. Leifer was awarded the AV Preeminent Rating by Martindale-Hubbell. The AV Rating is the highest possible peer review rating for both legal ability and ethical standards.

Mr. Leifer works on all cases personally and often meets clients on evenings and weekends to accommodate their schedule. He is an active member of the community in South Florida and is a proud supporter of numerous local charities, particularly those that benefit children. Mr. Leifer lives in Delray Beach with his wife and two children.

attorneys.bio:
John Elliott Leighton is a board certified civil trial lawyer who specializes in medical malpractice, nursing home, product liability, sexual abuse and inadequate premises security litigation.

A nationally recognized advocate for crime victims, Mr. Leighton has been a leader in the field of inadequate premises security litigation and is the author of two volume treatise Litigating Premises Security Cases, published by Thomson-West (2006). It is the most comprehensive treatise on investigating, preparing and trying inadequate security cases and representing crime victims. He is the President-elect of the National Crime Victim Bar Association.

His trial in Jeffery v. Publix Super Markets, a landmark inadequate security case, was the subject of an entire chapter in the treatise Persuasive Jury Communication: Case Studies from Successful Trials, Chapter 10 (Shepard's/McGraw-Hill, 1995). In addition to lecturing nationally on security and violent crime issues, Mr. Leighton has led training programs for crime victim advocates.

His verdicts and settlements for injured clients include $49 million for a sexual assault client, $24 million for a medical malpractice case and $24 million for an ATM shooting death.

Other published works by Mr. Leighton include chapters in Matthew Bender's Product Liability Practice Guide and Wiley Publishers' Litigating Spinal Cord Injuries books. His article on defective child car seats, entitled "Are Children Caught in the Seat of Disaster? Child Restraint Systems and Product Liability Cases" was published in the March 1998 issue of Trial magazine. This was followed by "Fighting New Defenses in Inadequate Security Cases," published in Trial (April 2000) and several others.

Mr. Leighton has also published "The Recall Process: Removing Defective Juvenile Products from the Market" in the Product Liability Law Reporter (May 1991) and "Market Share Liability: The Need for a Uniform Market Share Liability Act" in Trial (November 1985). He is a frequent lecturer at trial lawyers programs and has spoken and taught at seminars, colleges and conventions in over 15 states.

After serving as Chairman of the Association of Trial Lawyers of America's (ATLA) Motor Vehicle Collision, Highway and Premises Liability Section, Mr. Leighton has gone on to chair ATLA's (now the American Association of Justice) Inadequate Security Litigation Group. He is a charter member of the National Crime Victim Bar Association and is the recipient of their Advocate of Justice award. He is a member of the Board of Trustees of the National College of Advocacy. He is listed in Who's Who in America and Who's Who in American Law, and holds an AV rating by Martindale-Hubbell.

Mr. Leighton has been voted as one of the Top Lawyers in South Florida in the South Florida Legal Guide for the last five years, which is a peer selected listing of the leading 250 attorneys out of 23,000 practitioners, has been named a Florida SuperLawyer (and voted as one of the top 100 of all the state SuperLawyers), and has been elected to the Florida Trend Legal Elite Top Lawyers in Florida by peer selection. He has also been chosen as "Orlando Legal Elite" by Orlando Style magazine. He received his undergraduate and law degrees with honors from the University of Florida, where he was an editor of the Florida Law Review, competed on the Trial Team, and taught first year jurisprudence.

Mr. Leighton is the Chairman of the Academy of Trial Advocacy, a national invitation-only association of leading catastrophic injury attorneys. Mr. Leighton has been selected for inclusion in The Best Lawyers in America, Florida SuperLawyers, Top Lawyers in South Florida, Orlando Legal Elite, and Florida Trend magazine’s “Florida Legal Elite.”

attorneys.name: John Leombruno Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, Mr. Leombruno attended Penn State University, earning a Bachelor of Arts Degree in History. He continued his education at the Florida Coastal School of Law in Jacksonville, Florida. While in law school, Mr. Leombruno served as the treasurer of Phi Delta Phi legal honors society, served on both the Mock Trial and Moot Court Honor Boards, where he competed in several competitions. He finished in the top 25% of his class, earned the Legal Pro Bono award, and was elected by his peers to be the commencement speaker at graduation. Mr. Leombruno still remains active with the Florida Coastal School of Law, coaching young law students in mock trial competitions, and guest lecturing on trial practice.

Mr. Leombruno was also given the honor of being selected as a legal extern for Justice Kenneth B. Bell of the Florida Supreme Court. Following his externship, he worked as a clerk for the law firm of Pajcic & Pajcic. Mr. Leombruno later accepted a position as an Assistant Public Defender for the Fourth Judicial Circuit, Florida. For two and a half years he served the people of Jacksonville by providing legal services for indigent clients. As a Public Defender, Mr. Leombruno handled thousands of cases ranging from municipal ordinance violations to life felonies. Mr. Leombruno had 17 first chair trials while a public defender.

Since joining the Arnold Law Firm, Mr. Leombruno has represented clients in the fields of Criminal Defense, Family Law, and Civil Litigation. He is admitted to practice in the State of Florida and in the Middle District of Florida. In February of 2014, Mr. Leombruno earned from the Florida Supreme Court the distinguished certification of Family Law Mediator.

attorneys.name: Theodore J. Leopold
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Injury & Wrongful Death Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
Theodore J. Leopold has a state wide and national practice devoted solely to trial work. Mr. Leopold specializes in consumer justice litigation with a focus on complex products liability, managed care, catastrophic injury and class action litigation. Mr. Leopold has tried cases throughout the country and has recovered multi-million dollar verdicts, including jury verdicts in the eight-figure and nine-figure amounts.

Recently, Mr. Leopold obtained a $131 million verdict against the Ford Motor Company which was the eighth largest jury award in 2010 and the ninth biggest U.S. verdict against an automobile company in U.S. history. Mr. Leopold has also achieved many multi-million dollar settlements for his clients.

Mr. Leopold has been involved in significant class and antitrust cases. He was on the steering committee in the National Managed Care Class Action and the Plaintiffs’ settlement committee for the Ford/Firestone National Class Action. Currently Mr. Leopold is serving on the Plaintiffs’ trial team in the Rail Freight Fuel Surcharge Antitrust Litigation.

For many consecutive years, Mr. Leopold has been profiled in The Best Lawyers in America. His work has been featured in the National Law Journal’s Top Cases of the year and he was nominated for “Trial Lawyer of the Year” by the Public Justice Foundation for his ground breaking litigation involving the managed care industry.

Mr. Leopold lectures nationally to Bar and Professional Trial Associations throughout the country on issues such as personal injury, product liability, class action litigation, trial tactics and consumer justice issues. Mr. Leopold is also the author and co-author of several legal publications including Florida Insurance Law and Practice, an annual publication by Thomson/West. Additionally, Mr. Leopold has earned the Florida Bar Civil Trial Certification, which is the highest level of recognition by the Florida Bar for competency and experience within civil trial law.

attorneys.bio:
Jared M. Lerner is an attorney in Morgan & Morgan's Orlando office. Mr. Lerner was born and raised in New Jersey, and moved to Orlando, Florida, in 2011 to attend the University of Central Florida where he received a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science in 2014. He continued his studies at the University of Baltimore School of Law in Baltimore, Maryland, where he earned his Juris Doctor in 2017 with a concentration in Litigation and Advocacy. Mr. Lerner's love for "The City Beautiful" brought him back to Orlando, a city that has truly been his home away from home.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Lerner served the community as a prosecutor at the State Attorney's Office for the Ninth Judicial Circuit, where he was first-chair for several jury trials in Orange and Osceola Counties. He then continued his legal career working for one of Florida's premier insurance defense firms, focusing his practice on the defense of motor vehicle accidents, slip and falls, trip and falls, dog bites and animal attacks, and various other premises liability cases. Mr. Lerner now uses this valuable experience and insight in the pursuit of justice for the people of Central Florida who have been victimized by the actions of others.

Mr. Lerner intends to serve the Central Florida community in any way he can and can be contacted at any time via the information above.

Founding member of Lesak, Hamilton, Calhoun & Pontieri (2022-2025)

attorneys.bio:
Gary S. Lesser is President of The Florida Bar and Managing Partner of Lesser, Landy, Smith & Siegel, PLLC, a third-generation law firm with 95 years of dedication to helping people who have experienced life-changing trauma due to the carelessness and negligence of others.

A native of West Palm Beach, Gary is one of Florida's foremost personal injury attorneys, leading a team of skilled trial lawyers, working across four offices in Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast, who practice law with professionalism, integrity, ethics and a commitment to personal client service.

Gary is highly respected in the field and often serves as a guest lecturer and media commentator on the topics of personal injury, as well as ethical and legal issues. He is a dedicated community servant, having held leadership positions in numerous legal, nonprofit and civic-oriented organizations on a local, state and national level.

Gary was born in West Palm Beach. After graduating from Forest Hill High School, Gary attended George Washington University, where he graduated with a B.A. in International Affairs, and was named to the Dean's List and served as President Pro Tempore of the Student Senate. He was Associate Editor of the GW Hatchet, the school newspaper, and the Editor-in-Chief of the GW Journal, a monthly political opinion commentary. Gary attended the University of Miami School of Law earning his Juris Doctorate. attorneys.practice_type: Contracts Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Shepard P. Lesser was born in West Palm Beach in 1935. After graduating from Palm Beach High in 1953, Shep attended the University of Florida. He graduated with honors in 1957 and earned a B.A. in Political Science. He then attended University of Florida School of Law, graduating Phi Beta Kappa among other honors. He began practicing law with his father Joseph Lesser immediately after admission to the Florida Bar.

Shep continued the Firm's tradition of community involvement. Over the years, he has served as the Vice President of the Gulfstream Council of Boy Scouts of America, President of the Family Services Agency, and was also the President of the local B'nai Brith Chapter. Shep was also very involved with many other organizations, including but not limited to Temple Israel, and the Jewish Federation of Palm Beach County. Additionally, Shep has been Chairman and a long standing member of the Palm Beach County Bar Association's Speaker's Bureau and frequently lectures on real estate, estate planning and a number of other legal topics.

Shepard Lesser is presently the Firm's Senior Partner and handles the Firm's transactional matters. He concentrates his practice in real estate, probate, wills and trusts and elder law. He also handles contract preparation and review, condominium law and general corporate matters.

Personal/Biographical Information:

Born in West Palm Beach in 1935. Married to Lissie and has two children, Tami and Gary.

attorneys.name: Arthur H. Lester M.D., J.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation with Emphasis on Health and Contract Law Lawyers in Shalimar, FL
attorneys.bio:
Arthur H. Lester M.D., J.D., has assisted and cared for clients in several capacities - as both an attorney and a physician. His knowledge as a doctor benefits clients of the firm who are involved in matters such as personal injury, medical malpractice cases, workers' compensation claims, and other issues relating to injury and medical terminology and treatment. Dr. Lester has been licensed as an attorney since 1989 and is admitted to practice in Florida, the U.S. District Court Northern District of Florida, and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

Dr. Lester is a published author, having penned works relating to matters such as physician liability, assisted suicide, and technology in the law of medicine. He has also taught seminars and classes to a variety of medical and legal organizations, sharing his knowledge with colleagues in the medical and legal fields. In addition to his roles as lawyer and doctor, he teaches at the Department of Legal Studies of the University of West Florida

Dr. Lester has been involved in many community and professional organizations centered on medicine, the law, and the Fort Walton Beach Community. The American Bar Association, the National Health Lawyers' Association, and the Okaloosa-Walton Bar Association are just a few of the groups in which he has held membership. He has also been active in the Association for Retarded Citizens as a member of the Board of Directors, the Okaloosa-Walton Community College Foundation, the Okaloosa County Medical Society, and the Fort Walton Beach Chamber of Commerce in his efforts to contribute to the local community.

Dr. Lester earned his Juris Doctor from Florida State University College of Law, graduating with High Honors. At Chicago Medical School, where he obtained his M.D., Dr. Lester graduated in the top 10% and was Class Vice President. He has received several awards has been recognized in "Who's Who" in American Medicine, "Who's Who" in American Law Students, and "Who's Who" in American Attorneys.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Leuchtman was a partner with Beggs & Lane, RLLP for approximately 31 years prior to leaving to open the Law Office of Gary B. Leuchtman PLLC in January 2014. Mr Leuchtman is Board Certified by the Florida Bar in Wills, Trusts & Estates. He served on the Wills, Trust & Estates Certification Committee of the Florida Bar for 12 years (having chaired that committee in 2001-2002 and again in 2009-2010).

He also served 12 years as a member of the Probate Rules Committee of the Florida Bar (chairing the General Rules Subcommittee for most of those years). Mr. Leuchtman provides personal client service and has developed one of the most sophisticated and experienced estate planning practices in Northwest Florida.

He provides representation in all matters related in this area, including Wills, Trusts, Probate, Estate and Trust Administration, Estate and Trust Litigation, Asset Protection, Taxes, Business Planning, Charitable Planning and Exempt Organization representation. Whether you need basic estate planning to protect your family or you have complex estate planning, business succession planning or estate/trust administration issues confronting you, Mr. Leuchtman may be able to be of assistance.

Mr. Leuchtman has also served as President of the Northwest Florida Estate Planning Council, Chairperson of the United Way of Escambia County Foundation and on the Board of Directors for United Way of Escambia County, United Way of Florida and WSRE-TV for many years. He is committed to delivering comprehensive planning and solutions in a timely manner at a reasonable cost.

Mr. Leuchtman provides personal client service and has developed one of the most sophisticated and experienced estate planning practices in Northwest Florida.

He provides representation in all matters related in this area, including Wills, Trusts, Probate, Estate and Trust Administration, Estate and Trust Litigation, Asset Protection, Taxes, Business Planning, Charitable Planning and Exempt Organization representation. Whether you need basic estate planning to protect your family or you have complex estate planning, business succession planning or estate/trust administration issues confronting you, Mr. Leuchtman may be able to be of assistance.

Mr. Leuchtman has also served as President of the Northwest Florida Estate Planning Council, Chairperson of the United Way of Escambia County Foundation and on the Board of Directors for United Way of Escambia County, United Way of Florida and WSRE-TV for many years. He is committed to delivering comprehensive planning and solutions in a timely manner at a reasonable cost.

Lewis J. Levey, Managing Senior Partner of the Firm, is a graduate of the University of Miami School of Law and has been active as a trial lawyer in the State of Florida since 1987. Mr. Levey served as the 2007-2008 President of the University of Miami School of Law Alumni Association and remains active with the Law School and UM Alumni Association.

He is a member of the Dade County Bar, American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, and is Past President of the Coral Gables Bar Association. Mr. Levey served as an arbitrator in the Eleventh Circuit's Fee Arbitration Committee and is also a member on the Board of Arbitrators for the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) and Financial Industry numerous securities cases and attorney's fees disputes. Mr. Levey has served on the Professional Committee of the Dade County Bar Association and has been a member of the Federalist Society, the Hoeveler-Spellman Inns of Court, Big Brothers Big Sisters Committee of 100, and the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity.

Mr. Levey served as the International Vice President of the Greater Miami and Broward Chapter of the American Jewish Committee from 2002 to 2008 and has been President of the Venetian Chabad since 2003. Mr. Levey has twice chaired the Immigration and Naturalization Ceremony scheduled each December in Miami-Dade County.

attorneys.name: Jared A. Levy
attorneys.practice_type: Business Tort Litigation Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
"Jared A. Levy is a partner in the firm's Business Trial Group and chairs the Investment Recovery Group at Morgan & Morgan.

Jared has 20 years of litigation experience and is a versatile trial lawyer. He represents investors who were victims of misconduct by brokerage firms, investment advisors, and banks. He also represents clients in high-value business disputes involving deceptive trade practices, legal malpractice, breaches of contract and fiduciary duties, usury, and corporate divorces.

Jared has helped clients recover tens of millions of dollars and has won multiple trial verdicts of over $1 million. He represents all clients on a contingency basis.

Jared approaches every case with the mindset of getting the case to trial as quickly as possible and battling aggressively to maximize the case's value. He fights corporate malfeasance by leveraging the resources of Morgan & Morgan - the nation's largest contingency law firm with 700 attorneys and dozens of offices. Jared regularly practices in state and federal courts, and handles investor arbitrations across the nation.

Florida Trend Magazine has recognized Jared as one of Florida's "Legal Elite" - an award that less than 1.5% of Florida Bar members have received. He has served on the Florida Bar's Consumer Protection Committee for multiple years. He also belongs to the Public Investors Arbitration Bar Association, a national group that fights for investors against the country's largest financial institutions.

Before joining Morgan & Morgan, Jared was a partner at a boutique litigation firm, where he represented clients on a contingency basis for over 10 years. Before that, he worked for White & Case LLC, one of the world's largest law firms. He began his legal career by clerking for a federal district court judge in Charleston, South Carolina.

Jared attended college at the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill, where he graduated with distinction in 1995. He attended law school at Boston University School of Law, where he graduated cum laude in 1998. While in law school, Jared served on the Law Review and published his note."

attorneys.name: Jonathan T. Levy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan T. Levy is an invaluable member of Rosenthal, Levy, Simon & Sosa. In fact, he is a cut above the rest, in terms of belonging to the elite one percent of Florida Bar Members who are Board Certified Civil Trial attorneys. This is a distinguished honor that allows Jonathan to endorse himself as a Civil Trial Specialist. This is certified by the Supreme Court based on his experience, education, and expertise in civil trial practice.

BUILDING A SUCCESSFUL PERSONAL INJURY PRACTICE

Early on, Jonathan knew that he wanted to be of service to his community. His path to the practice of law began at the University of Vermont where he completed the Political Science Honors’ Program. He then proceeded to complete his Juris Doctor Program at the University of Wisconsin Law School in 1995.

Jonathan Levy began building his successful law practice specializing in litigation. Jonathan has only represented injured individuals, where he has never worked for an insurance company or major corporation. It is his expertise, complemented by a good professional relationship with his clients, that has enabled him to build a successful career in law. He comes highly recommended by his clients who remember him by his professionalism, reasonable expectations, and drive to succeed.

This passionate lawyer has dedicated his career to handling cases involving catastrophic medical malpractice, products liability, and vehicle collisions. It is his dedication to pursuing what is right and due, that has built him an extraordinary reputation in trial litigation. Jonathan has also achieved victories in securing insurance benefits beyond the policy limits for clients who have been denied by their claims in bad faith.

BUILDING THE NAME OF ROSENTHAL, LEVY, SIMON & SOSA

Jonathan’s talent and contribution to Rosenthal, Levy, Simon & Sosa paved his way to becoming a name shareholder of the firm in 2004. When asked his secret to success, Jonathan replies, “Injury cases can be tragic and complicated, that is why I establish a personal relationship with my client from the first time I meet them. I see my clients through all phases of a case, from the time of the injury through a trial or settlement.”

He is fueled by the aim to do what is best for his clients. Jonathan is known to be smart, aggressive, and relentless, with only the best interests of clients in mind. His years of experience have helped many live the quality of life they deserve.

Jonathan Levy is an example of an attorney committed to serving his community through the practice of law. He is a rare find; a perfect balance of compassion and work ethic.

In the 20 years since opening his practice, Mr. Levy has since become one of South Florida's most sought-after legal service providers, assisting both clients and attorneys navigate the time-consuming and technical aspects of both business litigation and the appellate process.

A member of the Florida Bar since 1976, AV-rated attorney, Jay M. Levy, focuses his practice on litigation of business and commercial disputes appeals, and is often asked to collaborate by other attorneys in trial matters.

Mr. Levy is Board Certified by The Florida Bar in Appellate Practice since 1992. He is an accomplished litigator, ranked by Chambers USA as one of the top 19 appellate lawyers in the Florida and has been recognized by his fellow lawyers as a Super Lawyer for the past nine consecutive years (2006-2014). With 35 years of experience, Mr. Levy has had hundreds of clients in both jury and non-jury trials, obtaining large verdicts while always protecting the rights of his clients.

attorneys.name: Daniel Lewin Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Daniel is a licensed Florida attorney with years of criminal defense experience, first as a public defender and then as a private defense attorney. Throughout the years, he has represented clients charged with traffic tickets, misdemeanors, and serious felonies. Daniel has consulted people on cases as simple as driving under the influence and as complex as murder. Now he has started his own law firm to provide you with quality criminal defense services at an affordable price.

Daniel was born in Miami and raised with a strong respect and appreciation for our unique freedoms and the danger that an accusation from the police or government poses to them. He went to college at the University of Tampa where he studied political science, government and world affairs, and business administration & management. From there, Daniel went to law school at Nova Southeastern University in Fort Lauderdale and graduated in the top 25% of his class. He took every criminal related law class he could because he knew right away he wanted to defend individuals and fight abuses of power. Daniel worked for private criminal defense law firms and government organizations in Fort Lauderdale while in law school.

Daniel took a job at the Palm Beach County Public Defender’s Office and litigated cases there for 4.5 years, first as an intern in law school, then in the misdemeanor and criminal traffic division as an assistant public defender, all the way up to being an attorney in the felony division handling serious cases for clients facing multiple decades in prison. Daniel left the public defender’s office to be a private criminal defense attorney in Key West. He represented clients charged with a range of serious offenses including but not limited to robbery, sexual battery, and driving under the influence causing serious bodily injury.

attorneys.name: Adam Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Coverage Lawyers in Saint Petersburg, FL
attorneys.bio:
Adam Lewis is a partner at Dicus Burke & Lewis, PLLC where he focuses his practice on assisting commercial and residential property owners with insurance claims against their insurance company. Based in Tampa, he represents clients throughout the state of Florida. Mr. Lewis has been admitted to practice in Florida since 2009, and he is additionally admitted to practice before the U.S. District Courts for the Middle and Southern Districts of Florida. Mr. Lewis is also a certified appraiser and umpire by the Windstorm Insurance Network and handles appraisals throughout the state of Florida.

Mr. Lewis has extensive experience in handling first-party insurance claim litigation, both as defense counsel for insurance companies, as well as on behalf of homeowners and other aggrieved parties. The types of cases that he has worked on have included damages and other losses stemming from wind, hail, hurricanes, flood and other water damage, sinkholes, lightning, and fire.

Mr. Lewis’s background has additionally encompassed personal injury and wrongful death litigation, and he has assisted plaintiffs who were seriously harmed as the result of the negligence of other parties as well as insurance companies and their policyholders who were named as defendants in these types of actions. The types of cases that Mr. Lewis has worked on in this regard have arisen from incidents involving premises liability, truck, motorcycle, and other motor vehicle crashes, auto-pedestrian accidents, and animal bites. His work on behalf of plaintiffs has resulted in his clients receiving substantial compensation through both jury awards and negotiated settlements, and it has resulted in him being named to the invitation-only Million Dollar Advocates Forum. A graduate of Stetson University College of Law, Mr. Lewis’s other honors include an AV Preeminent* peer review rating through Martindale-Hubbell.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. attorneys.name: Kathryn N. Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in North Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
"As an Assistant State Attorney, I spent years in the courtroom prosecuting those who took financial advantage of senior citizens. While it was incredibly rewarding to see justice served, I always wished I could have done something to help prevent the exploitation in the first place. Now, as an elder law attorney, I help my clients strategize & plan the best way to protect their assets from theft & fraud. I also help the victims & their families recover their assets, whether directly from the person who exploited them, or from the financial institutions that sometimes look the other way."

Kathryn N. Lewis earned her Bachelor's degree in 2004 from the Harriet L. Wilkes Honors College of Florida Atlantic University, and her Juris Doctor from Stetson University College of Law, in 2008. While at Stetson, she served as the Articles & Symposia Editor for the Stetson Law Review. Ms. Lewis began her legal career as an associate at a large law firm, but quickly transitioned into criminal law, serving as an Assistant State Attorney in Palm Beach County, from 2009 to 2016.

From 2012 to 2016, Ms. Lewis was a member of the State Attorney's Office White Collar Crime Unit, which handles complex financial theft & fraud cases. Ms. Lewis was also primarily responsible for handling crimes involving financial exploitation of the elderly. Among the indviduals she prosecuted were a man who stole $250,000 from an elderly victim with Alzheimers; a defendant who swindled dozens of senior citizens in a Ponzi scheme; and a caregiver who drained her client's checking account.

While at the State Attorney's Office, Ms. Lewis developed a special interest in the intersection of criminal, guardianship & probate matters. She continues to serve on the State Attorney's Elder Abuse Task Force, which coordinates the efforts of prosecutors, law enforcement and other members of the community, to safeguard the elderly against both financial & physical abuse. She is available to help the victims of crime make reports to law enforcement and to represent their interests as victims in criminal cases.

Ms. Lewis has spoken about crimes against the elderly and white collar crimes to several organizations, including the Florida State Guardianship Association, the Elder Law Section of the Palm Beach County Bar Association, the Palm Beach County Economic Crimes Forum, and Palm Beach Atlantic University.

Watch our informative video! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KDhBW-3fL9E

Before founding Light & Gonzalez, PLLC with Anthony Gonzalez, Esq., Mr. Light worked extensively on foreclosure defense and appellate matters at a small firm in South Florida. As a Plantation Florida Lawyer, Mr. Light actively looks for opportunities to help the local community and reaches out to those in need whenever he can.

Mr. Light earned his J.D. From St. Thomas University School of Law in May of 2015, graduating magna cum laude in the top 5% of his class. He is admitted to practice in the State of Florida and in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida. He is a member of the Broward County Bar Association and the Federal Bar Association.

At St. Thomas University School of Law, Mr. Light founded the St. Thomas Journal of Complex Litigation and served as its first Editor-in-Chief. He was elected Executive Vice President of the Moot Court Team where he competed at the Robert Orseck Moot Court Competition, coached the Moot Court team in the Prince Evidence Competition, and served as a research assistant for various other competitions. While in law school Mr. Light also served as the President of the Federal Bar Association Student Division at St. Thomas.

Prior to law school Mr. Light worked at a mass tort firm in New York on unsafe drug and medical device matters. Working in this area inspired Mr. Light to go to law school to continue his work helping people through the most difficult periods of their lives.
