In my experience, most people don't consider what insurance they need or have until after there is a claim. I understand why this is. People think insurance is complicated, and they are right. But, there are some simple concepts you need to know before purchasing insurance.

To learn more about me and how we can help with your insurance claim click HERE to download a free copy of my book Claim Denied.

Mark is Board Certified by in Civil Trial law and Business Litigation.

Mark is a graduate of the University of Florida College of Law, where he was an Editor of the Florida Law Review. He graduated with Honors, and was inducted into the Order of the Coif, a national organization which recognizes excellence in legal studies.

Bryn Natland is an associate at Dabdoub Law Firm specializing in disability insuarnce cliams, appeals and lawsuits. She has dedicated her time to helping people who have fallen ill or have become injured and can no longer work. Bryn handles all aspects of disability claims, including initial claim reviews, appeals of denials, and litigation. Her cases involve both private disability insurance policies and disability policies under ERISA.

Prior to joining Dabdoub Law Firm, Bryn gained invaluable experience working as an Assistant State Attorney in the Miami-Dade Office. She worked in the child support enforcement division, managing thousands of cases. In her time working for the State Attorney, she mediated and litigated in both Family and Child Support Courts, fervently working on behalf of single parents trying to obtain financial support for their children. It was during her time as an Assistant State Attorney that she learned, and appreciated, how much could be done using the law to help those in need.

Bryn is admitted to practice law in the State of Florida, United States District Court Southern District of Florida, the United States District Court Middle District of Florida and the United States Disctrict Court of Colorado. Bryn received her Bachelor of Science in Communication and Spanish from the University of Miami and her law degree from St. Thomas University School of Law.

attorneys.name: Angela R. Neave
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Angela first experienced divorce as a child and later as a parent who earned full custody of her daughter. Understanding how legal issues impacted the direction of her life, Angela switched careers and dedicated herself to family law. As a full-time single parent, Angela undertook an intensive five-year program in which she earned a Philosophy Degree from UCLA and her Juris Doctor degree from Southwestern University School of Law. She moved to South Florida, and guided by a client-centered philosophy, opened Neave Family Law Group, P.A.. Angela balances her work ethic and capacity for mastering complex legal work with large measures of empathy and respect.

“Issues of family law often put clients in a state of crisis at a time when the legal process demands they make major life decisions. My role is to advocate with good judgement and a commitment to helping clients recover their peace of mind.”

Angela is a skilled trial lawyer who has litigated all varieties of family law issues. She thrives in the courtroom, where she has earned a reputation for tenacious representation. Angela specializes in high-conflict custody cases and complex property-division matters.

“Family law is rarely winner takes all. Our record in the courtroom allows us to really push for our clients in negotiating settlements. And a good settlement is usually the best outcome for all involved.”

Angela is trained in collaborative divorce and offers it as an alternative to contested divorce litigation. She has also served as a pro bono guardian ad litem for the 17th judicial circuit in dependency matters and has been appointed as a guardian ad litem in family cases. Angela shares her expertise by teaching and sitting on panels for seminars by the Broward County Bar Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Aviation Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Andrew Needle is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the Florida Bar. Following graduation from Cornell University in 1974 and the University of Miami, cum laude, in 1977, he began practicing law with one of the premier personal injury and medical malpractice firms in Florida. Since then he has distinguished himself professionally both in and out of the courtroom as a trial lawyer, author, and lecturer.

He is a charter member of the Miami chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates, a trial lawyer organization dedicated to the preservation of the civil justice system and for which admission is solely by peer recognition and experience. Mr. Needle's courtroom victories include multi-million dollar verdicts in cases that have often pushed the outer boundaries of existing legal precedent. He is a former editorial consultant to Matthew Bender Law Books, and the author of "Post Trial Motions” Florida Civil Trial Practice, Chapter 18, Ninth Edition as well as Inside The Minds- Representing Plaintiffs in Medical Malpractice Cases "Current Challenges in Handling Medical Malpractice Actions: Statutory Protections, Expenses, and Societal Misconceptions", Thomson Reuters/Aspatore 2012.

For six years he was a member of the Florida Bar's Board of Governors, which sets policy and discipline (under the auspices of the Florida Supreme Court), for all lawyers practicing in the state of Florida. Named as one of South Florida's Top Lawyers in medical malpractice, personal injury and wrongful death by the "South Florida Legal Guide," every year since its inception, he has been selected as a "Heavy Hitter" in healthcare law by the South Florida Business Journal, February 10, 2006, recognized in 2013 by Florida Trend Magazine as among Florida’s Legal Elite, and has been selected for inclusion in The Best Lawyers in America®, 2007-2016 in the areas of Medical Malpractice and Personal Injury.

attorneys.name: Eric K. Neitzke Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Daytona Beach Attorney Eric K. Neitzke has aggressively represented clients for more than 30 years in criminal matters throughout Florida. He defends those accused of sex related offenses as well as other crimes and has has extensive experience dealing with complex family law matters.

Sometimes, in a stressful divorce, one person might accuse another of sexual abuse or of sexual abuse of a child to gain leverage. Such accusations are serious and must be addressed immediately - even if no arrests have been made. Being accused can be very damaging your reputation and may cause you to lose your job. If the accuser calls the police during an argument, the officer might have enough information to take you into immediate custody until an investigation is complete. An experienced criminal defense lawyer familiar with these specific types of situations can help.

Even if you criminal charges are dropped at a later time or, the long-term damage can be devastating and irreversible. You could lose the right to see your children, participate in their school activities or even parent them at all. The government is obligated to investigate allegations of abuse against children. If you are charged with a sex-related crime, or even accused by another person, take immediate action to protect your rights and contact Eric K. Neitzke.

Eric K. Neitzke can represent you even before you are charged and until your case is decided or dismissed. He will listen to your side of the story and develop a legal strategy to defend you against sex crime charges. Eric K. Neitzke has a reputation of being tough in the courtroom while protecting his clients' constitutional right to a fair trial.

Ashley Nelson was born in Georgia and has resided in Florida since primary school. Growing up in the coastal city of Fort Pierce, Ashley often advocated on behalf of others during their most vulnerable moments. Developing a passion for advocacy at a young age helped carve her pathway to law.

Ashley received a Bachelors of Science in Health Science from Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU); later, receiving her Juris Doctorate from FAMU Law.

While in law school, Ashley clerked with a litigation attorney at a mid-size personal injury firm in central Florida. There, Ashley was able to gain insight and experience in personal injury litigation. To diversify her background, during the summer of the second year of law school, Ashley studied abroad at Queen Mary University of London, via the Dispute Resolution Institution. During this educational experience, Ashley was able to enhance her skills in client advocacy, negotiations and litigation, as well as, gain invaluable experience in arbitration, earning a Certificate in Global Arbitration Law and Practice.

After graduating law school, Ashley immediately began to place her skills to work as an associate litigation attorney, fighting for the rights of accident victims throughout the state of Florida. Ashley also advocates for the students at the Pace Center for Girls-Orange County, as a volunteer on their Young Professionals Board.

attorneys.name: Alyssa Neufeld
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Aventura, FL
attorneys.bio:
Alyssa Neufeld, Esq., serves as an Associate Attorney at Elder Needs Law, PLLC, where she specializes in Medicaid Planning, Asset Protection, and Government Benefits Preservation. With a client-first mindset and a commitment to innovative solutions, Alyssa excels at creating personalized plans that align with her clients’ unique needs and long-term goals.

Alyssa’s expertise lies in navigating the intricacies of complex legal and regulatory frameworks, ensuring her clients retain the assets and benefits they have worked hard to achieve. She is particularly skilled at addressing challenges associated with Medicaid eligibility and crafting asset protection strategies that safeguard financial stability for individuals and families.

Alyssa’s approach combines professionalism, empathy, and a keen understanding of the legal landscape. She takes pride in simplifying complicated processes and providing clear, actionable guidance to her clients. Her dedication to staying ahead of industry developments ensures that her strategies are both effective and forward-thinking.

A graduate of the University of Miami with a Bachelor’s Degree and Nova Southeastern University with a Juris Doctor, Alyssa blends her academic background with over a decade of practical experience spanning Financial Services, Real Estate, and Corporate Law. This multidisciplinary foundation gives her a broad perspective, allowing her to offer comprehensive and well-rounded advice to her clients.

Through her work at Elder Needs Law, Alyssa is committed to empowering clients with knowledge and tools to protect their families, preserve their legacies, and achieve peace of mind.

Mrs. Liu is admitted to the Florida Bar and the U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida. She is an active member of the Jacksonville Bar Association and serves as the President of the Jacksonville Asian American Bar Association.

Mrs. Liu spent the first part of her career working for insurance defense firms where her practice focused on defending large corporations, insurance companies, big box stores, and city governments against personal injury claims including auto accident, slip and fall, and premises liability matters. Mrs. Liu now utilizes that experience to exclusively represent individuals and families who who have been injured in slip and fall, trip and fall, dog bite, and negligent security cases.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Stuart, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tim Nies, Esq.

Partner | Van Riper & Nies Attorneys, P.A.

Florida Personal Injury, Defense Base Act Lawyer, Longshore Lawyer, and Family Lawyer

Army Ranger Veteran | Veteran-Owned Law Firm

About Tim Nies

Tim Nies is a respected Florida trial attorney and founding partner of Van Riper & Nies Attorneys, P.A., a veteran-owned law firm with offices across South Florida, where he meets his clients, including Stuart, West Palm Beach, Delray Beach, Boca Raton, and Deerfield Beach. Before entering law, Tim proudly served as a U.S. Army Ranger with the elite 3rd Ranger Battalion, an experience that forged the discipline, leadership, and determination that define his approach to representing clients.

Practicing law since 2001, Tim is widely recognized for his work in Defense Base Act (DBA) and Longshore and Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act (LHWCA) claims, personal injury litigation, auto accident cases, and family law matters. Known by clients as a lawyer warrior, Tim applies his military training and strategic mindset to every case, fighting with precision, honor, and persistence to achieve the best results possible.

For the first eight years of his career, Tim served as a lead insurance defense attorney, representing national insurance carriers and Fortune 500 companies in complex injury litigation. This insider experience taught him how insurers analyze and defend claims, knowledge he now leverages to outmaneuver them and secure full compensation for injured clients. His background gives him a tactical edge when negotiating settlements or trying cases in court.

Tim’s hallmark is accessibility. Every client he represents receives his personal cell phone number, a reflection of his belief that open communication builds trust and confidence. He is hands-on, personally guiding clients through each phase of their case and ensuring they always know where they stand.

At Van Riper & Nies Attorneys, Tim’s commitment to service mirrors the values he lived as an Army Ranger: integrity, discipline, and loyalty. Whether advocating for an injured civilian contractor overseas, a longshoreman injured on the job, a car-crash victim, or a parent navigating divorce, Tim treats each client’s case as a mission—one that demands focus, preparation, and unwavering advocacy.

Practice Areas

Defense Base Act (DBA) Claims for Injured Civilian Contractors

Longshore & Harbor Workers’ Compensation Act (LHWCA) Claims

Personal Injury & Auto Accident Litigation

Family Law & Divorce Matters

Military Service

U.S. Army – 3rd Ranger Battalion (Airborne Ranger Veteran)

About Van Riper & Nies Attorneys, P.A.

Van Riper & Nies Attorneys is a Florida veteran-owned law firm representing clients statewide in Defense Base Act, Longshore, personal injury, family law, and criminal defense cases. The firm’s attorneys are known for being accessible, proactive, and results-driven—fighting for clients with the same courage and precision that Tim Nies brought to his Army Ranger service.

attorneys.bio:
Mary Nikezic grew up in Chicago, Illinois. She graduated from Loyola University on a scholarship, graduating Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Philosophy. Ms. Nikezic went on to attend Chicago-Kent College of Law, where she received a merit scholarship and was a dean's list scholar.

Before joining Zarco Einhorn Salkowski, P.A., Ms. Nikezic worked in Chicago, Illinois at several prominent litigation law firms, practicing as a trial lawyer in both state and federal civil litigation. She represented a broad spectrum of clients in the hospitality and beverage industries, including importers and suppliers, national hotel, restaurant and tavern and grocery store chains. She also has significant experience in areas of construction law, complex construction defect litigation, general liability, casualty defense, and first-party property, including all phases of litigation, contract negotiations, contract drafting, and alternative dispute resolution procedures.

Mary Nikezic's practice focuses on complex commercial and franchise litigation, representing institutional clients and individuals in a variety of business and civil disputes. Ms. Nikezic represents clients in state and federal courts and in arbitration proceedings throughout the United States. Ms. Nikezic is admitted to practice law in Florida and Illinois, as well as before the United States Southern District of Florida and the Northern District of Illinois.

In addition to her litigation practice, Ms. Nikezic maintains an active presence in the international business community through her involvement with global economic and investment forums, private leadership networks, and cross-border business organizations. She participates in high-level summits and strategic gatherings convening senior executives, institutional investors, and policymakers to address issues at the intersection of global commerce, capital markets, and innovation, including the Future Investment Initiative (FII), a global economic forum backed by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund.

sections.content:
Mary Nikezic grew up in Chicago, Illinois. She graduated from Loyola University on a scholarship, graduating Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and Philosophy. Ms. Nikezic went on to attend Chicago-Kent College of Law, where she received a merit scholarship and was a dean's list scholar.

Before joining Zarco Einhorn Salkowski, P.A., Ms. Nikezic worked in Chicago, Illinois at several prominent litigation law firms, practicing as a trial lawyer in both state and federal civil litigation. She represented a broad spectrum of clients in the hospitality and beverage industries, including importers and suppliers, national hotel, restaurant and tavern and grocery store chains. She also has significant experience in areas of construction law, complex construction defect litigation, general liability, casualty defense, and first-party property, including all phases of litigation, contract negotiations, contract drafting, and alternative dispute resolution procedures.

Mary Nikezic's practice focuses on complex commercial and franchise litigation, representing institutional clients and individuals in a variety of business and civil disputes. Ms. Nikezic represents clients in state and federal courts and in arbitration proceedings throughout the United States. Ms. Nikezic is admitted to practice law in Florida and Illinois, as well as before the United States Southern District of Florida and the Northern District of Illinois.

In addition to her litigation practice, Ms. Nikezic maintains an active presence in the international business community through her involvement with global economic and investment forums, private leadership networks, and cross-border business organizations. She participates in high-level summits and strategic gatherings convening senior executives, institutional investors, and policymakers to address issues at the intersection of global commerce, capital markets, and innovation, including the Future Investment Initiative (FII), a global economic forum backed by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund.

attorneys.name: Anna R. Norris
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tallahassee, FL
attorneys.bio:
Anna was born and raised in Tallahassee, Florida. She attended the University of Southern California (USC) in Los Angeles, graduating magna cum laude in 2003 with a Bachelor of Arts in English Literature and a minor in Business Administration. During her time as a college student, Anna competed on USC's Mock Trial Team and served as the team's Assistant Coach. Following graduation from USC, she worked as a Legal Project Assistant on a complex litigation team at Mitchell, Silberberg, and Knupp, LLP in Los Angeles.

Before law school, Anna volunteered in a United Nations Liberian Refugee Camp in Ghana, West Africa, for six months. She then attended the Boston University School of Law, earning her Juris Doctor in 2008. During law school, Anna was on the International Law Journal, competed in Moot Court, and spent a summer in Rome, Italy, volunteering for the United Nations' World Food Programme.

In 2008, Anna returned to her roots in Tallahassee and began working at the Florida Public Service Commission in the Office of the General Counsel's Economic Regulation Section.

In 2011, Anna became a prosecutor with the Second Judicial Circuit's State Attorney's Office (SAO). Anna prosecuted thousands of crimes, ranging from misdemeanor DUIs to the most serious felony offenses, including armed robberies, capital sexual batteries, and first-degree murders, and she specialized in prosecuting sex crimes. In 2018, Anna became a Felony Division Chief in Leon County. During her tenure at the SAO, Anna tried over 120 jury trials to verdict as lead trial attorney, and in 2017, she tried the most cases in her circuit (22 felony jury trials).

Anna joined Morgan & Morgan as a Personal Injury Litigation Attorney and she is passionate about pursuing justice and zealously advocating for those who have been wronged. She is licensed to practice in Florida, New York, and Massachusetts.

She enjoys running, going to the beach, and spending time with her friends, family, and dog.

attorneys.bio:
Bailey North is a native of Sarasota who joined Berlin Law Firm as an Associate Attorney in 2021. Ms. North is passionate about collaborating with her colleagues as part of a team and enjoys the challenge of complex work injury cases.

Bailey North received her Juris Doctor Degree from Florida Agriculture and Mechanical University College of Law. During law school, Ms. North worked as a law clerk for a prominent Orlando Workers’ Compensation firm, strengthening her interest in this field.

She also holds an undergraduate degree in Criminology from Florida State University. In addition, she received a Bright Futures Scholarship, participated in the Florida State University Youth Programs, and was the Team Leader for the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation.

Ms. North’s passion for advocacy began early in her career–her interests lie at the nexus between the medical field and the legal system. Recently, she worked on a research project for a forthcoming medical sociology casebook. She edited, proofread, and conducted research on developing informed consent laws and their impact on vulnerable populations.

In her spare time, she is most content in the Sunshine State’s great outdoors. She enjoys boating, fishing, and exploring new places. She also loves spending time with family, reading, and spoiling her two feline companions.

attorneys.name: Mitchell Jordan Nowack Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Chapter 7 Bankruptcy Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
The phone rings all day from your creditors. The threatening letters in the mail never stop coming. You have been served with a lawsuit. Your creditors are represented by Law Firms and Collection agents. You have no one on your side to help you and guide you through this difficult time. Not any more....

In my 17 years of experience as a bankruptcy attorney I have learned that 99% of my clients are good people that have fallen on hard times. Whether it is because they lost their job, got divorced, made bad investments or financial decisions, etc., regardless of the cause, there is one common theme…NO ONE PLANNED FOR THIS TO HAPPEN, IT JUST DID. Sometimes your financial life it is a lot like being rear ended at a traffic light. You did nothing wrong, but you are in the accident anyway.

“It is not whether you get knocked down, it is whether you get back up” – Vince Lombardi.

We are here to help you get back up. Everyone deserves a second chance, a “fresh start”. That is exactly what the bankruptcy laws were created for. Good people should not have to suffer with this financial stress for the rest of their lives for the mistakes that they made or for the things that have happened to them. Bankruptcy gives you the opportunity to stop all of the collection efforts against you in one simple legal proceeding.

I am one of the most experienced Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys in South Florida. I have personally handled thousands of bankruptcy cases in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties for both individuals and businesses. We provide every one of our clients with quality individual legal representation at an affordable price. Customer service comes first. We keep you informed through every step of the case and we are always here to answer your questions. Whether it is Chapter 7 or Chapter 13, we can represent you in your bankruptcy proceeding to help you achieve the results you are looking for.

I graduated from the University of Miami Law School in 1996 after earning my economics degree from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst in 1993. In 1997, I took my first law job as a bankruptcy attorney at a small boutique creditor’s rights firm in Coral Gables. In 2001, I opened my own firm and began representing individuals needing personal and business bankruptcy relief all over South Florida. In 2012, when the Southern District of Florida Bankruptcy Court created a panel of a few local consumer bankruptcy attorneys to help create and develop the Court’s Loan Modification Mediation (LMM) program, I was a part of the team of lawyers that helped the Court enact this very successful mortgage loan modification program.

We have the knowledge and expertise to obtain the goals you are looking for and to provide you with the relief from your debt that you so desperately need.

attorneys.name: Chelsea M. Nowel
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Chelsea M. Nowel is an attorney and owner of Dubrule & Nowel, PLLC. Chelsea was raised in Canada, France, and the US. She received her Honors Bachelor of Arts from the University of Toronto, Trinity College and received her law degree from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law where she graduated Cum Laude. Chelsea is trilingual, fluent in English, Spanish, and French.

Chelsea started her career resettling refugees in Cleveland, Ohio. Although she enjoyed the clients, she was frustrated that she could not provide long-lasting solutions to their legal problems. It was at that time that Chelsea realized her desire to practice Immigration and Nationality law.

After years in a big immigration firm, Chelsea decided to open her own firm, CMN Law, LLC in order to continue her fierce advocacy for intending immigrants to the United States. After meeting John, she felt that a merging of the two firms was the best way to expand her service to immigrants in her community and beyond.

Chelsea is barred in Ohio and is a member of AILA. She serves on the board of AILA Central Florida as the Tampa Bay Regional Vice Chair and is chair of the New Members Committee. She was also a distinguished speaker at:

the 2023 AILA National Conference in Orlando, Florida;

the 2022 AILA Central Florida Immigration Law Conference in Clearwater, Florida;

the 2019 AILA Central Florida Immigration Law Conference in St. Petersburg, Florida; and

the 2019 NAFSA Region VII Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Chelsea moved to Tampa Bay in 2016 and lives with her husband William and their twin children, Fiona and Michael.

attorneys.name: Steven E. Nurenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Trust Enforcement under the Perishable Agricultural commodities Act Lawyers in Naples, FL
attorneys.bio:
Steven E. Nurenberg brings more than 25 years of experience, integrity, and a breadth of legal knowledge to every case he handles. His analytical skills afford him the ability to recognize an approach or perspective that may not have been considered, and to view an issue from all sides. Steve has the innate capacity to interpret a client’s difficulty, and whether presenting the matter in a judicial setting or clarifying the circumstances in writing, he is able to communicate his client’s position in a concise and accurate manner. Steve builds relationships with his clients who come to trust and rely upon his incisive legal advice. He values these relationships by keeping his clients informed and allowing them to make decisions concerning what is of upmost importance to them, as the matter proceeds through legal channels or negotiations. Steve is a monthly contributor to "The PACA Law Perspective," a weekly article published in the Meuers Law Firm newsletter, "Produce and the Law," providing important information and items of interest to members of the produce industry. Steve has achieved a legal ability rating of “A” (very high to preeminent) and a general ethical standards rating of “V,” the highest possible ratings by the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory.

Steve counsels and assists clients with litigation matters, including trust enforcement cases under the Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (“PACA”) and disputes between produce companies in federal courts, and formal and informal reparation cases before the PACA Division of the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

Prior to joining Meuers Law Firm in 2006, Steve was a partner in a 90-attorney Detroit, Michigan firm, where he represented corporations and individuals in a variety of insurance-related litigation matters, including workers’ compensation, automobile liability, automobile no-fault, and property damage defense.

The lure of a warmer climate attracted Steve, his wife, Jan, and son, Jared, to Southwest Florida in July, 2006. As northern transplants, they enjoy the amenities Florida has to offer, including golf, fishing and spending time at the beach. Steve and his family are active members of their church and serve in different capacities on several of its committees.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Disputes Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Paulino A. Nuñez Jr. is a commercial litigator, who focuses his practice on business disputes, including banking and professional liability claims, insurance policy litigation, contract disputes, business torts and securities litigation. Mr. Nuñez has successfully represented clients having complex legal problems at trial and in appeals throughout the country. He has been instrumental in securing several multi-million dollar verdicts for his clients and has also successfully defended clients in lawsuits where multiple millions of dollars have been at stake.

Mr. Nuñez is a magna cum laude graduate of the University of Miami (J.D., 1989), where he was a member of the University of Miami Law Review and the Order of the Coif. He graduated from Florida International University (B.A., with honors, 1985).

Mr. Nuñez is a member of The Florida Bar (admitted 1989), the bars of the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida and the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the Fifth, Sixth and Eleventh Circuits, as well as the Dade County Bar Association and the Cuban American Bar Association. He was born in Miami, Florida and is fluent in Spanish. Mr. Nuñez is also active in representing indigent litigants on a pro bono basis and recently received a Pro Bono Service Award in recognition of outstanding contribution to the "Put Something Back" pro bono project sponsored by Florida's Eleventh Judicial Circuit and the Dade County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Wyatt M. Oakey
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injury Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Oakey began her first career as the Peptides Reagent Manager for a Biotechnology Company near Charlotte, NC, which offered her the opportunity to work directly with universities, corporations, and non-profit organizations in their efforts to research and develop treatments for diseases ranging from diabetes to cancer.

In 2008, Ms. Oakey moved to Gulfport, FL, to attend Stetson University College of Law. During law school, Ms. Oakey was actively involved with the local community as well as the Stetson community. Ms. Oakey spent her summers volunteering with a non-profit organization providing free legal aid to residents in the community and interning as a Law Clerk for The Office of the Public Defender for the Tenth Judicial Circuit.

During the academic terms, Ms. Oakey participated as a member of Stetson Law's Advocacy Board, which has repeatedly placed Stetson Law as the top law school in the nation for advocacy by U.S. News & World Report. Ms. Oakey competed on, both, the Alternative Dispute Resolution Board and the Trial Team, which has won first place in more national-level mock trial competitions than any other law school in the country. As a member of both teams, Ms. Oakey competed at the state as well as the national level and, in two competitions, Ms. Oakey was on one of only sixteen teams invited to compete from across the entire nation.

During her last semester as a law student, Ms. Oakey began clerking for The Law Offices of Keith Ligori where she conducted legal research and drafted an appellate brief that was successfully argued before Florida's Second District Court of Appeal. After being admitted to the Florida Bar, Ms. Oakey began practicing law with the firm as a Personal Injury Attorney.

In May 2013, Ms. Oakey accepted the position of Associate Counsel for the Law Offices of Jack D. Evans, Staff Counsel for Travelers Indemnity Company, where she gained invaluable trial experience and knowledge about the insurance industry. Within a year, Ms. Oakey won the national ""Rising Star"" Award for Travelers Claim Legal Trial Advocacy Program and was promoted to the position of Counsel. During her time with the Law Offices of Jack D. Evans, Ms. Oakey was recognized on numerous occasions for her work by, both, her clients and her colleagues in a national company-wide publication called ""Sharing Our Successes.""

When the honor to join Morgan & Morgan was offered, Ms. Oakey immediately accepted the invitation and moved to Pensacola in April 2017, where she now resides and proudly represents her clients across Northwest Florida.

During the academic terms, Ms. Oakey participated as a member of Stetson Law's Advocacy Board, which has repeatedly placed Stetson Law as the top law school in the nation for advocacy by U.S. News & World Report. Ms. Oakey competed on, both, the Alternative Dispute Resolution Board and the Trial Team, which has won first place in more national-level mock trial competitions than any other law school in the country. As a member of both teams, Ms. Oakey competed at the state as well as the national level and, in two competitions, Ms. Oakey was on one of only sixteen teams invited to compete from across the entire nation.

During her last semester as a law student, Ms. Oakey began clerking for The Law Offices of Keith Ligori where she conducted legal research and drafted an appellate brief that was successfully argued before Florida's Second District Court of Appeal. After being admitted to the Florida Bar, Ms. Oakey began practicing law with the firm as a Personal Injury Attorney.

In May 2013, Ms. Oakey accepted the position of Associate Counsel for the Law Offices of Jack D. Evans, Staff Counsel for Travelers Indemnity Company, where she gained invaluable trial experience and knowledge about the insurance industry. Within a year, Ms. Oakey won the national ""Rising Star"" Award for Travelers Claim Legal Trial Advocacy Program and was promoted to the position of Counsel. During her time with the Law Offices of Jack D. Evans, Ms. Oakey was recognized on numerous occasions for her work by, both, her clients and her colleagues in a national company-wide publication called ""Sharing Our Successes.""

When the honor to join Morgan & Morgan was offered, Ms. Oakey immediately accepted the invitation and moved to Pensacola in April 2017, where she now resides and proudly represents her clients across Northwest Florida.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office Of Douglas A. Oberdorfer, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Law Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
I started the Law Office of Douglas A. Oberdorfer, P.A. in 2003 after the unexpected death of my father. His clients were looking for help and I wanted to carry on his tradition of helping them with their family’s issues. Building upon my time litigating cases in the courtroom as an Assistant State Attorney, I decided to carry on his tradition of helping families in the areas of asset protection, estate planning, trust creation/management, probate administration and Medicaid planning. My goal is to be your family’s lawyer.

I was born and raised in Jacksonville and my family has been here for well over one hundred years. I am a proud graduate of Wolfson High School. I earned my Bachelor of Arts Degree from the University of North Carolina and my law degree from the University of Florida. After law school, I gained invaluable experience representing the citizens of Florida as an Assistant State Attorney. My time at the State Attorney’s Office was focused on litigating cases in the courtroom. I know what it takes to try a case and will put this experience to work for you.

In my free time, I enjoy spending time with my wife and two children. We are big sports fans and one of my greatest joys away from the office has been coaching youth baseball at our local ballpark.

attorneys.practice_type: Marital and Family Law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Monica D. Offredi, Esq., concentrates her practice in all areas of marital and family law, including dissolution of marriage, distribution of marital assets and liabilities, alimony, child custody (called “timesharing” in Florida), parenting, and child support, paternity, enforcement and modification proceedings, stepparent adoptions, parental relocation, domestic violence matters, dependency actions, drafting and negotiating prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, and other matters dealing with family law. Monica has extensive experience litigating high-conflict divorces with high-net worth clients with complex financial assets and investments. In addition, Monica frequently serves as a Guardian ad Litem appointed by the Court to assess and determine the best interest of minor children involved in contested custody matters.

Monica believes in providing personal attention and the highest quality of legal services to her clients. Monica understands the emotional difficulty her clients face, this is why Monica ensures she makes herself accessible and available, knowing the importance of continuing communication throughout the process.

Immediately prior to joining the Law Office of Forrest & Forrest, PLLC, Monica was a Senior Associate attorney in the marital and family practice group at a prestigious boutique litigation firm based in Boca Raton, Florida.

Monica began her legal career as an Assistant Regional Counsel for the office of Criminal Conflict and Civil Regional Counsel in Broward County, Florida, Dependency Division, where she gained extensive trial and courtroom experience.

Monica earned her Bachelor of Business Administration in Management from Florida International University where she was consistently on the Dean’s List. She went on to earn her Juris Doctor degree from Florida Coastal School of Law, where she received the Pro Bono Honors Award.

Monica is licensed to practice law in Florida and is admitted to practice before the United States District Court, Southern District of Florida.

Monica is fluent is fluent in spoken and written Spanish.

attorneys.name: Neil Ognibene
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Employment Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Neil Ognibene is a dedicated and hardworking associate attorney. He is a proven asset to the firm's growing team of attorneys. Neil is licensed to practice law in the Commonwealth of Virginia, and he heads the firm's Federal Employment Practice out of the Tampa, Florida office.

Neil comes to the Hoyer Law Group by way of the Whistleblower Law Firm, where he also specialized in a variety of federal employment matters. Prior to working with the Whistleblower Law Firm, Neil managed his own federal employment investigation firm for a decade, during which he gained a wealth of knowledge and experience in the federal employment space. He contracted with numerous federal agencies to serve as a neutral investigator for complaints of federal employment discrimination, harassment, and whistleblower retaliation. Neil now leverages that experience, from both the employee's and employer's perspectives, to advocate for his clients.

Since joining the firm, Neil has had tremendous success advocating for his clients against the federal government. He has successfully opposed multiple motions for summary judgment; negotiated numerous favorable settlement agreements; and has proven trial experience.

Not only does Neil have documented success advocating before federal administrative judges, but he also utilizes his exceptional people skills to relate to, and connect to his clients, who often feel overwhelmed taking on the federal government. He has a remarkable way of comforting his clients and putting them at ease as he assumes their legal stresses and anxieties.

Neil earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Richmond School of Law in 2004 and his Bachelor of Arts from the University at Buffalo, graduating with distinction in 2001. In 2000, Neil received a national Chairman of the Year award for a philanthropic organization in association with Pi Kappa Phi by raising awareness and providing support to children with disabilities. Neil continues to give back to his community by volunteering his time with the Knights of Columbus, and regularly donating to the St. Jude's Children's Research Hospital.

attorneys.name: Gary K. Oldehoff
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Stuart, FL
attorneys.bio:
As an experienced courtroom litigator and appellate advocate, Mr. Oldehoff knows how to assess and value a case, strategize to bring about a favorable settlement, prepare for a trial geared to maximizing the presentation of the client's case, and how to obtain the best possible outcome for the client. Mr. Oldehoff has tried cases lasting from as little as one day to as long as eight weeks. He has handled cases in all of Florida's state and federal courts, in the Florida Division of Administrative Hearings, and in the American Arbitration Association. He has argued appeals in each of Florida's District Courts of Appeal, the Florida Supreme Court, the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court.

Having served with three counties at the highest level in local government law, one of which as County Attorney, Mr. Oldehoff has experience with the entire spectrum local government practice. From advising government bodies, to writing ordinances and contracts, to overseeing projects, to writing and lobbying for litigation, Mr. Oldehoff knows how to accomplish the objectives and defend the actions of local governments.

Mr. Oldehoff's Land Use, Environmental, and Zoning Law practice has been at the forefront of the law in Florida. He has advised and represented local governments as well as private property owners. Mr. Oldehoff knows how to obtain the best possible outcome for the client.

attorneys.bio:
Michael attended college and law school at the University of Michigan where he received his B.A. in 1973 with high distinction and his J.D. in 1976, magna cum laude. He was an Associate Editor of the University of Michigan Law Review and elected a member of the Order of the Coif, the law school honor society, on graduation.

Michael is a past member of the Board of Directors of the Florida Justice Association, and of the Board of Governors of the American Association for Justice (AAJ). He served in both capacities for more than ten years. attorneys.name: Alberto H. Oliveri
attorneys.practice_type: Dog Bite & Animal Attacks Lawyers in Ocala, FL
attorneys.bio:
Alberto H. Oliveri is a personal injury attorney based out of Morgan & Morgan's Ocala office. His practice focuses primarily on premises liability, slip/trip & falls, negligent/inadequate security, and animal attacks, throughout Marion, Lake, Sumter, and Levy Counties.

Mr. Oliveri was born in Punta Del Este, Uruguay, and as teen moved to New York City. He graduated with honors from the University of South Florida with a BA in Economics and Criminal Justice. He completed his undergraduate education while working full-time for RadioShack, where he received numerous result-based recognitions including three President Circle Awards. Mr. Oliveri is a "Double Bull," having earned an MBA with a concentration in Finance also from the University of South Florida.

Prior to attending law school, Mr. Oliveri worked for many years as bank officer at Bank of America, where he received numerous result-based recognitions including two national Awards of Excellence. While attending Florida A&M University College of Law, Mr. Oliveri was a legal intern for the personal injury department of a multi-state law firm, where he developed an affinity for litigation. He finished law school a semester ahead of his classmates, and immediately passed The Florida Bar Exam.

Mr. Oliveri then joined an Orlando-based law firm as a plaintiff's attorney, where he worked in the areas of personal injury and civil litigation, and where he was quickly offered a managing attorney position. He continued expanding his law knowledge by joining a Brevard County-based law firm where he represented the subrogation claims of numerous insurance companies such as State Farm, USAA, Windhaven, and also the medical collection claims of physician groups and hospital groups such as Community Health Systems.

The same multi-state law firm where Mr. Oliveri had been a legal intern many years ago then asked him to re-join their ranks. There, Mr. Oliveri focused his practice 100% in the litigation of personal injury, premises liability, and slip/trip & falls cases.

At Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Oliveri proudly represents the best-interests of his clients by employing his economics and business school analytical background, his past experience representing insurance companies, and his innate passion for personal injury litigation. Mr. Oliveri is bilingual in Spanish.

attorneys.name: James E. Olsen
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Olsen was born and raised in Orlando. After graduating from Edgewater High School (1979) he earned a BA in Economics from UCF (1984). After graduating from UCF, he attended the Levin College of Law at the University of Florida and graduated in 1986. Mr. Olsen first started the practice of law under the tutelage of his father and brother as a partner in the law firm of Olsen & Olsen. While at Olsen & Olsen, he gained invaluable experience in a wide variety of practice areas such as landlord and tenant, domestic law, contracts, appeals, bankruptcy, and association law.

Mr. Olsen has spoken at numerous events on community association law including the CAI Legal Panel, Space Coast Condominium Association, and has been a frequent guest on the “Olsen on Law” radio show in Orlando. Mr. Olsen has been certified to teach the board certification courses, and has spoken on various other topics, including but not limited to, hurricane preparedness, contract review, and other issues relating to community association law. In addition, he authored several articles regarding association matters while being employed by Wean & Malchow, P.A.

Mr. Olsen currently focuses his practice on community association law. Over the past thirty years, Mr. Olsen has gained extensive experience in the area of community association law, including general litigation, construction defect litigation, condominium, homeowners, and co-op covenant enforcement, contract review, amendments to the governing documents, timeshare and real estate matters, and general association representation issues.

Mr. Olsen has been a member of the Florida Bar since 1986.

attorneys.name: Pam Olsen Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Ocala, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Olsen has practiced law since 1992. During her law school education and throughout career she knew, if it is not about people, she is not interested. Everything about people interests Ms. Olsen from the simple details of living to the most profound. She began her law career in a skyscraper in downtown Miami representing corporate interests. Within a VERY short time, Pam knew that side of the things in the world was not for her. Pam always loved all things medical and psychological. Her next job in law honed her interest in the more human aspects of law to insurance disputes and she represented most all of the big insurance companies. While those 5 years were a wonderful training ground, Pam knew that representing the injured and the people who felt powerless against big corporate interests was the only way she could continue in the legal field. Ms. Olsen has been practicing personal injury law for the last 20 years!

Pam began her career representing the injured by working within a large law firm. She grew to love meeting such an amazing variety of people but often felt that there was so much more Pam could do for her clients if she had the advantage of more time with them. In 2004, Ms. Olsen obtained her Master of Science in Mental Health Counseling. All of these experiences led Pam Olsen to have a very strong feeling that there was an even better way to practice law and represent the rights of the injured. Pam knew clients deserved more time from their attorney, more compassion, and an attorney who truly understood and was interested in the medical and psychological issues they faced.

attorneys.bio:
Stacy Ortiz joined Morgan & Morgan in 2017 with fifteen years of workers' compensation experience.

Ms. Ortiz was born in the Bronx, New York but spent her childhood through her college years in Tampa, FL. In 1998, she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree with high honors from University of South Florida (USF) and was one of the first recipients of the USF Latino Scholarship. She then earned her law degree from the University of Florida in 2002.

Following law school, she joined a defense firm in West Palm Beach, FL where she defended self-insured employers and served as lead counsel for various companies; she practiced for the defense bar for more than ten years.

In 2013, Ms. Ortiz relocated back to the Tampa Bay Area where she began exclusively representing injured workers. Her defense background provides a unique foundation to her practice as she knows how the employers and insurance companies approach worker's compensation claims. Ms. Ortiz is dedicated to assisting injured workers in obtaining the benefits they are entitled to and deserve.

She is a member of the Florida Bar's Workers' Compensation section, Florida Workers' Advocates (FWA), Inns of Court, and is certified by the Supreme Court of Florida as a circuit mediator.

She is fluent in both English and Spanish.

attorneys.bio:
Steven Osber is a Senior Partner at Conrad & Scherer's Fort Lauderdale office with a practice concentrating primarily on commercial and business litigation. Mr. Osber's case representation ranges from routine litigation matters to highly complex litigation including partnership/shareholder disputes, commercial eviction matters, real estate litigation and construction litigation.

In addition to his extensive experience in commercial litigation, Mr. Osber has handled a number of significant cases defending businesses in negligent security claims, and he provides security training to nightclubs, bars and restaurants. Mr. Osber is also valued as a contributing litigator in the firm's general workers' compensation cases and employment law cases.

Mr. Osber's expansive litigation experience includes more than 150 state and federal jury and non-jury trials, as well as extensive binding arbitration experience. He is also proficient in appellate cases, having prepared appellate briefs on a variety of matters argued before various appellate tribunals. He is rated AV Preeminent by Martindale-Hubbell, which indicates a demonstration of the highest professional and ethical standards and is the highest rating a lawyer can receive. attorneys.name: Neil D. Overholtz
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Overholtz specializes in pharmaceutical litigation, and has successfully handled thousands of fen-phen diet drug cases. In 2001, Mr. Overholtz was a member of the successful trial team whose work resulted in a $43 Million jury verdict against the manufacturer of the diabetes drug, Rezulin, in Corpus Christi, Texas. Additionally, Mr. Overholtz has served as co-lead counsel in the In Re America Online, Inc Version 5.0 Software Litigation, MDL Docket No. 1341 (S.D. Fla), helping to negotiate a cash settlement for affected AOL members in excess of $15 Million as well as significant injunctive relief.

Mr. Overholtz is currently the co-chair of the Defective Medtronic Pacemakers and Defibrillators MDL discovery committee, and is leading the firm's efforts in national litigation. Mr. Overholtz is a member of the Plaintiff's Steering Committee in the In Re Viagra MDL litigation. He is also co-chair of the AAJ Bausch & Lomb Contact Lens Solution Litigation Group.

Mr. Overholtz limits his practice to the areas of: pharmaceutical litigation, medical device litigation, consumer class actions, wrongful death and personal injury; and is currently involved in the following matters:Vioxx, Guidant and Medtronic Defective and Recalled Defibrillators, Viagra NAION Vision Loss Cases, Bausch & Lomb ReNu Contact Lens Solution, and Medical Malpractice claims.He is currently investigating claims based on the recent Permax recall and the Zelnorm Recall by the FDA.

Mr. Overholtz received his BA in Political Science (minor in History) with Honors from the University of South Alabama and graduated from the Stetson University College of Law in 1999. Before attending college, Mr. Overholtz graduated Valedictorian from Crestview High School in Crestview, FL. While in law school, Mr. Overholtz was an associate member of the Stetson Law Review and participated in Stetson's Trial Advocacy Program which was ranked number one in country by U.S. News and World Report from 1995-1999. Mr. Overholtz received Highest Grade Honors in several classes including Torts and Property. During law school he was nominated three times to the National Dean's List of law students. In law school, Mr. Overholtz served as an Honors Intern to the Honorable Elizabeth Jenkins on the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida. From 1999-2001 Mr. Overholtz volunteered as coach for the Tate High School Mock Trial Team, who won the 2001 Florida State Championship, finishing 6th nationally.

Mr. Overholtz is currently licensed to practice before all Florida State Courts, all United States District Courts of Florida, the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Courts for the Western District of Tennessee and the District Court of Colorado. Mr. Overholtz is a member of the Escambia-Santa Rosa County Bar Association, the American Association for Justice, the Florida Justice Association, and the American Bar Association.

Mr. Overholtz is currently the co-chair of the Defective Medtronic Pacemakers and Defibrillators MDL discovery committee, and is leading the efforts in national litigation.

Mr. Overholtz limits his practice to the areas of: pharmaceutical litigation, medical device litigation, consumer class actions, wrongful death and personal injury and is currently involved in the following matters: Ford Truck Litigation, Vioxx, Bextra, Fen-Phen, Ephedra, Guidant and Medtronic Defibrillators and Medical Malpractice Claims.

Aylstock, Witkin, Kreis & Overholtz, PLLC is a Pensacola lawfirm committed to seeking justice for persons injured as a result of ingesting a defective drug or a drug subject to a FDA recall, defective devices, consumer fraud, insurance fraud, hurricane fraud, Pensacola medical negligence or Pensacola medical malpractice, bad products, or any other bad conduct. AWKOLAW.com is also a website for people seeking a Pensacola attorney or Pensacola lawyer for representation in claims related to auto accidents or wrongful death.

attorneys.name: Karen Contegiacomo Ozyjowski
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Karen C. Ozyjowski, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Spring Hill, FL
attorneys.bio:
Karen Contegiacomo Ozyjowski established Jorgensen & Ozyjowski, P.A., a family, criminal and civil litigation law firm, with partner Jacqueline L. Jorgensen, in 2006. Prior to starting the firm, Ms. Ozyjowski served as an Assistant Public Defender for the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit for the State of Florida, representing indigent people charged with crimes ranging from misdemeanors to punishable by life first degree felonies. After leaving the Public Defenders office in 2001, Ms. Ozyjwoski went on to work as an associate attorney at the civil litigation firm of Meirose & Friscia, P.A., where she represented both individual and corporate clients in areas of practice including civil litigation, insurance defense, construction law, community association law and bankruptcy. Her extensive experience in the courtroom has made the transition into family law natural.

Karen C. Ozyjowski is originally from Brooklyn, New York, but was raised in Pasco County Florida. Ms. Ozyjowski graduated from the University of Central Florida, with a B.A. in legal studies and a minor in interpersonal communications. She then earned her Juris Doctor from Hofstra University School of Law, located in Hempstead, NY in May 1999, graduating at the top 15% of her class, and receiving honors that included the Dean’s List; the Judge Edward Hart Memorial Scholarship for Excellence in Trial Advocacy and was the 1999 National Student Trial Advocacy Competition Regional Champion. Ms. Ozyjowski was then admitted to the Florida Bar in September 1999.

Since being admitted to the Florida Bar, Ms. Ozyjowski has gained extensive litigation experience handling all aspects of family, civil and criminal legal matters, including appeals. She currently devotes a large portion of her practice to marital and family law concentrating in the areas of divorce, child custody, timesharing, spousal and child support, equitable distribution, domestic violence injunctions and enforcement. In addition, to her family law work, Ms. Ozyjowski also continues to handle criminal and civil matters including but not limited to, foreclosures, contract disputes, construction defects, construction liens, juvenile charges, DUI’s and all other criminal offenses.

attorneys.name: Mark J. O’Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
After beginning his career at the end of the last century as a prosecutor in Miami, Florida, Attorney Mark J. O’Brien started his own law firm on January 1, 2003. After nearly thirty years, Mr. O’Brien has expanded his firm beyond himself. Now named O’Brien Hatfield, Mr. O’Brien’s law firm has seven lawyers, one paralegal, four legal assistants, two private investigators (a retired IRS CID special agent and a retired DEA special agent), one sentencing mitigation specialist (a former United States Probation Officer), and numerous third-party experts who assist on a case-by-case basis.

Mark J. O’Brien, Managing Partner

Attorney Mark J. O’Brien is a nationally recognized federal criminal defense attorney with nearly thirty years of experience in criminal courts all throughout the country. After beginning his professional career as a Miami, Florida prosecutor in the late 1990’s, Mr. O’Brien organized his own law firm in 2002 based upon the professional lessons he learned to that point in his life with the goal defending those accused of federal and state crimes with a mix of old school values and new school ideas. He is the firm’s managing partner.

During his first decade in private practice from 2002 to 2012, Mr. O’Brien defended individuals and corporations charged with federal crimes throughout federal criminal courts in Florida. From 2012 to the present, Mr. O’Brien has accepted the defense of clients charged in federal criminal courts throughout the entire country, in addition to his previously established federal criminal defense practice in all federal courts in Florida. Case after case, success after success, in federal court after federal court, all throughout the country, has resulted in a growing legacy. To put it simply, Mr. O’Brien wins and, as a result, he is a lawyer in demand.

Mr. O’Brien is a licensed member of the Bar of the State of Florida (1998), the Bar of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (1998), and the Bar of the State of Montana (2023). He has practiced federal criminal defense as a member or a pro hac vice member of the following federal appellate and district courts:

Mr. O’Brien also handles Child Pornography Possession Offenses, Child Pornography Production Offenses, Child Pornography Transportation Offenses, Child Pornography Distribution Offenses, Child Pornography Receipt Offenses, Sex Trafficking Offenses, Conspiracy to Commit a Federal Sex Crime, and all other Federal Sex Crime Offenses. Mr. O’Brien also represents those charged with Drug Crimes, Gun Crimes, Conspiracy to Commit Drug and Gun Crimes, and all other General Federal Criminal Defense matters. He also handles Federal Grand Jury Investigations and Pre-File Criminal Investigations, including but not limited to Targets of a Federal Grand Jury Investigation, Subjects of a Federal Grand Jury Investigation, Witnesses of a Federal Grand Jury Investigation, and SEC, FBI, HSI, DEA, ATF, CIA, and NSI Investigations. The bottom line is if you are charged or being investigated for a federal crime, Mr. O’Brien will defend you.

Mr. O’Brien realized early on in his career that the people best positioned to defend a federal defendant are those individuals who once investigated and prosecuted federal defendants. It is important to stay one step ahead of the prosecution and their investigators and what better way to accomplish this goal than by hiring people who once did it?

Mr. O’Brien’s federal criminal defense team includes a former United States Marine Intelligence Officer and a retired United States Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) federal special agent. This team member has participated in all aspects of narco-trafficking law enforcement, including surveillance operations, wiretap operations, and arrest operations at the state and federal level. While a federal agent, he managed macro and micro narco-trafficking, money laundering, and weapons investigations at the state, national, and worldwide level. Over his career, he participated in world deployments, wherein he advised foreign nationals on the investigation of narco-traffickers, money launderers, and weapons distributors. He finished his career in the State of Florida, wherein he retired after twenty-five years with the DEA as a Group Supervisor. He understands how federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies and prosecutors operate nationwide.

Mr. O’Brien’s federal criminal defense team also includes a retired Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations Division, (IRS CID) federal special agent, who is also a certified fraud examiner and a forensic accountant. This team member provides invaluable knowledge and expertise in all the firm’s white-collar fraud and money laundering cases. While he was with the IRS CID, he was a special agent, group manager, assistant chief and executive officer in New York City, Denver, and Philadelphia. While a special agent, he investigated and prosecuted drug cartels and organized crime members such as the New York, New England, and Philadelphia Mafia, Frank Lucas (later played by Denzel Washington in the movie about his life American Gangster), and Nicki Barnes.

Mr. O’Brien’s federal criminal defense team also includes a former Senior Supervisory United States Federal Probation Officer who served the federal judges for over twenty-five years. He has a wide-ranging background related to the United States Sentencing Guidelines and criminal statutory penalties. Over the course of his career, he prepared and analyzed nearly a thousand presentence investigation reports for accuracy and completeness (including those prepared by subordinate probation officers). As a member of the law firm, and no other, he uses the knowledge and expertise he gained during his federal government career to assist firm clients in the pre-plea, pre-sentencing, and post-sentencing phases of their federal criminal cases.

Mr. O’Brien grew up and attended college in New York, attended law school near Philadelphia, and started his career as a prosecutor in Miami. As a result, there is almost nothing Mr. O’Brien has not seen, done, or dealt with in or out of a criminal courtroom over the course of his career. New York raised, Philly tough, and Miami tested, Mr. O’Brien brings nearly thirty years of criminal court experience to those accused of crimes in federal criminal courts throughout Florida, Massachusetts, and now the entire nation. Mr. O’Brien has the resources, both in his team and in his experience and his training, to tackle your federal criminal case and accomplish the only objective that matters: Win.

Thus, if you are being investigated and/or prosecuted by federal agents and/or federal prosecutors and are need of a federal criminal defense attorney – and a federal criminal defense team – anywhere in the United States of America, all Mr. O’Brien needs is a Wi-Fi Password and a plane to defend you.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
After beginning his career at the end of the last century as a prosecutor in Miami, Florida, Attorney Mark J. O’Brien started his own law firm on January 1, 2003. After nearly thirty years, Mr. O’Brien has expanded his firm beyond himself. Now named O’Brien Hatfield, Mr. O’Brien’s law firm has seven lawyers, one paralegal, four legal assistants, two private investigators (a retired IRS CID special agent and a retired DEA special agent), one sentencing mitigation specialist (a former United States Probation Officer), and numerous third-party experts who assist on a case-by-case basis.

Mark J. O’Brien, Managing Partner

Attorney Mark J. O’Brien is a nationally recognized federal criminal defense attorney with nearly thirty years of experience in criminal courts all throughout the country. After beginning his professional career as a Miami, Florida prosecutor in the late 1990’s, Mr. O’Brien organized his own law firm in 2002 based upon the professional lessons he learned to that point in his life with the goal defending those accused of federal and state crimes with a mix of old school values and new school ideas. He is the firm’s managing partner.

During his first decade in private practice from 2002 to 2012, Mr. O’Brien defended individuals and corporations charged with federal crimes throughout federal criminal courts in Florida. From 2012 to the present, Mr. O’Brien has accepted the defense of clients charged in federal criminal courts throughout the entire country, in addition to his previously established federal criminal defense practice in all federal courts in Florida. Case after case, success after success, in federal court after federal court, all throughout the country, has resulted in a growing legacy. To put it simply, Mr. O’Brien wins and, as a result, he is a lawyer in demand.

Mr. O’Brien is a licensed member of the Bar of the State of Florida (1998), the Bar of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts (1998), and the Bar of the State of Montana (2023). attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Anne O’Connor is dedicated to helping clients navigate the complex workers’ compensation system.

Originally from the suburbs of Chicago, Anne graduated with a bachelor’s degree from the University of Illinois. Before beginning her law studies, Anne worked as a district manager for a global grocery chain. It was during this time she learned firsthand how critical, but yet undervalued, employees can be.

Deciding to pursue a more fulfilling career, Anne enrolled in law school and while working full time graduated cum laude from the University of Illinois at Chicago School of Law. As a former college hockey player and corporate manager, Anne understands the work required to obtain results against large insurance companies and national conglomerates. What Anne enjoys most about representing injured workers is being able to provide answers and finding successful resolutions.

In her free time, you can find Anne exploring Tampa, on long walks with her dog and husband, or on the beach reading a book.

attorneys.name: Seth Pachter
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
From the time I interned in Law School at a domestic violence litigation clinic I realized that I wanted to use my legal career as a method to help those in need. I found it extremely rewarding to represent often terrified victims of domestic violence obtain an order of protection against their abuser by helping them fill out the necessary legal documentation, and to stand beside them in front of the judge. I was there not only for my legal knowledge, but to be a source of moral encouragement and support. To the end of helping those in need, I am privileged to have for over a decade represented victims of the negligence of others. It is an honor to help them through their difficult times and to make sure that they receive the compensation they so justly deserve for the hardships they have had to endure.

While monetary compensation will not heal their injuries it does make their hardships easier to face. Throughout my career I have assisted numerous victims of the negligence of others get just compensation. I am a lifetime member of the Million Dollars Advocate Forum. Its members have achieved a trial verdict or settlement in the amount of one million dollars or more. The organization was started in 1993 and has over 3000 members, yet fewer than 1% of lawyers in the United States are members. The purpose of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum is to recognize the accomplishments of trial lawyers who have achieved large recoveries for their clients.

The firms core values are a great fit for my personality and my work ethic as a personal injury attorney. I fight to win for our clients because without proper representation zealously advocating for them, they would be left at the mercy of the whims of insurance companies. It is my responsibility as a personal injury attorney to make sure that our clients can rest easy knowing that as they deal with their injuries, they have an advocate who will be there to stand up for them. Going through a traumatic injury is difficult enough without having to worry about whether there will be someone there to fight for you. So, I fight to win so that those injured through no fault of their own can better cope with their often life changing physical ailments.

On the personal side, I love spending time with my wife, Jeweleen, and my two children and my stepchildren. We enjoy going to the theater to see the various touring plays, or a simple night out consisting of a meal at our favorite restaurant and a movie at the local cinema. We particularly enjoy science fiction or action adventure movies. We get excited for the release of the latest Marvel or DC film. I also enjoy sitting back on the couch or going to the stadium to watch baseball, football, or basketball games.

attorneys.name: Danielle Padilla
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Maitland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Danielle Padilla has been working in the legal field since 2010 and brings a unique, well-rounded perspective to her role as an Associate Attorney at Gans Law. With experience on both sides of the justice system, Danielle combines academic excellence, real-world law enforcement insight, and a deep commitment to protecting her clients’ constitutional rights.

Danielle earned her Juris Doctorate from Florida A&M University College of Law, where she distinguished herself academically and served as a Teaching Assistant for Evidence. She excelled in key courses such as Criminal Procedure and Florida Constitutional Law, and further strengthened her legal foundation by earning an additional college degree in Criminal Justice. She completed her undergraduate studies in Legal Studies at the University of Central Florida (UCF).

Before becoming an attorney, Danielle was sworn in as a Police Officer in 2010, serving her community for several years. During her time in law enforcement, she handled investigations ranging from misdemeanors to serious felony offenses, conducting interviews, gathering evidence, and working closely with prosecutors. She also received specialized training in Interview and Interrogation techniques and earned a certification in Mental Health Crisis identification. This background gives her a trained eye for spotting critical errors in police investigations, including violations of Miranda rights—skills that now directly benefit her clients in criminal defense cases.

While completing her undergraduate degree, Danielle proposed a Youth Diversion Program designed to help young individuals accused of underage drinking avoid long-term consequences. Her proposal was selected by the former State Attorney and remains implemented within the circuit today. Danielle is proud to have her name attached to a program that continues to guide youth toward positive outcomes and second chances.

Danielle is bilingual, allowing her to serve a broader segment of the community with clarity and compassion. Outside of the courtroom, she enjoys spending quality time with her family and children and stays active through boxing, weightlifting, and jump-rope cardio sessions.

Attorney Padilla believes the justice system is a swinging pendulum—and she is committed to working tirelessly to make sure it swings in her clients’ favor.

attorneys.name: Mauricio Padilla, ESQ
attorneys.practice_type: State and Federal Criminal Defense Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mauricio Padilla is a criminal and civil trial attorney who has spent the last two decades battling for his clients in some of the nation's most notable cases. His practice mainly focuses on state and federal criminal defense. His civil practice involves catastrophic injury, wrongful death, negligent security/premises liability claims as well as medical malpractice cases. He represented Derick Medina in what the media referred to as "The Facebook Murder", he represented Sigfredo Garcia in the "Dan Markel murder" in Tallahassee Florida. He recently represented Dedrick Williams in the murder case of entertainer XXXTentacion.

Mr. Padilla started his career working for Dade County Legal Aid helping those that could not afford private counsel. After two years he was hired by a boutique Coral Gables Law firm that specializes in wrongful death and medical malpractice. At that firm, he handled a variety of catastrophic injury cases including aircraft disaster cases, and litigated a medical malpractice case that resulted in a jury verdict of more than 6 million dollars. Throughout his career, Mr. Padilla has represented injured clients who have been awarded more than 30 million dollars in jury verdicts, and or arbitration awards.

Early in his career, Mr. Padilla had the life-changing experience of being part of the first Emmaus Medical Mission that was founded by Dr. Landy Silva and traveled 11 times to Guatemala to help doctors and nurses bring medical relief to impoverished areas of Guatemala. Mr. Padilla is vice president of Blind Warriors Inc. a nonprofit he helped create along with blind jiujitsu black belt Carlos Alvarez. The mission of this nonprofit is to teach jujitsu to the visually impaired.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Mauricio Padilla is a criminal and civil trial attorney who has spent the last two decades battling for his clients in some of the nation's most notable cases. His practice mainly focuses on state and federal criminal defense. His civil practice involves catastrophic injury, wrongful death, negligent security/premises liability claims as well as medical malpractice cases. He represented Derick Medina in what the media referred to as "The Facebook Murder", he represented Sigfredo Garcia in the "Dan Markel murder" in Tallahassee Florida. He recently represented Dedrick Williams in the murder case of entertainer XXXTentacion.

Mr. Padilla started his career working for Dade County Legal Aid helping those that could not afford private counsel. After two years he was hired by a boutique Coral Gables Law firm that specializes in wrongful death and medical malpractice. At that firm, he handled a variety of catastrophic injury cases including aircraft disaster cases, and litigated a medical malpractice case that resulted in a jury verdict of more than 6 million dollars. Throughout his career, Mr. Padilla has represented injured clients who have been awarded more than 30 million dollars in jury verdicts, and or arbitration awards.

Early in his career, Mr. Padilla had the life-changing experience of being part of the first Emmaus Medical Mission that was founded by Dr. Landy Silva and traveled 11 times to Guatemala to help doctors and nurses bring medical relief to impoverished areas of Guatemala. Mr. Padilla is vice president of Blind Warriors Inc. a nonprofit he helped create along with blind jiujitsu black belt Carlos Alvarez. The mission of this nonprofit is to teach jujitsu to the visually impaired.

His goal is to bring value by using 40+ years of experience to find cost-effective solutions to business and personal problems.
