attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Overview:

Licensed for over 20 years, Eduardo Rodriguez is an experienced Orlando personal injury attorney and Partner at The Law Offices of Pardy & Rodriguez, P.A. - Empowered By Diversity

Born in the Dominican Republic and raised in Puerto Rico, Rodriguez graduated with honors from Strayer College in Washington, D.C.. He then furthered his studies by attending law schools at the Pontifical Catholic University in Ponce, Puerto Rico and Loyola University Chicago School of Law in Chicago, Illinois.

Mr. Rodriquez became licensed to practice in Puerto Rico in 1996, as well as Florida in 1999. Speaking both fluent Spanish and English, Mr. Rodriquez is able to offer services to a large width of clientele. Community involvement is something that holds great importance to Mr. Rodriguez as he actively serves as a member of the Florida Justice Association and the Hispanic Bar Association, as well as a Trustee at the Homeowners Association.

Mr. Rodriguez is passionate about representing injured Florida victims in a variety of personal injury cases and has done so successfully for over 20 years. To learn more about his services, he invites you to join him for a free consultation.

Interests:

His interests include hunting in Florida, especially waterfowl. He also finds interest in reading biographies and business journals, as there is always something new to learn from the teachings and records of others. His interests often take him to new places as he enjoys foreign travel, and broadening his horizons to new cities, cultures, and communities. His travels provide him with the chance to meet new individuals and hear their stories as he is personable and enjoys helping others. He's also able to implement these new cities and cultures into his recipes at home as he loves cooking and collecting cookbooks as well.

attorneys.name: Frank R. Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Disputes, Toxic Torts Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Frank R. Rodriguez is an experienced trial lawyer who specializes in representing corporate and individual clients as both Plaintiffs and Defendants in commercial disputes. Mr. Rodriguez’s practice has been concentrated in the handling of commercial litigation, including class actions, and arbitrations in the following areas: securities, business torts, bank fraud and abuse, contract disputes, professional liability, including lawsuits involving corporate directors and officers and accountants, employment disputes, secured transactions, creditors' rights, and toxic torts. He offers vast experience in litigation arising under federal banking regulations and ERISA. Mr. Rodriguez is listed “AV” by Martindale Hubbell’s lawyer rating service which is its highest rating for professional skill and ethical standards.

Mr. Rodriguez focuses his practice on bringing high-stakes, document-intensive cases to trial; his trial experience includes cases in federal and state courts throughout Florida and in federal courts all over the Country. He has tried cases before juries, judges, arbitrators, and administrative agencies and has been a FINRA arbitrator himself. Mr. Rodriguez has represented Fortune 500 companies, major insurance companies and their insureds, and large financial institutions as well as the FDIC in addition to individuals and smaller business entities. He has secured several multi-million dollar awards for his clients including jury verdicts of $18 Million (professional liability claim against directors and officers of a failed bank), $16 Million (a medical malpractice case against a hospital and surgeon), $14.5 Million (accounting malpractice claim against Ernst & Young) and $5.5 Million (breach of oral distribution agreement claim against Thomson Consumer Electronics), as well as successfully defended clients in cases where multiple millions of dollars were sought. Mr. Rodriguez has also obtained over $100 million in settlements for clients, including a $59 Million dollar settlement with DuPont stemming from a product liability claims. More recently, Mr. Rodriguez was one of the lead trial lawyers in a class action against Merrill Lynch that was settled, pending court approval, for $25 Million. His experience and success as a plaintiffs’ trial lawyer have given Mr. Rodriguez an insight and perspective that makes him a particularly innovative, resourceful and effective defense counsel.

Mr. Rodriguez is a member of the Florida Bar (admitted 1982), the Trial Bar of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida, a member of several United States Courts of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Rodriguez is bilingual and a member of the Cuban-American Bar Association. Mr. Rodriguez is a graduate of the University of Florida (B.A., 1978; J.D. 1981).

Awards and Honors

Honors

AV Rated, Martindale Hubbell

Jose Angel Rodriguez was born in New York City, and then did his primary schooling in Kissimmee, Florida. Mr. Rodriguez attended the University of Central Florida and earned his degree in Legal Studies in 1999, and then attended Nova Southeastern University Shepard Law Center where he earned his Juris Doctorate Degree in 2003.

After graduating from law school, Mr. Rodriguez then worked as an associate at several different law firms practicing in the areas of family law and worker’s compensation. In 2019, Mr. Rodriguez became a Florida Certified Family Law Mediator. In 2010, Mr. Rodriguez founded Jose A. Rodriguez Law, P.L. and provides services in the areas of family law, wills and family law mediation.

Mr. Rodriguez has extensive experience representing clients in divorces, child custody issues, parenting issues, property division, alimony, modification matters, child relocation, domestic violence injunctions and paternity. Mr. Rodriguez understands the importance of being compassionate, but always prepares to provide aggressive representation.

Mr. Rodriguez is licensed to practice in State and is a member of the Orange County Bar Association. Mr. Rodriguez provides legal and mediation services all throughout central Florida, including Orange, Osceola, Seminole, Lake and Polk Counties.

attorneys.name: Jose Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Claims Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jose's practice focuses on insurance claims, which include property, life, and disability claims. Jose is also experienced in civil litigation and personal injury. His mission is to process claims efficiently and for the highest possible recovery.

Jose comes from an extensive background in public service. Prior to practicing law, Jose was a congressional affairs manager at FEMA, where he managed claims from hurricane Irma. His expertise in government affairs comes from his experience working at the US House of Representatives as Director of Operations for a local congressman. Jose's community service has been recognized with a special certificate of congressional recognition.

This passion for public service is what inspired Jose to become an attorney. He obtained his law degree from Florida A&M University and his bachelor's degree in Paralegal Studies from Nova Southeastern University. He is a member of the Florida Bar and the American Civil Liberties Union.

A native of Puerto Rico, Jose is a proud husband and father of two. He enjoys spending his free time with his family, playing basketball, and volunteering at his church.

attorneys.name: Sabellys Silvestrini Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sabellys Silvestrini was born in Ponce, Puerto Rico.

She graduated with a Bachelor’s Degree in Forensic Psychology from the University of Puerto Rico. In 2015, she earned her Juris Doctor degree from the Pontifical Catholic University of Puerto Rico School of Law.

In 2016, Ms. Silvestrini relocated to Florida, where she discovered her passion for immigration law. She began her legal career assisting immigrants in matters including asylum applications, family-based petitions, U visas, VAWA petitions, appeals before the Board of Immigration Appeals, Cuban Adjustment Act applications, and removal defense before the Immigration Court.

She has represented clients in USCIS interviews, immigration court hearings, and proceedings before ICE in multiple jurisdictions across the United States.

Ms. Silvestrini’s personal experience of leaving her home country in search of new opportunities has allowed her to connect deeply with her clients and understand the challenges they face. She is committed to guiding and protecting them during moments of vulnerability, ensuring they have strong legal representation as they pursue a better future in the United States.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Karen Rodriguez, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Driving under the Influence Lawyers in Clermont, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mrs. Rodriguez was born in Ponce, Puerto Rico, but made Florida her permanent home since 1997. After finishing her undergraduate studies with concentrations in Business Management, Mrs. Rodriguez completed a Master's Degree in Organizational Management, where she graduated with High Honors and in the top 5% of her class.

Mrs. Rodriguez attended law school at the Florida A&M University (FAMU), College of Law, located in Orlando. While in law school, Mrs. Rodriguez was invited to become a member of FAMU's Law Review. Mrs. Rodriguez graduated cum laude from FAMU's College of Law and ranked in the top 12% of the total class.

After graduation, Mrs. Rodriguez worked, as a prosecutor, at the State Attorney's Office for the Fifth Judicial Circuit in both Marion and Lake County. Mrs. Rodriguez also worked as a prosecutor at the State Attorney's Office for the Ninth Judicial Circuit. There, she handled hundreds of county cases, including traffic and misdemeanors. Mrs. Rodriguez litigated many jury trials, with a high conviction rate.

Mrs. Rodriguez litigated numerous Motions to Suppress in DUI and Drug cases, and handled many court proceedings to include Arraignments, Initial Appearances, Pre-trial Conferences, Plea Hearings, Violation of Probation Hearings, Bond Hearings, and other proceedings, as applicable. In addition to handling part of a docket for her division, she was also in charge of handling Appeals for her cases, and answered appellate briefs on trial cases, as well as cases where defendants were asking for post-conviction relief.

In addition to being the President of The Law Office of Karen Rodriguez, P.A., Attorney Rodriguez is also a Florida Supreme Court Certified Mediator.

Mrs. Rodriguez strongly believes that every person deserves to have representation and considers herself to be an advocate for those in need of help. She has volunteered for the Legal Aid Society, where she has participated in assisting individuals in need of legal services. Mrs. Rodriguez believes that evaluating all of the events leading to an arrest is imminent in a criminal case, and she will look at every detail of your case to aggressively work towards a resolution. Mrs. Rodriguez considers herself to be a litigator and will fight for your rights in court, regardless of the effort and time required.

attorneys.name: Gerardo J. Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Stuart, FL
attorneys.bio:
Gerardo J. Rodriguez-Albizu is a seasoned attorney who represents domestic and international clients at both the trial and appellate levels. Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu has litigated a wide variety of cases, including matters under the federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act (RICO), complex commercial matters, international copyright infringement, Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act (FSIA) cases, foreign asset seizure, international commercial arbitration, partnership break up disputes, theft of trade secrets, disputes involving banks and financial institutions (including claims under Regulation X), commercial and residential landlord-tenant disputes, among other matters. Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu also has experience with matters pending or involving foreign jurisdictions, including Central and South America, the Dominican Republic, and the Turks and Caicos Islands. Drawing from his extensive litigation experience, Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu assists clients with their business law needs including forming new entities, drafting and negotiating joint venture agreements, shareholder agreements, operating agreements, and buy/sell agreements, negotiating franchise agreements, and various other contractual agreements. As a member of The Fund, Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu also has experience in representing U.S. and international clients with their real estate needs. Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu’s experience includes assisting clients in all facets of a real estate transaction – from negotiating the purchase and sale agreement, to conducting the closing and issuing title insurance. In this regard Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu possesses experience in handling construction to permanent financing transactions, transactions involving national lenders, and all cash deals. Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu also assists clients with drafting and negotiating both commercial and residential leases, either on behalf of landlords or prospective tenants. Throughout his legal career Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu has represented a wide spectrum of clients, including banks, small business owners, real estate developers, individuals, and mid-size companies. Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu has received numerous accolades from both clients and the local community in recognition of his legal services, including the “Most Effective Lawyers” award from the South Florida Daily Business Review and the “Outside Counsel of the Year” award from Areas USA, Inc. From 2016 through 2018, Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu was designated a “Rising Star” by Super Lawyers; a distinction bestowed on only 2.5% of all Florida attorneys under the age of 40. Prior to starting Rodriguez-Albizu Law, P.A., Mr. Rodriguez-Albizu worked at the international law firms Greenberg Traurig, P.A., and Diaz, Reus, and Targ, LLP.

attorneys.name: John Rogers
attorneys.practice_type: Motor Vehicle Crash Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
John obtained a B.S. in economics from the University of Pittsburgh in 2002 when he graduated magna cum laude. While attending Chicago-Kent College of Law, John was recognized as a Board of Directors Scholar and externed with a Federal Magistrate Judge. He graduated in 2009, with honors, and began his legal career at a national defense firm specializing in the defense of medical malpractice and other forms of catastrophic loss litigation. There he represented hospitals, physicians, business owners, and long-term care facilities facing personal injury litigation. In 2012 John accepted the opportunity to spearhead a new Pensacola office for that firm, which he grew over the span of several years.

Since 2015 John has worked exclusively on behalf of individuals injured as the result of another's negligence. His caseload has included motor vehicle crash, premises liability, medical malpractice, nursing home, assisted living facility, and negligent security cases. Over this time, he has obtained numerous seven-figure settlements on behalf of his clients and has gained substantial first-chair trial experience. In November 2021, on behalf of his clients, John obtained a jury verdict that ranked among Florida's top car crash litigation verdicts of the year.

At The Watson Firm, John is able to draw upon his years of experience defending corporations and insurance companies to his clients' advantage by providing sound advice and guidance through all phases of the claims handling and litigation processes.

attorneys.name: Ty G. Roland
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ty G. Roland, senior partner, co-founded the firm in 2004 when he combined his expanding personal injury practice with Frank Aloia’s business and real estate legal practice – a move many in the legal community considered risky. At the time, Roland was already very comfortable staring down risk.

Raised in a New Jersey household long on values and service to community, at 18, Roland left the comfort of those familiar surroundings and headed south 1,200 miles to Miami to attend The U. This would be the first in a long line of risks Roland would take in his life without flinching.

Roland’s injury and wrongful death practice grew steadily during the 2000s in large part based on this reputation to do what many other attorneys judged as too risky, namely going to trial. In an area of the law where the attorney does not get a fee if the injured party does not receive a cash award, the pressure is very often high to settle the case quickly and move on. Going to trial is a risk — especially against a giant corporation or insurance company where time and money are on their side.

The willingness of Roland to say, “See you in court,” and to back it up year after year has turned risk into reward for his many clients. Knowing that Roland, and partner Evan Lubell, will take on the risk of a trial to get justice and fair compensation for their clients regularly leads to a successful non-trial settlement. Should a case of Roland’s go to trial, as it did in December 2016 for a mother seeking justice for an electrocuted son, that “risk” produced a $23 million judgment.

Awards & Distinctions

Ty Roland is a stand-out in the legal community and has been recognized for his significant impact. In 2021, Roland joined the ranks of The National Trial Lawyers. Roland was named as the Top 100 Civil Plaintiff Trial Lawyers in Florida and is recognized in The Top 25 Motor Vehicle Trial Lawyers in Florida. Roland was honored with the AV-Preeminent 2021 Peer Rated for Highest Level of Professional Excellence by Martindale-Hubbell. At the close of 2020, Ty Roland was named “The Trial Attorney of Year” by the Southwest Florida chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates. In 2020, ALOIA | ROLAND | LUBELL was named the 2020 Gulfshore Magazine Best of Business in three categories: “Best Litigation Law Firm,” “Best Corporate & Business Law Firm” and “Best Commercial Real Estate Law Firm.”

Involvement & Education

Roland is deeply committed to serving his profession and the community at large. Since 1995, he’s been a member of the Florida Bar and is a member of the Trial Lawyers Section of the Bar. He’s admitted to practice in the Supreme Court of the United States of America, all State Courts of Florida, and in the Federal Courts of Florida’s Middle District.

Roland is a trailblazer in various professional associations. He has served in multiple leadership roles for the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA) Southwest Florida Chapter and the Calusa Chapter of the American Inns of Court. He’s active in the Florida Justice Association as an Eagle Member, the Southwest Florida Justice Association, the Lee County Bar Association, the American Board of Trial Advocates, and Roland is former chairman of the Florida Bar Grievance Committee of the 20th Judicial Circuit, Group D and continues to serve the committee. Furthermore, he’s active and supportive of various local community organizations and schools. Roland was conferred a Juris Doctor at Nova Southeastern Shepard Broad College of Law and holds a Bachelor of Science from the University of Miami. He has achieved Board Certification in Civil Trial by the Florida Bar and joins the less than 1% of all civil trial attorneys in Florida to earn the distinction.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Ty G. Roland, senior partner, co-founded the firm in 2004 when he combined his expanding personal injury practice with Frank Aloia’s business and real estate legal practice – a move many in the legal community considered risky. At the time, Roland was already very comfortable staring down risk.

Raised in a New Jersey household long on values and service to community, at 18, Roland left the comfort of those familiar surroundings and headed south 1,200 miles to Miami to attend The U. This would be the first in a long line of risks Roland would take in his life without flinching.

Roland’s injury and wrongful death practice grew steadily during the 2000s in large part based on this reputation to do what many other attorneys judged as too risky, namely going to trial. In an area of the law where the attorney does not get a fee if the injured party does not receive a cash award, the pressure is very often high to settle the case quickly and move on. Going to trial is a risk — especially against a giant corporation or insurance company where time and money are on their side.

The willingness of Roland to say, “See you in court,” and to back it up year after year has turned risk into reward for his many clients. Knowing that Roland, and partner Evan Lubell, will take on the risk of a trial to get justice and fair compensation for their clients regularly leads to a successful non-trial settlement. Should a case of Roland’s go to trial, as it did in December 2016 for a mother seeking justice for an electrocuted son, that “risk” produced a $23 million judgment.

Awards & Distinctions

Ty Roland is a stand-out in the legal community and has been recognized for his significant impact. In 2021, Roland joined the ranks of The National Trial Lawyers. Roland was named as the Top 100 Civil Plaintiff Trial Lawyers in Florida and is recognized in The Top 25 Motor Vehicle Trial Lawyers in Florida. Roland was honored with the AV-Preeminent 2021 Peer Rated for Highest Level of Professional Excellence by Martindale-Hubbell. At the close of 2020, Ty Roland was named “The Trial Attorney of Year” by the Southwest Florida chapter of the American Board of Trial Advocates. In 2020, ALOIA | ROLAND | LUBELL was named the 2020 Gulfshore Magazine Best of Business in three categories: “Best Litigation Law Firm,” “Best Corporate & Business Law Firm” and “Best Commercial Real Estate Law Firm.”

Involvement & Education

Roland is deeply committed to serving his profession and the community at large. Since 1995, he’s been a member of the Florida Bar and is a member of the Trial Lawyers Section of the Bar. He’s admitted to practice in the Supreme Court of the United States of America, all State Courts of Florida, and in the Federal Courts of Florida’s Middle District.

Roland is a trailblazer in various professional associations. He has served in multiple leadership roles for the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA) Southwest Florida Chapter and the Calusa Chapter of the American Inns of Court. He’s active in the Florida Justice Association as an Eagle Member, the Southwest Florida Justice Association, the Lee County Bar Association, the American Board of Trial Advocates, and Roland is former chairman of the Florida Bar Grievance Committee of the 20th Judicial Circuit, Group D and continues to serve the committee. Furthermore, he’s active and supportive of various local community organizations and schools. Roland was conferred a Juris Doctor at Nova Southeastern Shepard Broad College of Law and holds a Bachelor of Science from the University of Miami. He has achieved Board Certification in Civil Trial by the Florida Bar and joins the less than 1% of all civil trial attorneys in Florida to earn the distinction.

attorneys.name: William C. Roof
attorneys.practice_type: Trust & Probate Administration Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
William Colby Roof is a practicing estate planning attorney and experienced, fourth-generation trial litigator practicing in the areas of probate, trust, and guardianship dispute litigation, as well as will, probate, trust, and guardianship administration.

William’s goal is to provide peace of mind for clients who seek estate planning, probate, trust, and guardianship services by anticipating the disputes and issues that may arise long before they actually do. And when disputes do arise, William will fearlessly go to battle for his clients.

William received his bachelor’s degree from Florida State University, and both his JD and MBA with from the University of Florida—all with cum laude Honors. During law school, he was a member and officer of UF Law’s Trial Team, a member and editor of the Journal of Technology Law & Policy, and a member of the Business Moot Court team.

William has practiced at one of the nation’s largest civil, jury trial law firms where he took lawsuits all the way to jury verdicts. He has also practiced for a specialist law firm that negotiated and handled eight-figure disputes for one of the nation’s largest multinational general contractors. Over the course of his career, William has negotiated hundreds of settlement contracts and recovered more than $18 million for his clients.

William has represented clients in at least fourteen Florida courts, as well as the federal courts in Ocala and Orlando, Florida. The Florida Estate Firm is dedicated to helping Orlando and other Central Florida residents with their estate planning needs, as well as the needs of those facing probate, trust, or guardianship dispute litigation or uncontested administration. We serve the greater Central Florida area, including: Orlando, Winter Park, Windermere, The Villages, Altamonte Springs, Clermont, Kissimmee, Lake Nona, and other neighboring areas.

attorneys.name: George D. Root III Esquire
attorneys.practice_type: Condominium Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
George Root is an attorney in the Tampa office of Stockham Law Group, P.A. He focuses his practice on providing general counsel and litigation services for community association throughout Florida. His services as general counsel include deed restriction violation enforcement, delinquent assessment collection, compliance, preservation of governing documents, revitalization of governing documents, interpretation of governing documents, risk management, litigation, creditor bankruptcy services, board meeting attendance, board certification courses, and a myriad of other community association legal needs.

Prior to joining the Stockham Law Group, Mr. Root worked for over ten years providing general counsel services to community associations in Florida. Mr. Root is actively involved in several chapters of the Community Association Institute. Mr. Root spends time developing and teaching board certification courses for community associations and continuing education units for property managers.

Mr. Root attended law school at the Stetson University College of Law where he was a member of the school's Trial Team and a Stetson Ambassador. Prior to law school, Mr. Root spent almost five years serving in the United States Army after attending Saint Leo University.

attorneys.name: Eric S. Rosen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Davie, FL
attorneys.bio:
Eric Rosen has secured more than $100 million in jury verdicts for his clients in situations including wrongful death, personal injury, and catastrophic incidents.

Along with his law school background and work in both public and private practice, Eric is also a graduate of one of the nation's top trial schools, the Trial Lawyers College, founded by Gerry Spence. This is an intensive three-and-a-half-week trial skills program held in Dubois, Wyoming, by top litigators and trial instructors from around the country. Eric thoroughly studied new trial procedures there, including jury selection, opening statements, direct and cross-examination, and closing arguments. He continues to utilize those skills today.

Working as an accident lawyer in Fort Lauderdale, Eric has taught trial skills to attorneys nationwide while serving as a faculty member at the National Institute of Trial Advocacy. Additionally, he spends time educating high school students and law students in trial practice, product liability, and personal injury law.

attorneys.name: Jonathan H. Rosenthal
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal & Civil Litigation Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jon Rosenthal earned his Juris Doctor degree, cum laude, from the University of Miami School of Law in 1997. While there he served as a member of the editorial board of the University of Miami Law Review, and as Chairman of the Law Activity Fee Allocation Committee. Also while in law school, Jon clerked for several Miami law firms, as well as for the Honorable Joseph Nesbitt of Florida's Third District Court of Appeal. Jon holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in English from the State University of New York at Albany.

Jon is a Partner and Vice President of Malman, Malman & Rosenthal, with which he has been associated since 1997. He has extensive experience in both state and federal courts in matters including federal sentencing, white collar criminal defense, appellate practice, criminal law and civil litigation. Jon has also represented clients before various administrative agencies. Jon has been awarded the coveted "AV" peer review rating by Martindale-Hubbell, widely considered the foremost authoritative resource for information on the worldwide legal profession. This is the highest rating awarded by Martindale-Hubbell, and is truly a distinction and a source of great pride.

As an Adjunct Professor of Law on the faculty of Nova Southeastern University, Jon teaches second and third year law students in matters relating to sentencing issues, the Federal Sentencing Guidelines, and criminal law. Since 2008 Jon has been a contributing author to a treatise on Federal Sentencing, Practice Under the Federal Sentencing Guidelines, published semi-annually by Aspen Publishers, Inc. In 2010 Jon was appointed to serve on the International Committee of the Holocaust Documentation and Education Center and Museum in Hollywood, Florida. Jon also volunteers time serving as a judge in various mock trial and moot court competitions at both the University of Miami and Nova law schools.

In addition to his Florida admission, Jon is admitted to practice in the State of New Jersey, and before the Federal District Courts for the Northern, Southern and Middle Districts of Florida, the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York, the District of New Jersey, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. Jon is also a member of the Spellman-Hoeveler American Inn of Court, and served as Chair of a Grievance Committee of the Florida Bar. He maintains membership in Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity International, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the American Bar Association.

In 2005 Jon had the high honor and privilege of being appointed Honorary Consul of Denmark by Her Majesty Queen Margrethe II. In that capacity he has met with and hosted members of the Danish Royal Family, ministers and other Government officials. Prior to his legal career Jon held several retail management positions with the national department store Lord & Taylor. Among them were General Manager, Operations Manager, and Regional Control Manager for the Southeastern United States.

No stranger to the courtroom, Jennifer is a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer, a recognition earned by less than 2% of all Florida attorneys, and an even smaller percentage of female attorneys. She's also been named to the Super Lawyers "Rising Star" list.

Before joining Morgan and Morgan, Jennifer spent nearly 10 years working as a defense lawyer for various insurance companies nationwide. Before that she served as in-house counsel for a large insurance company where she oversaw two offices and trained younger attorneys in trial and litigation skills. During these years she learned the particulars of how carriers assess and value claims and injuries.

When not in the courtroom, Jennifer is likely to be found with one of her three dogs or four kids. Her oldest attends the University of Central Florida (where her husband also played football - Go Knights!). She loves the Miami Dolphins, the Florida Keys, and-like most Floridians-anything having to do with the ocean."

attorneys.name: Jared Ross
attorneys.practice_type: Premises Liability Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jared I. Ross is a South Florida native and a graduate of Dr. Michael Krop Senior High in North Miami Beach where he was a member of their Television News and Journalism Magnet program with aspirations of becoming an investigative news journalist. Jared attended the University of Florida before obtaining his Juris Doctor from Nova Southeastern University in 2010. Mr. Ross is a civil litigator with over 10 years of experience practicing at both the State and Federal levels in Florida.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan Jared worked for a boutique Plaintiff's Personal Injury law firm in Coral Gables, Florida exclusively representing injury victims with a focus on complex cases involving catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death litigation, including automobile and trucking collisions, premises liability (slip/trip and falls), negligent security, and maritime cruise accidents.

Additionally, Mr. Ross has experience as a civil defense lawyer and previously worked at a nation-wide insurance defense firm. During that time, Jared litigated on behalf of, and defended numerous well-known nationally recognized companies and brands in personal injury claims concerning slip/trip and falls, trucking accidents, and nursing home/assisted living facility negligence. As a result, Jared has obtained critical first-hand knowledge of insurance industry practices in evaluating and defending personal injury claims.

Now, Jared applies his defense background, his years of experience as a lawyer, and his journalism education to fully investigate and best approach his clients claims all with the aim of obtaining high value settlements on their behalf.

attorneys.name: Steve Rossi
attorneys.practice_type: Educational Law Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Steve Rossi has been a member of the Florida Bar for over 30 years. He has been recognized as a Board Certified Criminal Trial Attorney. Certification is the highest level of recognition by The Florida Bar of the competency and experience of attorneys in the areas of law approved for certification by the Supreme Court of Florida.

Mr. Rossi is a former Special Agent with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (F.B.I.). He was employed in both the New York and Miami field offices. He investigated civil and criminal matters.

He was a former prosecutor with the Broward County State Attorney Office. During this time, Mr. Rossi received several accolades including being recognized for most jury trials twice by the State Attorneys Office. While at the State Attorney's Office, Mr. Rossi prosecuted misdemeanor and felony cases.

Mr. Rossi has represented the Broward Teacher's Union (BTU) as its local, legal counsel. The Broward Teacher's Union has more than 15,000 members. The Broward Teachers Union's members are in the 2nd largest district in the state and the 6th largest in the country. He has handled various teacher-related cases in both civil and criminal matters. He has presented various lectures and workshops focusing on education law. He has been an annual instructor for the Broward County School District's New Teacher Orientation Program discussing various issues in teacher liability matters.

Mr. Rossi is a lawyer deeply rooted in the community. He is a long time South Florida resident. He has attended grade school, high school, college, and law school all in South Florida. He attended Barry University where he obtained his Bachelor of Science Degree and the University of Miami School of Law where he obtained his law degree. He has handled various legal matters throughout the state of Florida and around the country. He speaks Italian and conversational Spanish.

Attorney Steve Rossi is an Education Consultant and a National Education Advocate.

attorneys.bio:
I was born and raised in Miami, Florida to Cuban parents. From a young age, they instilled in me the importance of education and hard work. I admire their sacrifice and it is my drive in helping others. I received my law degree from St. Thomas University School of Law and I am licensed in Florida at both the State and Federal levels. Before attending law school, I received my Bachelors from the University of Miami where I focused my studies in Finance and the Spanish language.

After graduation, I worked as an associate attorney at a prominent South Florida law firm where I handled numerous family law matters as well as helping those facing foreclosure. After a couple of years I decided it was time to open my own firm to further my goal of helping families. I have represented countless individuals in divorce proceedings, child custody disputes, child support hearings, relocations, modifications, domestic violence injunctions, temporary custody by extended family members, dependency, and adoptions.

Outside of work, I enjoy traveling and spending time with family and friends. When I retire, I plan to open an animal rescue and dedicate my time to saving animals.

attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Radha Rothrock is Of Counsel to Rothrock Immigration Laywer. She has been licensed to practice law by the Supreme Court of Texas since 1995 and the Supreme Court of Florida since 1999.

Radha Rothrock has received numerous awards and recognition for her legal work, including the following:

Martindale Hubbell has rated Radha Rothrock as AV Preeminent®, which is the highest peer rating standard. This is given to attorneys who are ranked at the highest level of professional excellence for their legal expertise, communication skills, and ethical standards by their peers.

"10 Rating" by Avvo. Avvo.com is an online marketplace for legal services, that provides lawyer referrals and access to a database of legal information consisting primarily of previously answered questions. The Avvo Rating is the company's effort to evaluate a lawyer's background based on the information available in an attorney's Avvo profile. The company gave Radha Rothrock a "10" rating, which is its highest rating.

"Top Rated Lawyers in Florida, Taxation," Lawyers of Distinction, 2019, 2020, and 2021 as published in Forbes and the New York Times.

Named "Who's Who in America" by Marquis Publishing.

America's Most Honored Lawyers, 2020, (Top 5%), 2019 (Top 10%)

She is admitted to the State Bars of Texas and Florida, the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida, and the United States Tax and Immigration Courts in all fifty states. She has been appointed by the chief judges in ten out of twenty circuit courts in Florida to handle juvenile dependency and termination of parental rights cases and has submitted appellate briefs to the Courts of Appeal in the first, second, and third districts in Florida. Several of her cases have been published.

Ms. Rothrock received her J.D. from South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas, in 1994. The law school is nationally acclaimed for its moot court program. Ms. Rothrock was a quarterfinalist in the Leroy Jeffers Moot Court Competition while at South Texas College of Law and her appellate brief was voted top three in the competition. While at South Texas, Ms. Rothrock served as research assistant to Professor Bruce Burton and helped edit his real estate finance textbook. She received her LL.M. in Taxation from the University of Denver in 2002.

Radha maintained full time employment while obtaining her LL.M.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
David A. Rothstein was born September 28, 1970 in Yonkers, New York. Mr. Rothstein received his B.A. cum laude in 1992 from the College of the Holy Cross, where he also played varsity basketball and was elected Captain by his teammates as a senior. Mr. Rothstein graduated cum laude from the University of Miami School of Law in 1995. While attending law school, Mr.Rothstein served as a member of the University of Miami Law Review and authored The Salary Cap: A Legal Analysis of and Practical Suggestions for Collective Bargaining in Professional Basketball, 11 Univ. Miami Ent. & Sport L. Rev. 251 (1994).

From August 1995 until February 2000, Mr. Rothstein worked for Stearns Weaver Miller Weissler Alhadeff & Sitterson, P.A., one of Florida's premier full-service law firms, where his practice as a trial lawyer involved all aspects of civil litigation. Mr. Rothstein next joined Hanzman & Criden, P.A., where he focused his practice on complex commercial litigation and plaintiff-side class-action litigation and was named a partner of the firm in January 2002.

In 2003, Mr. Rothstein was recognized as a contributor to the article Establishing Injury By Reason Of Racketeering Activity: A Critical Analysis of the 11th Circuit's Per Se Detrimental Reliance Requirement and Its Impact on RICO Class Actions, 77 Fla.B.J. 36 (March 2003). In 2006, Mr. Rothstein was named a charter member of the Ad Hoc Committee for the Eleventh Judicial Circuit's Business Litigation Division, which established the framework and procedure's for Miami-Dade County's Business Litigation Division. Mr. Rothstein also is a long-standing member of the Board of Directors of Miami-based City Theatre, a professional theatre company dedicated to the solicitation, development, and production of short (one-act) plays unique to the cultural community of South Florida.

attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse Lawyers in North Miami Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Rotundo practices in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home abuse and cases involving catastrophic injury. He has extensive litigation and trial experience throughout Florida and the Southeastern United States.

Mr. Rotundo is AV Rated by Martindale Hubbell*, the highest rating awarded by that publication. Martindale Hubbell ratings are determined by the confidential opinions of other lawyers. He has a 10.0 “Superb” rating by Avvo, the highest rating awarded by that website. Avvo ratings are determined based upon experience, industry recognition and professional conduct.

Born in upstate New York, Mr. Rotundo received his Bachelor of Science degree from The State University of New York at Buffalo in 1987. He received his Juris Doctor from the University of Notre Dame The Law School in 1991. Mr. Rotundo has been practicing law in South Florida since 1991.

Among his other activities, Mr. Rotundo lectures in his areas of practice; serves as a guardian ad litem for Miami-Dade and Broward counties; teaches as a guest lecturer at a local university; and, serves as The Florida Bar fee arbitrator.

Mr. Rotundo is a member of The Florida Bar, the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Middle District of Florida, the Dade County Bar Association, the Broward County Bar Association, Miami Dade Justice Association, and the American Association for Justice.

When he is not working, Mr. Rotundo enjoys spending time with his family, woodworking and gardening.

Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review RatingTM fall into two categories - legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jesse Rowe was born in Baltimore, Maryland where he fell in love with good seafood, lacrosse, and NFL football. He moved to Orlando, Florida in 1997 and was quick to call it home. After high school, Mr. Rowe attended the University of Central Florida and became a member of the Delta Upsilon Fraternity. In 2007, he graduated with honors and received his Bachelor's Degree in Legal Studies.

In 2007, Mr. Rowe began his legal career as a workers' compensation paralegal. In 2014, Mr. Rowe graduated Cum Laude with his Juris Doctorate from Florida A&M University Law School and was admitted to the Florida Bar. Since then, his sole career focus has been representing injured workers in their workers' compensation claims.

Mr. Rowe is a member of the Workers' Compensation Section of the Florida Bar, Florida Workers' Advocates and is a committee chair in the Judge William Wieland Inn of Court.

Mr. Rowe resides in Ormond Beach, Florida with his wife and daughter.

attorneys.name: Samuel Adam Rubert
attorneys.practice_type: Alcoholic Beverage Law Lawyers in Weston, FL
attorneys.bio:
I got interested in the food and beverage industry as a young child - copying down my first receipt at age 5 (my mom still has it framed in her kitchen). While in high school, I spent too much time watching the newly launched Food Network and trying to cook like they did. I played football in high school and continued to play for two years at Columbia before succumbing to injury. Durring college I started working in bars as a barback and bartender. After graduation, I attended the French Culinary School (now known as the International Culinary Center) in New York, and upon completion I began working for Dan Barber at Blue Hill in New York which earned two stars from the New York Times. When I finally turned to law school (both my parents were lawyers and it felt inevitable since I was negotiating my allowance from age 8 on), I hoped to be a Restaurant and Bar Lawyer, unsure if such a thing existed, and was happy and lucky to get a job as a law clerk for a firm that focused on the alcoholic beverage industry. When I went out on my own several years later, I decided to remain focused on the industry. I find alcoholic beverage industry members to be just a bit weird - which I like - and I think my own weird path to where I am, and my experience in their industry, allow me to provide legal services like someone from the service and hospitality industry - focused on the client and thier needs and how we can help them accomplish their goals. We are proud of our 5 star rating on google, showing our dedication to clients, and our Martindale Hubble AV rating - the highest rating one can receive from peers.

attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Rubinstein is the partner-in-charge of our law firm. Jeff specializes in real estate and commercial litigation, and offers a wealth of expertise with over 30 years’ experience as both a transactional lawyer and a trial lawyer of commercial disputes. Jeffrey’s cross-disciplined practice enables him to provide insights and judgments that can only be gained from the type of broad based experience that Jeff brings to every engagement.

By virtue of the depth of his experience in both the Courtroom as a trial lawyer, as well as his corporate and real estate background, Jeff offers clients a wealth of experience in dealing with problematic real estate projects, land use matters or loans secured by real estate. Jeff has been involved in handling lender liability claims and prosecuted numerous large foreclosures. Jeff handles various types of commercial cases in the State and Federal courts, and commercial foreclosures throughout the State.

Jeff received his B.A. degree with a major in Economics from George Washington University, after transferring there from Bates College, and received his Juris Doctor Degree from the University of Miami School of Law in 1974.

He resides in Pinecrest, Florida.

attorneys.name: Marc Ruddy
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Marc Ruddy was born in Richland, WA and grew up in Pittsburgh, PA. He graduated from The Pennsylvania State University in 2002 with a Bachelor of Arts in International Politics. Mr. Ruddy attended New England School of Law and was admitted to the Massachusetts Bar in 2006.

Mr. Ruddy began his career as an Assistant District Attorney in the Northwestern District Attorney's Office in Northampton, MA. As an Assistant District Attorney, Mr. Ruddy prosecuted misdemeanor and felony cases in the District Courts of the Northwestern District of Massachusetts from 2006 to 2009.

In 2009, Mr. Ruddy went into private practice. He was accepted into the Franklin County Bar Advocate Program in Franklin County, MA. As a bar advocate, Mr. Ruddy accepted court appointments to represent indigent criminal defendants. He was also a member of the Franklin County Bar Advocate for Elders Grant Program and Franklin County Bar Advocate for Women Grant Program. As a member of the Franklin County Bar Advocate for Elders Grant Program, Mr. Ruddy represented indigent elderly residents of Franklin County in consumer rights matters. As a member of the Franklin County Bar Advocate for Women Grant Program, Mr. Ruddy represented indigent victims of domestic violence in Franklin County Probate and Family Court.

While Mr. Ruddy enjoyed living in Massachusetts, he and his family relocated to Florida in 2012 after he accepted an offer to practice in a high volume Social Security and VA disability law firm based out of Ft. Lauderdale, FL. Mr. Ruddy represented thousands of claimants denied Social Security disability benefits as an associate of that firm from 2012 to 2017.

Mr. Ruddy joined Morgan & Morgan in March 2017. He brings a wealth of Social Security disability experience to the firm. Mr. Ruddy is limited to practicing Social Security disability only.

Mr. Ruddy lives in Tampa with his wife and two children. He enjoys fishing and going to the beach.

attorneys.practice_type: Prenuptial and Postnuptial Agreements Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Howard M. Rudolph, managing partner of Rudolph & Associates LLC, is Board Certified in Marital and Family Law with an emphasis on complex divorce litigation.

He graduated from Rutgers University, B.A., and Hofstra University, J.D., where he was Editor of Law Review. Mr. Rudolph is admitted to the Bar in Florida, New Jersey and New York, and is a member of the ABA, giving him the unique ability to handle multi-jurisdictional cases.

He is AV-rated by Martindale-Hubbell, is named in Florida’s Legal Elite, and sits on several Family Law Section committees. He lectures on family law topics. He represents high net worth clients, numerous professional athletes and members of the entertainment industry in their paternity, child support, and divorce matters.

Howard Rudolph and his wife Julie, are active supporters of the Heart Association, Cancer Alliance, South Florida Science Museum and Big Dog Ranch Rescue. Julie is also an active member of the Junior League of the Palm Beaches. Howard also supports the Town of Palm Beach Police and Fire Department. Howard lectures at the Sports Law Association. Howard is an avid sportsman who loves paddle boarding, watersports, and hiking. He spends his free time with his wife of over 25 years, their family, and man’s best friend, Chonk.

attorneys.bio:
Dear Prospective Client

I am a licensed Florida attorney and an LL.M. graduate of Temple University's top ranked Trial Advocacy Program. This academic training, coupled with my hands-on legal experience, has afforded me a strong foundation in litigation and trial practice. I am a former prosecutor dedicated to zealous and aggressive representation in Traffic, DUI, Misdemeanor and Felony Criminal Defense cases.

In 2005, I was appointed as a prosecutor with the Office of the State Attorney for the 15th Judicial Circuit, Palm Beach County, Florida. During my time with the State Attorney's Office, I sat first chair in over one hundred criminal cases that went to trial; most of which were argued before a jury.

In private practice, I have dedicated myself towards pursuing justice for those who are accused of committing crimes. I advocate for, and strive to find, sentencing alternatives to jail or prison for those who are suffering from drug, alcohol and/or dual diagnosis disorders. I have addressed numerous schools, community groups and programs in order to educate both young adults and adults about the criminal justice system, domestic violence and the penalties associated with drug and alcohol related crimes.

It is my experience as a prosecutor that makes me a zealous defense attorney and I will be just as proud to serve you, my client, with the same zeal and aggressiveness.

attorneys.name: David Anthony Ruiz Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Ruiz’s practice focuses on representing those injured at work.

David Ruiz grew up in Miami, Florida and attended high school at Christopher Columbus before graduating from Florida International University with a degree in Political Science. He was later admitted to Stetson University College of Law, wherein he graduated cum laude in 2014. While in law school, David served as a federal judicial intern for the Honorable Mark A. Pizzo of the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, and as a state judicial intern for the Honorable Samantha L. Ward of the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit Court of Florida. He also served as an editor for the Journal of International Wildlife Law and Policy, and he still maintains a strong interest in conservation efforts.

Following law school, David worked at an insurance defense firm in Orlando, Florida, wherein his practice solely focused on workers’ compensation cases. After representing insurance carriers and employers for over 8 years, David saw the injustices that many injured workers would go through throughout the course of their claims. He then decided that it was time to help those in need, and in 2023, David began working for the Berlin Law Firm, wherein he has served as the managing partner of the Tampa office. He enjoys coming into work each day fighting for the rights of injured workers.

In his spare time, David enjoys spending time with his wife, playing golf and watching all types of sports, including his home teams from Miami.

attorneys.name: Amy Ruiz
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Amy Ruiz is a seasoned attorney with a diverse legal career, specializing in criminal defense, traffic law, and personal injury cases. She is the founder of Amy Ruiz Law, PL, and is dedicated to providing exceptional legal representation to clients in the Tampa Bay area.

Amy holds a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with a focus on Marketing and International Economics from the University of Florida (2000) and a Juris Doctorate from the Florida State College of Law (2004). While at Florida State, she was a member of the Journal of Transnational Law & Policy and participated in the Institute on World Legal Problems in Austria, where she studied Comparative Constitutional Law under U.S. Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia.

After earning her law degree, Amy returned to Tampa and began her legal career as an Assistant Public Defender for the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit (2004–2006), handling motions, hearings, and trials. She then transitioned to a role as an Assistant State Attorney (2006–2011), where she successfully litigated a wide range of cases, from misdemeanors to serious felonies.

In 2011, Amy broadened her legal experience by joining a firm specializing in insurance defense, where she worked on high-profile cases, including the Chinese Drywall Multi-District Litigation. In 2012, she founded her own firm, Amy Ruiz Law, where she has since built a reputation for her compassionate yet aggressive approach to criminal defense and personal injury law.

Amy is actively involved in the local legal community. She is a board member and immediate past president of the Tampa Hispanic Bar Association and is a member of the Tampa Bay Inn of Court. She has also served as a Special Magistrate for the City of Tampa and as Secretary of the Traffic Rules Committee.

Among her many honors, Amy was awarded the 2024 Sheriff’s Hispanic Advisory Council’s Raymond E. Fernandez Award, recognizing her significant contributions to the criminal justice system in Hillsborough County.

Licensed to practice in both state and federal courts in Florida, Amy is committed to upholding justice and advocating for her clients with integrity and dedication. Her results-driven solutions have established her as a trusted advocate in her areas of practice.

Since taking over as a full-time POD attorney in 2019, Mr. Russo has lead his team of 8 to obtain over 40 million dollars in settlements and verdicts for his clients. Mr. Russo strongly believes in fair justice and fighting on behalf of his clients all the way through trial.

attorneys.name: Anthony Gerald Ryan
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Anthony G. Ryan was born in Berwin, Illinois in 1970. He majored in Finance and minored in History at the University of Florida, where he graduated with a B.S. in Business Administration in 1992. While attending the University of Florida, Mr. Ryan was a member of both Phi Kappa Phi (Scholastic Honor Society) and Omicron Delta Epsilon (Economic Honor Society). Prior to entering the legal profession Mr. Ryan worked for Enterprise-Rent-A-Car in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida.

Mr. Ryan graduated cum laude (with honors) from the University of Miami School of Law in 1997. During law school he was a member of Phi Delta Phi (Honorary Legal Fraternity), served on the Business Law Journal, and made Dean's List. Mr. Ryan also studied law in London and interned at the Public Defender's Office in Ft. Lauderdale, where he assisted with three criminal jury trials prior to graduation. After admission to the Florida Bar, Mr. Ryan began practicing with Vernis & Bowling of the Florida Keys, P.A., a statewide insurance defense firm. He then accepted a position as an Assistant Public Defender in Ft. Pierce, Florida where he gained valuable criminal trial experience. After two years with the Public Defender's office, Mr. Ryan entered private practice in 2002. He has been the principal of his own firm, practicing criminal defense law ever since.

Mr. Ryan is a Florida Bar, Board Certified Criminal Trial Lawyer, which is the highest level of recognition possible for a criminal defense attorney.

He is also a member of the Florida Bar, the Sarasota County Bar Association, and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys, both the statewide organization and the Sarasota County Chapter. Mr. Ryan is also a member of the Federal Bar, admitted to practice in the Northern and Southern Districts of Florida.

In addition to handling all misdemeanor and felony cases, Mr. Ryan also handles a limited number of false arrest claims, criminal appeals, driver's license hearings, and forfeitures.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Ryan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Plantation, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Ryan is a seasoned civil trial attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., bringing more than 25 years of experience to the representation of clients in complex personal injury and catastrophic injury litigation. Widely respected for his extensive legal knowledge, courtroom excellence, and client-first approach, Mr. Ryan has successfully led high-stakes cases across Florida and nationwide.

His areas of concentration include medical malpractice, pharmaceutical and product liability, and serious personal injury claims. Over the course of his distinguished career, he has contributed to securing over $250 million in verdicts and settlements for injury victims—solidifying his reputation as a formidable advocate within the legal community.

Mr. Ryan earned his B.B.A. in Finance from The George Washington University and graduated summa cum laude with his Juris Doctor from Case Western Reserve University School of Law. He began his legal career as a federal law clerk in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida and honed his litigation skills through roles in both state and federal public defender offices before transitioning into civil practice.

Outside the courtroom, Mr. Ryan is a dedicated public servant and community leader. Since 2010, he has served as Mayor of Sunrise, Florida, spearheading initiatives in public safety, education, and sustainability. His commitment to civic engagement includes charitable service on multiple boards, participation in long-distance fundraising events for veterans, and volunteering with organizations such as the U.S.O. Wounded Warrior Center.

His professional and civic accomplishments have earned him numerous awards, including:

- Broward County Bar Association’s Walter G. “Skip” Campbell Jr. Lawyer-Public Servant Award (2019)

- Sustainable Civic Leader of the Year – GreenCITYSummit24 (2024)

- Environmental Champion Award – Broward Sierra Club (2024)

- “Irishman of the Year” (2014) and “Honorary Scotsman of the Year” (2025)

Mr. Ryan is also recognized for his leadership in electronic discovery and complex litigation and frequently contributes to the legal field as a lecturer and author. His role as a youth coach, PTA leader, and advocate for education further reflects his holistic commitment to justice and community wellbeing.

At Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., Michael J. Ryan continues to combine legal expertise with public service, standing as a powerful voice for those seeking accountability and recovery.

attorneys.name: Sam J. Saad III
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Sam J. Saad III
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Naples, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sam J. Saad III is an accomplished attorney specializing in real estate, business law, and title services in Southwest Florida. A graduate of Creighton University Law School (cum laude, 2003), Sam also holds degrees in business and political science from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln.

With a commitment to helping Realtors®, local professionals, entrepreneurs, and property owners navigate complex legal landscapes, Sam brings a common-sense approach to every client relationship, emphasizing economical solutions that fit each client’s unique needs. Known for his accessibility and dedication, he remains a reliable legal partner for those looking to close real estate transactions smoothly and effectively.

Sam actively participates in numerous professional organizations, including the Florida Bar Association, the Collier County Bar Association, and the Naples Area Board of Realtors (NABOR). He also serves on key committees such as the Florida Realtor-Attorney Joint Committee (2024-2025) and as scribe and past chairman of the NABOR Legal Resources committee. Sam’s service extends to the Greater Naples Chamber of Commerce, where he graduated from the Leadership Collier program in 2013.

Recognized for his contributions to the industry and community, Sam was honored by Gulfshore Business Magazine’s "40 Under 40" (2012) and awarded the Golden Cedar Award by the Lebanese American Chamber of Commerce (2006). A lifetime member of the National Eagle Scout Association, Sam is an active supporter of local nonprofits, including St. Matthew’s House, Collier Harvest, and Youth Haven.

Sam’s experience includes roles as Presidential Appointee under President George W. Bush, a former City Council Member of Naples and President of Paradise Coast Title & Escrow. His legal knowledge, dedication to clients, and community commitment make him a trusted advisor in real estate and business law across Southwest Florida.

attorneys.name: Adam C. Sabocik
attorneys.practice_type: Estate and Trust Litigation Lawyers in Palm Beach Gardens, FL
attorneys.bio:
Adam has over two decades of legal experience, and focuses his practice on estate and trust litigation, guardianship litigation, estate, trust and guardianship administration, and estate planning. He has extensive experience in representing fiduciaries, beneficiaries, and interested parties in complex and contested probate, trust, and guardianship matters.

He is admitted to practice law in Florida and the U.S. District Court Southern District of Florida. He graduated with highest honors from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminology in 1998. He earned his Juris Doctor degree from the Florida State University College of Law in 2002. Before joining Barner & Barner, P.A., Adam served as a staff attorney for the Fifteenth Judicial Circuit Court in Palm Beach County, Florida from 2002 to 2005. He then worked as an associate attorney at Sachs, Sax, Klein, P.A. from 2005 to 2008, and as a partner at Boyes, Farina & Matwiczyk, P.A. from 2008 to 2023.

Adam achieved the highest peer rating from Martindale-Hubbell, “AV Preeminent,” is a member of the Florida Bar, Real Property, Probate and Trust Law Section, the Palm Beach County Bar Association, and the Craig S. Bernard American Inns of Court, LIV (emeritus member). He has also contributed to and presented several seminars on topics related to estate and trust litigation, guardianship law, and estate planning.

He was born in Detroit, Michigan, but was raised in DeLand, Florida and is an avid Florida Gator fan. He enjoys spending time with his family, and when he has a chance, motorcycling, golfing, and both salt and freshwater fishing. He is also a USA Swimming official. Adam is committed to providing high-quality legal services to his clients with professionalism, integrity, and compassion.

attorneys.bio:
Allison focuses her law practice on probate and trust litigation and administration. She has extensive experience in handling complex and contested matters involving wills, trusts, estates and guardianships. She also represents clients in related appeals.

She was born in Bridgeport, Connecticut, and moved to South Florida during her freshman year of high school where she attended Santaluces Community High School.

Allison graduated with highest honors from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminology and earned minors in Spanish and French. She then earned a Master of Arts degree in International Business from the University of Florida Warrington College of Business. She then received her ,Juris Doctor degree from the University of Florida Levin College of Law, where she served as a research editor for the Journal of Law and Public Policy.

Allison began her Iegal career in 2004 as a staff attorney and law clerk for the Fifteenth ,Judicial Circuit Cowi in Palm Beach County, Florida. She then joined Miller & O·Neill, P.L., where she practiced probate and trust litigation. In 2009, she moved to Pankauski Hauser, P.L.L.C., where she continued to handle probate and trust matters until 2018. Allison continued her focused work on probate and trust matters at Boyes, Farina & Matwiczyk, PA from 2018 to 2023, before joining Barner & Barner, P.A.

Allison is admitted to practice law in the State of Florida, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, and the United States Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. She has achieved the highest peer rating from Martindale-Hubbell, "AV Preeminent". She is an Emeritus member of the Craig S. Barnard American Inns of Court UV, the Palm Beach County Bar Association (Co-Chair of Probate CLE Committee 2018-20'19 and 2021-2022), and has served as a Co-Chair of the Probate Committee for the annual Palm Beach County Bar's Bench Bar Conference.

She has also been a speaker at various seminars and conferences on topics related to probate and trust law, such as legislative and case law updates, trends and hot topics, and guardianship law.

Outside of the office, Allison is a mom to her son (an honor roll student and competitive swimmer). and enjoys spending time with her family. jogging, and cooking.

attorneys.name: Ruben Martin Saenz Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wage & Hour Litigation Lawyers in Aventura, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Lima, Peru in 1974, R. Martin Saenz's interest in law can be traced back to his childhood in Peru. His father was a judge and a practicing attorney in Peru before retiring in the United States. Martin followed in his father's footsteps and is currently domiciled in South Florida, where he is the managing partner of The Saenz Law Firm, P.A.

Martin's educational background and experience can be traced to the beginning of his legal training in a Peruvian law school (San Martin de Porres) where he spent three years studying law. During this time, he also served as a clerk for the Law Offices of Escurra, Rubio and Villar, a commercial and labor and employment litigation firm in Lima, Peru.

Following the first three years of law school in Peru, Martin moved to the United States. Here, he studied political science and pre-law at Syracuse University in Utica, New York. He graduated Magna Cum Laude in 1998 with a Bachelor of Arts degree and was awarded with the Outstanding Senior in Political Science award. His study of law in the United States continued when he attended the Syracuse University College of Law in Syracuse, New York. In addition to his classes, Martin interned for U.S. District Court Judge, Andrea Simonton; was the executive director to the Syracuse Journal of International Law and Commerce; an associate editor to the Syracuse Law & Technology Journal; a member of the Vienna International Commerce Moot Court Team and a member of the National Security Law Team. In May of 2002, Martin graduated with a Juris Doctor degree and a Global Law and Practice certificate.

In addition, Martin has authored the following articles/books: Mis Derechos Como Empleado en los EEUU, Part I: Los Derechos Basicos; LexisNexis Practice Guide: Florida Business Torts (Pub 1388): Fraud; LexisNexis Practice Guide: Florida Business Torts (Pub 1388): RICO; Florida Practice Guide on Civil Procedure: Motions: Disqualification of the Judge (LexisNexis 2005); Florida Practice Guide on Civil Procedure: Motions: Consolidation and Severance (LexisNexis 2005); and Florida Practice Guide on Civil Procedure: Motions: Perpetuation of Testimony (LexisNexis 2005).

Prior to opening The Saenz Law Firm, Martin acquired extensive experience representing a large clientele base in cases arising out of a broad spectrum of legal disputes such as labor and employment litigation, real estate litigation, and business and commercial disputes. With an eye for preventing litigation Martin is also experienced in drafting and negotiating contracts in Spanish and in English among his additional litigation duties.

Today, Martin seeks to offer the best representation in legal matters to his clients. He is fluent in Spanish and English. His bar admissions include the Supreme Court of Florida, the United States Southern District of Florida, and the United States Middle District of Florida.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Magna Cum Laude; The Outstanding Graduating Senior in Political Science, 1998

Syracuse Journal of International Law and Commerce, Executive Editor—Award for Excellence, 2001 - 2002

attorneys.name: Jeremy C. Sahn
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation - Appellate Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jeremy has extensive experience litigating complex business disputes in both state and federal courts. His broad-based background in trial practice includes contract litigation, insurance law, shareholder and partnership disputes, trademark, copyright and intellectual property litigation, financial institution litigation, environmental law, marine vessel construction, and various forms of disputes relating to commercial real property. In addition to representing clients in adversarial circumstances, Jeremy also regularly advises clients on methods and strategies for structuring business transactions so as to avoid pitfalls that may lead to costly litigation in the future.

EXPERIENCE

Represented a Connecticut hedge fund client as lead trial counsel in a commercial property dispute relating to a golf course, country club and surrounding residential and commercial property. At the conclusion of trial, Jeremy’s client was awarded a final judgment for $8.8 million.

Obtained a final judgment award for $1.2 million on behalf of a national special servicer as lead counsel in a commercial finance payment guaranty action against former NBA basketball player Stephon X. Marbury.

Personally won final judgment awards totaling over $.5 billion in more than 20 Florida state-court jurisdictions against commercial properties including hotels, office buildings, townhome complexes and shopping malls.

Representing shipbuilding industry leader in dispute against the City of New York relating to the construction of two 140-foot, state-of-the-art, fast-response FDNY fireboats.

Represented mortgage-lending companies in mortgage-buyback litigation against JPMorganChase Bank, US Bank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America and the FDIC as receiver for IndyMac Bank and Lehman Brothers in nationwide federal lawsuits relating to the secondary market sale of hundreds of residential mortgages.

Represented Fortune 500 human capital management software development company in multi-state federal court litigation relating to trademark, intellectual property and non-compete disputes.

Represented developer/owner of a well-known, historic Miami Beach hotel in defense of over 30 lawsuits relating to the hotel’s $1-billion-dollar property renovation and rejuvenation project.

Represented industrial distribution center in defense of toxic tort claims exceeding $10 million.

RECOGNITION

attorneys.name: R. Ryan Sainz
attorneys.practice_type: Boating Accidents Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
R. Ryan Sainz is a native of Tampa, Florida. He graduated from Chamberlain High School. Following his graduation, he attended Florida College where he was a 2-year letter winner in baseball and part of the 2004 National Championship team. Mr. Sainz's athletic accomplishments led to a full baseball scholarship to Savannah State University where he continued his leadership as a 2-year letter winner and team captain.

Following the completion of his athletic eligibility, Ryan returned home to Tampa where he completed his undergraduate degree from the University of South Florida. After graduation, Mr. Sainz attended the Barry University Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law.

While attending law school, Mr. Sainz was an active member of the nationally recognized trial team. His desire to become a trial attorney was confirmed after being a member of the team that won the ABA National Criminal Justice Trial Advocacy Competition in 2012.

Following his graduation from law school, Mr. Sainz was admitted to the Florida Bar and began his legal career for a large national civil defense law firm. During his time as a defense attorney, Mr. Sainz was retained by insurance companies and large corporations to defend lawsuits filed by the injured. In his career, Mr. Sainz has tried multiple cases throughout Florida involving auto negligence, chemical burns, slip and falls, wrongful death and traumatic brain injuries.

Mr. Sainz's desire to shift his focus from defending corporations to defending the injured is what led him to Morgan & Morgan. Today, Mr. Sainz is able to use his extensive litigation experience to represent clients, specializing in automobile accidents.

attorneys.name: Ravin Sahadeo
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ravin is a litigation attorney at Morgan & Morgan, P.A. in the Orlando office. He assists clients with various negligence claims including: Personal Injury, Premises Liability, and Wrongful Death.

Ravin started with the firm at 20 years-old in 2013, where he worked in the firms Social Security Department as an intake specialist. Following, Ravin was the firms' youngest legal assistant in the Social Security department where he was responsible for successfully recovering benefits for hundreds of clients.

In 2015, Ravin became a case manager in the Personal Injury Department handling various matters including wrongful death, car accidents, catastrophic injuries, slip and falls, dog bites and trip and fall cases. Ravin worked in that role for almost 5 years before becoming an attorney. Ravin ranked at the top of the firms list as one of the top case managers each year since starting in that position.

Ravin received his bachelor's degree in Political Science with a minor in Legal Studies from the University of Central Florida (UCF). While attending UCF, Ravin was an active member of the Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity where he served as the Chair of the Mock Trial Team. Under Ravin's leadership, the Mock Trial Team exceled by placing as a top five finalist at the 2015 National Tournament in Washington D.C.

In the fall of 2016, Ravin enrolled into the part-time program at Barry School of Law while maintaining his full-time case manager position at Morgan & Morgan, P.A. In his third year of law school, Ravin was selected into Barry's Juvenile Defense Clinic where he represented multiple minors accused of felonies and misdemeanors. Ravin successfully had multiple charges for his clients dropped without the need of going to trial. Also, in his fourth year, Ravin clerked for The Honorable Judge Harris and the Ninth Circuit where he worked on high-felony cases including murder, capital sexual abuse, armed robbery and death penalty cases.

Ravin graduated from Barry School of Law in the May of 2020 with honors in Litigation and passed the October 2020 Bar Exam. Ravin considers it is a privilege and honor to be trusted with our client's case in their most vulnerable time.

Ravin started with the firm at 20 years-old in 2013, where he worked in the firms Social Security Department as an intake specialist. Following, Ravin was the firms' youngest legal assistant in the Social Security department where he was responsible for successfully recovering benefits for hundreds of clients.

In 2015, Ravin became a case manager in the Personal Injury Department handling various matters including wrongful death, car accidents, catastrophic injuries, slip and falls, dog bites and trip and fall cases. Ravin worked in that role for almost 5 years before becoming an attorney. Ravin ranked at the top of the firms list as one of the top case managers each year since starting in that position.

Ravin received his bachelor's degree in Political Science with a minor in Legal Studies from the University of Central Florida (UCF). While attending UCF, Ravin was an active member of the Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity where he served as the Chair of the Mock Trial Team. Under Ravin's leadership, the Mock Trial Team exceled by placing as a top five finalist at the 2015 National Tournament in Washington D.C.

In the fall of 2016, Ravin enrolled into the part-time program at Barry School of Law while maintaining his full-time case manager position at Morgan & Morgan, P.A. In his third year of law school, Ravin was selected into Barry's Juvenile Defense Clinic where he represented multiple minors accused of felonies and misdemeanors. Ravin successfully had multiple charges for his clients dropped without the need of going to trial. Also, in his fourth year, Ravin clerked for The Honorable Judge Harris and the Ninth Circuit where he worked on high-felony cases including murder, capital sexual abuse, armed robbery and death penalty cases.

Ravin graduated from Barry School of Law in the May of 2020 with honors in Litigation and passed the October 2020 Bar Exam. Ravin considers it is a privilege and honor to be trusted with our client's case in their most vulnerable time.
