attorneys.name: Khristopher Salado Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Miami Lakes, FL
attorneys.bio:
Khristopher Ryan Salado is a Cuban-American attorney with close ties to the South Florida community. Born and raised in Miami, FL, he prides himself on being a "local product." He graduated with honors from Florida International University before graduating Magna Cum Laude from St. Thomas University School of Law with a Certificate in Tax Law. While in law school, he interned at prominent personal injury firm and played an integral part of a jury trial that resulted in a five million dollar ($5,000,000.00) verdict. He also served on the Executive Board for the St. Thomas Law Review, the Moot Court Board, the Cuban American Student Bar Association, and was initiated into the prestigious Order of the Barristers for his excellence in oral advocacy.

During his years of litigation practice, Salado has successfully recovered over $40 million dollars for his clients and has been selected as a Super Lawyer Rising Star six years in a row (2019-2024). His practice focuses on personal injury litigation involving premise liability, traumatic brain injuries, auto collisions, catastrophic injury, and complex products liability. He has successfully litigated bad faith cases against some of the largest insurance companies in the nation and recovered millions against manufacturers of defective products. Salado is dedicated to helping people of all walks of life who have been wrongfully harmed by the negligence of others and has successfully recovered millions of dollars for his clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Immigration Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio: Since 1995, Ms. Salama DiMitri has been engaged in the private practice of immigration law at Behar Law Group. She specializes in complex cases involving U.S. immigration and nationality issues, particularly in the corporate context. Her experience covers all corporate as well as family immigration matters. On the nonimmigrant side, Ms. Salama DiMitri has worked on cases such as: professionals (H-1B), multinational executives/managers (L-1), religious workers (R-1), Trade NAFTA (TN), investors (E-2), traders (E-1), students (F-1/M-1), trainees (J-1/H-3), extraordinary ability (O-1), athletes (P-1) and fiance(e) (K-1) visa matters. On the immigrant side, Ms. Salama DiMitri focuses on matters pertaining to labor certification (pre-PERM and PERM), extraordinary ability individuals, multinational executives/managers, entrepreneur investors (EB-5), family preference and immediate relative cases, victims of domestic violence, among others.. She also handles waiver applications, applications for U.S. citizenship and nationality, as well as consular matters at embassies and consulates throughout the world.

attorneys.name: Erick M. Salazar
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Erick M. Salazar was born in Valencia, Venezuela. At a young age, his family immigrated to South Florida where he grew up before relocating to Central Florida for his studies.

As a first-generation immigrant, Mr. Salazar began his journey toward becoming a lawyer at an early age by helping his parents overcome language barriers and advocating on their behalf. This experience inspired him to pursue the legal profession and set him off on a mission to advocate for those who are unable to stand up for themselves.

Mr. Salazar earned his bachelor's degree in Political Science from the University of Central Florida and earned his law degree from Barry University, Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law. In addition to holding leadership roles in various organizations during his tenure at Barry, Mr. Salazar was also an active member of the school's Nationally recognized Trial Team, competing in various competitions. In late 2018, he earned the privilege to represent Barry University in the Hon. E. Earle Zehmer Memorial Mock Trial Competition hosted by the FJA Young Lawyer's section, where he and his team took first place, after going undefeated among 15 teams from 8 different law schools.

Today, Mr. Salazar uses his experience having worked for the insurance companies, and then litigating against them to formulate a winning strategy for your case. His experience has helped him develop the essential skills necessary to make sure his clients receive exceptional service both in and out of the courtroom.

The process after a car accident can be stressful and overwhelming, which is why Mr. Salazar prides himself on being readily accessible for his clients and fighting to achieve the best possible outcome for their cases.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Jacqueline A. Salcines P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jacqueline Salcines, Esq. was born and raised in Miami, Florida. She graduated high school from Our Lady of Lourdes Academy. She then went on to earn a Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, from the University of Miami School of Business. Thereafter, Ms. Salcines attended and graduated from the University of Miami School of Law in 1998. She has been practicing law in South Florida for over 19 years.

Prior to attending law school, Ms. Salcines worked for the family accounting practice as a bookkeeper since the age of 16, and later as an accountant for 5 years after graduating. That is when she decided to pursue her passion for business law, and enrolled in law school. Working as a paralegal in law firms during the day and attending law school at night, Ms. Salcines obtained her Juris Doctorate degree in Law in 1998.

Ms. Salcines began her legal career interning at the Miami Dade County State Attorney’s Office. Prior to opening her own law firm, she worked as an Associate at a federal/civil litigation, criminal defense and real estate law firm. Thereafter, she went out on her own and established Jacqueline A. Salcines, PA in the year 2000. She continued to practice real estate, litigation and business law.

Since 2000, Mrs. Salcines’ practice has consisted primarily of real estate law, title and business law matters. With an emphasis on real estate transactions, debt settlement and corporate litigation, Ms. Salcines firm represents clients both locally and internationally. Robert concentrates his practice in franchise law and complex commercial litigation.

Yoelyn is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Albert A. Sanchez Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Litigation Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Albert A. Sanchez has practiced law in the Sarasota and Manatee area. His areas of concentration are construction law, real estate law and business law.

Born in Tampa, Florida, he graduated from Riverview High School in Sarasota, Florida with High Honors and was a member of the National Honor Society. He received his undergraduate degree with High Honors from the University of Florida and his Juris Doctorate from The University of Florida where he was Articles Editor for the Law Review.

From 1998 through 2014, in addition to representing select clients, he acted as managing partner of multiple commercial and residential developments and construction projects in areas including St. Armand's Circle, downtown Sarasota, Palmer Ranch and Lakewood Ranch.

Mr. Sanchez is Board Certified in Business Litigation and a Certified Building Contractor from 2012 through 2020 in the state of Florida and a member of ABA Forum on Construction - Divisions for Construction Litigation, Dispute Resolution and Contract Drafting.

Mr. Sanchez was a two-term member from 2018 through 2024 of the Florida Supreme Court Business and Contracts Jury Instruction Committee.

Mr. Sanchez is a member of the Florida Bar Business Law Section, the Real Property, Probate and Trust Law Section and the Trial Lawyers Section.

Mr. Sanchez is the 2024-2025 Chair of the Business Law section of the Sarasota Bar Association.

Awarded the 2005 Outstanding Alumni Award from the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Florida, Mr. Sanchez has been an avid supporter of the University of Florida. He has been a member of various boards of charitable organizations including The Boys and Girls Club of Sarasota where he was awarded the Outstanding Board Member of the year in 2007.

While his sons were players, he coached Little League baseball for four years, All-Stars for three, and served as a board member of the organization.

Mr. Sanchez has been married to Carolyn since 1981 and is the proud father of three children, Kate, Harrison, and Colin.

attorneys.name: Adam Santana
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Adam Santana was born in Miami, Florida and has resided in South Florida for most of his life. He attended the University of Florida where he graduated with honors before obtaining his Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the Florida State University College of Law. He is admitted to practice throughout the State of Florida as well as in the United States Southern District Court.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Santana was both a Public Defender in Leon County, Florida and an Assistant State Attorney for the Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office where he served as a courtroom training attorney and was amongst the most active trial attorneys in his class. He took over two dozen cases to jury verdict in addition to countless more bench trials for a variety of criminal prosecutions ranging from DUIs to all degrees of felonies.

After transitioning to civil practice, Mr. Santana joined two prestigious Miami law firms well-known in the legal community for their defense prowess. During that time, he litigated countless personal injury and medical malpractice actions while representing physician groups, medical facilities and entertainment venues, and their respective insurance companies. This provided him in-depth insight on how insurance companies evaluate personal injury claims and their strategic mechanisms for defending such cases. Moreover, his time in the medical malpractice arena gives Mr. Santana a distinct advantage when assessing the intricacies of an acute injury to not only prove his case, but to ensure his clients receive the appropriate care given their unique circumstances.

With this background in mind, Mr. Santana has firsthand knowledge of how best to approach such claims against those same kinds of institutions on behalf of his clients when they have been injured due to another's negligence. This, in turn, enables him to attain maximum value for each claim. He is a trial attorney, first and foremost, and uses those skills to zealously litigate for his clients today.

attorneys.name: Ryan T. Santurri
attorneys.practice_type: Trademark and Copyright Acquisition and Counseling Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Santurri practices law in the area of intellectual property and related litigation involving patents, trademarks, trade secrets, copyrights and right of publicity. He also provides trademark and copyright acquisition and counseling services. Ryan has also been involved in successful appeals to the Federal Circuit, including favorable appellate decisions on rulings from trial and from the United States Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.

Ryan attended law school at the University of Florida, Levin College of Law, where he graduated with honors. While in law school, Ryan was a member and chairman of the Justice Campbell Thornal Moot Court and competed in the team's final four competition. Ryan was also a member of the Journal of Technology Law and Policy and was a teaching assistant for the courses Legal Research and Writing and Appellate Advocacy. attorneys.name: Michael Sapourn
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Lawyers in Melbourne, FL
attorneys.bio:
When you have a problem with your insurance company or your agent, you need a knowledgeable Insurance Lawyer. Mr. Sapourn spent 23 years running a large, privately-held insurance brokerage in the Washington D.C. area. He moved to Florida in 2002, and is now an Agency Owner. “Prime-One Insurance Corp” serves Floridians with the highest level of experience and customer service.

Mr. Sapourn is hired by other attorneys for his Insurance expertise. He has been qualified as an expert in federal and state court in the areas of Bad Faith Insurance Claims practices, Insurance Agent’s Standard of Care and Insurance Policy Interpretation. His insider’s knowledge makes him a valuable ally to those who must litigate Insurance matters to obtain a Just result.

He also spent almost 10 years running the legal compliance departments for two Registered Investment Advisors (RIA). He knows the Standard of Care expected of Life and Annuity salespersons. If you believe you were sold an Annuity or Investment you didn’t understand, the salesperson may be responsible for reimbursement of your loss.

Mr. Sapourn brings his customer orientation as a businessperson to his law practice. He takes a personal interest in every client and moves his cases along with the same energy that he brought to his many business enterprises. Through his attention to case management, no case will “linger” in the legal process if Mr. Sapourn can help it.

attorneys.name: William Sarubbi
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Will Sarubbi has always had a passion for helping people and a strong desire to make a positive impact in everything he does.

Mr. Sarubbi was the first-named partner at Senior Justice Law Firm, a nationally recognized law firm specializing in nursing home and assisted living abuse litigation. As a trial lawyer, Mr. Sarubbi has dedicated his law practice to fighting for the rights of injured clients, as well as the families of the victims of wrongful death. Mr. Sarubbi has represented numerous victims of nursing home abuse, assisted living negligence, wrongful death and medical malpractice. During his representation, Mr. Sarubbi has successfully recovered 10+ million dollars for his clients and their families.

Due to his reputation for professional excellence and ethics in the legal field, Mr. Sarubbi is AV Preeminent® Rated by Martindale-Hubbell, receiving the highest rating from other members of the bar and judiciary. Mr. Sarubbi has also consistently earned professional accolades from Super Lawyers, Florida Trend Legal Elite, Palm Beach Illustrated and National Trial Lawyers Top 40 Under 40 as a top-rated attorney.

Mr. Sarubbi earned his Juris Doctorate degree from Stetson University College of Law, nationally ranked as a top law school for trial advocacy. He received his undergraduate degree from Florida State University. Mr. Sarubbi is licensed to practice law in Florida Courts and in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

Before joining Senior Justice Law Firm, Mr. Sarubbi represented skill nursing facilities, assisted living facilities and insurance companies in abuse and wrongful death cases. Because of his background and knowledge of defending nursing homes, Mr. Sarubbi is well-suited to effectively represent victims who wish to bring a claim against facilities and healthcare providers. Mr. Sarubbi is active in all courts in Florida and is regularly called upon by his peers to share his expertise.

attorneys.name: Cynthia N. Sass
attorneys.practice_type: Labor and Employment Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Cynthia N. Sass has been practicing law in Florida over 35 years. She formed the Sass Law Firm in 1993 to exclusively focus on representing public and private sector employees in employment disputes. The mission of her firm is to provide the client with an honest assessment of each case, ensure each client is educated on the options and remedies available to them through the law, and strategize with the client to accomplish his or her goals. In doing so, her firm takes an individual approach to each case, advising clients as to the potential results, costs of litigation and other means of resolving their employee disputes. In order to provide her clients with the best service, Ms. Sass makes it a priority to keep current on the trends affecting employee rights, changes in rules and agency positions, and the most recent applicable case law.

Cynthia is often asked to write or speak on employment law-related topics, especially those related to representing employees. She is the current Editor-in-Chief for the national treatise, Employment at Will, A State-by-State Survey, published by the American Bar Association and Bloomberg. Starting in 2011, Cynthia served as the treatise’s Southeast Regional Editor, while co-authoring the Florida chapter and its annual supplements. Ms. Sass authored a chapter on Discovery and Deposing the Alleged Harasser and Defense Witnesses: The Plaintiff’s Perspective, for the TIPS book Sexual Harassment and Retaliation: A Practical Handbook for Plaintiff and Defense published by the American Bar Association in 2019. She was appointed by the Florida Supreme Court and served on the Standard Jury Instructions Committee – Civil Cases, a Special Committee of The Florida Bar. During her time on that committee, she was Chair of the Spoliation Subcommittee and a member of the Employment Subcommittee, as well as the Negligence Subcommittee. These committees were responsible for drafting the standard state jury instructions on spoliation, private-sector whistleblowing and the Florida Civil Rights Act. Cynthia Sass is also a successful litigator, with published opinions. Ms. Sass holds various national and regional leadership positions, along with committee appointments, and is an active Federal Mediator/Florida Supreme Court Mediator Circuit Civil.

Sass Law Firm has been nationally recognized as a Best Law Firm in Employment Law for Individuals in Tampa by U.S. News & World Report since 2011. Cynthia Sass has been honored by various local, state and national independent sources including being AV Preeminent™ Peer Review Rated by Martindale-Hubbell and listed by The Best Lawyers in America® in Employment Law – Individuals since 2007, and named its Attorney of the Year in 2017 in that category for Tampa. Cynthia has also been recognized by Super Lawyers® in Employment Law since 2006, and has made the Super Lawyers® Top 50 Women in Florida list as published by Thomson Reuters. In addition, she has been recognized by Tampa Magazine as a Top Lawyer in Labor and Employment in the Tampa Bay Area. Ms. Sass is honored to be a member of the National Trial Lawyers Top 100 and one of the 500 Leading Plaintiff Employment and Civil Rights Lawyers as listed by Lawdragon. The various honors she has received accurately reflect Cynthia’s reputation as an attorney, dedication to assisting her clients and high ethical values.

For a full list of Cynthia’s awards, publications, speaking engagement and associations, check out her Resume CV.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sauer practices in all areas of intellectual property law, representing a wide range of clients in connection with the acquisition, transfer, enforcement and defense of their intellectual property rights. He has represented foreign and domestic clients in connection with patent and trademark prosecution, as well as in proceedings before the United States International Trade Commission.

Prior to practicing law, Mr. Sauer served on active duty as a submarine officer in the United States Navy. At sea, Mr. Sauer served onboard the USS Nebraska, completing his submarine and nuclear engineering officer qualifications. On shore, Mr. Sauer was a submarine tactics instructor at the U.S. Naval Submarine School.

attorneys.name: Thomas C. Saunders Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bartow, FL
attorneys.bio:
Thomas C. Saunders was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in 1957 and move to Miami, Florida in 1969. Following high school, and after a brief tour in the United States Navy, Tom enrolled at the University of Notre Dame in South Bend, Indiana where he obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in English literature in 1980. Tom attended the University of Florida College of Law obtaining his Juris Doctor degree in December, 1982.

Thomas C. Saunders has been in practice in the State of Florida since 1984 and began his career as an Assistant City Attorney in Tampa, Florida. Following that, Tom joined a private insurance defense firm in Tampa representing insureds in all aspects of product liability claims, medical negligence claims, automobile accidents, slip and falls and catastrophic injury claims.

It was during that time, as an insurance defense attorney, that Tom became intimately familiar with the manner in which an insurance company handles and services claims.

In 1991, Tom moved with his family to Polk County, Florida where he joined a private firm working in Plaintiff’s personal injury, commercial litigation and family law. In this position, Tom tried cases ranging from motorcycle claims, automobile cases, medical negligence, contract claims, and all aspects of family law.

In 1991, Tom became Board Certified by the Florida Bar as a specialist in Civil Trial and has been recertified in Civil Trial in 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011 and 2016.

In 1997, Tom was also Board Certified by the Florida Bar as a specialist in Business Litigation and was recertified in 2002, 2007, 2012 and 2017.

Less than 2% of all lawyers in Florida are Board Certified and an even smaller percentage have been fortunate enough to obtain certification as a specialist in more than one area of law.

In 2002, Tom opened his own practice which is no known as Saunders Law Group. The firm is dedicated to litigation of claims involving personal injury, medical negligence, commercial litigation and family law matters.

Tom has been the President of the Polk County Trial Lawyer’s Association, Chairman of the Florida Bar Civil Trial Certification Committee, Chairman of the Tenth Judicial Circuit Judicial Nominating Commission and Chairman of the Bench Bar Committee for the Tenth Judicial Circuit.

Tom has been awarded an AV rating by the prestigious international publication of Martindale-Hubbell and this is the highest rating possible. The rating is established by consultation with peers and judges who rate the attorney not only on the skills demonstrated by the lawyer but also on that lawyer’s adherence to the highest ethical standards. Tom has also been recognized for high professional legal standards in Martindale-Hubbell’s Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers.

Tom is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates where membership is by invitation only. Tom is also a Master level member of the Willson American Inn of Court, Polk County, Florida.

Tom is a member of the American Bar Association, the American Trial Lawyer’s Association, the Florida Bar Association, the Florida Justice Association and is admitted to practice in all courts in the State of Florida as well as the Middle District Federal Court.

Tom is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum where membership is limited to those individuals who have achieved a settlement or verdict in excess of one million dollars. Additionally, Tom is listed as a lifetime member in Strathmore’s Who’s Who and inclusion in this listing is limited to those individuals who have demonstrated leadership and achievement in their occupation, industry or profession.

Tom is also Certified by the Florida Supreme Court as a Circuit Civil Mediator and a Family Law Mediator where alternatives to litigation can often result in a cost savings and far more expedient resolution of disputed matters.

Tom lives in Polk County, Florida with his wife and their two adult children.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of B. Shannon Saunders, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Marianna, FL
attorneys.bio:
B. Shannon Saunders was born in 1973 in Dothan, Alabama. He graduated from Auburn University in 1996 with a degree in Criminology. Following graduation from Auburn University, he attended Nova Southeastern University School of Law, graduating with honors in 1999. During his last semester in law school, Shannon interned with the Broward County State Attorney's Office in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, gaining extensive trial experience.

Following graduation from law school, he began working at the Public Defenders office in Panama City, Florida. There, he tried many serious criminal felony cases. In 2001, Shannon began working for the law firm of Cochran, Cherry, Givens & Smith, P.C. in Dothan, Alabama. There, he specialized in personal injury and wrongful death cases. He participated in the trial where a jury in Dale County, Alabama, returned a record verdict of twenty-five million, which is the largest verdict ever returned in a Dram Shop case in the state of Alabama.

In 2005, Shannon left the Cochran Firm and returned to his home state of Florida, opening up his own practice. His goal was to take the knowledge and experiences gained and apply it to provide injured clients the level of specialized care and attention they deserve and oftentimes don't get from larger firms. Today, he continues to specialize in the area of personal injury and wrongful death cases. He represents injured victims and their families across the Southeast.

attorneys.name: Shelby Savage
attorneys.firm_name: Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
At the Pensacola-based law firm Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes, Shelby Savage is a passionate advocate for policyholders facing unfair treatment by insurance companies. She champions clients whose claims have been unjustly underpaid, delayed or denied, and also handles personal injury cases. In her inaugural year of practice, she has adeptly argued motions in court on intricate discovery issues and masterfully mediated cases, achieving settlements far more favorable than the insurance companies' initial offers. Her talents extend to guiding clients through challenging insurance claim negotiations and resolving complex property damage disputes.

Ms. Savage is committed to understanding her clients on a personal level, listening closely to their stories and needs to effectively convey their experiences to insurers, mediators, judges and juries. Her dedication lies in building trust with her clients and equipping them with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions about protecting their rights and seeking recovery. Whether someone has suffered an injury or feels mistreated by an insurance company, she is eager to offer her support.

A 2019 honors graduate in English and political science from the University of South Alabama, Ms. Savage obtained her J.D. from the University of Alabama School of Law in 2022. She became licensed to practice in Florida that same year and gained admission to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida in 2023. A respected figure in her field, she functions on the executive council of the Escambia-Santa Rosa County Bar Association and is an active participant in its Young Lawyers Division.

During her time in law school, Ms. Savage earned a Public Interest Certification and received the Student Pro Bono Award. She was an articles editor for The Journal of the Legal Profession and had her student note, "The Best of Both Worlds: Granting Derivative Use Immunity for Parents in Juvenile Proceedings," published in its 46th Edition. She also distinguished herself as a semifinalist in the 2021 Campbell Moot Court Competition and as an Outstanding Advocate in the 2022 Duberstein Bankruptcy Moot Court Competition.

attorneys.name: Mr. Scott F. Sawtelle Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Scott F. Sawtelle, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in DeLand, FL
attorneys.bio:
Scott Sawtelle was born in Cambridge, Massachusetts where he lived and worked around the historic City of Boston all his life before joining the U.S. Army. Mr. Sawtelle served domestically and overseas as a Military Policeman for a number of years before being honorably discharged from active to reserve duty. Mr. Sawtelle returned to the City of Boston to study sociology and criminal justice at Suffolk University and shortly thereafter graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1997.

Mr. Sawtelle went on to study law at the Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan where he concentrated in trial litigation before earning a Jurist Doctor in 2001

After law school, Mr. Sawtelle immediately accepted a position as an Assistant Public Defender in Seminole County before transferring to the Volusia County Public Defender's Office, where he practiced criminal defense in the County and Circuit Courts between 2002 and 2006.

During this time, Mr. Sawtelle gained valuable criminal defense experience in the areas of; motion practice, depositions, negotiation skills, and criminal trial litigation by defending indigent clients charged with various felony crimes; including capital sex batteries, armed robberies, aggravated assault and batteries, armed home invasion, DUI manslaughters, drug trafficking, and other various felony and misdemeanor crimes.

Mr. Sawtelle has been a member of the Florida Bar since 2002 and in U.S. Middle District of Florida since 2004. Mr. Sawtelle is currently a member of the Central Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Catherine M. Saylor
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Catherine "Casey" Saylor is the daughter of founding partners, Jacob and Kim Munch. Casey was born and raised here in Tampa, Florida, and is a graduate of H.B. Plant High School. After graduating from Plant, Casey graduated from Georgia Southern University with a B.S. in Education, majoring in Special Education. During her time at Georgia Southern, Casey was an active member and leader of the Phi Mu Sorority.

After a rewarding three years spent as a Special Education Teacher at Grayson Elementary in Grayson, Georgia, Casey decided to follow in her parents' footsteps and pursue a law degree. As a life-long advocate, Casey's history of advocating for children with special needs has proven to bring a unique quality to her work in representing accident victims.

Casey graduated from Stetson University College of Law in Gulfport, Florida in December of 2014. While at Stetson, she graduated with honors, participated in a year-long honors program, and received multiple high grade awards. Casey also had the great honor of interning with United States Magistrate Judge Anthony Porcelli during her last semester at Stetson. At Stetson, Casey was selected to be a Student Ambassador, and held memberships in the Hillsborough Association for Women Lawyers at Stetson and the Admiralty Law Society. Casey is a Florida Bar board certified specialist in admiralty and maritime law.

Much like her father, Casey and her brothers spent countless days out on the boat, learning basic boating skills and navigational rules of the road at a young age. A true Florida girl, Casey has always had a great appreciation for life on the water. Now this appreciation has translated into a dedication to the study of maritime law and advocating for victims of maritime-related accidents.

attorneys.name: Sherri Scarborough
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Winter Haven, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sherri Scarborough was born and raised in Haines City and now resides in Winter Haven. Mrs. Scarborough is certified by the Florida Bar as a specialist in Civil Trial Law, a distinction less than 2% of Florida Lawyers hold. She is the only female attorney in Polk, Hardee and Highlands County that is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law.

Sherri is a member of the Tenth Judicial Circuit Grievance Committee for the Florida Bar, a committee that investigates and assesses ethical complaints against lawyers in Polk, Hardee and Highlands County. She is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell, the highest professionalism and ethical rating from the nationally recognized service for rating lawyers. Sherri is a member of the Winter Haven Rotary and the Winter Haven Women’s Bar Association.

Sherri is a member of the Lawyers Advising Lawyers program for the Florida Bar. This program assists young attorneys who do not have much experience in a particular field in resolving legal issues. As a Lawyer Advising Lawyers member, Sherri has the opportunity to mentor young attorneys and teach them the value of practicing with diligence and professionalism.

She attends the Church of the Redeemer. Sherri is a former Assistant State Attorney for the 10th Judicial Circuit of Florida. She has tried more than 50 jury trials and over 30 trials before the court. She is admitted to practice in all Florida state courts. She graduated from Troy State University and Nova Law School in 1993. She is married, has two children and enjoys sports, fishing and spending time with her family.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Brooksville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly A. Scarano began her legal career in 2005 as an Assistant State Attorney for the Sixth Judicial Circuit in Pinellas and Pasco County, Florida. During her time at the State Attorney’s Office, she tried misdemeanor, felony and juvenile delinquency cases.

In 2008, she left the State Attorney’s Office and worked for seven years as a senior attorney for the Florida Department of Children and Families. As a senior attorney, she was responsible for all aspects of dependency child abuse cases, including termination of parental rights proceedings. She tried a variety of cases, many of which included cases of serious physical and sexual abuse. She also provided legal counsel to child protective investigators, case managers, and to adoptions case managers in her role as adoptions specialist.

Ms. Scarano joined the law firm of Jeffrey P. Cario, P.A. in September of 2015. Since 2015 she has extensive experience litigating complex family law and custody matters.

Ms. Scarano received her Juris Doctorate degree from the Stetson University School of Law in 2005 and her Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Central Florida in 2000.

She is a member of the Florida Bar Association, Hernando Bar Association, and the Hernando-Citrus Inn of Court.

Jeffrey P. Cario, P.A. concentrates its’ efforts on providing clients with quality, ethical representation in their family and criminal law cases. We personally attend to your case needs. Discuss your case with an attorney by scheduling a consultation.

attorneys.name: Ryan C. Scarpa
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Ryan serves as a driving force behind the strategic direction and operational growth of the firm, with a substantive focus on both commercial and residential real estate matters, as well as high-profile business transactions, including mergers and acquisitions.

A seasoned real estate professional, Ryan's practice spans the full spectrum of residential and commercial transactions, encompassing property purchases, sales, financing, deal structuring, construction, and large-scale development projects. His expertise extends to a wide range of business transactions, where he advises on entity formation, corporate governance, mergers, acquisitions, and intricate contract negotiations. Ryan has represented some of the nation's largest Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), franchisees, and prominent real estate investment and development firms, particularly in their Florida-based dealings.

Ryan's unique blend of legal acumen and real-world business experience further enhances his ability to provide exceptional value to clients. His hands-on approach and deep understanding of deal structuring and market dynamics allow him to strategically leverage his network to help clients achieve their goals. Outside of his work at Block & Scarpa, Ryan has personally identified, operated, and successfully exited over $250 million in real estate ventures and business enterprises. He has also overseen and helped scale several multi-million-dollar businesses in industries including real estate, consumer product goods, marketing and representation, and hospitality.

Ryan has represented hundreds of athletes, entertainers, and high-profile celebrities in negotiating complex sponsorship deals, endorsement agreements, and NFT (non-fungible token) releases.

Recognized for his diligence and unparalleled advocacy, Ryan is frequently invited to speak on a wide array of legal and business topics. His dedication to excellence and client success has earned him recognition by Super Lawyers each year since 2020, where he has been honored for his exceptional contributions to both the firm and the legal profession. Ryan has also been named to Florida Trend Magazine’s prestigious list of Notable Managing Partners on multiple occasions, based upon peer nominations. Ryan’s leadership has been instrumental in driving the firm’s remarkable growth, with Block & Scarpa expanding by more than 1000% in the past decade.

attorneys.name: Marshall Schaap
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Marshall Schaap was born and raised in Ocala, Florida. He graduated from Belleview High School and then went to the University of Florida on a football scholarship. After two years at UF, he transferred to the University of Wyoming, where he graduated with a business degree. He then returned to Florida for law school, attending Stetson University College of Law, where he met his wife, Natalie. The couple has two remarkable daughters.

After spending more than a decade litigating injury cases at one of Tampa's best defense firms, Mr. Schaap joined Morgan & Morgan, where he represents people injured in vehicle accidents. With his background as an athlete who had a reputation as an aggressive, hard-nosed football player, he enjoys the intensity of trial as being similar to game day. Mr. Schaap enjoys getting to know his clients, and takes pride not only in getting his clients the best possible outcome, but also in giving them straightforward advice about their situation.

Mr. Schaap makes the most out of time with his family, and especially enjoys sharing his love of the outdoors with them, such as fishing, camping, hiking, and hunting.

As a Type 1 diabetic, he is a volunteer coach with Sam Fuld's USF Diabetes Sports Camp for children with Type 1 diabetes, and previously served on the Board of Directors for the Tampa Bay Chapter of the Juvenile Diabetes Research Foundation.

attorneys.name: Dominic Scavo
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Palm Harbor, FL
attorneys.bio:
Dominic grew up in Hornell, New York - a small town located in the Finger Lakes region of Western New York. Dominic graduated cum laude from Alfred University and Stetson University College of Law. While at Stetson Law, Dominic gained valuable insight into our legal system by serving as a judicial intern to the Honorable Edward C. LaRose of Florida's Second District Court of Appeal.

Dominic became interested in representing injured individuals due in part to his unique injury history. Throughout the years, Dominic suffered injuries including a fractured left femur, broken right elbow, and shattered left thumb. Additionally, Dominic has undergone surgeries to his lumbar spine, left knee, right shoulder, and left femur. Such daunting experiences give Dominic a unique understanding of what his clients are going through and how best to serve their needs. Furthermore, Dominic prides himself on maintaining an open line of communication with each of his clients. In support of this sentiment, Dominic provides each client with his personal cell phone number and makes himself available to each at all hours of the day.

Dominic resides in Saint Petersburg, Florida where he enjoys spending time with his adopted dog, Storm, exercising, and watching his New York Mets and New York Jets.

attorneys.name: Kevin Schaefer
attorneys.bio:
Kevin Schaefer is an associate attorney at Dabdoub Law Firm. Kevin began his legal career as a law clerk at the firm while in law school. His passion for helping people get the disability benefits they deserve became a full-time job when he joined the firm as a disability lawyer after graduating from law school.

Kevin focuses on assisting clients with claims for short term and long term disability benefits. He handles long term disability appeals when those benefits are wrongly denied or terminated and lawsuits for disability insurance benefits in state and federal court. His clients are entitled to disability benefits through individual or group disability insurance policies. The majority of his clients’ claims fall under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Since joining Dabdoub Law Firm, Kevin has represented clients with claims against all major disability insurance companies. His clients suffer from many different medical conditions, including, but not limited to, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, chronic fatigue syndrome, multiple sclerosis, stroke, cardiovascular disease, Meniere’s disease, cognitive impairments, and concussions. Kevin has also represented former NFL players in their fight for total and permanent disability benefits under the NFL’s disability plan.

Kevin graduated magna cum laude from the University of Miami School of Law in 2016. Prior to joining the firm, Kevin worked in an in-house legal department for a large infrastructure corporation. While attending the University of Miami School of Law, he received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award for his work in Representing a Pro Sports Franchise course. Prior to attending law school, Kevin graduated summa cum laude from the University of Central Florida and earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Management, along with a minor in Sports Business Management.

attorneys.name: Steven M. Schain
attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Finance Litigation Lawyers in Miami Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
2019 National Law Journal “Finance, Banking, & Capital Markets Trailblazer” award winner, Steve is admitted to practice in Pennsylvania and New Jersey and represents entities, governments and individuals in litigation, regulation, compliance, preparing and submitting license applications, entity formation, and drafting legislation.

A nationally recognized consumer finance litigation, banking law and cannabis law expert, Steve is an American Lawyer Media columnist, frequent Pennsylvania Bar Institute and National Bar Institute author and lecturer and serves as a court appointed judge pro tempore and arbitrator.

Steve is also an Adjunct Faculty Member of, and teaches “Cannabis Law” at, Stockton University, one of only 12 universities offering a major in Cannabis and Hemp Studies. A Psychedelic Bar Association founder, Steve serves on, and makes regular presentations to, the American Society of Testing and Measurement, the National Cannabis Industry Association, the International Cannabis Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Credit Union Association, Bank Secrecy Act Compliance Group, Cannabis Professional Advancement Series, and Marijuana Business Daily.

Steve also serves on both Commonwealth of Pennsylvania and Philadelphia County administrative committees charged with drafting and revising state and local cannabis related regulations.

Steve earned his B.A. degree from Pennsylvania State University and his J.D. degree from the University of Pittsburgh School of Law, where he served as an editor of the Law Review and graduated with honors.

Before entering private practice, Steve served as law clerk to a U.S. District Court judge for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Schahrer (pronounced “Share-er”) grew up in Naples, Florida and attended Gulf Coast High School. He then earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a Master of Public Administration from Florida Gulf Coast University.

Mr. Schahrer continued his studies at Liberty University School of Law where he earned his Juris Doctor. While in law school, Mr. Schahrer was a Senior Staff Member of the Law Review and a competitor with the Trial Team. During his time with the Trial Team, Mr. Schahrer was the senior member of the team that placed among the top four teams at a national Mock Trial Competition where he was also recognized as one of the top five Advocates in the entire competition. Mr. Schahrer received the Trial Advocacy Award for outstanding achievement in Trial Advocacy from Liberty University School of Law and graduated third in his class.

Mr. Schahrer has a diverse professional background including experience working for the Florida State Legislature, the United States Marshals Service headquarters in Washington D.C., and the local non-profit, St. Matthew’s House. He joined the Boatman Law Firm as a Law Clerk in 2016 and worked with the Firm throughout his time in Law School and then joined the Firm as an Associate Attorney. In his spare time, Mr. Schahrer enjoys training and teaching Martial Arts and spending time with his family in beautiful Naples, FL.

Hunter is a native Floridian who has spent much of her life living in Lake Worth, Florida. Hunter now uses her research and litigation experience at Barner & Barner to fiercely advocate for her clients.

Hunter is an active member of the Palm Beach County Bar Association and Real Property Probate and Trust Law section of the Florida Bar.

attorneys.name: Mitch Schermer
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Lease & Real Property Litigation Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mitch Schermer is a partner with Morgan & Morgan's Business Trial Group in Tampa, Florida. Mitch's practice is dedicated to the representation of businesses and individuals in commercial and real property litigation. Mitch also focuses on construction litigation, representing clients in construction defect, lien, and payment dispute litigation. Throughout his career, Mitch has obtained favorable results for clients in high-stakes matters in both state and federal courts.

By litigating matters exclusively on a contingency-fee-basis, Mitch works tirelessly to assist his clients in obtaining the justice that they deserve. Mitch's practice is well-positioned to allow his clients to litigate against opponents with deep pockets in order to right wrongs and to be fairly and adequately compensated for their damages.

Mitch is rated AV-Preeminent by Martindale Hubble, demonstrating that his peers view him as exhibiting the highest level of legal skill, acumen, and ethical standards. This distinction is awarded to approximately 10% of lawyers nationwide. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mitch practiced at a boutique litigation firm in Tampa, focusing on business and commercial litigation, construction litigation, and real property litigation.

Mitch is a graduate of Stetson University College of Law, where he served as Student Body President in his third year. While in law school, Mitch worked as a research assistant focusing on consumer protection law and antitrust. He also served as an intern to the Honorable Pamela A.M. Campbell of Florida's Sixth Judicial Circuit. Mitch is an honors graduate of Florida State University, where he obtained degrees in political science and international relations.

Currently, Mitch serves as Vice President of the Stetson University College of Law Alumni Association, and is also the President-Elect of the organization. Mitch has been appointed to serve on Florida Bar Committees, and has given his time in service of non-profit organizations.

Mitch is fluent in Spanish and maintains conversational proficiency in Hebrew, allowing him to better serve his clients.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Martindale Hubble AV-Preeminent Rating 2020, 2021

attorneys.name: William R. Scherer
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
William "Bill" R. Scherer cofounded Conrad & Scherer in 1974 with his late partner Rex Conrad. Over the past almost four decades, Mr. Scherer has grown the firm into one of Florida's leading law firms and has expanded the firm's presence with offices in New York, New York, Brevard, North Carolina, and Quito, Ecuador.

AV® PreeminentTM Peer Rated by Martindale-Hubbell® since 1987, Mr. Scherer is a seasoned trial attorney. He has litigated over 100 trials in both jury and non-jury cases before state, appellate, and federal courts. Mr. Scherer's cases and legal accomplishments have received coverage by major television networks such as CNN, CNBC, MSNBC and FNN and national and local newspapers such as The New York Times, Los Angeles Times, The Wall Street Journal, South Florida Business Journal, the Daily Business Review, the Sun-Sentinel and the Miami Herald.

Mr. Scherer was lead counsel for victims of the infamous multi-billion dollar Ponzi scheme orchestrated by Scott Rothstein. Notably, Mr. Scherer led his complex litigation team and achieved an historic settlement returning to investors what is said to be the highest percentages of recovery for victims of a Ponzi scheme. News outlets described the settlement as a "huge victory" and a "landmark" lawsuit.

In 2005, Mr. Scherer served as plaintiff's counsel in a high-profile commercial lawsuit involving the sale of a health insurance company and obtained, by jury verdict, one of the largest damage awards in Broward County history.

During the historical 2000 Presidential Election Litigation in Florida, Mr. Scherer led a team of attorneys representing President George W. Bush and personally represented the President in the Broward County recount.

In addition to his litigation practice, Mr. Scherer has also served as counsel to various government entities. From 1988 to 2005, Mr. Scherer served as General Counsel to the North Broward Hospital District, one of the largest public health care providers in the nation, with four hospitals and nine specialized treatment centers. As General Counsel for the Hospital District, he supervised teams of legal experts in healthcare and malpractice law, and was responsible for all trials and legal actions taken by or against the Hospital District.

Mr. Scherer began his legal career as a law clerk to the Indiana Supreme Court and the Honorable Charles Fulton, Former Chief of the United States District Court for the South District of Florida.

attorneys.name: Marc Schiller
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Davie, FL
attorneys.bio:
Marc Schiller is a managing and founding partner of the The Schiller Kessler Group. Born in Merrick, New York, he moved to Florida with his family in 1984. He received his Bachelor’s Degree in Criminology and Criminal Justice from Florida State University in 1992, and his J.D. Degree from St. Thomas University School of Law in 1995.

Upon graduating from law school, Mr. Schiller worked as an associate at a prestigious law firm specializing in personal injury and wrongful death claims. After a few years, Mr. Schiller left his associate position with that firm and opened his own law firm, focusing solely on personal injury and wrongful death cases.

Mr. Schiller has committed his life to representing those people injured as a result of someone else’s negligence. Mr. Schiller limits his practice exclusively to personal injury, wrongful death, premises liability and nursing home abuse cases. He is a member of The Florida Bar, Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers, Association of Trial Lawyers of America, Broward County Bar Association, Tort and Insurance Law Committee, as well as several other associations. Mr. Schiller has conducted numerous seminars over the years, educating people on current issues related to personal injury and insurance coverage cases. Mr. Schiller also routinely performs Pro Bono work in the community for those less fortunate.

As one of the busiest and most well respected personal injury law firms in Florida, Mr. Schiller and his firm have handled over 10,000 personal injury cases, aggressively representing their clients to recover the maximum monetary compensation possible.

attorneys.name: Philip J. Schipani ESQ
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Philip J. Schipani Board Certified in Matrimonial and Family Law by the Florida Bar, a distinction held be less than 10 percent of attorneys in Florida. Mr. Schipani practices all aspects of Family Law. Schipani was admitted to the Florida Bar in 2002 and is a 1998 graduate of Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University where he received his Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science. He graduated from the University of Miami School of Law with a Juris Doctor degree in 2001, Cum Laude.

Philip grew up in Northern Virginia outside of Washington D.C. Philip began practicing Family Law during his second year of Law School, when he obtained his certificate as a certified legal intern, which allowed him to practice in the State Courts of Florida. During that time, he interned with the Miami-Dade County Legal Aid Society. At Legal Aid in Miami, Philip litigated divorce cases and represented numerous individuals obtaining domestic violence injunctions.

Upon graduation of Law School, Philip's first job was working for two Miami-Dade County Family Court Judges as a case manager. During his time working with the Court system he gained valuable experience and knowledge of the family court system from the inside out. Part of his duties were to manage the Judges' caseloads and help pro se litigants obtain divorces and other relief in the Family Court system.

During law school, he was a Judicial Intern for Federal Magistrate John J. O'Sullivan in Miami, FL.

Philip is an active member of the Florida Bar Family Law section, in which he has chaired the Domestic Violence Committee, the Rules & Forms Committee and the Ad Hoc Special Needs Children Committee. He is also a member of the Family Law section of the Florida Bar executive council and the legislative committee.

In addition, Philp was a program chair and a workshop leader for the 2019 Family Law Section Trial Advocacy Workshop wherein he was teamed with a family law magistrate to teach litigation and courtroom skills. Schipani has also twice lectured at seminars on domestic violence presented by the Family Law Section of the Florida Bar.

Philp has two children. One of which is his son, who is non-verbal autistic. Philip’s passion for his own child has led him to give several local seminars to the Sarasota Bar Association on dealing with special needs children in divorce cases as well as chairing and speaking at the first full day seminar presented by the Family Law Section of the Florida Bar on special needs children issues in family law cases.

He is also a member of the Family Law section of the Florida Bar executive council and the legislative committee.

In addition, Philp was a program chair and a workshop leader for the 2019 Family Law Section Trial Advocacy Workshop wherein he was teamed with a family law magistrate to teach litigation and courtroom skills. Schipani has also twice lectured at seminars on domestic violence presented by the Family Law Section of the Florida Bar.

Philp has two children. One of which is his son, who is non-verbal autistic. Philip’s passion for his own child has led him to give several local seminars to the Sarasota Bar Association on dealing with special needs children in divorce cases as well as chairing and speaking at the first full day seminar presented by the Family Law Section of the Florida Bar on special needs children issues in family law cases.

attorneys.name: Gregory R. Schmitz
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Gregory Schmitz joined the national law firm of Morgan & Morgan, P.A. after spending his career practicing employment law with some of the largest employment law firms in the world, representing Fortune 500 corporations. Immediately prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Schmitz spent several years working at the largest labor and employment law firm in the world, Littler Mendelson. Mr. Schmitz now uses that experience to better serve his current clients. Mr. Schmitz is a specialist in the field of employment law. Mr. Schmitz also has arbitration, bench trial, and jury trial experience. Using his wide range of expertise, he has litigated claims throughout the country, under federal and state law, including sexual harassment, race, age, disability, religion, gender, as well as retaliation and whistleblower claims. Mr. Schmitz has also litigated numerous overtime and wage-related lawsuits, including nationwide collective and class actions. In addition to the practice of law, Mr. Schmitz is involved with a number of organizations. Mr. Schmitz is a member of the Labor and Employment Sections of the Florida Bar, American Bar Association, and the Orange County Bar Association. Mr. Schmitz received his Bachelors of Arts degree from Florida Atlantic University and his Juris Doctor degree from Emory University, School of Law, graduating from both institutions with honors. Mr. Schmitz is admitted to practice in Florida, the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida.

attorneys.name: Carl F. Schoeppl
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Carl F. Schoeppl is the Managing Shareholder of the Schoeppl Law, P.A. Mr. Schoeppl is a former senior federal prosecutor with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"), Division of Enforcement, and prosecuted some of the most notable securities fraud cases on behalf of the SEC in federal courts throughout the Southeastern United States at that time, including SEC v. Chapnick, [1993-1994 Transfer Binder] Fed. Sec. L. Rep. (CCR) r 98,076 (S.D. Fla. Feb. 11, 1994)(an insider trading and $33 million securities fraud case involving former officers of the failed Commonwealth Savings and Loan Association of Florida); and SEC v. Bradt, [Current Transfer Binder] Fed. Sec. L. Rep. (CCR), r 98,624 (S.D. Fla. Mar. 7, 1995)(a $27 million "Ponzi" scheme case involving the notorious con-man Thomas R. Mullens and the defunct Omni Capital Group, Ltd.). Mr. Schoeppl also served as Ethics Counsel for the SEC's Southeast Regional Office, and was responsible for rendering ethics opinions and legal advice on ethical issues to a staff of over fifty. Prior to his tenure at the SEC, Mr. Schoeppl was a Special Assistant District Attorney in Atlanta, Georgia with responsibility over trying major felony criminal cases.

Mr. Schoeppl has been appointed by the United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, upon the recommendation of the SEC, as the Receiver for five different corporations in an SEC enforcement action styled SEC v. Schaefer, et al., Case No. 98-343-CIV-ORL-22A (M.D. Fla.)($3.5 million securities fraud/Ponzi scheme case involving the sale of promissory notes). Mr. Schoeppl has also been appointed by the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, upon the recommendation of the Federal Trade Commission ("FTC"), as the Receiver for Transworld Enterprises, Inc. in an FTC enforcement action styled FTC v. Transworld Enterprises, Inc., et al., Case No. 00-8126-CIV-GRARAM (S.D. Fla.)($3 million nationwide franchise fraud case involving the sale of ATM business opportunities). Mr. Schoeppl was appointed by the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, upon the recommendation of the SEC, to serve as the Receiver for U.S. Capital Funding, Inc. in a $48 million securities fraud case styled SEC v. First Capital Services, Inc., et al., Case No. 00-8445-CIV-MIDDLEBROOKS (S.D. Fla.). Recently, Mr. Schoeppl was appointed by the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, upon the recommendation of the FTC, as Temporary Receiver for America's Shopping Network, Inc. ("ASN"), Consumer Services, Inc., Karen Zagami, Carianne Sica, Louis Gangi, RME, Inc., and John Epstein in an FTC enforcement action styled FTC v. America's Shopping Network, Inc., et al., Case No. 02-80540-CIV-HURLEY (S.D. Fla.). In ASN, the Defendants allegedly conducted a nationwide fraudulent work-at-home scheme. Mr. Schoeppl has also served as an expert witness for the SEC in SEC v. Web Hosting Headquarters Partnership, et al., Case No.: 00-4975-CIV­ RIGRSMITR/GARBER (S.D. Fla.). Mr. Schoeppl is a Florida Supreme Court Certified Circuit Civil Mediator.

attorneys.name: Rachel R. Schrager
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Rachel R. Schrager is a respected shareholder and personal injury attorney at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A., known for her dedication to protecting the rights of injured individuals. With a dynamic career that spans both sides of the courtroom, she brings a rare depth of perspective to personal injury litigation—having previously served as a Partner at a national firm defending insurance carriers and civil litigants.

Her experience in complex insurance coverage and defense work now fuels her advocacy for plaintiffs, ensuring that clients benefit from her strategic insight and comprehensive understanding of the legal landscape. Her approach is both compassionate and results-driven, reflecting her commitment to achieving justice for those affected by injury or negligence.

Mrs. Schrager earned her Juris Doctorate from Wake Forest University in 2012, where she actively engaged in youth and child advocacy through legal clinics and held leadership roles, including President of the Women in Law Student organization. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree, cum laude, from Syracuse University, with majors in Special Education, Elementary Education, and Sociology—an academic foundation that underscores her empathetic and inclusive mindset.

A skilled litigator with a passion for advocacy, Rachel Schrager continues to be a strong voice for clients throughout Florida, blending legal precision with personal commitment at Kogan & DiSalvo, P.A.

attorneys.name: Timothy W. Schulz
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Commercial Litigation Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Timothy W. Schulz, an attorney with Timothy W., Schulz, P.A., is also Of Counsel to Jacobson Law P.A. Tim is a former police officer with the Atlantic City Police Department in Atlantic City, New Jersey. After suffering injuries in a serious on-duty automobile accident and, after ten years of service, he retired from law enforcement and attended law school at the Nova Southeastern University Shepard Broad Law Center in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

During his law school years he worked in Miami, Florida as a summer law clerk for Roy Black, Esq., one of the country's premier criminal defense trial attorneys; was a judicial intern for the Hon. William H. Hoeveler, United States District Court, Southern District of Florida; and spent a semester working full-time as a Certified Legal Intern with the Miami-Dade County State Attorney's Office, where he tried several felony jury cases to verdict under the direction and supervision of a senior Assistant State Attorney.

Upon graduation, Tim was hired as an associate attorney by Black, Srebnick & Kornspan, P.A., in Miami, Florida, where he continued to work with Roy Black, Esq., co-counseling and co-trying numerous state court criminal cases and trials, including a nationally televised murder trial covered live by Court TV. Tim also co-counseled a case in which Albertsons, a Fortune 500 Company, was charged with corporate criminal manslaughter in the death of shoplifter during a struggle with supermarket employees. A dismissal of that case was ultimately obtained. During his five years at Black, Srebnick & Kornspan, Tim developed a special niche in crime scene investigation, criminal forensics and the cross-examination of expert witnesses in areas such as forensic pathology, ballistics, trace evidence, and DNA comparisons.

In 2000, Tim decided to apply his trial experience gained in Miami in the area of commercial and business litigation, and joined the litigation department at Greenberg Traurig, P.A., one of the largest and most respected domestic and international law firms today. While at Greenberg Traurig, Tim represented a number of Fortune 500 and other publicly traded and private companies in a myriad of complex litigation matters, often dealing with multi-million dollar disputes.

Tim concentrates his practice in the areas of complex commercial litigation, real estate litigation, and white collar criminal defense. In 2013, Tim obtained an order striking an opposing party's pleadings and granting attorneys' fees as a sanction after proving that the opposing party submitted a "doctored" email to the court in support of statutory claims which sought economic damages over $40,000,000.00. Following a four day trial, the court found, "by clear and convincing evidence, that either [the opposing party] or his attorney ... fraudulently doctored the email." See Palm Beach Fla. Hotel v. Nantucket Enters., Inc., 2013 WL 686433 (Fla. Cir. Ct. Feb. 25, 2013).

Tim is admitted to practice law in Florida; the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida;; and the Courts of Appeals for the Fourth and Eleventh Circuits, and the United States Supreme Court.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Deland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Schumann received a Juris Doctor from Louisiana State University, Paul M. Hebert Law Center in 1988. Originally from New Orleans, Louisiana, Ray relocated to Southwest Florida in 1991. In 2011 he and his family moved to Central Florida. His status as a Florida Bar Board Certified Real Estate Attorney places him in a category achieved by less than ½ of 1% of all currently licensed Florida Attorneys. He is also a member of Orange County Bar Association, Louisiana State Bar Association, and Volusia County Bar Association.

Ray concentrates his practice on commercial and complex real estate and business transactions. With his comprehensive and extensive real estate and business expertise, he focuses primarily on matters involving real estate and business transactions, acquisition, development, strategies and planning. Ray has significant experience in commercial real estate financing, mortgages, loan restructuring and workouts by representing numerous lending institutions and private entities; he utilizes his facilitation mind-set in negotiating, closing and enforcing commercial contracts, leases and property management agreements for brokers and investor/owners, and providing title issuance, rectification and defect resolution advice, guidance and services for all those involved in the transactions. Ray is well known for his unique solution-minded approach while keeping the "end goal" in mind to achieve the desired results.

attorneys.name: Charles A. Schuster
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from Florida State College of Law with Honors, Charles A. Schuster began his career as a trial lawyer with the oldest defense firm in Florida rising to become partner. In that capacity he was involved in a wide range of personal injury claims including automobile and trucking accidents, boating and personal water craft accidents, premises liability claims including slip and fall accidents and negligent security claims, product liability claims including asbestos, defective fork lifts and a helicopter crash in the Philippines and medical malpractice claims.

Based on his interest in effective and efficient conflict resolution, Mr. Schuster became a Florida Supreme Court Certified Mediator in 1991 and assisted hundreds of parties in reaching fair settlements of their personal injury claims.

When he was an Insurance Defense Lawyer, 20% of his practice was devoted to representation of injured victims of negligence. In 2002 he joined Gross & Schuster and now spends 100% of his time representing the injured against insurance companies.

He has lectured in the field of medical malpractice and effective mediation.

He is an avid motorcyclist and has a special interest in representing the victims of motor cycle accidents.

Mr. Schuster has been Board Certified as a specialist in Civil Trial Law by the Florida Bar since 1988 and has been certified as a Civil Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy since 1990.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Schwartz practices in the firm's Securities Law and Commercial Litigation practice groups. In addition to representing financial institutions, broker-dealers, and investment advisers in securities litigation and arbitration related matters, Mr. Schwartz's areas of focus also include breaches of contracts and warranties, products liability, negligence, the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, fraud, and fiduciary duties. Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Schwartz worked at a boutique law firm in Miami where he handled complex commercial litigation cases and class action lawsuits in federal and state courts at both the trial and appellate levels. Mr. Schwartz was also responsible for various transactional matters, including preparing commercial and corporate contracts for foreign and domestic companies.

While attending law school, Mr. Schwartz was the Research Editor for the University of Florida Journal of Law & Public Policy, a member of the Dean's List, earned Book Awards for the highest grades in his Legal Research & Writing and Comparative Constitutional History courses, and was recognized with an award for his commitment to pro bono service. In addition to interning for one of Florida's distinguished United States senators, Mr. Schwartz has also clerked for the Office of the Attorney General for the State of Florida, the Office of the Public Defender for the Eighth Judicial Circuit of Florida, and an illustrious circuit court judge in Florida's Seventeenth Judicial Circuit.

attorneys.name: Eric T. Schwartzreich
attorneys.practice_type: Murder Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Westchester County, New York and raised in Rye Brook, New York. Eric attended Kents Hill School in Kents Hill, Maine. Upon graduating high school, Eric attended Muskingum University in New Concord, Ohio, receiving a bachelor’s degree in psychology. After college, Eric attended Nova Southeastern University in Fort Lauderdale, Florida earning a master’s in business administration. After receiving his M.B.A., he went on to receive his Juris Doctor, from St. Thomas University School of Law, in Miami, Florida.

Mr. Schwartzreich has extensive trial experience throughout the State of Florida, with nearly 25 years spent handling adult and juvenile matters, in state and federal court. Mr. Schwartzreich's trial experience of over 200 trials, both bench and jury trials, has made him a skilled litigator.

Mr. Schwartzreich's office is located directly across from the Broward County Courthouse in downtown Fort Lauderdale. Mr. Schwartzreich predominantly handles cases in Broward, Miami Dade, and Palm Beach counties but often represents clients throughout the State of Florida.

While an avid trial lawyer, Mr. Schwartzreich also handles criminal appeals, arguing before the Florida Appellate Courts and Florida Supreme Court. Most recently, Mr. Schwartzreich successfully argued before the Florida Supreme Court for a law enforcement officer's right to use Florida's Stand Your Ground Laws. Mr. Schwartzreich was the first attorney in Florida to successfully make this argument.

Mr. Schwartzreich has argued many Stand Your Ground Motions throughout the State of Florida and has lectured on the topic at the Broward Bench and Bar Conference, a conference for lawyers and judges.

He has represented clients with a wide range of felony and misdemeanor charges including murder, all drug offenses including drug trafficking, rape/ sexual battery, grand theft, fraud, and DUI/DWI. Eric represents individuals facing probation violations and who have other probation related issues. Eric handles white collar cases including health care fraud.

Mr. Schwartzreich represents members of several law enforcement unions, the Police Benevolent Association, the International Union of Police Associations, and the Broward Sheriff's Office Deputies Association. Eric represents many police officers through the internal administrative process within the police agencies they work for and when charged in criminal court.

Mr. Schwartzreich and his firm have been featured on Dateline, 48 Hours, Fox Business News Network on the Neil Cavuto Show, Fox Headline News, CNN, MCNBC, and other national news networks. Eric's cases are covered by local and national media outlets and newspapers. Mr. Schwartzreich has been quoted in articles in the ABA Journal, the Daily Business Review, Miami Herald, Sun Sentinel, Orlando Sentinel, Palm Beach Post and other newspapers and periodicals throughout the country and worldwide. Eric continues to be a legal commentator on national news talk shows and is frequently asked to comment on local legal news stories on television and print media.

Mr. Schwartzreich enjoys sharing his love of the legal system though teaching and lecturing. Mr. Schwartzreich's was invited to lectured three times at the prestigious Russian Legal Academy in Moscow, Russia, to Russian judges and law students about the American criminal justice system. Mr. Schwartzreich has been invited by judges of the 17th Judicial Circuit to lecture to their law student and college student interns. Mr. Schwartzreich has been a guest lecturer at Saint Thomas University Law of School, his al ma mater.

Mr. Schwartzreich has successfully advocated before the Florida Legislature as well as to local city and county commissions for the firm's clients and for the rights of citizens. He has also testified before the Senate Appropriations Committee in Tallahassee, Florida.

Eric's passion for the law and the legal system bought him to the American Heritage High School Law Program, in Plantation, Florida, where he has been coaching a high school mock trial team for many years. His students have won over ten (10) Broward County Mock Trial competitions, five (5) State Championships, and three (3) titles in the prestigious Empire Mock Trial Competition, in both New York City and San Francisco, against the best teams in the U.S. and international teams.

In 2019, the Florida Law Related Education Association presented Eric with the Ed Lange Award for his commitment to legal studies and dedication to teaching professionalism, legal skill, and knowhow to his students.

He is a former Assistant Public Defender for the 17th Judicial Circuit in and for Broward County. In 1995, the Public Defender's Office recognized Eric as Intern of the Year. He is a Member of the Florida Bar, former President of the Broward Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, former Treasurer of the Broward Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, former member of the Dade County Bar Association and Federal Bar Association, former member of the National Trial Lawyers Association and member of the International Legal Fraternity Phi Delta Phi.

Mr. Schwartzreich's past and current community involvement include the Fort Lauderdale Beach Rotary Club. He was previously appointed to the Human Rights Board by then Broward County Commissioner Lori Parrish. He was appointed by former Councilwoman Sharon Uria of Plantation to serve as an alternate on the City of Plantation's Zoning Board.

Mr. Schwartzreich is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell, Super Lawyers and Avvo.

Eric is married to attorney Mila Schwartzreich and they have two children.

attorneys.bio:
Michael H. Scott brings a unique perspective to 5241619Lesser, Landy, Smith & Siegel, PLLC, joining the West Palm Beach and Stuart offices after 10 years of litigating cases in state and federal courts, primarily as a defense attorney.

During his tenure at defense firms in Florida, Massachusetts and Connecticut, Michael gained substantial experience and invaluable insight into the strategies and tactics often employed by defendants and their insurers in worker’s compensation, property insurance, automobile, and premises liability lawsuits.

Eager for more rewarding results for injured clients and their families, Michael joined Lesser, Landy, Smith & Siegel, PLLC in October 2024 and focuses his practice on representing individuals and families who have suffered serious personal injury, wrongful death, or have been victimized because of the bad faith practices of an insurance company.

Originally from New England, Michael graduated from the University of Connecticut School of Law, and is admitted to practice in Florida’s state and federal courts. He is also licensed in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and is a Florida Supreme Court Certified Mediator and Arbitrator. In addition to his legal work, he is a supporter of, and contributor to, diversity within Florida’s Bar and a leader in the local UConn Alumni Association.

Michael enjoys attending local events, traveling and playing sports, and networking with others in South Florida.

Call Michael today at 561-655-2028 or email mscott@lesserlawfirm.com.

attorneys.practice_type: Landlord / Tenant Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Patrice Scott grew up in Central Florida. Attorney Scott decided to pursue and earn a Bachelor’s degree from the University of Central Florida graduating with a Bachelor Degree in Legal Studies with a Minor in Criminal Justice. A few years later, Patrice earned a Juris Doctorate from Florida A&M University of Law.

Patrice has several years’ experience working in litigation for Florida based law firms, in areas such as housing and real estate law, foreclosure law representing banks in pursuit of foreclosing on single-family homes, and affordable housing. Additionally, Attorney Scott has worked under one of the largest private sector developers and continues to work with local start-ups and established companies. Attorney Scott gained extensive knowledge in landlord-tenant law, particularly government subsidized properties, during her time as a Legal Fellow under the Equal Justice Works AmeriCorps Program sponsored under the Housing and Urban Development, “HUD” in the Affordable Housing Division. While working as a Legal Fellow, Attorney Scott trained in landlord-tenant law, including the Rental Assistance Demonstration Program, government subsidized programs such as LIHTC, Project Based Section 8, and the processes of funding both for landlords and developers. Attorney Scott continues to represent Developers, Homeowners and Landlords in tackling many Code Enforcement, Landlord-Tenant and Real Estate issues.

Thomas Scully, Esq. has devoted the past 25 years of his professional career to helping injured workers collect the full benefits they deserve. Admitted to the Florida bar in 1997, he is a renowned specialist in work injury claims.

Thomas Scully received his undergraduate degree from the University of Albany and his J.D. from the St. Thomas University School of Law.
