attorneys.name: Allana Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Allana "Lana" Smith is a Litigation Associate in our Miami, FL office. Having grown up in Ohio watching her mother run her own law practice, Ms. Smith developed a passion for professionalism and advocacy at an early age.

Ms. Smith began her legal career as an intern at the Supreme Court of Ohio where she worked alongside Chief Justice Maureen O'Connor, the Ohio House of Representatives, and the Ohio Senate on Ohio's bail reform. She graduated from the University of Dayton with a dual bachelor's degree in Psychology and Criminal Justice Studies in 2017. In 2020, Ms. Smith received her Juris Doctorate from the University of Florida Levin College of Law. During law school, Ms. Smith competed in national and local mock trial and moot court competitions, which strengthened her ability to debate, negotiate, and advocate on behalf of her clients.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Smith defended national corporations against high-profile negligence claims and represented homeowner's associations and single-family homeowners in bringing complex construction defect claims. Having represented both plaintiffs and defendants, Ms. Smith is equipped with the knowledge and unique skill set to properly handle all aspects of your case.

In her spare time, Ms. Smith enjoys spending time with her family, friends, two dogs, and 30 houseplants. She also enjoys baking, writing, barre, and creating content for social media. Ms. Smith is a devout Christian.

attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Christopher J. Smith has been a practicing attorney in Tampa, Florida since 1989. He is a sole practitioner, representing injured workers and disabled individuals throughout Tampa Bay and west central Florida. Mr. Smith received his undergraduate degree from Wake Forest University in 1986. He received his juris doctor degree from Stetson University College of Law in 1989. He has focused on workers' compensation law since he began his practice in 1989, and he has been Board Certified by The Florida Bar in Workers' Compensation Law since 1996. In addition to his handling of workers' compensation claims, he also represents individuals in connection with Social Security Disability claims. He has been a member of the Board of Directors of Florida Workers' Advocates since 2003 and was president of that organization in 2008 - 2009 and 2018 - 2019. He has also been a member of the Executive Council of The Workers' Compensation Section of The Florida Bar since 2007 and was Chair of the Council in 2013 - 2014. He was a member of the Rules Advisory Committee of The Florida Bar from 2011 - 2014. He has spoken at numerous legal conferences throughout his practice on a variety of workers' compensation topics.

Smith finds gratitude in his work through "the ability to leave someone in a better situation than when they came to you." He loves meeting and interacting with people, and encourages you to call him today!

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Conti Moore has quickly earned a reputation in the Central Florida legal community as being a fierce advocate for her clients. Her fighting spirit in championing the rights of her clients makes her a formidable opponent for any opposing counsel, no matter their resources or professional pedigree. “Stress less. Choose Moore.” is not merely a slogan—it is the credo by which Conti Moore Law, PLLC operates. It is the guiding principle by which all matters are handled from inception to favorable final judgment.

When Conti Moore takes on a case, she brings with her a wealth of knowledge obtained from the best schools in the state. Litigation—both criminal and civil—is nothing less than a war made up of many small battles which are won or lost long before a case is brought to trial. Conti’s determined approach to winning every one of those small battles was crafted when she attended Florida A&M University whose call to action is to “Strike, Strike, and Strike Again.” It was at Florida A&M University where Conti earned a Bachelor of Science in computer information systems with a minor in business, gaining the acumen she now utilizes to operate her own successful business and represent her clients in business law matters.

The unyielding, battle-ready disposition that Conti brings to every case was fortified when she attended and earned her Doctor of Jurisprudence at the College of Law at Florida State University whose alumni proudly boast the “unconquered” spirit of the Seminole Tribes of Florida. It was here that Conti’s aptitude for law and litigation shone through as she was honored to have become a member of the FSU Journal of Transnational Law and Policy. She was also a member of the FSU Mock Trial Team, placing first at the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyer’s Mock Trial Competition and second at the Association of Trial Lawyers of America’s Mock Trial Competition.

Conti’s professional accomplishments mirror the laurels she achieved as an outstanding student leader at the Florida State University College of Law. Upon graduation, Ms. Moore became licensed to practice in the States of Nevada and Florida, and she became an associate attorney at one of Las Vegas’ most prestigious law firms. Right away, Conti earned a reputation for aggressively representing her clients from inception through trial and appeal, litigating matters such as business disputes, personal injury, family law issues, landlord/tenant disputes, and employment discrimination.

While she holds her clients’ expressed satisfaction in the highest regard, it is always wonderful to be recognized by one’s colleagues. In 2010, Attorney Moore received such acknowledgement when she was recognized by the National Bar Association and Impact as one of the Nation’s Best Advocates: 40 Lawyers Under 40. The accolades, however, did not end there, as she was also presented with the coveted Excellence in Service Award in recognition of her unyielding commitment to community service.

Attorney Conti Moore strives daily to provide excellent, cost-effective representation to her clients, but her dedication to fighting for the rights of those needing legal assistance does not end there. Conti has contributed several hundred hours of pro bono service to her community. In 2008, her extensive pro bono work was recognized by the Clark County Bar Association and the Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada when they bestowed upon her the prestigious Lied Award for Most Pro Bono Hours in the county.

Attorney Conti Moore’s commitment to alleviating the stress of her clients by providing exceptional, aggressive, and strategic legal representation is unquestionable and thoroughly evidenced by her record. When she isn’t going above and beyond the call of duty to produce favorable results for her beloved clients, Conti is enjoying time traveling with her husband, Nicholas, and three sons.

Stress Less. Choose Moore.

attorneys.bio:
Dan Smith is originally from Kansas City, Missouri but has called Florida home since 2005. He received his B.A. in business management from William Jewell College, where he was also a four-year letterman, scholar athlete, and team captain on the football team. After completing his business degree at William Jewell College he moved to Florida where he obtained his J.D. from St. Thomas University School of Law in Miami. During law school Mr. Smith also studied international law at the University College London and was intern at 23 Essex, a large London-based law firm.

After graduation and being admitted to the Florida bar, Mr. Smith began his legal career as an assistant public defender in Miami-Dade and Brevard County where he gained significant jury trial experience in both county and circuit court. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Smith was the Central Florida litigation manager for the state's largest non-standard insurance company. His current practice focuses on representing physicians in payment disputes with insurance companies.

Mr. Smith lives in Tampa, Florida with his wife Katie and their daughter Ivy.

attorneys.name: Eric C. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
A native Floridian, Eric Smith was born and raised in Central Florida. He received a Bachelor's Degree in Journalism from the University of Florida in 2009, graduating summa cum laude and as valedictorian of the College of Journalism and Communications after maintaining a perfect 4.0 throughout his undergraduate career. During his undergraduate career, Mr. Smith served as a student senator, President of the Journalism and Communications College Council and as a director for the world-renown Gator Growl, the largest student-run pep rally in the world. He was also active with Dance Marathon at the University of Florida, the most successful student-run philanthropy in the Southeastern United States, where he served as both a dancer/fundraiser and liaison between the organization and the families of young patients at Shands Children's Hospital.

Eric Smith graduated cum laude with his law degree from the University of Florida Levin College of Law in May 2012. He sat for, and passed, the Florida Bar in July 2012. While in law school, Mr. Smith was inducted into the prestigious Florida Blue Key and served as a teaching assistant for both Legal Research and Writing and Appellate Advocacy. He received the "book award" for the highest grade in both Evidence and Trial Practice. Eric was selected to participate in the school's County Court Mediation Clinic where he had the opportunity to observe and co-mediate actual small-claims cases, which allowed him to acquire status as a County Court Mediator, certified by the Florida Supreme Court. Eric also had the privilege of serving as a legal extern to the Honorable Anne C. Conway, Chief Judge of the Middle District of Florida.

Mr. Smith began his law practice defending some of the largest insurance companies and employers in Florida, gaining extensive and imperative insight into how these companies approach a dispute. He joined Morgan & Morgan in 2013. Outside of the practice of law, he currently serves as a board member on the Key Initiative Committee for the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Central Florida.

attorneys.name: Jocelyn Smith Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation and Disputes Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jocelyn Smith is a member of the Florida Bar and has practiced in state and federal court for the past fifteen years. She has experience in litigating a variety of business contract disputes, as well as copyright, consumer class actions, restrictive covenant disputes and consumer and commercial debt collection.

After obtaining her J.D. from Georgetown University in Washington, D.C., Jocelyn returned to Florida and represented businesses in a variety of disputes ranging from single-plaintiff consumer protection claims to class actions and complex, multi-year intellectual property disputes in federal courts. She has represented clients in over 100 mediations and numerous arbitrations before AAA and JAMS. She also spent five years representing low-income individuals in a non-profit clinic during the foreclosure crisis. Her experience allows her to tackle dynamic cases while providing a path towards the optimum resolution for her clients.

Jocelyn grew up in Gainesville, Florida and received her B.A. from the University of Florida before obtaining her J.D. from Georgetown University. At Georgetown, Jocelyn participated in Moot Court, the Harrison Institute Public Policy Clinic, and the Georgetown Gilbert & Sullivan Society.

attorneys.name: Meredith Pitts Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Altamonte Springs, FL
attorneys.bio:
Meredith Pitts Smith is a seventh generation Floridian and a third generation Orlando attorney. Meredith received her Bachelor of Science degree in biological studies from Florida State University where she was a member of Pi Beta Phi and Mortar Board Honor society, an Honor Studies Graduate, and on the Dean’s List. Meredith then attended Florida State University for law school where she was a member of Phi Alpha Delta Honor Society and on the Dean’s List. During law school Meredith was able to intern at the Second Judicial Circuit State Attorney’s Office where she developed her interest in litigation.

After graduation Meredith accepted a job with the Ninth Judicial Circuit State Attorney’s Office. During her employment, Meredith tried over 150 jury and non-jury trials ranging from misdemeanors to first degree felonies, served as a DUI/domestic violence specialist and sat second chair on an attempted murder trial. After her time with the State Attorney’s Office, Meredith was able to work alongside her father, Hon. Neal P. Pitts, until his appointment as an administrative judge of workers’ compensation. Of note during their practice together was voiding a ten million dollar trust that was obtained through fraud.

Meredith is a member of the Florida Bar, United States District Court for the Middle District Court of Florida and the Central Florida Association of Women Lawyers. Her areas of practice are broad and include: complex personal injury claims, including medical malpractice, automobile negligence and wrongful death; complex civil litigation; probate; guardianship; criminal defense; family law and appellate work.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Tavares, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael Smith is the managing partner of the Tavares and Ocala office locations in Lake and Marion County, Florida and is also a member of the firm's state-wide risk management committee. Mr. Smith has been practicing law since 1996 and is admitted to the Florida Bar. In 2009, he achieved board certification in civil trial law which recognizes highly specialized achievement and expertise very few lawyers in Florida acquire. He currently maintains this recognition with the Florida Bar.

He was raised in Ocala, Florida and graduated with high honors from Forest High School. He attended the University of Florida, graduating with a bachelor of science degree in Zoology with honors.

Mr. Smith then attended Stetson University College of Law where he also graduated with honors. Mr. Smith began his legal career as an assistant state attorney for the State of Florida. He prosecuted such crimes as drug trafficking, sex crimes, and was specially appointed as a felony domestic violence prosecutor. During the 3 years he served as a prosecutor, he conducted over 50 jury trials. Following his government service, Mr. Smith was an in-house attorney for State Farm Insurance Company as a claims litigation attorney. He worked for 2 years for State Farm specializing in personal injury and insurance dispute cases.

Since joining Morgan and Morgan in 2001, Mr. Smith has represented thousands of clients and their families injured by the negligence of others. He has obtained awards from juries in far excess of the offers made by insurance companies and has even successfully obtained settlements from major corporations.

attorneys.name: Michael S. Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mickey Smith has practiced law in Florida for more than 30 years. After graduating from the Duke University School of Law, Mickey began representing insurance companies and large corporations. He ultimately became a senior shareholder at Kubicki Draper and concentrated his practice on the defense of claims involving serious personal injury, wrongful death, and insurance bad faith. After trying over 100 cases for insurance companies, he became increasingly frustrated because his talents were merely being used to minimize or defeat victims' claims. Mickey wanted to use his talents to help ordinary people who had valid claims. On May 1, 2002, Mickey joined Slawson Cunningham Whalen & Smith, P.L., as a shareholder. He refused to represent insurance companies and strictly limited his practice to representing victims with significant claims.

His dream of practicing law with his best friends, Gary Lesser and Joe Landy, was fulfilled in August 2004, when Lesser, Landy, Smith & Siegel, PLLC was formed. Mickey's practice continues to be limited to representing individuals and families who have suffered serious personal injury, wrongful death, or have been victimized because of the bad faith practices of an insurance company.

Without question, Mickey's vast experience in litigating and trying some of the insurance industry's worst cases is a major asset in representing victims with significant claims. Since focusing his efforts on the interests of the injured in 2002, Mickey has maintained an active trial practice and has achieved verdicts and settlements for his clients that total in the tens of millions of dollars. His peers have named him one of The Best Lawyers in America.

Mickey was born in Williamson, West Virginia, in 1960. Mickey excelled in high school and received a merit scholarship to attend Virginia Tech. He was thrilled since neither of his parents could attend college. Mr. Smith majored in Engineering at Virginia Tech and received his degree, magna cum laude, in 1982, graduating with a 3.70-grade point average (3.96 in his major). His hard work in college was rewarded with a merit scholarship to the Duke University School of Law. While in law school, he was elected to the prestigious Order of the Coif, based on his outstanding academic achievements at Duke. Mickey received his degree in 1985, with high honors.

attorneys.name: R. Blake Smith
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Prior to joining Block & Scarpa in 2023, Blake spent the last ten years at a local law firm practicing incapacity, guardianship, and mental health law. Blake started his career as an Assistant Public Defender in Vero Beach and spent 5 years as a felony trial attorney.

Blake hails from Richmond, Virginia and attended the University of the South in Sewanee, Tennessee for undergraduate studies and obtained his Juris Doctor from Coastal School of Law in Jacksonville.

Blake's unique concentration on incapacity and mental health law combined with his criminal and civil probate experience have made him one of the leading voices in this emerging field of law. He has developed an unparalleled approach to avoiding guardianship filings and has provided his client's families with more privacy and dignity using estate planning documents with a boldness and creativity that is unmatched. By utilizing his criminal law experience and his passion for understanding mental illness, addiction, and human behavior, he can guide your family through the most tumultuous times. Mental Health law spans a variety of legal practice areas, and he can guide you through all of them.

Blake works closely with families, their financial advisors, and other attorneys seeking specialized advice during times of crisis. As an emerging field of law, it can be helpful to specifically define what mental health and incapacity law often entails:

a) Private removal of Trustee due to mental incapacity by utilizing physician's certificate(s) and installing successor,

b) Filing for judicial determination of legal incapacity and avoiding guardianship using lesser restrictive alternatives like Durable Power of Attorney,

c) Emergency Temporary Guardianship filing to seek immediate delegation of civil rights to stop exploitation or abuse,

d) Incapacity and Guardianship appointment filings in the absence of estate planning documents and without viable alternatives,

e) Addiction Recovery Contracts to guide families through the long process and provide an incentivized path that considers the need to address issues like co-dependency and enabling,

f) Trustee/Guardian of the Property service when the circumstances preclude a corporate fiduciary, g) Baker Act and Marchman Act advice,

h) Criminal defense and preparation of NGI (not guilty by reason of insanity) defense or guidance on ITP (incompetent to proceed), and

i) Guardianships for Minors in lieu of grandparent adoption or for safekeeping funds inherited or earned until adulthood.

attorneys.bio:
30 Plus Years of Trial Experience

Weston F. Smith has been a trial lawyer for 32 years, with a civil trial practice representing injured parties and their families in significant, often catastrophic, personal injury, medical malpractice, and nursing home lawsuits.

His cases frequently involve people who have been severely and permanently injured or who have died due to the negligence of others, including health care providers and nursing homes.

Wes is a third generation native of St. Petersburg, Florida, having grown up on St. Pete Beach in the 1970's and 1980's. Wes attended St. Jude's Cathedral School and St. Petersburg Catholic High School. He graduated from the University of Florida in 1989 and attended Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham, Alabama, graduating in 1992.

Wes became a criminal prosecutor in 1992, working for Bernie McCabe as an Assistant State Attorney for the 6th Judicial Circuit's State Attorney's Office in Pinellas County, Clearwater, Florida. He worked there for over five years, conducting over 60 jury trials while prosecuting misdemeanor and felony crimes, including DUI manslaughter, rape and murder cases.

Upon leaving the State Attorney's Office in 1997, Wes began defending people sued in automobile accident, premises liability and other types of personal injury cases. He eventually began defending nursing homes, health care providers (such as doctors and nurses) and health care facilities in nursing home and medical malpractice lawsuits.

During this time, Wes worked with Deacon, Moulds & Smith, in St. Petersburg, where he was a partner and shareholder for a decade, from 2004 to 2014.

In 2014, Wes left Deacon, Moulds and Smith and effectively "switched sides" to become a shareholder at Masterson, Hoag & Smith, where he joined two close friends and began representing the injured and their families in personal injury, medical malpractice and nursing home lawsuits.

Finally, in 2021, Wes opened this firm, his own office, Weston Smith Law, PLLC, where he continues to represent those who have suffered severe and permanent injuries due to the neglect of others. He continues to focus his practice on catastrophic injury and death cases in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home, auto and other personal injury cases.

Litigation and Trial Experience

Wes has had the advantage of overseeing litigation and conducting trials in the criminal arena, and on both the defense and plaintiff side of personal injury, medical malpractice and nursing home litigation.

Now, as a plaintiff attorney representing the injured party and their family, he has the advantage of understanding the strategies employed by defense attorneys and insurance companies.

Wes is a trial attorney. He has conducted over 80 jury trials, more than 20 of those being medical malpractice and nursing home trials. He has conducted countless mediations and arbitrations.

Wes teaches trial advocacy to other lawyers every year at The Florida Bar Trial Lawyers Section's Advanced Trial Advocacy School. This is a week-long interactive program in which lawyers conduct every aspect of a trial while receiving detailed instruction, feedback and lectures.

Wes is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocacy (ABOTA). This is an invitation only national association of experienced trial lawyers and judges. The members must have conducted the required number of jury trials and exhibited the virtues of civility, integrity and professionalism required of the organization.

He currently serves as the Chapter's President in 2024.

Wes is a member of The Florida Bar's Trial Lawyers Section Executive Council. The Executive Council is the board that oversees the activities of the Trial Lawyers Section which consists of over 5000 trial lawyers throughout the State.

The Trial Lawyers Section conducts seminars for trial lawyers, oversees various programs for judicial and civics education, monitors legislative activity important to the State's trial lawyers, and publishes guidelines and handbooks related to the conduct of trial lawyers in the State. Wes is currently the Chair of the Section beginning June 2022.

Wes lives in St. Petersburg with his wife of 25 years, Peggy Smith, a pre-school teacher, and they have three children. Aidan. sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
30 Plus Years of Trial Experience

Weston F. Smith has been a trial lawyer for 32 years, with a civil trial practice representing injured parties and their families in significant, often catastrophic, personal injury, medical malpractice, and nursing home lawsuits.

His cases frequently involve people who have been severely and permanently injured or who have died due to the negligence of others, including health care providers and nursing homes.

Wes is a third generation native of St. Petersburg, Florida, having grown up on St. Pete Beach in the 1970's and 1980's. Wes attended St. Jude's Cathedral School and St. Petersburg Catholic High School. He graduated from the University of Florida in 1989 and attended Cumberland School of Law in Birmingham, Alabama, graduating in 1992.

Wes became a criminal prosecutor in 1992, working for Bernie McCabe as an Assistant State Attorney for the 6th Judicial Circuit's State Attorney's Office in Pinellas County, Clearwater, Florida. He worked there for over five years, conducting over 60 jury trials while prosecuting misdemeanor and felony crimes, including DUI manslaughter, rape and murder cases.

Upon leaving the State Attorney's Office in 1997, Wes began defending people sued in automobile accident, premises liability and other types of personal injury cases. He eventually began defending nursing homes, health care providers (such as doctors and nurses) and health care facilities in nursing home and medical malpractice lawsuits.

During this time, Wes worked with Deacon, Moulds & Smith, in St. Petersburg, where he was a partner and shareholder for a decade, from 2004 to 2014.

In 2014, Wes left Deacon, Moulds and Smith and effectively "switched sides" to become a shareholder at Masterson, Hoag & Smith, where he joined two close friends and began representing the injured and their families in personal injury, medical malpractice and nursing home lawsuits.

Finally, in 2021, Wes opened this firm, his own office, Weston Smith Law, PLLC, where he continues to represent those who have suffered severe and permanent injuries due to the neglect of others. He continues to focus his practice on catastrophic injury and death cases in the areas of medical malpractice, nursing home, auto and other personal injury cases.

Litigation and Trial Experience

Wes has had the advantage of overseeing litigation and conducting trials in the criminal arena, and on both the defense and plaintiff side of personal injury, medical malpractice and nursing home litigation.

Now, as a plaintiff attorney representing the injured party and their family, he has the advantage of understanding the strategies employed by defense attorneys and insurance companies.

Wes is a trial attorney. He has conducted over 80 jury trials, more than 20 of those being medical malpractice and nursing home trials. He has conducted countless mediations and arbitrations.

Wes teaches trial advocacy to other lawyers every year at The Florida Bar Trial Lawyers Section's Advanced Trial Advocacy School. This is a week-long interactive program in which lawyers conduct every aspect of a trial while receiving detailed instruction, feedback and lectures.

Wes is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocacy (ABOTA). This is an invitation only national association of experienced trial lawyers and judges. The members must have conducted the required number of jury trials and exhibited the virtues of civility, integrity and professionalism required of the organization.

He currently serves as the Chapter's President in 2024.

Wes is a member of The Florida Bar's Trial Lawyers Section Executive Council. The Executive Council is the board that oversees the activities of the Trial Lawyers Section which consists of over 5000 trial lawyers throughout the State.

The Trial Lawyers Section conducts seminars for trial lawyers, oversees various programs for judicial and civics education, monitors legislative activity important to the State's trial lawyers, and publishes guidelines and handbooks related to the conduct of trial lawyers in the State. Wes is currently the Chair of the Section beginning June 2022.

Wes lives in St. Petersburg with his wife of 25 years, Peggy Smith, a pre-school teacher, and they have three children. Aidan. He is a devoted father, an accomplished triathlete, a retired little league baseball, softball and soccer coach, an ongoing fan of his children's sports and a celebrator of their successes.

attorneys.firm_name: Darla K. Snead, P.L. Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Lakeland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Darla K. Snead is a Polk County Florida native and focuses her family law and personal injury practice in the Central Florida area. Ms. Snead is a Florida Supreme Court Certified Family Law Mediator and a Florida Arbitrator. She has been practicing law for over 25 years and has experience representing clients in many different areas of the law including family law, divorce, medical malpractice, wrongful death, and personal injury. Ms. Snead started Darla K. Snead, P.L. in 2009 after leaving a law firm in Lakeland, Florida where she was a partner in a firm practicing on the defense side of personal injury and wrongful death litigation. Using the valuable experience Ms. Snead gained on the defense side, she currently represents individuals who have been injured in auto accidents, motorcycle accidents or trucking accidents, as well as family members who have had a loved one die in an auto accident. Ms. Snead also represents clients in the area of family law, including divorce, paternity, child support, and timesharing issues, as well as modifications of final judgments. Ms. Snead has represented clients in over 100 trials and over 1,000 mediations.

Ms. Snead graduated from Western Michigan Thomas M. Cooley Law School in Lansing, Michigan. She began her career as an Assistant State Attorney at the State Attorney's Office in Bartow, Florida. After obtaining her license to practice law in the State of Illinois, she practiced law in the Chicago area in the areas of criminal law, family law, and medical malpractice defense before returning to the Lakeland, Florida area.

When you are faced with an important life decision regarding a family law issue or have been injured in a car accident, the advice and assistance of an experienced attorney like Darla K. Snead will prove crucial to your understanding of the issues involved.

We are proud to welcome Kyle Soch to BillBone Law Group as our Associate Trial Lawyer. Kyle brings exceptional litigation experience and a strong commitment to justice for the injured, strengthening our team’s ability to stand up for clients across South Florida.

Experience & Education

Kyle earned his Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the University of Florida Levin College of Law in 2021 and his Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy and Classical Studies, magna cum laude, from the University of Florida. While in law school, he served as an Editor of the Journal of Technology Law and Policy and contributed as both a coach and competitor on UF’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Team.

Before joining our firm, Kyle practiced at Carlton Fields, P.A., a national law firm where he focused on mass tort and product liability defense. That experience gave him valuable insight into the strategies used by corporations, which he now applies to protect and advocate for individuals harmed by negligence.

Kyle is admitted to practice in Florida and in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida as well as the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida.

Recognizing that life is a journey — from Gen Z to the Greatest Generation and beyond probate — Max Solomon focuses his practice on elder law. His work spans guardianship, probate administration and litigation, health care issues, public benefits, wills, trusts and estate planning, financial exploitation, and appeals.

Max is widely recognized throughout Florida for his strength in exploitation litigation and his holistic approach to resolving disputes. He is equally known for creating estate planning solutions tailored to younger individuals and couples, blended families, LGBTQ couples, and other nontraditional family structures.

His peers have repeatedly nominated him for inclusion in Rising Stars in Florida Elder Law (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025). He serves in multiple leadership roles within the Elder Law Section of The Florida Bar, sits on the Cybersecurity and Privacy Law Committee and the Mental Health and Wellness Committee of The Florida Bar, and was President of the Tallahassee Regional Estate Planning Conference in 2023. Max is also a published author in privacy law and public international law, and a frequent speaker on the intersections of guardianship, privacy, fiduciary representation, and even pop culture’s surprising influence on the law. He has presented to judges, attorneys, and professionals statewide.

Outside the courtroom, Max maintains an active pro bono practice assisting veterans, children, LGBTQ individuals, and low-income seniors. He also enjoys partnering with animal rescue organizations and has a special passion for establishing pet trusts.

A proud triple ’Nole, Max earned his Juris Doctor, Master of Science in American Politics and Policy, and bachelor’s degrees in History and International Affairs from Florida State University. He also studied at St Edmund Hall, University of Oxford, in the summer of 2016, where he focused on Public International Law.

When not practicing law, Max can be found hiking with his two Pembroke Welsh Corgis and tabby cat, traveling, or loyally (and sometimes painfully) cheering for international soccer, Florida State Seminoles athletics, the Tottenham Hotspur, Pittsburgh Steelers, Penguins, and — begrudgingly — South Florida sports.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Public International Law Book Award, 2017

attorneys.name: Alex Solomiany Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Alex Solomiany, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Nationality Law Lawyers in Aventura, FL
attorneys.bio:
Alex Solomiany is Board Certified as an expert in Immigration and Nationality Law by the Florida Supreme Court. Board certification recognizes Mr. Solomiany's special knowledge, skills and proficiency in the area of Immigration and Nationality Law. Less than 0.1% of attorneys in the State of Florida are Board Certified in Immigration Law. Since he handles all areas of immigration law, Mr. Solomiany has the knowledge to select the most appropriate strategy to meet your goals.

Alex Solomiany has over 25 years of experience handling complex immigration cases. He has appeared before every immigration law judge in the Miami and Orlando immigration courts and has appeared in immigration courts throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. He also handles immigration appeals before the Board of Immigration Appeals and U.S. federal courts, and has represented clients before the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) throughout the United States.

Before becoming a specialist in immigration law, Mr. Solomiany was a criminal defense attorney. This valuable experience and his expert knowledge of immigration law, allows him to serve as a consultant to criminal defense attorneys to help them strategize possible ways to resolve criminal charges for noncitizens in order to avoid immigration consequences.

Mr. Solomiany was born in Guaynabo, Puerto Rico. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor and attended Tulane University School of Law in New Orleans. He has appeared on television, radio and in print articles discussing immigration law issues. He has also lectured on Immigration and Nationality Law at numerous seminars throughout the United States. Mr. Solomiany is a member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association and has served on the Florida Bar Board Certification Committee, most recently as the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Solomiany is driven and determined to achieve positive results for his clients. He is goal-oriented, not only in his professional life, but also in his personal life which he enjoys with his wife and children. He does not give up. He will go with you to the finish line.

attorneys.name: Helmuth Solis
attorneys.practice_type: DUI Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Helmuth Solis was born and raised in Miami, Florida where he has lived all his life. He graduated from Florida International University with honors, acquiring a Bachelor of Arts. He immediately proceeded to law school, where he earned his law degree from the University of Miami with honors.

After law school, Helmuth began his career in criminal law as an Assistant State Attorney at the Miami-Dade State Attorney's Office. As a DUI Prosecutor, Helmuth quickly rose to the position of DUI training attorney, where he trained other attorneys on the law relating to DUI. Now, as a defense attorney, Helmuth uses his talent and knowledge to thoroughly defend individuals facing criminal charges. He uses his experience in the State Attorney's Office to his clients' advantage, anticipating the prosecution's tactics and employing strategies that are capable of withstanding them.

As a co-founder of Beckham Law Firm, Helmuth focuses his practice exclusively on criminal defense. He has been a member of the Florida Bar since 2007 - as such, he is eligible to practice before all state courts in Florida. He is also admitted to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida. Helmuth is fluent in both English and Spanish.

attorneys.name: Neal R. Sonnett
attorneys.practice_type: Legal Ethics Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
NEAL R. SONNETT, P.A. engages exclusively in federal and state criminal defense throughout the United States, emphasizing corporate, white collar, and complex crimes litigation. The Firm represents individuals and corporate entities in regulatory and grand jury investigations, trials and appeals, and federal sentencing guideline and post-conviction issues. The Firm has acted as counsel in investigations and cases involving environmental crimes, health care, criminal tax, insurance, securities and mail fraud, money laundering, federal asset forfeiture and international extradition cases, and administrative, attorney ethics, and disciplinary matters.

The Firm provides aggressive, innovative and quality representation. We are committed to professional responsibility and development, are active in local, state, and national bar and civic associations, and lecture and write extensively on substantive, trial and appellate practice topics.

Neal R. Sonnett, the Firm's Managing Partner, is a former Assistant United States Attorney and Chief of the Criminal Division for the Southern District of Florida. He received his J.D. degree from the University of Miami School of Law in 1967.

A nationally respected trial lawyer, Mr. Sonnett has been profiled by the National Law Journal as one of 10 of the "Nation's Top Litigators" and one of the "Nation's Top White Collar Criminal Defense Lawyers." He has been selected three times by that publication as one of the "100 Most Influential Lawyers In America," he is listed in every edition of "The Best Lawyers in America," and was named as one of the four "Most Respected Attorneys in Miami" by Miami Today in June 1996.

Mr. Sonnett currently serves as a director and member of the Executive Committee of the American Judicature Society, as chair of the ABA Coordinating Committee on Immigration Law, and as president of the Spellman-Hoeveler American Inn of Court in Miami, Florida.

He is a former chair of the ABA Criminal Justice Section, which he now represents in the ABA House of Delegates, and is past president of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He was a member of the ABA's High Profile Trial Resource Team and the ABA Coalition for Justice, and served on the Executive Committees of the ABA Section Officers Conference and the National Conference of Bar Presidents.

Mr. Sonnett is a past president of the Florida Bar Foundation, which administers the Bar's Interest on Trust Accounts program and awards grants to provide greater legal assistance to Florida's poor and improve the administration of justice. He has also served as president of the national Metropolitan Bar Caucus, the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, the Dade County Bar Association, and the Federal Bar Association, South Florida Chapter.

Mr. Sonnett received the 1989 Florida Bar Foundation Medal Of Honor Award, the highest award that can be bestowed upon a lawyer by the legal profession in Florida, for "his dedicated service in improving the administration of the criminal justice system and in protecting individual rights precious to our American Constitutional form of government."

Pricing Structure :

Free Consultation

attorneys.name: Jonathan Sooriash Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
If you face wage garnishment, tax liens or other enforced collection actions, you may feel overwhelmed or confused about your options.

J. David Tax Law, LLC, located in Jacksonville, Florida, can offer guidance on these technical issues and help you identify potential solutions. Attorney Jonathan Sooriash has negotiated with the Internal Revenue Service to resolve thousands of cases and his law office is committed to finding a custom tax solution that enables you to move past your tax debt.

Whether you forgot to file a tax return, are preparing for an audit or have unpaid personal or payroll taxes, Mr. Sooriash can help you understand your legal options. He also can offer guidance if you face tax penalties, carry expired tax debt, require assistance in preparing income tax returns or need to request abatement of tax interest and penalties. Mr. Sooriash welcomes prospective clients to schedule a free consultation to discuss any of these issues.

If you face collection actions, Mr. Sooriash can help you explore various options for halting them. By seeking currently not collectible status, the law office may be able to help you obtain temporary relief from, or even prevent, an IRS levy, asset seizufgre or wage garnishment. You also might be eligible to permanently resolve your debt through an installment agreement or an offer in compromise. Additionally, if you were not aware that your spouse made errors on your joint return, you may be able to seek innocent spouse relief.

The law office of J. David Tax Law, LLC, provides customized solutions to clients from Florida and all 50 states. From your first consultation, Mr. Sooriash is committed to keeping you informed of the progress of your case and all available options. Furthermore, he is prepared to provide assistance during each step of the process, from identifying the appropriate strategy to presenting your case to the IRS.

David Spain began his career as an Attorney in September 1989 and has been with Morgan and Morgan, P.A. since February 1996. He received his undergraduate degree from the University Of Central Florida (UCF) and his Law degree from the University of Florida (UF) College of Law.

Mr. Spain has an extensive background in both Civil and Criminal law. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, P.A., he served as Chief City Prosecutor for the City of Orlando, as an Assistant Statewide Prosecutor for the State of Florida, and as an Assistant Public Defender in the Ninth Judicial Circuit and as a Special Agent for the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Since joining Morgan & Morgan, he has focused his practice on civil trial litigation, disability insurance claims, ERISA Claims, insurance disputes, life insurance claims, plaintiff insurance litigation, property damage claims, and sinkholes.

As an Adjunct Law Professor at the University of Central Florida, David Spain taught pre-law courses for 4 years. He has also served on a Florida Bar Rules Committee and various Citizen Advisory Boards addressing a variety of state and local issues. Mr. Spain has also been a frequent lecturer on legal practice topics for Attorneys, Colleges and Professional Associations.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
David Spain began his career as an Attorney in September 1989 and has been with Morgan and Morgan, P.A. since February 1996. He received his undergraduate degree from the University Of Central Florida (UCF) and his Law degree from the University of Florida (UF) College of Law.

Mr. Spain has an extensive background in both Civil and Criminal law. Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, P.A., he served as Chief City Prosecutor for the City of Orlando, as an Assistant Statewide Prosecutor for the State of Florida, and as an Assistant Public Defender in the Ninth Judicial Circuit and as a Special Agent for the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Since joining Morgan & Morgan, he has focused his practice on civil trial litigation, disability insurance claims, ERISA Claims, insurance disputes, life insurance claims, plaintiff insurance litigation, property damage claims, and sinkholes.

As an Adjunct Law Professor at the University of Central Florida, David Spain taught pre-law courses for 4 years. He has also served on a Florida Bar Rules Committee and various Citizen Advisory Boards addressing a variety of state and local issues. Mr. Spain has also been a frequent lecturer on legal practice topics for Attorneys, Colleges and Professional Associations.

attorneys.name: Bryce P. Spano
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Bryce Spano was born and raised in Kansas. He attended the University of Kansas where he was a member of the University's Division I Men's Cross Country and Track & Field Teams, receiving his B.S. in Business Administration in 1999. In 2002 he received his Juris Doctorate Degree from the University of Kansas. While attending Law School in Lawrence, he was a Law Clerk at the Office of the Kansas Secretary of State.

Before joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Spano worked for insurance companies where he tried and defended auto negligence and premises liability cases. He now dedicates his practice to representing individuals and families who have been injured due to the negligence of others. Mr. Spano has received an "AV" rating by Martindale-Hubbell, which is a testament to the fact that his peers rank him at the highest level of professional excellence. Mr. Spano is also a Board Certified Civil Trial Lawyer - a very prestigious recognition which is attained by less than two percent of all Florida attorneys.

Mr. Spano is married and he and his wife, Jamie, have a son and a daughter. In his free time, Bryce enjoys running, playing golf, and spending time with his friends and family.

attorneys.name: Kevin Sparkman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
He sees litigation as an art and treats mediation and trial work as a craft.

He always searches for ways to resolve cases through negotiation when possible, but never shies away from trials because of his extensive courtroom experience.

Kevin's sole goal is to make a difference for his clients and obtain the most successful outcome possible.

The bench considers him a lawyer who is composed, talented, and immensely just. His clients will tell you he is sharp, even-tempered, honest, and ethical. And his peers will tell you he's one of the best lawyers around.

In 2013, Managing Partner Kevin Sparkman was named a Rising Star by Super Lawyers, a ranking service that honors the top 2 percent of young attorneys in the country based on nominations by other attorneys and judges.

But don't be fooled by his age. Kevin is a seasoned veteran, having spent nine years practicing in the areas of personal injury, business law, criminal law, and family law.

With such long hours, he fuels himself with health foods by juicing kale,

beets, pears, and blueberries and his passion - fitness. He's completed many half marathons and runs in every new city he visits as his first " tour " of that city.

No matter what town he's visiting with his family, Kevin enjoys discovering new farm-to-table restaurants for more than their fresh ingredients. He believes in supporting local businesses to help build strong economies and create vibrant communities.

Whether at work or at play, Kevin leads his life by the one law that isn't in the books. And that's the Golden Rule.

Kevin is the type of person and lawyer everyone wants as their personal advocate.

attorneys.name: Christopher P. Spath
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lakeland, FL
attorneys.bio:
"Christopher Spath was raised here in Polk County and began working at the age of 14 in his family owned a jewelry store in Bartow. After graduating from Bartow High School, he attended USF and achieved his Bachelor of Science with a double major from the USF College of Business. Three years later, he earned his Juris Doctorate (J.D.) degree and began his legal career as a solo practitioner in the Tampa Bay area where he handled Wills, Trust, and Estates for high net-worth individuals.

From there, Mr. Spath gained criminal law experience working as an Assistant State Attorney for the Tenth Judicial Circuit of Polk County. During his time as an Assistant State Attorney, Mr. Spath's excellence in the courtroom was recognized by all, and he was swiftly promoted to chief of his felony division. As Chief, he was entrusted to handle high profile media cases, including homicides, vehicular manslaughter, armed home invasion robberies, drug trafficking, and white collar crimes.

Mr. Spath now continues his legal career by joining the Law Offices of Morgan and Morgan where his practice focuses primarily on litigating personal injury claims. Mr. Spath has received numerous accolades for his efforts in the courtroom and fundamentally believes in seeking justice for the people."

attorneys.name: Danny Spiker Jr. Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Danny Spiker, Jr., Esq. endeavors to live a life of public service, beginning his career in the United States Navy and serving our country for nearly ten years before transitioning into the legal field.

Born and raised in the Tampa Bay area, Danny previously enlisted in the United States Navy as a Hospital Corpsman. While honorably serving his country for nearly ten years, Danny received numerous accolades, including the Combat Action Ribbon, and deployed to locations in Afghanistan, Japan, Australia, and Cuba.

Desiring to continue in a career of public service, Danny was discharged from the United States Navy in 2020 in order to attend law school at St. Thomas University. During law school, Danny served on the Moot Court, where he competed in the E. Earle Zehmer National Moot Court Competition, which focuses on Workers’ Compensation. After graduating from law school in May 2023, Danny was admitted to the Florida Bar in September 2023.

In his free time, Danny enjoys spending time with family and watching Tampa Bay Rays, Buccaneers, and Lightning games.

Awards and Honors

Honors

United States Navy Veteran, Awarded The Combat Action Ribbon

attorneys.name: James A. Staack Esq.

Jim is licensed in and for the State of Florida and has practiced in Pinellas County since 1980. attorneys.name: G. Alan Stagmeier
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Alan Stagmeier was born in Hinesville, GA in 1979. He received his B.S. in Political Science and graduated Magna Cum Laude from Georgia Southern University in Statesboro, GA in 2000 before obtaining his J.D. from Mercer University in Macon, GA in 2004.

After graduating law school, Mr. Stagmeier worked with and eventually became a Partner at a state-wide law firm defending doctors, businesses and insurance companies in civil litigation involving medical malpractice, wrongful death, catastrophic personal injury, sexual misconduct, breach of contract, professional negligence, products liability, automobile and trucking negligence and premises liability.

Mr. Stagmeier has distinguished himself as a young attorney, and was selected as one of Florida Trend Magazine's "Legal Elite Best Up & Coming Attorneys" for 2010, as well as a "Rising Star" for 2011 by Florida Super Lawyers Magazine.

Florida Trend recognizes the top 1.8% of lawyers practicing in the state. Those named to the "Legal Elite" list were selected in a nomination process that involves all of Florida's practicing attorneys, who named lawyers whom they hold in the highest regard and the "best up and coming attorneys" who were under age 40 or in practice for fewer than 10 years.

Florida Super Lawyers recognizes the top 2.5% of the State's young lawyers. To be eligible for "Rising Stars," an attorney must be under the age of 40 or have been practicing for 10 years or less. A multiphase selection process is used to determine which attorneys will receive this distinction, and nominees are evaluated on the basis of peer recognition and professional excellence.

Mr. Stagmeier now devotes 100% of his practice to representing those who have been injured due to the negligence of others.

attorneys.name: Scott D. Stamatakis
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Scott Stamatakis is a native of Tampa, Florida and practices law in a variety of areas including bankruptcy, foreclosure and collections defense, credit repair, debt settlement, sinkholes, insurance claims, IRS tax debt settlement, real estate, title insurance, business law and asset preservation just to name a few. Scott graduated from Gaither High School which is located in North Tampa on the boundary lines of Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco and Polk Counties in close proximity to Carrollwood Village, Northdale, North Lakes, Lutz, Odessa and Land O Lakes, Florida. After high school, Scott moved to Tallahassee, Florida and attended Florida State University where, as a Seminole, he earned his Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in criminology, magna cum laude, in 1995 while working part time at the State Attorney’s Office for the Second Judicial Circuit, William N. Meggs, as well as the Department of State, Division of Licensing. Florida’s 2nd Judicial Circuit is situated in the Federal Northern District of Florida and comprised of Leon, Franklin, Gadsden, Jefferson, Liberty and Wakulla Counties. Tallahassee is also the capital of Florida and houses the state legislature, the First District Court of Appeals, as well as the Florida Supreme Court and the Florida Bar.

After graduating from FSU, Scott relocated to Gainesville, Florida where he attended the University of Florida’s College of Law which is also known as the Fredric G. Levin College of Law. As a Gator, Scott earned his Juris Doctorate, or ‘law degree’, from UF in 1998. Gainesville is located in the Eighth Judicial Circuit which is comprised of six counties extending all the way from the Georgia border to the Gulf of Mexico including Alachua, Baker, Bradford, Gilchrist, Levy and Union Counties. Florida’s Eighth Judicial Circuit is situated in the Federal Middle District of Florida. While attending law school, Scott studied a number of different areas of law including, real estate, bankruptcy, contracts, banking law and torts just to name a few. Scott also studied international law and the French Civil Code abroad at the University of Montpellier located in France. It was during this time that Scott also met his first and current law partner, Sami Thalji.

Scott passed the Florida Bar exam and earned his license to practice law in 1999. Scott relocated back to Tampa, Florida and began his legal career with the law firm of Echevarria, McCalla, Raymer, Barrett & Frapier, which is now know as Florida Default Law Group, PL and considered to be one of the largest plaintiff ‘foreclosure mills’ in the State of Florida. Tampa is located in the Thirteenth Judicial Circuit which is situated in the Federal Middle District of Florida and comprised of Hillsborough County, FL. Tampa Bay is also located in close proximity to the Sixth Judicial Circuit which is comprised of the cities of Clearwater and St. Petersburg, as well as Pinellas and Pasco Counties. As an attorney for Mike Echevarria, Scott’s practice focused on creditor and debtor work providing legal representation in secured transactions to banks and mortgage lenders in areas such as bankruptcy, mortgage foreclosure, real estate closings and litigation. Scott was also a title insurance agent for First American Title Insurance Company. As a result of his work with Echevarria and Associates, Scott has been involved thousands of foreclosures, bankruptcies, debt collection law suits and real estate closings.

After Scott’s stay with the Florida Default Law Group, Scott expanded his legal career with a commercial business law practice and was also an in house attorney for a public company. During this time, expanded on his legal knowledge by practicing in a number of different legal issues such as business law, franchises, collections, repossessions, replevins, credit cards, credit agreements, wage and bank garnishment, landlord and tenant, sinkholes, insurance disputes and claims, commercial real estate and retail real estate selection and development, land use, zoning and construction. Scott has also been involved in highly complex litigation and has gained extensive experience litigating numerous consumer based claims, injury claims, insurance claims, HMO and medical claims. While in private practice, Scott has represented many high profile corporate clients including: Bank of America; First Union; Manufacturer’s Trust and Trading Company; Conti, Fairbanks Capital Corporation; Litton Loan Servicing; Principal Residential Mortgage; Attorneys Title Insurance Fund (the ‘FUND’); Fidelity National Title Insurance Company; Old Republic National Title Insurance Company; WellCare HMO; WellBorn HMO; HealthEdge; Bay Area Primary Care & Associates, Inc.; American Healthcare Holdings, Inc.; Visionary Medical Services, Inc.; Bay Gardens Retirement Village, LLC; Soft-Aid, Inc.; U.S.MD, LLC; Choice Healthcare; WebUnited; MDVIP, Inc.; MedQ, Inc.; Insights Health Network, Inc.; Tequesta Urgent Care; Provider Services of America, Inc.; Florida Medical Association; 2K Medical; and American Medical Software, Inc.

In 2003, Scott decided to begin his own law practice along with his friend and law partner, Sami Thalji, when they decided to use their vast knowledge and experience of the inner-workings of big business and big government to advocate justice on behalf of consumers throughout the State of Florida.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Stanton
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
During his legal career, Michael has gained experience in a wide variety of business law and civil litigation, including cases involving business disputes, financial services litigation, workplace disputes, complex commercial litigation and even class action litigation. He has represented individuals as well as businesses of all sizes, from the local “mom and pop” business all the way up to multi-national corporations, in state and federal courts throughout Florida, as well as nationally in arbitrations before the FINRA, NYSE and AAA.

In addition to his courtroom experience, Michael has represented individuals and businesses in commercial transactions, such as lease negotiations, business entity formation, and employment contract review. Notably, Michael gained a wide array of transactional experience working as part of a team that acted as general counsel for a large nationally recognized hospital. Additionally, Michael has been named a Super Lawyers Rising Star in each year from 2010 through 2014.

Over the last several years, Michael has been involved in international litigation in addition to his statewide practice. This experience involved traveling throughout North America and Europe to prepare the case for what was ultimately a three-year trial and multi-year appeal in The Hague, Netherlands. It was a challenging and rewarding professional experience. The time away from home also made him truly appreciate all that his home in Florida has to offer. Following this, Michael wanted to use the experience gained in practicing law nationally and internationally to create his own firm with a focus on clients or client issues closer to home.

Michael Stanton was born on Long Island, New York but moved to the Tampa Bay area while in grade school. He graduated summa cum laude from East Lake High School in Tarpon Springs before attending the University of Florida’s Honors Program. During his time as an undergraduate at the University of Florida, Michael marched in the “Pride of the Sunshine Marching Band” and is to this day an avid college football fan. It is his love of college football that later led him to help found the college football blog, EveryDayShouldBeSaturday.com. While at UF, Michael was named an “Anderson Scholar with Highest Distinction” for academic achievement. After graduating magna cum laude with a degree in History, he attended the University of Florida’s Law School on a full academic scholarship. He graduated with honors and amongst the top of his class. Upon graduation, Michael returned to the Tampa Bay area to be closer to family and to start his legal career. Although his practice has led him to work in many countries around the world, he has always been based in the Tampa Bay area.

In his spare time he enjoys being with his wife, children and his large extended family enjoying many of the things the great State of Florida has to offer. He remains active in the community through such organizations as the Upper Tampa Bay Chamber of Commerce, where he serves on the board of directors, The Inspire Foundation and the Tampa Theatre Wine Fest Committee. He also enjoys coaching his sons in youth soccer, going to the beach, boating, fishing and of course watching and cheering for all the area sports teams, especially the Florida Gators.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Stanton
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
During his legal career, Michael has gained experience in a wide variety of business law and civil litigation, including cases involving business disputes, financial services litigation, workplace disputes, complex commercial litigation and even class action litigation. He has represented individuals as well as businesses of all sizes, from the local “mom and pop” business all the way up to multi-national corporations, in state and federal courts throughout Florida, as well as nationally in arbitrations before the FINRA, NYSE and AAA.

In addition to his courtroom experience, Michael has represented individuals and businesses in commercial transactions, such as lease negotiations, business entity formation, and employment contract review. Notably, Michael gained a wide array of transactional experience working as part of a team that acted as general counsel for a large nationally recognized hospital. Additionally, Michael has been named a Super Lawyers Rising Star in each year from 2010 through 2014.

Over the last several years, Michael has been involved in international litigation in addition to his statewide practice. This experience involved traveling throughout North America and Europe to prepare the case for what was ultimately a three-year trial and multi-year appeal in The Hague, Netherlands. It was a challenging and rewarding professional experience. The time away from home also made him truly appreciate all that his home in Florida has to offer. Following this, Michael wanted to use the experience gained in practicing law nationally and internationally to create his own firm with a focus on clients or client issues closer to home.

Michael Stanton was born on Long Island, New York but moved to the Tampa Bay area while in grade school. He graduated summa cum laude from East Lake High School in Tarpon Springs before attending the University of Florida’s Honors Program. During his time as an undergraduate at the University of Florida, Michael marched in the “Pride of the Sunshine Marching Band” and is to this day an avid college football fan. It is his love of college football that later led him to help found the college football blog, EveryDayShouldBeSaturday.com. While at UF, Michael was named an “Anderson Scholar with Highest Distinction” for academic achievement. After graduating magna cum laude with a degree in History, he attended the University of Florida’s Law School on a full academic scholarship. He graduated with honors and amongst the top of his class. Upon graduation, Michael returned to the Tampa Bay area to be closer to family and to start his legal career. Although his practice has led him to work in many countries around the world, he has always been based in the Tampa Bay area.

In his spare time he enjoys being with his wife, children and his large extended family enjoying many of the things the great State of Florida has to offer. He remains active in the community through such organizations as the Upper Tampa Bay Chamber of Commerce, where he serves on the board of directors, The Inspire Foundation and the Tampa Theatre Wine Fest Committee. He also enjoys coaching his sons in youth soccer, going to the beach, boating, fishing and of course watching and cheering for all the area sports teams, especially the Florida Gators.

attorneys.name: Robert Joseph Stanz
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Lakeland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Robert J. Stanz practices in the area of real property law, with special emphasis on land use and development, commercial and residential transactions and mortgage law. He has significant experience with zoning, land development regulations, lending, leasing and has served as claim's counsel for various title companies. Mr. Stanz has represented real estate developers, property owners and energy companies in complex land use matters.

Mr. Stanz has considerable experience regarding the permitting, purchase, sale and leasing of communications towers, as well as Florida timeshare law and property owners' associations. He has represented members of the communications, phosphate, timber and energy industries throughout the State of Florida. Mr. Stanz' local government experience includes work throughout the states of Florida and Kentucky, including representation of various municipal organizations, including cities and fire departments.

Prior to joining Holland & Knight, Mr. Stanz worked for Attorney's Title Insurance Fund, Inc. in Orlando, Florida, where he gained substantial expertise in Florida land title issues. He also practiced law in Kentucky and Indiana, with an emphasis on real property, probate and local government. Mr. Stanz is an Army veteran of "Operation Just Cause" in Panama and has served with distinction in both the Army and Army Reserve over the past twenty years. He currently serves as the Assistant Staff Judge Advocate for the 143rd Transportation Command in Orlando, Florida, and his duties include advising the unit commander and providing legal assistance to soldiers within the Command.

He is admitted to practice in Florida, Kentucky and Indiana, and is a member of the American Bar Association, Florida Bar Association and the Lakeland Bar Association. Mr. Stanz is a member of the Polk County Builders Association, the Florida Home Builders Association, the National Association of Home Builders and the Lakeland Realtors Association. He lives in Lakeland, Florida and currently serves on the board of directors of the Child Development Center of Polk County and Junior Achievement of West Central Florida (Polk County).

Mr. Stanz earned his B.S. magna cum laude and his M.S. from the University of Louisville. In 1997, he earned his J.D. from the Louis D. Brandeis School of Law at the University of Louisville.

As both a prosecutor and criminal defense attorney, Ben has conducted over 35 Jury Trials, 100 Judge Trials, and handled in excess of 2,000 Criminal/DUI/ Traffic cases.

Ben is a former collegiate basketball player who lives in Tampa with his wife and two dogs.

attorneys.name: Manuel F. Stefan
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Kissimmee, FL
attorneys.bio:
Manny Stefan is an Associate Attorney out of Morgan & Morgan's Kissimmee office located in Osceola County, just outside the metro Orlando area. He earned his Bachelors Degree from the University of Central Florida. He then went on to earn his Law Degree from Barry University. During law school he was fortunate enough to clerk at one of the states most powerful and reputable firms, getting early exposure to the courtroom.

Mr. Stefan then continued on to advance his legal career specifically in the world of Personal Injury. He worked at a local Plaintiff's law firm for several years; wherein, he helped out hundreds of people. His services reached anything dealing from auto accidents to slip and fall cases. Many times taking on the challenges of hard nose litigation and having to fight some of the biggest names in the consumer and insurance world.

Mr. Stefan was born in Honduras, and at the young age of 8 years old moved to the United States. He grew up in the Central Florida area. He is the son of hard working and dedicated parents, and a brother to a loving sister. Throughout his childhood summers he would return to Honduras to spend time with his family. Over the years he was exposed to a country like Honduras, and others, rich in culture and love, but poor in progression and exploited by the powerful. This created a desire for him to want to help those who lack the ability or resources to combat the powerful in moments of righteousness or turmoil.

Mr. Stefan brings his desire to help others when they feel they cannot help themselves, and combines his prior experiences to be able to help you, the people. He is an advocate of responsibility and having a house of accountability.

Mr. Stefan loves his family, his wife, baseball, and most importantly, his dog!

Mr. Stefan speaks Spanish fluently.

attorneys.name: Mark Steinberg
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Pinecrest, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mark Steinberg grew up in the suburbs of Miami not far from where he now practices law. He graduated with honors from Miami Killian Senior High and the University of Miami before attending law school at Stetson University College of Law in Gulfport Florida.

While at the University of Miami, Mark attended and resided in the University's first ever honors residential college. He majored in communication and minored in marketing. Mark was very active in the student and business community, even serving as student representative to the Chamber of Commerce's Miami's for Me initiative. While attending Stetson College of Law, Mark served as editor of the alumni publication "The Stetson Lawyer" and participated in mock trials and moot court events.

Mark has been a member of several professional associations, including the Bankruptcy Bar Association, the First Family Law Inn of Court, ant the National Association of Recording Arts and Sciences. He is a past vice president of the Florida Motion Picture & Television Association, and served two terms on the Florida Bar's Eleventh Judicial Circuit Grievance Committee.

Mark is admitted to practice law in all state courts and the Southern and Middle Districts of Florida.

Mark has practiced various areas of the law but currently focuses on the three areas where he believes he can most make a difference in people's lives: bankruptcy, family law including collaborative law, and estate planning.

In his spare time, Mark volunteers at the Pelican Harbor Seabird Station, practices yoga, and enjoys visiting local art galleries.

attorneys.bio:
Andy Steingold is a Senior Trial Attorney with MANEY | GORDON Trial Lawyers, who practices in the areas of Medical Negligence, Nursing Home Abuse, Wrongful Death, Products Liability and Personal Injury. Mr. Steingold is an active member of this community and is currently serving as a Safety Harbor City Commissioner and an Administrative Hearing Officer for the Hillsborough County Dangerous Dog Court. Mr. Steingold was the Mayor of the City of Safety Harbor from 2006-2017 during which he served on the Pinellas Planning Council, Metropolitan Planning Council, Pinellas Charter Review Commission, Emergency Medical Services Advisory Council, Pinellas Prescription Drug Abuse Council, Suncoast Transit Authority (PSTA) and Gulf Coast Jewish Family Services Board. While serving as the Mayor of the City of Safety Harbor Mr. Steingold was elected by his political peers as President of the Pinellas County Mayors Council.

BACKGROUND

attorneys.name: Christopher J. Steinhaus
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Chris Steinhaus is a third generation Orlando resident following in the footsteps of his mother and his grandfather, who moved here with his parents and brothers in 1918. Mr. Steinhaus graduated from Furman University, having obtained a bachelor's degree in Biology. Upon graduating from law school at Florida State University, Mr. Steinhaus stayed in Tallahassee and began working for the Agency for Health Care Administration, serving the citizens of the state of Florida in prosecuting licensed nurses who had alleged to have violated the Nurse Practice Act.

After leaving the Agency, the focus of Mr. Steinhaus's practice had been defending law enforcement agencies, hospitals, nursing homes and individual health care practitioners in both civil and administrative actions, from civil rights violations to complex medical malpractice claims to premises liability claims. During that time, Mr. Steinhaus gained extensive experience in representing clients in trials and hearings before the Florida Boards of Medicine and Nursing, multiple Circuit Courts of Florida, multiple District Courts of Appeal, and the Division of Administrative Hearings. In 2012 and 2013, Mr. Steinhaus was recognized by SuperLawyers as a 40-and-under Rising Star in the fields of Health and Personal Injury Law.

Mr. Steinhaus is excited to return to serving the citizens of the state of Florida by using the knowledge he has gathered as a defense attorney and putting it to work evaluating and prosecuting our clients' potential claims. On a personal note, Chris lives with his wife and two children in the College Park area and enjoys coaching flag football and playing tennis.

attorneys.bio: In our experience, we find that, like anyone else, law enforcement officers can and do make mistakes. Additionally, while there are thousands of dedicated, honest police officers in Florida, we have, unfortunately, seen examples of 'bad cops' filing charges based on false police reports, planted evidence or untruthful witness statements. An experienced criminal defense attorney may be able to show whether the officers acted inappropriately in your case.

attorneys.name: Jessica L. Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Panama City, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jessica L. Stewart has over 12 years of experience representing clients in their divorce, paternity, child custody, child support, alimony, domestic violence injunction, asset and liability distribution, and child relocation matters.

Jessica spent her formative years in Mobile, Alabama where she developed a passion for various aspects of dance, including competitive dance. She attended The University of Southern Mississippi and graduated Magna Cum Laude from Auburn University in 2008 with a Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science and minor in Psychology. The skills that she acquired dancing earned her a scholarship and a position on the Dixie Darlings dance team while she attended The University of Southern Mississippi. Jessica was also a member of the Pi Sigma Alpha Honor Society while attending Auburn University.

After graduating from Auburn University, she continued her education at Mississippi College School of Law, where she obtained her law degree. While attending law school, she received the Best Paper Award on two occasions.

Jessica initially joined The Reed Law Office in March 2014, and her practice focuses primarily on Divorce and Family Law matters. Her background also brings a wealth of efficiencies to our legal team. Jessica’s experience in Family Law, the discovery process, trial preparation, drafting pleadings, and all other aspects of the process, is invaluable to the firm’s success.

Ms. Stewart has practiced Family Law as well as general civil litigation in Bay, Escambia, Santa Rosa, Okaloosa, Walton and Leon Counties in Florida with several other firms. Her familiarity and span of knowledge in these surrounding counties is invaluable to her clients.

As part of The Reed Law Office legal team, her determination and creative strategies are truly comprehensive to deliver the best possible outcome for every client. Jessica is also an involved and dedicated member of the Walton and Bay County communities. Jessica is a member of the Bay County Bar Association, Northwest Florida Collaborative Law Group, Bay County Family Law Bench & Bar, and Family Law Section of the Florida Bar. Jessica is also a past member of the Okaloosa County Bar Association, Walton County Bar Association, Bay County Women Lawyer’s Association, St. Andrews Bay Inn of Court, Florida Bar Young Lawyer Division, Trial Lawyers Section of the Florida Bar, and volunteer for Northwest Florida Legal Services. She is a dependable problem-solver who is result-driven and zealously represents her clients in and out of the courtroom. She spends her spare time with her husband and two children. Jessica enjoys running, traveling and enjoying the beautiful beaches.
