attorneys.bio:
Tyler is an Associate at GMTB Law, where he represents clients in a broad range of civil litigation matters, with an emphasis on civil, real estate, business, and personal injury law. He brings extensive experience in insurance disputes, general liability, first-party property claims, insurance defense, and real estate transactions. Tyler has a proven track record of consistently delivering successful outcomes for clients.

He started his career as an Assistant Public Defender in Florida’s 9th Judicial Circuit in Orlando where he represented indigent defendants and took numerous cases to trial that sharpened his trial advocacy skills. From there, Tyler worked for three of Florida’s leading litigation firms where he gained invaluable experience litigating cases from their inception to trial or resolution. Tyler also managed his own private practice where he focused primarily on transactional law, contractual law, regulatory law, real estate law, and civil litigation.

Tyler earned his Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Oregon and then continued on to Barry University School of Law where he received his Juris Doctor, graduating cum laude and in the top 20% of his class. While in law school, he was chosen to represent his school on the Moot Court team and participated as an oral advocate and brief writer in 2 national competitions. Tyler also served as a judicial intern in Florida’s Eighteenth Circuit.

Outside of practicing law, Tyler enjoys spending time with his family, being outdoors, and fishing along Florida’s coast.

attorneys.name: Donna DeVaney Stockham, Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Property Insurance Litigation Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mrs. Stockham attended Auburn University and then received her Juris Doctor from Stetson University College of Law, Cum Laude. She was admitted to the Florida Bar in 1997. After graduating law school, Mrs. Stockham joined Carlton Fields, P.A. where she worked in the General Litigation Department. In that position, she represented Defendants in various civil and business litigation matters. She then joined the Products Liability Group where she represented pharmaceutical companies in the Fen Phen and Latex Glove litigation. After becoming a Shareholder at Carlton Fields, Mrs. Stockham wanted to diversify her experience and do Plaintiffs’ work. She began working at Merlin Law Group in 2006. While there, she represented Plaintiffs in property damage cases throughout Florida and Texas. She then started her own law firm in 2013 where she continued to focus her practice on first party property insurance litigation. However, her Firm also handles Condominium and Community Association Law and Nursing Home abuse cases. She is a member of the Florida Bar, the Texas Bar, and the Northern, Middle, and Southern Districts of Florida. She belongs to several Associations including the Windstorm Insurance Network where she is currently serving as the Secretary. She is a member of the Tampa Bay Business Journal's Leadership Trust, which is an invitation-only group for Presidents and CEOs of businesses. She was also recently selected as one of the Women to Watch in 2022 by Tampa Magazine.

She has been an AV Preeminent Peer Review Rated™ attorney by Martindale-Hubbell® for over 25 years. She has been selected for inclusion to the Florida Super Lawyers® list for thirteen consecutive years (2013-2025). Prior to that, she was selected as a Florida Super Lawyers Rising Star® from 2010-2012. She was also selected to Florida Trend’s Legal Elite from 2016-2020. Mrs. Stockham has recently been named to Florida Trend’s 2024 “Legal Elite Notable – Managing Partners” List. Her outstanding knowledge and experience awarded her the opportunity to speak at the American Bar Association Tort Trial and Insurance Practice Section (TIPS), Property Insurance Law Committee, Spring CLE meeting in Carlsbad, California on the topic of Mediating Property Insurance Cases. In addition to the above achievements and awards, she received a rating of 5.0 out of 5.0 from peers from the Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review.

Mrs. Stockham is a trial lawyer with a diversified background as both a defense lawyer and a plaintiff’s lawyer. She has tried cases as both defense counsel and plaintiff’s counsel. She is detailoriented, fair, and experienced in a variety of legal areas.

attorneys.bio:
Katie is a Brevard County native who graduated cum laude from Florida State University College of law in December of 2018. The summer after her first year of law school she interned with former Chief Judge Tonya Rainwater working on civil litigation over $15,000. The summer after her second year of law school she worked as a Certified Legal Intern in the juvenile division of the State Attorney’s Office.

Growing up in Brevard County, Katie was an avid soccer player. She played locally on state championship winning teams for Satellite High School as well as for coach Fidgi Haig’s Indialantic Force club team. During high school she received various honors including Florida’s Gatorade Player of the Year. After high school, she earned a full athletic and academic scholarship to play soccer at the University of Central Florida. She captained the team for her junior and senior seasons before graduating with a degree in Biology from UCF’s Burnett Honors College. After college, she taught science and leadership skills for one year at Eau Gallie High School before moving abroad to Switzerland and New Zealand to play professional soccer. In New Zealand, she also worked one-on-one with students from the special needs classes at a local high school, coached high school girls’ soccer, and waitressed at a local pub.

Katie lives in Indialantic with her husband and two daughters.

attorneys.name: Michael G. Stofer
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in St. Petersburg, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mike was born in Arkansas but moved to St. Petersburg, Florida, when he was about two years old and grew up in the Tampa Bay area. After high school, he began working full time and attending college. He first enrolled at St. Petersburg Junior College and in 1992 he earned an A.A. Degree, with a focus on criminal justice. He then attended the University of South Florida (enrolling at the St. Petersburg Campus) and earned a B.A. Degree in Political Science (Government and International Affairs) in 1994. Upon earning his B.A. Degree, Mike attended Florida State University in Tallahassee, Florida, where he earned his J.D. (Juris Doctorate, with honors) in 1996.

Being the son of a police officer, Mike always had an interest in law enforcement and began his legal career at the State Attorney's Office in Pinellas County, Florida. In approximately five years at the State Attorney's Office, Mike prosecuted juvenile cases, misdemeanor cases, domestic batteries, DUI's, felonies, drug trafficking cases and murders. Mike was specially assigned to investigate and prosecute child abuse cases and handled a number of capital child abuse trials. Mike was also assigned to the DUI Manslaughter Squad, which was a special team of prosecutors that assisted in the investigation and prosecution of motor vehicle related fatality cases.

After gaining valuable trial experience, Mike took a position as an associate at the law firm of Caglianone, Miller & Anthony in Tampa, Florida. He continued his focus on litigation primarily in the areas of insurance defense and motor vehicle liability, along with some personal injury cases and some appellate work.

In 2005 Mike joined the firm of Deacon, Moulds & Smith. He continues to practice litigation in several areas, focusing in the areas of medical malpractice and nursing home defense, defending doctors, nurses and nursing homes that get sued by their patients. In addition to these areas of civil litigation, and based upon the significant criminal and trial experience gained during his time at the State Attorney's Office, Mike has continued to practice in the area of criminal law representing those charged with traffic infractions, DUI's, misdemeanors and felonies.

Mike still lives in St. Petersburg, Florida with his wife and two boys. He is actively involved in his church and enjoys sports.

attorneys.name: Bonnie Sockel Stone
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Bonnie Sockel-Stone is a Board Certified Specialist by the Florida Bar in Marital and Family Law, which is her sole area of practice. She has been a member of the Florida Bar since 1989 and is a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers and International Academy of Family Lawyers and has an AV Preeminent Rating by Martindale-Hubbell. Bonnie has also been recognized as a Top-Rated Lawyer by Super Lawyers, an Outstanding Lawyer in Florida Trend's Legal Elite and was selected by Attorney At Law Magazine as one of the 13 to Watch in 2013 and has been recognized by Best Lawyers. Bonnie was the recipient of the Florida Bar Family Law Section Integrity Award in 2021, the Chair's Award for Extraordinary Service in 2019, the Chair's Award for Special Merit in 2019, the Above and Beyond Award in 2018 and 2019 and the Legislative Award in 2016, 2017 and 2018.

Bonnie has a J.D. from the University of Florida Levin College of Law and a B.S. in Accounting from University of Florida Fisher School of Accounting. She began her professional career with the accounting firms of Deloitte, Haskins and Sells and Ernst and Young. Her extensive accounting experience is utilized on a regular basis in her Marital and Family law practice.

Bonnie has authored articles for the Daily Business Review titled Divorcing Spouses Should Consider Tax-Filing Options, Preventing Same-Sex couples from Divorcing is Unjust and Plan Ahead for Holiday Time With Children in Divorce and has authored an article for the Huffington Post titled Discovering Hidden Assets: What Your Spouse Hasn't Disclosed During Your Divorce. She has also authored a module on Prenuptial Agreements for the Lexis Practice Advisor. Bonnie has lectured on Domestic Violence issues and has participated as a speaker for the Dade County Bar Association Family Law Committee Continuing Education Seminar, The Florida Bar Family Law Section Case Law Update and Mechanics of Board Certification and the AAML Webinar, A Matter of Trust: Trust Instruments in Divorce.

Bonnie is the Vice Chair of the Florida Bar Marital and Family Law Certification Committee for 2021-2022 and served as the Chair of the Florida Bar Constitutional Judiciary Committee for 2020-2021. Bonnie has been a member of the Florida Bar Family Law Section Executive Council since 2015. She served as Co-Chair of the Family Law Section Legislative Committee (2016-2018) and was actively involved in advocating for the 2018 legislation that bans child marriages. Bonnie has served as Co-Chair of the Equitable Distribution Committee from 2018-2021 and served as Chair of the of the 2019 Marital and Family Law Review Course Committee. Bonnie also serves on the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers Florida Chapter Legislative, Institute and Webinar Committees. Bonnie is a member of the Miami-Dade County Bar Association, the Miami-Dade County chapter of the Florida Association of Women Lawyers, Florida Family Law Inns of Court, and the American Bar Association.

Bonnie is always interested in providing pro bono legal services, especially regarding children's issues. She has served as a Lawyer For Children pro bono lawyer for foster care youth, provides pro bono legal services to domestic violence victims and has served as a pro bono Guardian Ad Litem.

Bonnie devotes a great deal of her free time giving back to the community. She served as President of the National Council of Jewish Women Greater Miami Section and received the Myra Farr Volunteer

Service Award. She also served as President of Kidside, Inc. and served on the CHARLEE board and the Temple Beth Sholom School Board.

attorneys.name: Clark Alan Strandell
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Lauderdale, FL
attorneys.bio:
Clark Alan Strandell began his career as an attorney in 2005 with the Law Office of the Broward County Public Defender. For the next several years he defended those accused of committing crimes. While employed as an Assistant Public Defender, Mr. Strandell tried over 50 jury trials to completion.

Prior to becoming an Assistant Public Defender, Mr. Strandell graduated from Florida State University. While at F.S.U., Clark was a member of the elite Florida State cheerleading squad.

Following his graduation from F.S.U., Mr. Strandell pursued a law degree from Nova Southeastern University. After attaining his education, Mr. Strandell continued honing his legal expertise and was awarded a full scholarship to Gerry Spence's intensive Trial Lawyers College. As a result of this additional educational experience, Mr. Strandell became well versed in defending clients against corporate and government oppression.

Mr. Strandell has worked with the firm since 2011 and has since partnered with Michael Gottlieb, P.A.. While working in conjunction with Mr. Gottlieb, the two have enjoyed numerous successes in formulating motions and winning strategies to help their clientele win suppressions and dismissals in State and Federal Court. Mr. Strandell works with Mr. Gottlieb, with both lawyers reviewing each and every aspect of their clients' cases thus affording each client the opportunity to have two lawyers reviewing their cases. This formula has proven successful and will continue to provide the law firm with winning strategies moving forward.

Should you ever find yourself being charged criminally, it is wise to hire an aggressive and knowledgeable criminal attorney, such as Mr. Strandell for legal assistance and representation. Set up a free consultation with Clark Alan Strandell to help ensure that your rights are properly protected.

attorneys.name: Christian A. Straile
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Gainesville, FL
attorneys.bio:
This trial focused practice has the goals of delivering quality legal services, providing to clients personal services while developing strong, trusted relationships through effective communication, analysis, planning and litigation skills seeking the best result possible.

Mr. Straile has been an attorney since 2003 and been an intern within the justice system since 2001; he is a member of the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, a member of the Florida Bar, and a past treasurer for the Eighth Judicial Circuit Young Lawyers Division.

Mr. Straile focuses his practice on trial law specializing in DUI, traffic, criminal, domestic violence, injunctions, automobile accidents, family, business law and limited other civil litigation or civil trial matters. Mr. Straile handles cases from civil traffic to trafficking narcotics and cases ranging from misdemeanors to life felonies. Mr. Straile handles all levels of criminal offenses and all issues related to criminal offenses from investigation to verdict and appeal. Family cases include divorce, custody, paternity, modification, domestic violence, injunctions, child abduction, division of assets, parenting plans, and marital settlement agreements. Mr. Straile represents businesses from start up to litigation after sale. Many clients also have used Mr. Straile to provide general consulting regarding business decisions.

Mr. Straile earned an LL.M (advanced law degree) from the University of Florida in tax law, a J.D. from St. Thomas University and a B.S. from Lambuth University. Prior to entering the legal field Mr. Straile worked providing financial services and advice at Banker's Life & Casualty and Morgan Stanley.

Mr. Straile spent two years between the Third District Court of Appeal in Miami and the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit State Attorney's Office in Ft. Lauderdale . While in Law school Mr. Straile was active in trial competitions, and coached the St. Thomas Trial Team.

Mr. Straile's volunteer work includes the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program and the Boy Scouts of America. Mr. Straile served as an organizer of the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program and a liaison between the program and the Internal Revenue Service. sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
This trial focused practice has the goals of delivering quality legal services, providing to clients personal services while developing strong, trusted relationships through effective communication, analysis, planning and litigation skills seeking the best result possible.

Mr. Straile has been an attorney since 2003 and been an intern within the justice system since 2001; he is a member of the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, a member of the Florida Bar, and a past treasurer for the Eighth Judicial Circuit Young Lawyers Division.

Mr. Straile focuses his practice on trial law specializing in DUI, traffic, criminal, domestic violence, injunctions, automobile accidents, family, business law and limited other civil litigation or civil trial matters. Mr. Straile handles cases from civil traffic to trafficking narcotics and cases ranging from misdemeanors to life felonies. Mr. Straile handles all levels of criminal offenses and all issues related to criminal offenses from investigation to verdict and appeal. Family cases include divorce, custody, paternity, modification, domestic violence, injunctions, child abduction, division of assets, parenting plans, and marital settlement agreements. Mr. Straile represents businesses from start up to litigation after sale. Many clients also have used Mr. Straile to provide general consulting regarding business decisions.

Mr. Straile earned an LL.M (advanced law degree) from the University of Florida in tax law, a J.D. from St. Thomas University and a B.S. from Lambuth University. Prior to entering the legal field Mr. Straile worked providing financial services and advice at Banker's Life & Casualty and Morgan Stanley.

Mr. Straile spent two years between the Third District Court of Appeal in Miami and the Seventeenth Judicial Circuit State Attorney's Office in Ft. Lauderdale . While in Law school Mr. Straile was active in trial competitions, and coached the St. Thomas Trial Team.

Mr. Straile's volunteer work includes the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program and the Boy Scouts of America. Mr. Straile served as an organizer of the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program and a liaison between the program and the Internal Revenue Service. For the Boy Scouts Mr. Straile taught merit badges, served as quartermaster, and assistant scout master. Mr. Straile is an Eagle Scout.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Tammy Strohl, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Naples, FL
attorneys.bio:
I have been a plaintiff trial lawyer in Naples, Florida for over 17 years. I choose to practice personal injury because I enjoy it and it is my belief I can make a difference. I like the idea that I am able to meet a lot of different people from this area and from all over Florida and other states, even Canada and Europe. My client does not need to be a US citizen nor do they need money. My clients have diverse backgrounds. Some have lived in Florida their whole lives and many have relocated to Naples, some are simply visitors. This is what makes the profession interesting. Many people find themselves in serious conditions due to do the injuries caused by the negligence of others.

We are a small office and I can give our clients the personalized attention they need. I can really take the time to get to know everyone, since I have four years within which to bring a claim from the date of occurrence. I have patience and can sympathize and understand how their lives have changed because of the accident injury. I return clients’ phone calls in a timely fashion, letting them know I am always available to them and care about their concerns. I listen to my clients when they explain how the injuries have affected their lives and loved ones. I am a perfectionist by nature and so is my staff. When presenting a claim I want to be thorough and net as much money for my client as possible. Personal injury cases take time, are emotional and consuming but when done correctly help people. That is what my law firm strives to do.

My goal is to exceed my clients’ expectations. I want my client(s) to be happy with the way their claim is handled. My reputation is the most important thing to me.

No one gives you your reputation; it is the one thing that you have to earn through hard work. Please give me the opportunity to work hard for you.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate and Trust Planning and Administration Lawyers in Boca Raton, FL
attorneys.bio:
Peter S. Strobis is Senior Counsel with Pannone Lopes Devereaux & O'Gara LLC and a member of the firm's Estate and Trust Planning, Administration and Litigation Team. He focuses his practice on developing comprehensive estate plans with full advanced directives specifically tailored to fit his client's unique circumstances and goals. He also provides counsel to personal representatives, trustees, and beneficiaries during administration. In addition, he represents clients throughout all phases of probate and trust litigation.

Attorney Strobis is also highly skilled at developing and implementing business succession plans, asset protection techniques and tax minimization strategies including simple revocable trusts, irrevocable trusts, and complex trusts, such as Intentionally Defective Grantor Trusts, Irrevocable Life Insurance Trusts, and Charitable Remainder Trusts. His keen knowledge of the ever-changing landscape of state and tax laws ensure his clients are in full compliance with federal and state regulations.

Attorney Strobis earned his J.D., with honors, from Florida International University College of Law, and his Bachelor of Science degree, with honors, from Florida State University. He is licensed to practice in Florida and is a member of the Florida Bar Association's Real Property, Probate, and Trust Law and Young Lawyers Sections.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Wilton Manors, FL
attorneys.bio:
Founded in 2016, Strunin Law, PLLC is committed to shaking off the cumbersome practices of old-fashioned law firms, in favor of modern, client-centered legal services.

We relentlessly focus on achieving every client’s unique goals by checking our ego at the door, listening carefully and thoughtfully, and providing tenacious representation with the minimal possible disruption in our clients’ lives.

Keith is admitted to practice before all Florida Courts and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida. Keith devotes his practice to representing plaintiffs in personal injury matters, as well as estate planning and probate.

Keith’s personal injury practice involves representation of individuals who have been injured due to negligence. Using his years of experience handling these matters exclusively, Keith will relentlessly work to obtain the maximum possible compensation for people who have been injured in serious accidents of all kinds, including motor vehicle and bicycle collisions, pedestrian accidents, wrongful death, premises liability, funeral home & cemetery abuse, and medical malpractice.

Keith’s estate planning practice employs his combination of business and legal training to assist clients with all of their estate planning needs, including the creation of wills and trusts. He also represents clients in probate matters such as the administration of estates and trusts, as well as any contested matters that require litigation.

attorneys.name: Angel Stull
attorneys.practice_type: Pharmaceutical/Medical Device Mass Torts Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
Angel N. Stull is native to the Florida Panhandle. She earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Florida State University, graduating magna cum laude. Mrs. Stull was a recognized as a Florida Scholar and remained on the National Dean’s List through matriculation.

Mrs. Stull earned a Juris Doctorate from Barry University, Dwayne O. Andreas School of Law, as part of an accelerated program, graduating in only two years. Mrs. Stull received Highest Grade Book Awards in several classes including Wills, Trusts & Estates and Children in the Law. During law school, she became a Certified County Mediator for the State of Florida and assisted in forming the Real Property & Probate Trust Law group at Barry University. Additionally, Mrs. Stull coordinated the start of VITA, Volunteer Income Tax Assistance, as a coordinator and was quoted in Student Lawyer Magazine for her care and assistance towards the Central Florida community.

Beyond academics, Mrs. Stull gained significant legal experience working with the Orange County Mediation Office and as a student practitioner for the Legal Aid Society in Central Florida (appearing before the court and advocating for many underprivileged clients). Never one to rest (or rest on her laurels), Mrs. Stull secured summer internships within the in-house Intellectual Property Legal Department for the world renowned fashion company Burberry, in Manhattan.

After ultimately determining that she wanted to find a niche within the world of complex products liability, Mrs. Stull sought a position with the nationally recognized pharmaceutical and medical device firm, Aylstock, Witkin, Kreis & Overholtz PLC, where she currently practices in the areas of pharmaceutical and medical device mass torts. Mrs. Stull is currently involved in the following matters: Transvaginal Mesh Devices, Avandia, Reglan/Metoclopramide and Steven Johnson’s Syndrome.

Mrs. Stull is licensed to practice law before all Florida state courts and all New York state courts. Additionally, Mrs. Stull is a member of the American Bar Association, the Florida Bar, the New York Bar, the Escambia/Santa Rose County Bar Association, Pensacola Young Professionals and the American Association for Justice.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Highest Grade Book Award-Children in the Law

Highest Grade Book Award-Wills, Trusts & Estates

attorneys.name: Rene Suarez
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Rene Suarez was born in Pahokee, Florida to Cuban immigrant parents and grew up in Miami. At an early age, Rene learned the virtues of hard work from his blue collar, practical family. Rene’s father was a welder and his mother was a lab tech at a sugar refinery. Rene received his bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, with high honors, from Florida International University where he was first in his class. Mr. Suarez received his law degree from St. Thomas University School of Law in Miami where he graduated Magna Cum Laude and ranked third in a class of 130. Rene passed the bar exam on his first try in July 2001 with one of the highest scores recorded for that testing session and the highest score of any student from a Florida school.

Rene and his wife Yohany, who is also the firm’s Administrator, have three children who keep them quite busy when they are not in the office. When time permits, Rene is a muscle car enthusiast who can be spotted in his driveway tinkering with a variety of vehicles, much to the dismay of Yohany.

Mr. Suarez has worked for large civil defense firms and as in-house counsel for a Fortune 500 company. Rene found his true calling in helping people caught up in the criminal justice system: “There is hardly a more noble calling than defending the individual rights that the founding fathers of this Nation fought and died for. One of the most fundamental of those rights is the government’s burden to have to prove someone guilty beyond, and to the exclusion of, every reasonable doubt. It is my job as a criminal defense attorney to make sure the prosecutor, the judge, and the jury recognize and respect that most fundamental principle.”

Professional Background:

As the Managing Partner of Founders Law in Georgia, I bring over five years of dedicated legal practice to our firm. My journey at Founders Law began at the age of 18 as a legal assistant, where I developed a deep understanding of personal injury law. Over the years, I've grown into a leadership role, overseeing operations and ensuring exceptional client service.

Education and Credentials:

I graduated from Monsignor Edward Pace High School in Opa Locka, Florida, before earning a Bachelor's degree in Accounting. Inspired by a desire to deepen my impact in solving legal challenges, I pursued my Juris Doctor at St. Thomas University, graduating in 2023. I am licensed to practice law in Georgia, Florida and California.

Areas of Specialization:

In addition to personal injury law, I am a licensed real estate broker and mortgage loan originator in Florida. My expertise extends to real estate law, where I have contributed to significant transactions and legal resolutions.

Professional Philosophy:

Driven by the belief that attorneys play a crucial role in shaping our society, I entered the legal profession to solve complex issues and advocate for justice. I prioritize putting clients first, upholding principles of respect, honesty, integrity, and confidentiality in every case.

Personal Interests: Outside of my legal career, I find solace in outdoor activities such as fishing and hunting. These hobbies not only provide relaxation but also instill a sense of discipline and patience, qualities that resonate in my approach to legal practice.

Community Involvement:

I am actively involved in community initiatives aimed at promoting legal education and access to justice. Through pro bono work and volunteer efforts, I contribute to making legal resources more accessible to underserved communities.

Future Aspirations:

Looking ahead, I am committed to expanding Founders Law's impact across Georgia and Florida, continuing to deliver exceptional legal services, and staying at the forefront of legal advancements in personal injury and real estate law.

attorneys.name: Robert A. Sugarman
attorneys.practice_type: Employee Benefits Law Lawyers in Miami (Coral Gables), FL
attorneys.bio:
Bob Sugarman grew up as the son of a union butcher. As a teenager he became a union member himself; he attended college with the support of a union sponsored scholarship and later worked as a union organizer. Bob saw firsthand the positive benefits that fair wages, a secure retirement pension and safe working conditions had on his family and on others. He decided to dedicate his life's work to helping working people, a vocation he continues today.

Bob attended the University of Virginia School of Law after working as a union organizer with the Retail Clerks International Association and its Local 400 in Washington, D.C. At UVA Law he had the privilege of working as a research assistant to Professor Frank McCulloch, former Member and Chairman of the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) from 1961 to 1970.

Bob returned to his native Florida after receiving his law degree in 1972. Bob Sugarman met Howard Susskind soon thereafter; they have been working together for over 35 years. They established Sugarman & Susskind in 1985 in order to represent employee benefit funds, workers, and labor organizations.

Currently Bob represents the boards of more than 65 municipal pension and health care plans. He also represents unions and workers in all industries, including fire fighters, government workers, education, construction, transportation, entertainment, and health care.

In 2001 Bob became one of the first Florida Bar Board Certified Labor and Employment Lawyers. He has also served as an executive board member of the Florida Bar Labor Law Section. He is a longtime member of the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans, the National Association of Public Pension Attorneys and is a board member of the AFL-CIO Lawyers Coordinating Committee. Bob was elected by his peers as a Fellow of the College of Labor and Employment Attorneys.

Bob is a frequent guest speaker and lecturer on employee benefits law topics. He is a permanent faculty member of the International Foundation's Certificate of Achievement in Public Pension Policy (CAPPP TM) certification program and has taught for the Certified Employee Benefit Specialist program, a joint venture between the International Foundation of Employee Benefits Plans and the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. He is also a frequent speaker at conferences of the International Foundation, the Florida Public Pension Trustees Association, the Florida Division of Retirement, the Society of Actuaries and the Government Finance Officers Association. He has also served an adjunct professor at Florida International University.

Bob has been listed in The Best Lawyers in America continuously since 1989. He was also recognized as a Top Lawyer by South Florida Legal Guide and has been listed in Florida Super Lawyers since 2006.

attorneys.name: Howard S. Susskind
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Law Lawyers in Miami (Coral Gables), FL
attorneys.bio:
Howard Susskind has dedicated his career to representing workers, their unions and employee benefit plans. He and Bob Sugarman created Sugarman & Susskind in 1985 to provide quality legal services for the benefit of working people, a commitment that continues to this day.

Howard attended the University of Miami School of Law and graduated in 1974, the same year that the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) became law. Howard wanted to represent labor unions and working people; he also recognized that ERISA was about to change how pension and health benefits would be provided to such workers. By combining these interests Howard developed a practice focused on protecting employee wages, safe working conditions, and pension and health benefits.

Howard has advised the trustees of multiemployer benefit plans subject to ERISA requirements from the day that ERISA began to govern such plans. Howard has experience in all facets of labor law, from organizing campaigns to collective bargaining agreements to arbitrations to unfair labor practice hearings. He's brought actions under the National Labor Relations Act and appeared before the National Labor Relations Board. He's also brought actions seeking unpaid wages and overtime under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

Howard is a frequent guest speaker on ERISA, employee benefits law and labor law topics for organizations such as the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans. He is a longtime member of the AFL-CIO Lawyers Coordinating Committee, is currently serving on the Regional LCC Committee for the NLRB Reform Project, and previously served on the LCC Advisory Board.

Howard was honored by his peers in 2004 when he was elected as a Fellow of the College of Labor and Employment Attorneys. He has been listed in The Best Lawyers in America for many years; was recognized as a Top Lawyer by South Florida Legal Guide in 2006 and 2007; and was listed in Florida Super Lawyers in 2007.

attorneys.name: Paul L. Sutherland
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Maitland, FL
attorneys.bio:
Paul Sutherland is a Central Florida native, having lived in the Central Florida area for the past 34 years. Paul graduated from Central Florida's own Cypress Creek High School. He continued on to Valencia where he earned his AA degree before obtaining two BA's from the University of Central Florida. After receiving his MS from Henley-Putnam, Paul attended Barry University School of Law in Orlando, Florida and was ranked seventh overall at the time of graduation.

While obtaining his JD, Paul gained legal experience as a judicial extern for the Honorable Patricia Doherty and the Honorable Kim Shepard in the Ninth Judicial Circuit Court of Florida. Paul then furthered his legal education when he became a Certified Legal Intern with the City of Orlando Attorney's Offices civil litigation team.

Paul has never been one to shy away from challenges. Since the age of 16 he has worked in the ever-evolving information technology field where he taught himself how to program, troubleshoot, and deploy network, server, and end user technology systems. With this vast IT background, Paul is eager and able to tackle any case involving technical discovery.

Paul is exceptionally proud of his history as a volunteer. Having called the Central Florida area home his entire life, the improvement of his community and the people who live in it is one of the driving forces behind his passion. He routinely donates his time and labor to organizations which help those in need, as well as participates in and raises money for charities which benefit local Floridians. It is the commitment to community improvement and mentorship that Wilson McCoy P.A. champions that lead Paul to choose Wilson McCoy P.A. to be his home.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Michael Sutton was born in Orlando Florida on April 3, 1952. A native Floridian, he was educated in the Orange County Public School System and graduated from Maynard Evans High School in 1970. He is a member of St. Charles Catholic Church and Knights of Columbus where he has been actively involved in fund raising for mentally and physically challenged children. Mr. Sutton is an avid outdoorsman enjoying hunting, fishing, and cattle ranching. He married Adrienne Brunelle on 1972 and shares a beautiful child named Jennifer Michelle Tyler.

In 1993, the Florida Bar named Mr. Sutton as a Board Certified Civil Trial Attorney, a distinction given to less than 2% of all attorneys practicing in the State of Florida. This certification is the highest level of recognition by the Florida Bar in the area of Civil Trial Litigation.

Mr. Sutton has been honored with the prestigious "A V rating" by Martindale-Hubble, the preeminent national publication in the legal field. This rating is based upon evaluations by other lawyers and is the highest ranking attainable by an attorney for ability and ethics in the practice of law. It is a distinction reserved for a select few in the legal community.

attorneys.name: John J. Sweeney
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sweeney's practice focuses primarily on Wills, Trusts, and Estate Planning as well as Elder, Tax, Business, Mergers, Acquisitions, and International Law. He is a practical, business-oriented lawyer who strives for solutions. He is experienced in setting up estate plans tailored to each client's unique situation, including all manner of wills, trusts, and other estate planning tools and instruments. This experience includes planning for estates with multiple jurisdictional and international aspects, assets and legal considerations. It also includes trusts for tax planning, probate avoidance, and asset protection purposes.

His tax experience is deep and varied including extensive US tax and international taxation in Europe, Asia and South America. Mr. Sweeney has counseled corporations, individuals and other entities in cross border taxation and methods to minimize taxation or prevent double taxation. His business, mergers and acquisitions background is rooted in his experience as a lawyer, manager and CFO for startup, growth, insurance, and financial service companies and is the basis for his unique business oriented approach. He has worked for both private and public companies. He has over 10 years of international experience spanning Europe, South America and Asia. He has a deep background in international and domestic tax planning. His extensive M&A experience includes over 30 deals totaling $12B in assets, many international.

John's business experience includes acting as the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) for a public dot com (.com) and as the Head of Tax for an international insurance company with $6B in revenue. He was also CFO, General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer for a private equity portfolio company. Formerly, he was the CFO for ING International Insurance Holdings, a complex multinational insurance operation with revenues of over $4B. His prior work experience also includes roles with Aetna International as its Tax Director and AIG as a tax lawyer at its world headquarters.

John is a member of the Connecticut, New York and Washington D.C. bars.

attorneys.name: Glenn M. Swiatek
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Crestview, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Swiatek opened his practice in Fort Walton Beach in 1998 gaining experience in all of the Florida State Court systems. He has argued cases before the County, Circuit and the District Court of Appeals as well as the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles. Mr. Swiatek also practices in the federal court system and is admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Northern District of Florida in Pensacola. His experience ranges from representing the accused in cases of domestic violence, battery, DUI and robbery to murder. Mr. Swiatek has provided research for cases argued before the United States Supreme Court and was an editor of the Oklahoma Tribal Court Reports. He has been the Law Week Chairman for the Okaloosa-Walton Bar Association for the past four years and also serves as the Vice-President of the Okaloosa-Walton Chapter of the Florida Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. attorneys.name: Michael Sznapstajler
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Lawyers in Daytona Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sznapstajler joined Cobb Cole after participating in the firm's summer program in 2007 and graduating from Stetson University College of Law in 2008. Mr. Sznapstajler practices in the areas of environmental law, land use and civil litigation. As part of his environmental practice, Mr. Sznapstajler represents businesses and redevelopers with environmental due diligence, assessment and cleanup of contaminated properties, redevelopment of properties through state and federal brownfield programs, submerged lands permitting, and wetland and species issues. As part of his land use practice, Mr. Sznapstajler focuses on obtaining entitlements and approvals for development of property. As part of his litigation practice, Mr. Sznapstajler represents clients in commercial litigation, local government, land use and environmental litigation, administrative hearings and appeals.

Mr. Sznapstajler is a Past President of the Florida Brownfields Association, which is a nonprofit, volunteer, service organization dedicated to advancing the cleanup and redevelopment of brownfields in Florida and frequently speaks before local governments, trade organizations, and environmental professionals regarding brownfield redevelopment. Mr. Sznapstajler is also active in the local community, having served as Chair of the Daytona Beach Downtown Development Authority, President of the Young Professionals Group, and on the Ormond Beach Brownfield Advisory Board. Mr. Sznapstajler has also served on the Board of Directors of the Jewish Federation of Volusia and Flagler Counties, on the Jewish Heritage Festival Planning Committee, and the Checkered Flag Committee.

Mr. Sznapstajler is married to Jessica Sznapstajler and has a daughter and son.

Mr. Sznapstajler holds an AV rating, which is the highest rating obtainable by an attorney from Martindale-Hubbell.

attorneys.name: David Tamaroff
attorneys.practice_type: Computer Fraud Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
David Tamaroff is a partner in Morgan & Morgan's Business Trial Group. Based out of the law firm's Miami, Florida office, he litigates cases in federal courts throughout the state and across the nation, primarily representing plaintiffs in intellectual property cases. His knowledge of intellectual property law runs deep, with substantial experience in litigation involving copyright infringement, patent infringement, trademark infringement, counterfeiting, and unfair competition. He possesses a notably comprehensive understanding of copyright litigation in the context of the internet, specifically with relation to embedding and hyperlinking, BitTorrent file sharing, and the Digital Millennium Copyright Act's (DMCA) safe harbor provisions.

In various copyright cases, Mr. Tamaroff has recovered hundreds of thousands of dollars for his clients, including photographers, film production companies, musicians, and artists. He has successfully managed multi-jurisdictional patent enforcement campaigns on behalf of inventors, and resolved trademark disputes on favorable terms for clients, including a mobile app developer, online news site, and luxury real estate broker. He is also adept at litigating claims for deceptive or unfair trade practices, computer fraud or abuse, fraudulent inducement, breach of contract, and business torts. Frequently representing plaintiffs in federal courts, Mr. Tamaroff is no stranger to arguing complex issues of jurisdiction, venue, and civil procedure.

Mr. Tamaroff has a perfect 10.0 rating on Avvo.com, and has been recognized as Florida Super Lawyers ͞Rising Star͟ in Intellectual Property Litigation from 2015-2018. Before he joined the Business Trial Group, he was a partner in a boutique intellectual property law firm in downtown Miami, Florida. Prior to pursuing a legal career, he worked as a laboratory assistant researching cancer drug development and genetic therapeutics at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, in Boston, MA, and Dr. Susan Gilbert's Laboratory at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, in Troy, NY.

attorneys.bio:
Nathan joined Lake Law Firm in March 2021 as an associate attorney and self-proclaimed ‘learn-it-all' where he continues to grow and expand his legal experience. He graduated Magna Cum Laude from WMU Cooley Law School in 2020, where he was the recipient of various merit-based awards and recognitions, as well as an active member and competitor of both the Tampa Bay Moot Court Board and Tampa Bay Mock Trial Board, serving as the Chief Justice and President respectively. He also volunteered at Thomas M. Cooley Law School's Debt Relief Clinic guiding indigent clients through the process of Chapter 7 Bankruptcy. Prior to law school, he graduated from Indiana University majoring in Political Science, and spent a semester abroad at Mannheimer Abendakademie und Volkshochschule GmbH in Mannheim, Germany studying German Language.

Nathan has been nurturing his passion for law from a young age as he watched his late father's nearly 40-year legal career flourish. He was inspired to pursue a legal career himself by his inherent "passion for using law to discover truth and serve justice." He enjoys serving his community and advocating for his clients' best interests - legally, ethically, morally, and financially. Outside of the office, Nathan trades in his suit and tie for hiking shoes and a backpack, as he enjoys being in the great outdoors, soaking up all of the nature and travel that he can.

Nina Tarafa is the Senior Attorney at the Corona Law Firm. Ms. Tarafa practices out of the firm’s Main Office located in Miami, Florida. She practices primarily in the area of criminal defense, contested litigation and trial work.

Ms. Tarafa has sat as lead counsel in over fifty jury trials and has extensive trial experience both in civil and criminal court. Ms. Tarafa is a zealous advocate who practices with professionalism. She is well versed in the law and rules of evidence and uses all legal tools available to zealously advocate for each of her clients.

Since 2016, Ms. Tarafa has focused on family law litigation including high-conflict cases, uncontested matters, dissolutions of marriage, child support, paternity, step-parent adoptions and other related family law matters.

Prior to joining The Corona Law Firm, Nina Tarafa served the community for approximately five years as a prosecutor for the Miami-Dade County State Attorney’s Office. She prosecuted cases ranging from misdemeanors and DUIs to Armed robberies and homicides. She quickly rose through the ranks of the office serving as an Assistant Chief of the Career Criminal and Robbery Unit, a Felony Division Chief and a member of the Traffic Homicide Unit.

As a law student at the University of Florida, Ms. Tarafa served an internship at the Alachua County Public Defender’s Office.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Nina Tarafa is the Senior Attorney at the Corona Law Firm. Ms. Tarafa practices out of the firm’s Main Office located in Miami, Florida. She practices primarily in the area of criminal defense, contested litigation and trial work.

Ms. Tarafa has sat as lead counsel in over fifty jury trials and has extensive trial experience both in civil and criminal court. Ms. Tarafa is a zealous advocate who practices with professionalism. She is well versed in the law and rules of evidence and uses all legal tools available to zealously advocate for each of her clients.

Since 2016, Ms. Tarafa has focused on family law litigation including high-conflict cases, uncontested matters, dissolutions of marriage, child support, paternity, step-parent adoptions and other related family law matters.

Prior to joining The Corona Law Firm, Nina Tarafa served the community for approximately five years as a prosecutor for the Miami-Dade County State Attorney’s Office. She prosecuted cases ranging from misdemeanors and DUIs to Armed robberies and homicides. She quickly rose through the ranks of the office serving as an Assistant Chief of the Career Criminal and Robbery Unit, a Felony Division Chief and a member of the Traffic Homicide Unit.

As a law student at the University of Florida, Ms. Tarafa served an internship at the Alachua County Public Defender’s Office.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Peter A. Tappert received a degree in finance from the University of Miami, and a law degree cum laude from the University of Miami School of Law, where he was a member of the Law Review. Mr. Tappert was admitted to The Florida Bar in 2006. He is admitted to practice in all of Florida’s state courts, the U.S. Supreme Court, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, and the U.S. District Courts and U.S. Bankruptcy Courts of the Southern, Middle, and Northern Districts of Florida. Mr. Tappert has spent his entire career at Weissman & Dervishi, and became a shareholder in 2013.

attorneys.name: Joe Taraska
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Joe Taraska graduated from the United States Air Force Academy in 1969 and was honored with the distinction of being selected as the outstanding cadet in law. Following that, he received his law degree at the University of Pennsylvania. He was then competitively selected for special training at the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology. He subsequently served as one of six forensic medical/legal consultants for the United States Air Force.

In 1976, Mr. Taraska began a statewide litigation practice in Florida, specializing in the representation of healthcare professionals, hospital and other healthcare organizations and their insurers.

He was a founding partner of Taraska, Grower, Unger and Ketcham, P.A. in Orlando, Florida. He served on the Bioethics Committee of Florida Hospital and as council to the CEO of the Adventist Health Systems/Sunbelt campuses in Central Florida.

In 2009 Mr. Taraska joined Morgan & Morgan, P.A as a senior trial lawyer in complex litigation representing those who have been seriously injured by the negligence of others.

His areas of practice include wrongful death, medical malpractice, nursing home abuse, defective products, defective pharmaceuticals, tobacco litigation, civil rights, health law, hospital law, hospital credentialing, hospital bylaws, hospital risk management, state medical licensure, and managed care. He is a member of The Florida Bar, The Pennsylvania Bar, The United States District Court, Middle District of Florida, The United States Court of Appeals, Eleventh Circuit and The United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Taraska has written and spoken extensively. He is the author of the 1,500-page text, "A Legal Guide for Physicians" and various chapters including, "Death - Withholding and Withdrawing Life Support," "Physician Discipline," "Preventive Medicine for the Cancer Specialist," as well as authored 75 articles in health law. In addition to his writing, Mr. Taraska has spoken throughout Florida and the United States.

Mr. Taraska's honors include being board certified as a civil trial lawyer by The Florida Bar since 1984. He has earned the highest national peer review rating "AV" and was selected as a Florida Super Lawyer by his peers in 2007. He is currently a member of The American Board of Trial Advocates, The Florida Board of Trial Advocates, The Volie A. Williams, American Inns of Court, The American Association for Justice, The Florida Trial Lawyer's Association, and The Florida Bar.

attorneys.bio:
My goal in my law practice is to do the best to provide my clients with highly personalized service. I will do all that is required to make you a happy satisfied client so that not only will you return over and over again but that you will recommend me to your friends and neighbors. attorneys.firm_name: Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability/SSI Lawyers in Pensacola, FL
attorneys.bio:
As one of the founding partners of Taylor, Warren, Weidner, Hancock & Barnes, Stephanie Taylor practices law in cases involving insurance disputes, disability law, Social Security Disability (SSD) and Supplemental Security Income (SSI), serious injury, and wrongful death. She serves clients in the Pensacola, Florida, area.

Prior to beginning her law career, Ms. Taylor earned her Bachelor of Science from the University of Colorado in 1988 and her Juris Doctor from the Florida State University College of Law in 1993. She served as president of the Florida State College of Law Student Bar Association. Having earned her law degree with honors and received the Book Award in Elder Law during her law school career, she went on to begin her career as an associate at McKenzie and Soloway, P.A., where she later became a partner in 1998. In 2006, she along with two other attorneys from the firm formed Taylor, Warren & Weidner, P.A.

Ms. Taylor is admitted the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit. She is also admitted to the Florida state courts. She was admitted to practice law in California, but has gone on inactive status in California.

As an active contributor to the legal community, Ms. Taylor is a member of several professional associations, including the Florida Justice Association, the Escambia-Santa Rosa County Bar Association, the Academy of Florida Trial Lawyers and the American Association for Justice. She contributes to her community by also taking part in pro bono activities as a board member for the Mental Health Association of West Florida.

attorneys.name: Mitchell Lasher Teitelbaum
attorneys.practice_type: Education Law Lawyers in Sarasota, FL
attorneys.bio:
Mitch comes to Windsor law as an extremely proficient and experienced education law attorney and trial attorney after overseeing the legal department for the School District of Manatee for almost a decade. He was the Assistant Superintendent of Administration.

Mitch was one of the most cross-trained individuals in the school district. Mitchell was the attorney in charge of the Legal Department. He also oversaw Public Records, Charter Schools, and Risk Management as well as the Office of Professional Standards. Mitchell also launched and oversaw the entire Guardian Program after the tragedy at Marjory Stoneman Douglas. He took immense pride training every class of guardians.

One of the most filling responsibilities was Mitchell's role as an Exceptional Student Education Attorney. Assisting the school district on countless IEP meetings, 504 Plan meetings, Manifestation Determination meetings, Behavioral reassignment meetings, Parenting issues, and Court proceedings.

Mitchell proudly has certifications from Florida State University in Public Records, Sunshine Laws, and Ethics. Mitchell is a master of FERPA and educational records of students. Also, he has expertise in the new Parental Bill of Rights. He often defended numerous complaints filed against the School District, including Office of Civil Rights, State Complaints and complaints from the Florida Department of Education Office of the Inspector General.

Mitch was born and raised in California then moved to NY where he obtained a bachelor's degree in psychology from New York University and earned the Founders Day Award, for the highest scholastic preferment by New York University. Mitchell also obtained his master's degree in liberal arts from New York University. Mitchell graduated cum laude from his law school Yeshiva University.

Mitchell is one of the few attorneys in the Country to be admitted to the California Bar, New York Bar and Florida Bar.

Prior to moving from NY to Florida, Mitch served as House Counsel to American International Group, the largest insurance company in the world as a trial attorney. Mitchell also worked for Eagle Insurance Company defending clients in numerous motor vehicle and property cases. Mitchell also had the pleasure to work for State Farm Insurance Company as their trial attorney. Mitch routinely tried cases in the hardest venues in New York.

Mitchell went into private practice and served as a Partner of Torino & Bernstein. Mitchell oversaw the New York City Housing Authority Account for almost a decade. He successfully tried countless cases for the firm.

Proudly married to his gorgeous wife Joanna for over thirty years. He takes considerable pride in her being a Realtor and the Top Producer in the region for Keller Williams on the Water.

Mitch and Joanna raised three children. They are proud of having two children who are teachers. One who even specializes in Exceptional Student Education, the other in Elementary Education. Mitchell's other son is also a realtor.

Attorney Teitelbaum's school district experience and litigation background makes him an ideal addition to Windsor Law. His unique skills are a complement to all our staff and tremendous benefit for our clients.

attorneys.name: David F. Tegeler
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Lawyers in Winter Park, FL
attorneys.bio:
David F. Tegeler is Board Certified by The Florida Bar as a specialist in Construction Law.

Mr. Tegeler is a trial lawyer with the firm of Michael C. Sasso, P.A. in Winter Park, Florida. He has practiced law for more than 26 years and has extensive experience in the area of construction law and commercial litigation. As an attorney, David Tegeler has represented all types of participants in the construction process, including owners, general contractors, subcontractors, sureties, and design professionals. In addition to his trial practice, he also regularly counsels clients regarding the preparation and negotiation of contracts and related transactional documents for construction projects.

David Tegeler earned his Bachelor of Architecture degree at Carnegie-Mellon University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. He received a Juris Doctor degree from Duquesne University, where he was selected to serve on the Duquesne University Law Review. He has been a Registered Architect for more than 35 years, and has experience in the design and construction of residential, institutional, industrial, recreational, and commercial projects. Mr. Tegeler has been a member of the American Institute of Architects, and served on the Board of Directors of both the Florida Association of the AIA and the Orlando Chapter of the AIA.

Attorney Tegeler is admitted to practice law by the United States District Court, Middle District of Florida, and The Florida Bar, where he is a member of the Section on Real Property Probate and Trust Law and its Construction Law Committee. He is also a member of the Orange County Bar Association. David Tegeler has also been trained as a Circuit Civil Court Mediator in Florida.

Mr. Tegeler has served for over 29 years as an Arbitrator on the Commercial Panel of the American Arbitration Association, primarily in construction cases. He has actively participated in many professional organizations and community service groups. David Tegeler has authored several articles regarding construction law for professional publications, and has presented many seminars to professional groups over the years, including architects, engineers, landscape architects, contractors, subcontractors, and surveyors.

attorneys.name: Briana Ashley Texter
attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in New Port Richey, FL
attorneys.bio:
Briana Texter, Esquire, is a passionate and skilled attorney with a broad legal background encompassing business/commercial transactions, family law, immigration, and civil litigation. With a focus on providing comprehensive and client-centered legal services, Briana is dedicated to pursuing positive outcomes in her clients’ matters. Known for a deep commitment to litigation, Briana is not afraid to take cases to trial when necessary to advocate for client's rights and interests.

Briana earned a Juris Doctor with a concentration in Business Transactions from Thomas M. Cooley Law School, where Briana demonstrated academic excellence, earning Dean’s List and Honor Roll honors throughout the entirety of the law program. Briana was awarded Certificates of Merit for multiple core courses, including Contracts, Torts, and Civil Procedure. This dedication to academic rigor was complemented by leadership roles, including serving as President of the Real Property, Probate, and Trust Law Society, Treasurer of the Student Bar Association, and Editor-in-Chief of the Cooley Pillar Newspaper. Briana also regularly competed as a member of the Moot Court Board, where skills in oral advocacy were sharpened through competition.

In addition, Briana has demonstrated a deep sense of social responsibility through volunteering as a Guardian ad Litem for Pasco County, advocating for the best interests of children in legal proceedings. This role reflects Briana's commitment to justice, equity, and the welfare of vulnerable populations.

Beyond law, Briana is also the Chief Executive Officer and President of Forefront Medical Billing Corporation, a role in which Briana has leveraged leadership and business skills to run a successful enterprise since 2018. This experience, combined with a Juris Doctor (JD) degree from Thomas M. Cooley Law School, specializing in business transactions, gives Briana a unique and well-rounded perspective, particularly in navigating the intersection of business and law.

Skills and Expertise

Business Transactions – Focused academic concentration, equipping Briana with a strong foundation in business law.

Litigation – Proven experience in litigation, including business litigation and family law matters.

Family Law – Advanced skills in family law mediation, helping clients reach resolution in difficult disputes.

Legal Research Proficiency – Highly skilled in legal research ensuring thorough preparation and accurate legal analysis for every case.

With a career marked by a strong commitment to client advocacy, academic excellence, and community service, Briana continues to be a dynamic force in the legal community. Briana is dedicated to delivering impactful legal solutions and ensuring justice is served.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in St. Petersburg, FL
attorneys.bio:
Steven Teuber understands not only the litigation process and the legal arguments in your unique matter but also has 25 years of corporate experience outside of law to understand the conflict from a real world perspective. Steven understands that each mediation is unique and special to the parties. The diversity of subject matter, the spectrum of complexity, the variety of personalities all require individualized attention and consideration. Steven understands that a mediator's toolbox must be filled with creative approaches and thinking to assist all stakeholders in building a solution to the conflict.

Using a proactive approach, Steven is extremely effective in bringing a case to closure, resulting in early dispute resolution that translates into cost savings and a reduction of emotional and mental stress and fatigue. Steven focuses on both the substantive portions of the case but is also sensitive and empathetic to all concerned.

attorneys.name: Helena Tetzeli Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Helena M. Tetzeli is a partner at Kurzban Kurzban Tetzeli & Pratt, P.A.

Ms. Tetzeli has a nationwide reputation as a leading immigration attorney. She is frequently asked to write and speak on immigration law topics. Her immigration practice areas include E and L visas, EB -5 visas, Extraordinary Ability visas and National Interest Waivers for clients in the sciences, arts, business and athletics. Additionally, she represents clients in federal and administrative court litigation, including removal defense, habeas, and APA cases. Her immigration clients include unions for major league professional athletes, high profile U.S. and foreign companies, individual investors and others seeking to do business or immigrate here, as well as start-ups in a variety of business and industrial sectors.

In addition to her immigration law practice, Ms. Tetzeli also represents her clients in federal and state court and in arbitration and mediation proceedings in a variety of complex matters including substantial collection cases and defense of discrimination, FLSA, ADA and other employment law claims. She also advises her business and institutional clients on a variety of compliance and policy matters to minimize the risk of litigation.

Ms. Tetzeli has been recognized by Who's Who in American Law, The Best Lawyers in America, Super Lawyers, Chambers and Law Dragon. Because of her successful track record and high degree of ethics in all of her professional endeavors, she has received the highest possible AV Preeminent* peer review rating by Martindale-Hubbell.

attorneys.name: Gregory Alan Thacker
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Clearwater, FL
attorneys.bio:
Greg Thacker is a civil trial lawyer who is passionate about the law, his clients and providing personal attention to each of his clients in order to make the legal process as stress free as possible while achieving the best possible outcome. Greg litigates all types of injury cases including car accidents, commercial trucking accidents, general negligence, slip and fall accidents, motorcycle accidents, biking accidents, defective products and wrongful death cases.

Greg was born and raised in Clearwater, Florida and comes from a long line of Florida attorneys including his great grandfather, grandfather and grandmother who were all attorneys in Kissimmee, Florida. His father and brother are also established attorneys in Pinellas County, Florida.

Greg graduated from Clearwater High School in 1998. He attended college at the University of Central Florida. After college, he attended law school at Stetson University College of Law. While at Stetson, Greg received the top grade in several of his courses including Real Property, Trusts and Estates, Evidence and Trial Advocacy. He was awarded the Melvyn Trute P.A. Trust award and graduated Cum Laude in 2006. While in law school, Greg interned at the Pinellas County State Attorney’s office where he was certified to take misdemeanor cases to trial before a jury prior to even graduating from law school. This is when he fell in love with being in the courtroom and trying cases before a judge and jury.

After working as a prosecutor for three years, Greg left the State Attorney’s Office to go into private practice where his focus was the practice of family law. He continued his experience of regularly being in the courtroom as lead trial counsel on numerous family law cases including complex child custody, divorce, paternity, domestic violence injunction, business valuation, asset valuation and dependency related matters. He handled numerous multi-million dollar divorce cases with highly complex family law and business related issues. Additionally, he personally handled and won several appeals before the 2nd District Court of Appeals including giving oral argument before the appellate court. Several of the family law judges in the sixth judicial circuit appointed Greg to act as a pro bono Guardian Ad Litem on behalf of children involved in highly contentious family law matters where he acted as a voice for the children and made recommendations to the court regarding various child related issues.

Greg Thacker is a Life Member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum which are limited to attorneys who have won million and multi-million dollar verdicts, awards and settlements. Fewer than 1% of U.S. lawyers are members.

After practicing family law for over seven years, Greg decided he wanted to invest his efforts in a new area of law. He always had an interest in being a litigator in the area of personal injury law and he accepted a position at an established personal injury law firm in Pinellas County, Florida. There he handled numerous personal injury matters and fell in love with the area of law and helping guide his clients to get healthy again and obtaining the compensation they deserve for their injuries.

With a strong desire to personally handle all aspects of his client’s cases, Greg left the firm he was with to start Thacker and Mulvihill, PLLC, P.A. in July of 2019. Greg’s goal is to work directly with his clients from the date he meets them through the conclusion of their case. All of Greg’s clients are given his personal cell phone number so he can be available to them at all times.

Being injured through no fault of your own is a life changing experience. Greg wants to minimize the stress of bringing a claim or lawsuit so his clients can focus on getting better. The slogan “Let Thacker Be Your Backer” means Greg will personally have your back throughout all aspects of your case so you can focus on getting better while Greg handles the rest.

When Greg is not practicing law he enjoys spending time with his wife of over 15 years and their two daughters, dog, cats, bearded dragon and foster birds and squirrels.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Life Member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum

Jay, a native of Brevard County, graduated from the University of Florida with a Bachelors degree in Finance and minors in Entrepreneurship and Criminology. He continued his studies at the University of Florida Levin College of Law, earning his Juris Doctorate in 2010.

Jay is very active in both the local and state Bar Associations. Jay served on the Board of Governors for the Young Lawyers’ Division of The Florida Bar representing the 18th Judicial Circuit comprised of Brevard and Seminole County, an organization with approximately 30,000 members. Jay also served as the past President of the Young Lawyers Division of the Brevard County Bar Association and the past President of the Brevard County Bar Association. Jay currently serves on the Board of Directors for the Brevard County Legal Aid.

Jay has been recognized nationally by Super Lawyers since 2015 and has been the recipient of the Associate of the Year Award twice from Vassar B. Carlton American Inns of Court.

In his free time, Jay enjoys traveling and spending time with his wife and two boys.

attorneys.name: Katherine Thanos
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Katherine Thanos is an attorney in the Morgan & Morgan Business Trial Group. Ms. Thanos's practice focuses on representing businesses and individuals in commercial litigation.

Ms. Thanos was born and raised in Jacksonville, FL. She received her undergraduate degree from the University of Florida, majoring in both English and Economics. She later returned to Gainesville to earn her Juris Doctorate degree, with honors, from the University of Florida Levin College of Law. While in law school, Ms. Thanos was an Ethos of Excellence Scholar, a research assistant, a member of UF Law's Alternative Dispute Resolution Team and a coach for Florida's arbitration team.

Ms. Thanos has a long-standing commitment to serving the public. During law school, she interned at the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission in Tampa, FL, investigating Title VII violations on behalf of employees wrongly discriminated against by their employers. In addition, Ms. Thanos spent a summer at the Southern Poverty Law Center in Atlanta, advocating for detained immigrants seeking political asylum. She spent her final semester of law school in Washington, D.C. at the Department of Justice. There, she worked as a legal intern in the Criminal Antitrust Division to advance cases against companies engaged in illegal price-fixing and bid-rigging agreements.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: Amelia Island Company. Served as debtor's counsel in Chapter 11 reorganization and sale of $67 million 5 star golf and tennis resort located on Florida's Northeast coast. Auction resulted in sale of resort and conference facilities to Omni Hotels and spin off of signature golf course to club members.

Halifax Hospital Medical Center. Represented Halifax Hospital in action against competitor hospital for $122 million deficit in uncompensated healthcare promised under a 2005 settlement agreement between the parties.
Tijuana Flats Restaurants. Served as debtor’s counsel in complex Chapter 11 reorganization involving 65 company owned and 29 franchised “Tex-Mex” restaurants located across Florida.

Surge Transportation, Inc. Served as debtor’s counsel for national freight broker with over 1,600 creditors and $20+ million in debt. Debtor successfully reorganized with full satisfaction of sums due its secured lenders.
RMS Titanic. Seved as creditors’ committee counsel for reorganization and eventual sale of company holding salvage rights for the RMS Titanic.

Persimmon Hollow Brewing Company. Served as debtor’s counsel in Chapter 11 reorganization for a Central Florida craft beer distributor and taproom operator. Debtor successfully “retrenched” operations in its flagship location after being “un-saddled” of nearly $10 million in debt.

Black News Channel. Served as debtor’s counsel in Chapter 11 sale of national cable news network and the only provider of 24/7 programming dedicated to covering the unique perspectives, challenges and successes of various minority communities.

NRP Lease Holdings (Adventure Landing). Successfully reorganized Jacksonville, Florida based network of 17 family entertainment, sports and amusement centers located across the Eastern United States. Was one of the few Chapter 11 cases in the country to obtain an injunction requiring the SBA to extend PPP funding to a Chapter 11 debtor.
Shrimp Basket Intermediate Holdings. Oversaw wind-down and eventual sale of 29 company owned restaurants located across Alabama, Mississippi and Northwest Florida.

BayView Healthcare. Represented 120 bed assisted living facility and skilled nursing center in connection with complex bond restructuring and eventual sale of the retirement community in the midst of the COVID-19 crisis.
Protogroup South Tower. Assisted borrower with workout and restructuring of $55 million loan facility secured by oceanfront hotel.

M.D. Moody & Sons, Inc. Served as debtor's counsel in Chapter 11 reorganization of 100 year-old crane distribution company located in Jacksonville, Florida. The reorganization involved nearly $30 million in secured and unsecured debt.

Life Care St. Johns, Inc. Served as debtor's counsel in complex Chapter 11 reorganization of $54 million in publicly traded bond debt secured by Glenmoor, a Continuing Care Retirement Community located in the World Golf Village.
Trailer Bridge, Inc. Served as creditors' committee counsel in reorganization of Jacksonville, Florida based shipping company having over $98 million in secured and unsecured debt.

Bryco Arms. Represented $21 million judgment creditor against manufacturer of defective firearm which moved to Florida in an effort to frustrate collection efforts. Case gained worldwide attention as the judgment creditor, a young man who was rendered a paraplegic as a result of the defective firearm

Citation: attempted to purchase the very company which manufactured the defective gun. Our Firm successfully caused liquidation of the gun manufacturer and distributor, and the collapse of at least four family trusts established to shield assets from reach of creditors.

Winn-Dixie Stores, Inc. Represented City of Jacksonville, numerous landlords and trade vendors in the Chapter 11 reorganization of Winn-Dixie Stores, one of Jacksonville, Florida's largest homegrown businesses.

Westminster Apartments. Ltd. Besides reorganizing 240-unit apartment complex, was successful in obtaining a $1.7 million judgment against Orkin Pest Control for failing to properly detect and treat severe termite infestation.
