attorneys.name: Sami Thalji
attorneys.practice_type: Auto Accident And Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Sami Thalji is a native Floridian, born in Clearwater and raised in St. Petersburg, Florida. Sami spent much of his childhood and teenage years working various jobs throughout Pinellas County, including Clearwater Beach, St. Petersburg Beach, Pinellas Park, Largo, Belleair Beach, and the Countryside area. Sami graduated from Osceola High School in Seminole, Florida before attending and receiving my Bachelor of Science and Juris Doctor from the University of Florida in Gainesville, Florida. Sami started his legal career in law enforcement as a public servant in Tampa at the Hillsborough County State Attorney's Office. In 4 short years, Sami personally handled thousands of cases and worked in every department at the State Attorney's Office. Sami led the first ever juvenile rocket docket program where he handled thousands of files as the lone prosecutor. Sami also worked in the Domestic Violence, Misdemeanor and DUI divisions. During his time prosecuting drunk drivers and domestic violence offenders, Sami tried more then 50 DUI jury trials and 12 domestic violence jury trials. Sami was ultimately promoted to the felony division where he earned the job of Felony Lead Trial Attorney within one year. During his time in felony court, Sami tried more then 50 jury trials, including 38 jury trials in his last 12 months as a prosecutor. On Sami's last day as a prosecutor he spent it trying a jury trial for armed robbery and kidnapping. Sami's dedication to his job led to a promotion to the Major Crimes Division. During his time as a felony prosecutor, Sami tried serious cases such as kidnapping, armed robbery, sexual assault, various 10-20-Life cases, carjacking, manslaughter, arson, DUI serious bodily injury, attempted murder, and murder. Sami won more than 90% of his jury trials while at the State Attorney's Office, including a perfect 5-0 record in murder trials.

Once Sami left the State Attorney's Office, he joined a statewide criminal defense firm. During his two years there, he tried many high profile defense cases, including the successful defense of an 18 year old man wrongfully accused of a hate crime by the Pinellas County Sheriff and the Pinellas County State Attorney. The hate crime case received an extreme amount of media attention and took more than 1 year of litigation, 2 jury trials and 1 mistrial to resolve. Once Sami presented his closing arguments the jury deliberated only 5 minutes before returning a verdict of not guilty on the hate crime. Sami has often said that case was one of his proudest moments as a lawyer. Sami's client was clearly not guilty of the hate crime and Sami's work revealed the State's heavy handed tactics were employed solely for cheap political gain rather than the pursuit of justice.

After two years working as a criminal defense attorney, Sami moved on to a new challenge. Sami started STAMATAKIS + THALJI with my colleague, law school classmate, and friend, Scott Stamatakis. Initially, STAMATAKIS + THALJI represented banks in foreclosure actions. Ultimately, STAMATAKIS + THALJI evolved into one of the State's largest and most effective full service, consumer justice firm. STAMATAKIS + THALJI represents consumers throughout the State of Florida in auto accident and personal injury claims, sinkhole claims, bankruptcy, foreclosure defense, collections defense, loan modifications, short sales, real estate, title insurance, and credit repair.

When Sami is not in court or at the office you will probably find him at the Northdale YMCA, where he coaches youth sports teams in soccer, basketball, and football.

attorneys.name: Carl
attorneys.practice_type: International Tax Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Carl Christian Thier is a founding shareholder of Urban Thier & Federer, P.A., an international law firm with offices in the US, Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, the Dominican Republic, and Ecuador. He frequently travels between the firm's offices to coordinate international legal and business matters.

Mr. Thier's works primarily in the area of business and corporate law, with a particular focus on international business and contract law, structuring of complex business structures in the US and cross border. He negotiates complex business deals and supports the management of US and international corporate clients with strategic advice.

He advises startup companies and newly formed subsidiaries of international companies in the US.

Mr. Thier structures multi-level business holding and management structures with a focus on liability and tax optimization across borders, which often involves rules of Treaties for the Avoidance of Double Taxation ("Double Taxation Treaty”).

Mr. Thier also offers a wealth of experience in cross-border estate planning and international inheritance matters, serving clients in the U.S., U.K., Germany and across the world. His deep understanding of the international laws governing inheritance and international estate planning allows him to navigate complex situations from a position of strength.

Mr. Thier manages the New York office of the firm.

Mr. Thier is a member of the New York Bar Association as well as the German Bar Association. Until Brexit, he was also admitted to practice in the United Kingdom. He serves as President and Chairman of the Central Florida Chapter of the German American Business Chamber (GABC). He also teaches International Law at Lawline, a leading US provider of continuing legal education. He is a member of the steering committee of the German Wirtschaftsrunde in New York. Mr. Thier is Honorary Consul of the Republic of Austria.

attorneys.name: Shari Thieman
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Navarre, FL
attorneys.bio:
Shari Thieman-Greene (pronounced "t-man green") graduated from the University of Nebraska College of Law in 1998. Before that, she attended Creighton University in Omaha, Nebraska, on scholarship, and graduated in 1990. Then, she worked in banking and saw that sometimes, it is the smallest details that make the biggest differences, which inspired her in law school and today. Shari is very active personally and professionally and served as president of the Escambia Santa Rosa Bar Association from 2010 - 2011.

Shari also has a deep appreciation of military personnel and issues. In 2002, Shari met her now-husband who was stationed at Kirtland Air Force Base in Albuquerque, New Mexico. When he came to Hurlburt Field Air Force Base in 2003, Shari came with him, and they fell in love with Northwest Florida. Because of this relationship, Shari knows what it is like to be in the military and to be the spouse or family member of someone in the military. Please ask Shari about a military discount on your construction law case, contract review or any other legal issue.

Angela Thomas is Jacksonville born and received her undergraduate degree in Psychology from the University of North Florida, where she graduated magna cum laude. During her time at Florida Coastal, Ms. Thomas was a Justice on the Honor Court, Student Bar Association Treasurer, Mock Trial Team member, Phi Delta Phi member and interned at the City of Jacksonville's Office of the General Counsel.

Ms. Thomas joined Morgan & Morgan in 2017 and now represents consumers as an associate in the firm's Breach of Warranty department.

attorneys.name: Christina J. Thomas Mazaheri
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
I am a native South Carolinian, the oldest of three daughters, and the product of a working class, eat-your-okra-first-and-mashed-potatoes-second style family.

In highschool I was one of a handful of International Baccalaureate degree candidates, who, due to limited resources, had to choose between learning Spanish or French. I chose French because I wanted to communicate with the French Canadians who came to visit the beach each spring. Seven years later, a trusted college advisor signed me up for my first solo trip abroad to a Spanish-speaking country.

By the time I graduated college, I had completed six weeks of Spanish-immersion in Costa Rica, a semester in Washington, D.C. as a Congressional Fellow with Representative John Spratt, and two semesters as a civilian Research Assistant to a U.S. Army Recruiting Command Psychologist who studied the relationship between active duty in Iraq, posttraumatic stress disorder, and combat soldier reintegration. I also conducted an independent study on Physical Fitness Reform in South Carolina's Public Schools and defended an Honors Thesis on applying mechanical engineering's version of Dynamic Systems Theory to Healthcare Reform. In 2004, I graduated from the University of South Carolina's Honors College, magna cum laude, with a Baccalaureus Artium et Scientiae degree in Interdisciplinary Studies, including Biology, Political Science, French and Spanish.

After college, I landed a year-long gig teaching French at my hometown middle school and began making plans for travel. In the fall of 2005, I literally hopscotched over Hurricane Katrina on my way to Honduras and spent the next three months sharpening my Spanish skills, conducting schematic research for an HIV/AIDS education pilot program, and watching my home country flounder from a distance. In my spare time, I went fishing with the locals and explored the native Mayan Ruins of Copan. In January of 2006, after only one month at home, I flew to Malawi for a six-week volunteer experience with World Camp for Kids, Inc. In Africa, we reached out to more than 1,000 schoolchildren, teachers and community members in an effort to bring a scientific understanding of the HIV/AIDS epidemic to the region and encourage young people to stand strong against the rape culture that permeated their villages.

The next fall, I went back to school. I made the Dean's List five of my six semesters at the Charleston School of Law, became Managing Editor of the Charleston Law Review, and had the honor of being one of only four of my classmates to give an appellate-level argument before two federal court judges and the Mayor of Charleston in the final round of our school's IL Moot Court Board Competition.

In the summer of 2007, I went back for more World Camp, doubling as a Program Coordinator in Honduras and a student researcher for a paper entitled Transnational Civil Procedure: Practicing Law in Honduras. A year later, my travel bug itched again, and I moved to Miami, Florida, where I interned for a high-profile immigration law firm in which eighty percent of the workplace conversations occurred in Spanish.

The next fall, I volunteered with South Carolina Legal Services in Charleston, S.C., where I helped prepare federal cases against violators of federal laws regulating migrant farm workers and workplace discrimination. I also participated in legal services outreach programs within the neighboring Hispanic communities and received my school's "Giving Back" Award for community service. I graduated from the Charleston School of Law in 2009, cum laude, and secured a contract as a statewide Migrant/Limited English Proficiency paralegal with South Carolina Legal Services, where I stayed until I was sworn into the Florida Bar in December 2009.

Interestingly, the jobs missing from my resume are the ones that made my entire resume possible. For the last twelve years I have been forced, for economic reasons, to wear many different hats. Besides being an attorney, I was once a waitress, a hostess, a street vendor, a summer camp counselor, a customer service associate, a tutor, a bookkeeper, a theme park character, a pancake slinger, a bartender, a seamstress, a biscuit maker, a night watch"woman, " a campground reservationist, a Spanish radio public service announcer, and a daycare worker. All of these jobs I held in addition to my internships, sometimes juggling two paying jobs and one non-paying job to make ends meet while completing my studies.

When I'm not working, my passions are cooking, fishing, playing the piano, and teaching my ninety-five pound Treeing Walker Coonhound to sit still when he sees a duck. I love my family and science-fiction movies, and I look forward to learning at least three more languages, having my own garden, and one day, becoming a mother.

I joined The Amlong Firm in February 2010 as an Associate where I primarily practice employment discrimination litigation. It is a true honor to be part of a team of professionals dedicated to protecting workplace fairness. I am pleased to offer my services in both English and Spanish and am determined to bring a little South Carolina "charm" to both the Florida courtroom and to my relationships with clients, who, just like me, are working hard for their American Dreams.

attorneys.bio:
Brian Thompson has been practicing law for over 25 years with 15 years in plaintiff's law. He received his undergraduate degree from Loyola University, magna cum laude, in 1979 and his Juris Doctorate degree, with honors, from Loyola School of Law in 1987.

For the first ten years of practice he represented the insurance companies in personal injury cases. Since then, for over ten years he has solely represented victims of abuse and neglect. Because of his extensive background and knowledge of the insurance industry he is better positioned to represent those who wish to file claims against them.

From 1987-1992 Mr. Thompson practiced with Gelpi, Sullivan, Caroll & Laborde in New Orleans. From 1992-1996 he practiced with Gunn, Ogden & Sullivan, P.A. in Tampa, and 1996 until 2006, with Wilkes & McHugh, P.A., where he was responsible for several multi-million dollar jury verdicts.

Mr. Thompson and John Cummings formed Thompson & Cummings, P.A. in April of 2006. They remained in practice until coming to Morgan and Morgan, P.A. in January, 2012. At Thompson & Cummings, P.A. he had two multi-million dollar jury verdicts.

Mr. Thompson is licensed to practice law in Florida, Mississippi, and Pennsylvania. He is a member of the Florida Bar, and the American Board of Trial Advocates. He has been recognized as one of Florida's "Legal Elite" by Florida Trend magazine and has been named one of Florida's Super Lawyers consecutively since 2008.

attorneys.name: Stephen D. Thompson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fort Myers, FL
attorneys.bio:
Steve is a Board Certified Marital and Family Lawyer, a Certified Family Mediator, Collaborative Lawyer, and an Arbitrator. He handles a wide variety of marital and family law cases, with particular emphasis on divorce litigation and post-judgment modification. Having practiced law since 1979, Steve believes strongly that marital disputes can be handled in a manner that will be the least damaging to the family, and include negotiations which will arrive at a settlement with emotions on both sides held in check. Bottom line: Saving money and time.

Steve’s years of experience as a family law attorney include a great interest in the value of preserving family relationships. He helped design and create the County Clerk’s Support and Visitation Enforcement Program, for which he received the Florida Bar President’s Pro Bono Service Award. He participates in numerous other programs and organizations such as the Child Protection Team and the Children’s Alliance, and for a number of years was involved in the Guardian Ad Litem Program.

Co-author of Florida Legal Forms - Domestic Relations, published by West Publishing Company, Steve has also published “Hot Tips for Successful Mediations” in The Family Law Commentator for The Florida Bar; co-presented portions of a seminar sponsored by National Business Institute, and others. He is founding member and organizer of the Collaborative Lawyers of SW Florida and is actively involved in a number of civic organizations.

Steve was admitted to The Florida Bar in 1979. He received his B.S., cum laude, in chemistry and pre-medical studies from the University of Miami, Coral Gables, Florida, in 1973. In May 1978 he received his J.D. from the University of Miami School of Law. Honors include Dean’s List and Lawyer of the Americas Student Board.

attorneys.practice_type: Brain Injuries Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan Thomson (JT) was born in Birmingham, Alabama before moving to Orlando, Florida as a child. After graduating from Bishop Moore High School in Orlando, he attended the University of Miami for his undergraduate education receiving a Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance in 2001. Upon receiving his degree, he attended Brooklyn Law School in Brooklyn, New York, before returning to Orlando in 2009 following graduation.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, JT worked at a prominent Florida civil defense firm where he specialized in defending insurance companies and their insureds in personal injury lawsuits. As part of a highly respected defense firm, he developed a keen awareness for how insurance companies (de)value cases for those injured as a result of the negligence of others. Furthermore, his time on the defense allowed him to frequently spend time in the courtroom developing invaluable knowledge and experience.

Mr. Thomson joined Morgan and Morgan in August 2019, and now utilizes his prior experience as a defense attorney to prepare his clients for what to expect from the insurance company during the handling of their claim. This experience allows his clients to know that their attorney will ensure their case is being handled with utmost professionalism and attention to detail. Mr. Thomson primarily represents clients who have been injured as a result of a motor vehicle accident and premises liability claims, but is happy to be of help to anyone who needs legal assistance in their time of need.

You may reach Mr. Thomson directly at any time via e-mail at JonathanT@ForThePeople.com or by telephone at 407-420-1414.

Mr. Thornburg is a Registered Patent Attorney with extensive experience in the areas of patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, and related technology litigation. He also represents clients in the areas of patent and trademark prosecution, domain name disputes, and electronic discovery counseling.

Mr. Thornburg is an active member of the Florida Bar. He currently serves on the Executive Counsel of the Business Law Section, where he is the Vice Chair of the Intellectual Property Law Committee. He is also a past Chair of the section’s Computer Law Committee. Additionally, he serves on the Florida Supreme Court Trial Technology Committee, and the Florida Bar Civil Rules Subcommittee on Electronic Discovery. An avid Gator, Mr. Thornburg is a member of the executive committee of the University of Florida Law Alumni Counsel.

Mr. Thornburg is an active lecturer on topics relating to intellectual property and electronic discovery and has served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Florida College of Law, Florida State University College of Law, and the University of Notre Dame College of Engineering. He also has participated in various panels, including Thomson LegalWorks’ 2006 A-Z Electronic Discovery in Miami. While in law school, he served as Vice-Chair of the Moot Court Board, Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of Technology Law & Policy, and President of the Florida Intellectual Property Law Association.

attorneys.name: Robert G. Thornhill III
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Winter Haven, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tri Thornhill was born and raised in Winter Haven. He has lived in Polk County almost his entire life. He is a sixth generation Floridian. He is Florida Bar Board Certified in Civil Trial law. This is the highest level of recognition by The Florida Bar of the competency and experience of attorneys approved for certification by the Supreme Court of Florida. He is AV rated by Martindale Hubbell, the highest professionalism and ethical rating from the nationally recognized service for rating lawyers.

Tri currently serves as chair of the 10th Judicial Circuit Professionalism Committee, which was formed by the Florida Supreme Court to receive, screen, and act upon complaints of unprofessional conduct by attorneys. Tri served as a member and the Chair of the Grievance Committee for the Florida Bar, a committee that evaluates ethical complaints against lawyers in the Tenth Judicial Circuit. In the past, Tri has served as a reader for the Florida Bar examination essays. He also serves as Inn Administrator for the Willson American Inn of Court, an invitation only association of lawyers and judges of the Tenth Judicial Circuit. Tri is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates.

With respect to charitable work, Tri is a member of Kiwanis Club of Lakeland. He is a volunteer for the Justice Teaching program which teaches the judicial system to middle school children. Tri delivers groceries to home bound seniors through VISTE, a Lakeland organization that serves the elderly. He is a member of St. Paul Lutheran Church.

Tri graduated second in his class from the University of Florida School of Law, was on Law Review, received the Book Award for Torts, Contracts, and Property, and received Order of the Coif. He was magna cum laude from Dartmouth College and second in his class from Winter Haven Senior High. Prior to working at Howell & Thornhill, Tri worked as a law clerk for Judge Federico Moreno, the Chief Judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida. Tri is admitted to practice in all Florida state courts, United States District Court for the Middle District of Florida, United States District Court for the Southern District of Florida, and the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals.

When he is not mowing or pressure washing, he enjoys running and triathlons.

attorneys.name: Jana K. Thornbury
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jana Thornbury grew up in Sarasota, Florida, and has lived in Florida all of her life. She graduated Magna Cum Laude from Florida Atlantic University with a degree in Economics in 2006. She earned her Juris Doctorate in 2009 from Florida State University College of Law. During law school, she interned for the Office of the State Attorney, Second Judicial Circuit.

Ms. Thornbury‘s experience after law school included representing banks and financial institutions in creditors' rights proceedings. During her time litigating foreclosure actions, Ms. Thornbury tried over 100 non-jury trials across the State of Florida.

Acting on a desire to change course and begin representing individuals, she began litigating property insurance claims on behalf of homeowners, including those related to sinkhole damage. In 2014, she began working for a local law firm representing individuals in personal injury matters including wrongful death, premises liability, and auto negligence. She is proud to continue representing and fighting for the rights of injured individuals as an attorney with Morgan & Morgan.

attorneys.name: Jessica L. Thorson
attorneys.practice_type: Business Tort Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Jessica Thorson represents clients in state and federal courts throughout the country and has significant experience in complex litigation involving business torts, contract disputes, intellectual property rights, civil rights, and disability discrimination, among others. She also has extensive experience handling civil appeals brought in the United States Court of Appeals for the Second, Eleventh, and Federal Circuits, as well as Florida's District Courts of Appeal.

Prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, P.A., Ms. Thorson worked as an intern for the Juvenile Advocacy Clinic at the University of Florida where she represented children in delinquency and dependency cases. She also worked as an intern for the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Florida and Pasco County Attorney's Office. She earned her Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Florida, Levin College of Law with honors. While at the University of Florida, she was elected to the Order of the Coif and received a certificate for her pro bono work.

attorneys.name: Vivianna Tijerino
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Vivianna Tijerino is the daughter of Nicaraguan and Colombian immigrants. She attended Florida State University, where she graduated summa cum laude with a degree in psychology. Her volunteer work with National Voices for Equality, Education, and Enlightenment (“NVEEE”), where she supported underserved communities as the Director of Mentoring Services, fueled her passion for social justice and human rights.

She then attended Florida International University College of Law, where she graduated cum laude. While attending law school, Ms. Tijerino participated in the Immigration and Human Rights Clinic, led by Attorney Juan Carlos Gomez, where she gained valuable experience on how the immigration system works.

Being the child of immigrants, Ms. Tijerino is dedicated to defending the immigrant community. She is fluent in English and Spanish.

attorneys.name: Alexandra N. Tosado
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
As an Orlando-native, of Hispanic descent, Alexandra Tosado decided to pursue her passion in law in the beautiful city she was born and raised. She attended the University of Central Florida where she graduated with honors with a bachelor's degree in Legal Studies. During her undergraduate studies, she gained experience helping people as she handled, probate matters, and family law matters, at a law firm while attending school. She then was recruited as an "all-star" to attend Florida A&M University College of Law with a scholarship due to her high academics and testing scores. During her studies in law school, she became passionate about trial after taking a course in "trial practice" and decided she wanted to continue helping people and pursue her dreams of becoming a trial lawyer.

She interned with a criminal defense firm working on high-profile cases, and also participated in a criminal defense clinic where she successfully represented over 100 indigent defendants assisting them in defending their constitutional rights.

Alexandra has also earned experience helping injured people, working at a small personal injury law firm in central Florida for eight years. There, she worked on complex litigation cases including car accident cases, traumatic brain injury cases, and wrongful death cases.

Alexandra's passion for the community has been recognized by the Hispanic community as she has received awards for being the "Youngest Hispanic Business Professional," and has been a member of the Hispanic American Law Student Association, the Orange County Bar Association, and the Hispanic American Professional Business Woman Association. In addition, she has been involved with non-profit Organization United Way for several years, participating with various charity and volunteering events.

On her free time, Ms. Tosado enjoys the outdoors, yoga, and cooking. As an associate at Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Tosado will continue her passion helping people, and representing those who are unable to represent themselves.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Youngest Hispanic Business Professional

attorneys.bio:
Adrienn N. Toth is an attorney in Morgan & Morgan's Orlando office. She was born in Budapest, Hungary, but has resided in Orlando, Florida most of her life. She received her undergraduate degree from the University of Central Florida in legal studies. She began her legal career at the age of 18 working for a small personal injury firm, helping injured people. She went on to attend Barry University School of Law, where she gained valuable courtroom and trial experience as a certified legal intern for the Office of the State Attorney for the Ninth Judicial Circuit.

After graduating from law school, and prior to joining Morgan & Morgan, Ms. Toth worked for Florida's largest insurance defense firm where she focused primarily on motor vehicle accident and premises liability claims. While defending corporations and insurance companies, she gained valuable insight and experience which she now uses to fight for her clients who have been injured.

attorneys.bio:
Mark A. Touby is the managing partner of Touby, Chait & Sicking, PL in Coral Gables, Florida. He earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Finance from the University of Florida in 1992 and received a Juris Doctor from the University of Miami in 1995. Mr. Touby is Board Certified in Workers’ Compensation and has been representing claimants since 1995. He is rated AV Preeminent 5.0/5.0 by Martindale-Hubbell, AVVO rated 10.0/10.0 and was recognized as a Rising Star in Florida Super Lawyers Magazine in 2009 and as a Super Lawyer in 2015. Mr. Touby has served on the Board of Directors of Florida Workers’ Advocates since 2003. He currently serves on the Executive Council of the Workers' Compensation Section of the Florida Bar. He served as Chair of the Workers' Compensation Rules Advisory Committee from 2014-2015. In addition, Mr. Touby serves as a trustee and Vice-President of Fundraising for the Friends of 440 Scholarship Fund. He has served as President of the Friends of 440, Inc. from 2009-2010 and Vice-Chair of the Dade County Bar Association Workers’ Compensation Committee from 2009-2013. Mr. Touby is a frequent lecturer and his practice also includes Unemployment Appeals, Social Security Disability and Personal Injury cases.

attorneys.name: Clay M. Townsend
attorneys.practice_type: Entertainment Law Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Clay Townsend was born in Jackson, MS, July 12, 1955. He was raised in Orlando, Florida and graduated from Boone High School in 1973. He graduated from the University of Florida in 1978, cum laude, and from the University of Florida Law School, cum laude, in 1982 where he was a member of Florida Blue Key and the Alpha Tau Omega Fraternity. Mr. Townsend also studied English common law at St. Edmonds Hall, Oxford University, England in 1979.

Mr. Townsend formed the law firm of Griffin, Morgan, Linder and Townsend, P.A. in 1985 with John Morgan. He has represented clients in personal injury claims, as well as commercial, entertainment, and intellectual property litigation in multiple jurisdictions - state and federal - resulting in numerous million-dollar-plus verdicts, judgments, and settlements. Mr. Townsend has handled such high-profile cases, including suit against Britney Spears by her former manager, suit by the Backstreet Boys against their former manager, suit by Harlem Globetrotters legends like Curly Neal and Meadowlark Lemon against The Harlem Globetrotters, intellectual property cases for Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones, and suit against Steven Spielberg regarding the iconic "Rear Window" to name a few.

Mr. Townsend's recent verdicts include a $17.5 million judgment in October 2014 after an almost 3-week long trial in Orange County, Florida (Good Gateway, LLC and SEG Gateway, LLC v. Orlando Gateway Partners, LLC, et al) and a $900,000.00 verdict in June 2015 after a one-week trial (Blackwell v. Simmons) in West Palm Beach County, Florida.

He is active in a variety of community activities, including the Boone High School Athletic Board, President of the Gator Football Parents Association, being a founding member of The Orlando Shakespeare Festival, SunTrust Advisory Board, social chairman of The Orange County Bar Association and host/sponsor for 28 years of Central Florida's Largest educational living history event - The Battle of Townsend's Plantation - a Civil War re-enactment.

He founded Townsend's Fish House and Tavern, a restaurant and night club, which he owned and operated from 1980 - 2000. He also developed the historic Townsend's Plantation in Apopka, Florida, the site of numerous outdoor music festivals featuring national acts. Mr. Townsend has also managed artists, written and produced a play, "Your Humble Servant, Samuel Johnson," and composed the original music.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Brandon, FL
attorneys.bio:
Christine Thornhill graduated from Florida Southern College in 1997, and then went on to graduate in 2001 with her Juris Doctorate from St. Thomas University School of Law in 2001.

She was sworn into the Florida Bar in September 11, 2001, and accepted into the U.S. District Court, Middle District of Florida in 2003. She is also a member of the American Business Women's Association and the Winter Haven Women's Bar Association.

Ms. Thornhill also volunteers as a Guardian Attorney Ad litem for abused, abandoned, or neglected children as well as in family law matters and as an Attorney Ad Litem - Teen Court Judge.

After passing the bar, her career began at the Public Defender's Office of the Tenth Judicial Circuit serving Polk, Highlands, and Hardee counties where she practiced criminal defense representing clients accused of misdemeanors and felonies.

In 2005, she opened her own law firm and renewed her love of family law from law school. Ms. Thornhill has a passion for practicing family law and advising clients on their rights, protecting their interests, and promoting a healthy future. She devotes the time and patience to help people face these life challenges inside and out of the courtroom. She assists clients in thinking ahead and plan for potential complications down the road. Planning and protecting yourself now leads to a smooth transition and minimizes future conflict.

Ms. Thornhill also works on other issues issues including divorce, alimony, child custody, child visitation or timesharing, child support, paternity, child relocation, name changes, etc.

Let Christine Thornhill use her expertise to help guide you through the tough decisions of your family law matter.

attorneys.name: Andrew V. Tramont
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Litigation Lawyers in Coral Gables, FL
attorneys.bio:
Over more than four decades, Andrew Tramont has successfully represented both plaintiffs and defendants, securing favorable verdicts and settlements in numerous multi-million-dollar actions in state and federal courts, as well as arbitration forums throughout the United States. As plaintiffs' counsel, he has recovered tens of millions of dollars from accounting firms in audit malpractice cases, including a $14.5 million verdict in Mississippi federal court against accounting giant Ernst & Young after a one-month jury trial, which was affirmed by the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. His insurance litigation practice includes victories and successful settlements on claims of bad faith, failure to defend, and breach of contract arising from insurers’ refusal to honor personal insurance policies. Mr. Tramont has also represented businesses and homeowners in major property and casualty litigation resulting from hurricane disasters and other forms of property damage, obtaining verdicts at both the trial and appellate levels.

Mr. Tramont has been recognized as a “Top Attorney in Florida” by the Miami Herald, Tampa Bay Magazine, and Orlando Life Magazine, a “Top Rated Lawyer in Insurance Law” by American Lawyer Magazine, and a “Super Lawyer in Insurance Coverage” by Super Lawyers Magazine. He is designated “AV/Preeminent” by Martindale-Hubbell—the organization’s highest rating for professional excellence and ethical standards—and “10 out of 10 / Superb” by AVVO.

In addition to heading the firm’s Insurance Practice section, Mr. Tramont advocates on behalf of investors in individual and class-action securities litigation and arbitrations nationwide. His successes include a multi-million-dollar recovery from Citigroup/Smith Barney for an elderly investor following an eight-day arbitration hearing in California, as well as a multi-million-dollar settlement on behalf of 220 clients following the prosecution of multiple securities cases in the state and federal courts of Florida.

Mr. Tramont also represents clients in discrimination cases, successfully prosecuting and defending wrongful termination claims in federal and state courts involving gender, disability, and racial bias, as well as racially hostile work environments. He also represents individuals pursuing claims against employers for failure to pay overtime compensation.

In addition to his trial practice, Mr. Tramont serves as an arbitrator for both the American Arbitration Association and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority.

He is licensed to practice in New York, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, and Wyoming and is active in numerous state and federal bar organizations. He is a member of the American Bar Association’s Tort, Trial and Insurance Practices Section, and the New York Bar’s Trial Lawyers Section. He currently serves on the Florida Bar’s Professional Ethics Committee and has previously chaired the Florida Bar’s Judicial Administration and Evaluation Committee, as well as served on The Florida Bar’s Professionalism Committee. Mr. Tramont is also active in pro bono work, representing indigent litigants in cases involving violations of their federal and state civil rights.

Mr. Truppman has been an AV Preeminent rated trial lawyer since 1994 and was named a “Super Lawyer “ by his peers in 2021.

Mr. Truppman’s areas of specialty include all areas of insurance law including first party residential and commercial property insurance claims for windstorm, fire, water, collapse, theft, marine, bad faith and catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death. He has been litigating insurance claims on behalf of insureds against their insurance companies for 35 years.

attorneys.name: Jason Turchin Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Weston, FL
attorneys.bio:
Fort Lauderdale Personal Injury Attorney Jason Turchin has handled more than 5,500 cases, including personal injury, accident, medical malpractice, wrongful death and crime victim's rights. The firm expanded to better serve our client's needs and now handles cases involving commercial litigation, probate litigation, probate administration, commercial debt collection, commercial and residential leases and landlord-tenant disputes.

Ft Lauderdale Accident Lawyer Jason Turchin started his legal career as a contract analyst on the MCI-WorldCom merger in Washington DC. He then worked as an investigative legal assistant at Steir, Anderson and Malone handling civil RICO claims and white collar crime investigations. Jason then attended law school at University of Miami School of Law. During law school, Jason was retained as a computer crime investigator by Roy Black's firm Black, Srebnick, Kornspan and Stumpf to investigate and defeat an allegation of cybercrime by another attorney. After their client was acquitted, he was hired as an associate and worked on both civil and criminal high profile cases.

During the 6 years following his work with Roy Black, Jason Turchin worked at Bernstein and Maryanoff where he handled personal injury, accident and wrongful death cases. As a victim's rights advocate, Jason carved out a niche handling civil DUI cases on behalf of accident victims, and representing victims of molestation, rape and murder in civil claims.

Today, Jason represents clients throughout Fort Lauderdale and Florida, and in New York and Washington DC at the Law Offices of Jason Turchin.

At the Law Offices of Jason Turchin, we handle the following cases:

Motor Vehicle Accidents: car accident, truck accident, scooter accident, taxi accident, bus injuries, uninsured motorist claims

Wrongful Death: Fatal car accident, medical malpractice, pool drowning, nursing home neglect, murder victims

Cruise Injuries: Carnival, Royal Caribbean, Celebrity, Disney, Norwegian, Discovery

Personal Injury: Slip and fall, food poisoning, general negligence, trip and fall, pharmacy errors

Medical Malpractice: misdiagnosis, birth injuries, x-ray misreads, items left in patients, operation on wrong areas

Nursing Home Abuse

Crime Victim's Rights: rape, molestation, sexual assault, murder victim

Probate: Probate litigation, will drafting, probate administration

Life Insurance Disputes

attorneys.name: Daniel W. Uhlfelder
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Santa Rosa Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
A seasoned attorney with over 25 years of legal experience, Daniel W. Uhlfelder excels at representing clients with complex civil litigation and other general legal matters. Daniel has a general practice law firm located on Scenic Highway 30-A in Walton County, Florida, establishing it after working nationwide for various prestigious law firms.

Mr. Uhlfelder graduated from Stanford University in three years with a B.A. in History in 1993. After graduating from Stanford, he attended the University of Florida College of Law and the Georgetown University Law Center as a visiting law student. Mr. Uhlfelder received his J.D. from the University of Florida College of Law in 1996.

While in law school and as an undergraduate, Mr. Uhlfelder served as a law clerk, summer associate and staff aide in the White House, the United States Attorney General's Office, the United States Senate, the United States House of Representatives, and at various law firms in Florida and Washington, D.C. including Greenberg Traurig, LLP, Hopping, Green & Sams, P.A., and the Robert Augustus Harper Law Firm, P.A.

After graduating from law school, Mr. Uhlfelder served as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable Donald M. Middlebrooks, United States District Court Judge for the Southern District of Florida in Miami, Florida. After completing his judicial clerkship with Judge Middlebrooks, Mr. Uhlfelder spent two years as a trial attorney with a top trial law firm, Colson, Hicks, Eidson in Miami. He handled products liability, personal injury, commercial, and criminal matters while working at Colson, Hicks, Eidson.

Mr. Uhlfelder is a long term resident of North Florida and is dedicated to serving his community. He takes a significant number of matters to trial each year. As such, he is highly skilled and efficient in conducting the strategic and tactical preparations that can make or break a case. He handles a wide variety of legal matters for businesses and individuals in Northwest Florida. His practice focuses primarily in the areas of civil and commercial litigation, construction litigation, divorce and family law, real estate, personal injury, and criminal law.

He is the first non-minority member of the Okaloosa County Branch of the NAACP, serving as Chair of the Legal Redress Committee. He was recently awarded the NAACP's Foot Soldier in the Sand Award by the NAACP for his work in the area of civil rights.

Mr. Uhlfelder was a member of the Florida Bar's First Circuit Unlicensed Practice of Law Committee. He was appointed by Governor Bush to the newly created Committee for a Sustainable Emerald Coast.

Mr. Uhlfelder is a member of the University of Florida Levin College of Law Alumni Council.

Mr. Uhlfelder is actively involved in his community serving as counsel for the Catherine Cole Taylor Center for the Arts. He and his wife, the parents of two young children, volunteer and serve on the board of directors of numerous Walton County local education and charity organizations.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Zahra Umansky was a former Assistant Public Defender in the 18th judicial circuit in Brevard and Seminole Counties. As a former Public Defender, Zahra was involved in over a hundred criminal trials that included crimes such as theft, assault, prostitution, drugs trafficking, DUI, and many other felonies and misdemeanors offense. She protected her client's right to liberty and secured countless not guilty verdicts and judgments of acquittal. After Zahra left the Public Defender's office, she was appointed by Mayor Glenda Hood as the prosecutor for the City of Orlando.

As City Prosecutor, Zahra was successful in the implementation and prosecution of many types of criminal matters and also served as the prosecutor before the City's Nuisance Abatement Board. She was also a legal advisor to local law enforcement officials where she trained police officers in matters of search and seizure laws, Miranda laws, and other constitutional rights. She also reviewed search warrants, wiretap applications, and gave police last minute advice they needed before they made arrests. During her time as City Prosecutor, Zahra was appointed as Special Assistant State Attorney for the Ninth judicial circuit.

Zahra’s unique experience as a former prosecutor and legal advisor, gives Zahra the ability to evaluate your case from both sides of the law. As a former police legal advisor, she understands how the Police investigate and secure their evidence and as a former prosecutor, understands how the State of Florida will present their case in court against you. Zahra approaches each case with aggressive and diligent representation. She is dedicated to defending the rights of her clients and committed to treating every client with the dignity and respect they deserve.

Zahra Umansky was a former Assistant Public Defender in the 18th judicial circuit in Brevard and Seminole Counties. As a former Public Defender, Zahra was involved in over a hundred criminal trials that included crimes such as theft, assault, prostitution, drugs trafficking, DUI, and many other felonies and misdemeanors offense. She protected her client's right to liberty and secured countless not guilty verdicts and judgments of acquittal. After Zahra left the Public Defender's office, she was appointed by Mayor Glenda Hood as the prosecutor for the City of Orlando.

As City Prosecutor, Zahra was successful in the implementation and prosecution of many types of criminal matters and also served as the prosecutor before the City's Nuisance Abatement Board. She was also a legal advisor to local law enforcement officials where she trained police officers in matters of search and seizure laws, Miranda laws, and other constitutional rights. She also reviewed search warrants, wiretap applications, and gave police last minute advice they needed before they made arrests. During her time as City Prosecutor, Zahra was appointed as Special Assistant State Attorney for the Ninth judicial circuit.

Zahra’s unique experience as a former prosecutor and legal advisor, gives Zahra the ability to evaluate your case from both sides of the law. As a former police legal advisor, she understands how the Police investigate and secure their evidence and as a former prosecutor, understands how the State of Florida will present their case in court against you. Zahra approaches each case with aggressive and diligent representation. She is dedicated to defending the rights of her clients and committed to treating every client with the dignity and respect they deserve.

Schedule a free case review with Zahra today!

attorneys.name: William D. Umansky
attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
William D. Umansky or "The Lawman" as he is affectionately known by his peers has almost two decades of experience offering "Second Chances" to clients who have either been injured as a result of someone else's negligence or who have, unfortunately, been charged with a crime. His practice is based in Central Florida and he advocates for his clients throughout Florida. He is the Managing Partner of the Umansky Law Firm where he directs a team of lawyers dedicated to success and to working hard to try and achieve the results the firm's client's desire. He has appeared or been quoted in many national media outlets including USA Today, The Wall Street Journal, Newsweek, People Magazine, NBC, CBS, ABC and FOX affiliates around the country. Recently, Bill was named a Top Criminal Lawyer by Orlando Home and Leisure Magazine. Bill is a lawyer, entrepreneur, business owner and number one Amazon best selling author of "Power Principles of Success".

Bill's practice is focused on providing his clients with "second chances" and Bill prides himself on working hard to see that people who are injured are given compensation to begin their journey towards a new and better life-- a life they can begin as masters of their own destiny, not merely as victims of circumstance. Bill handles all personal injury cases including car accidents, truck accidents, motorcycle accidents, sex abuse, negligent security, slip and fall and premise liability cases.

View Recent Case Results

Additionally, Bill has helped numerous people who have become entrenched in the Criminal Justice system after being caught making a mistake. He makes it his mission to provide his clients with the second chance they deserve by getting the charges dropped or reduced. In every case he serves as not just a lawyer but also a counselor, giving his clients the guidance they need to address their particular problem, such as drug or alcohol abuse, so they do not find themselves in trouble again. He has handled all types of Felony, Misdemeanor and Ordinance charges including cases involving drunk driving, drug sale or possession, trafficking, prostitution, mortgage fraud, theft, shoplifting, false imprisonment, ponzi schemes, suspended licenses, battery, domestic violence, obstruction charges and many others.

Bill honed his skills as an attorney by serving as Assistant State Attorney in Florida as well as The City Prosecutor for the City of Orlando. As a prosecutor, Bill gained invaluable experience trying a voluminous number of cases. In addition to working as a prosecutor and criminal defense lawyer, he also worked for two of the most preeminent Personal Injury law firms in Orlando prior to opening his own law firm. Bill has extensive courtroom experience and won't hesitate to try a client's case, when necessary, to try and attain the results his clients need. Bill has an active "mock courtroom" at his office that he uses to prepare his clients to overcome the stress of attending court and to prepare their cases to win.

Bill graduated cum laude from the University of South Florida with a bachelor's degree in Psychology and obtained a law degree from the University of Florida College of Law. During law school, Bill was a member of the University of Florida Trial Team and received a Certificate of Recognition for Outstanding Contribution to the University of Florida Law School. He also earned an award for achieving the top grade for his work in Negotiations and Dispute Settlement. Mr. Umansky also attended the Tulane Institute of European Legal Studies.

In addition to his role as a lawyer, Bill has been involved with teaching others about the law. He has also been a Police Academy Instructor, former Police Legal Advisor, an Adjunct Professor at Florida Metropolitan University and a Legislative Assistant to a United States Senator.

Bill Umansky is active in the Orlando community. He is currently on the Board of Directors for the Orange County Bar Association, Teen Court and Teen Alternatives, Inc. and previously served as a board member for the YMCA of Central Florida, Rotary Club of Avalon Park and the Orange County Legal Aid Society. Bill is actively involved in a number of legal organizations including The Florida Justice Association and Central Florida Trial Attorney Association. Aside from his legal contributions, Bill has served the youth of the community coaching and serving as a volunteer for youth soccer, basketball and football teams in the Orlando area.

Bill is married to his wife Zahra Umansky, who is also an accomplished criminal trial lawyer, and he is the proud father of two great boys. He lives life with the motto of "Carpe Diem" and truly believes that every day needs to be lived to its fullest with passion and intensity-- because every day could be the last day one has on earth.

attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Vero Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Savannah Jordan Harris Unruh has family roots in Vero Beach stretching back over a century. She graduated from the University of Florida a year early, summa cum laude. While there she received the distinction of the Michael G. Hauptman Medal for excellence, which is awarded to the top student in each department, thanks to her honor's thesis, and was also inducted into the Phi Beta Kappa Society. Following in the footsteps of both her mother and grandfather, Savannah then attended the University of Florida Levin College of Law. After earning her Juris Doctor she returned to Vero Beach, joining Block & Scarpa's Civil Litigation department. Savannah’s practice area focuses on general civil litigation and dispute resolution, including successful representation at the appellate level.

Savannah is also very involved in the community and recognizes the importance of civic service, devoting time as a Director of the Scholarship Foundation of Indian River County, a program that awards lifechanging financial support to students pursuing higher education, and as a Founding Partner of the Gifford Legal Services Clinic, which provides pro bono legal services to the indigent.

attorneys.name: John L. Urban
attorneys.practice_type: Business, Commercial and Civil Litigation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
John L. Urban is a founding shareholder of Urban Thier & Federer, P.A., and managing shareholder of the law firm's Orlando office. He is based in Orlando and also works out of the offices in Atlanta, New York and London. Mr. Urban focuses his practice on civil litigation in business and contract disputes, commercial law, debt collection, recognition and enforcement of foreign court decisions, international law, real estate law, wills/probate law, significant personal injury and wrongful death matters. He has handled all manner of litigation cases including trials, appellate cases and arbitration proceedings. He has served as the lead attorney for over 500 federal court lawsuits and over 100 state court lawsuits, as well as numerous appeals in federal and state appellate courts, throughout the United States. These appearances include appearing as lead attorney in the Supreme Court of the United States, in multiple federal Circuit Courts of Appeal, in multiple state courts of appeal, in trial courts throughout the United States, and arbitration proceedings before the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), the American Arbitration Association (AAA), and other arbitration organizations.

Mr. Urban is a member of the State Bars of Florida, New York, and Georgia, the Bar of the Supreme Court of the United States, the Bar of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit, the United States District Courts for the Southern, Middle, and Northern Districts of Florida, and the United States Bankruptcy Courts for the Southern, Middle, and Northern Districts of Florida. He is also a licensed foreign lawyer with the United Kingdom's Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA). Additionally, he has appeared pro hac vice (temporary admission) as lead attorney in multiple other jurisdictions, including Texas, California, Washington and others.

attorneys.name: Scott J. Uricchio
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Scott Uricchio was Born in Coral Gables, FL in 1965. He was the youngest of 3 children.

Mr. Uricchio grew up in Orlando and Winter Park, graduating from Trinity Preparatory School in 1983. He established his roots in the local area with family and friends who have gone on to become local leaders and representatives in medical, legal and community activities throughout Central Florida.

After graduating from the Florida State University College of Communications in 1989, Mr. Uricchio explored advancements in Orlando's budding film and production industry. He eventually took the opportunity to rely on his legal and medical heritage and pursue a career in law. Mr. Uricchio graduated from St. Thomas University Law School in 1995 and returned to Central Florida where he began his legal career representing wronged individuals against responsible parties. From his first day of legal practice, Mr. Uricchio has only represented injured individuals and families. His strong local ties and family history inspired him to establish his own law firm in 1997, where he honed his practice representing solely injured people who were the victim of injuries resulting from motor vehicle accidents, workplace defects, negligent security and products liability.

In 2001, Mr. Uricchio joined his practice with Morgan & Morgan. He has continued to fight against improper insurance company denials. The majority of Mr. Uricchio's practice at Morgan & Morgan has focused on representing injured workers and helping them navigate Florida's complex and ever-changing Workers' Compensation system.

Mr. Uricchio's background and roots in Central Florida, from Tampa to Daytona Beach and from Ocala across to Melbourne, have provided a unique and enhanced perspective that he will bring in representing victims rights an arena where the innocent are oftentimes treated unfairly. He continues in his efforts to represent victims against those responsible for the damage done.

attorneys.name: Arturo Uzdavinis
attorneys.practice_type: Real estate Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Arturo is one of the founding partners of Bonardi & Uzdavinis, LLP. His practice areas include real estate, construction, personal injury, and business litigation. Prior to founding Bonardi & Uzdavinis alongside Daniel Bonardi, Arturo started his early practice working at two highly regarded boutique law firms and had the distinct pleasure of gaining invaluable experience under the tutelage of several attorneys regarded as some of the most elite trial attorneys in their respective practice areas across three states. Now, Arturo focuses on zealously representing individuals and corporations in the Tampa Bay Area, and throughout the State of Florida.

Arturo earned his Juris Doctor degree, graduating cum laude from Barry University School of Law. Prior to law school, he spent two years playing offensive tackle for several National Football League organizations. He also graduated from and played football at Tulane University in New Orleans, Louisiana. Arturo is a Tampa native who attended Jesuit High School and returned to the Tampa Bay Area after law school to get back to his roots and community.

Arturo is a Spanish-speaker who comes from a pedigree of distinguished attorneys in Puerto Rico. His grandfather, Hector Reichard de Cardona, former attorney general of Puerto Rico, continues to practice at the law firm he founded nearly 40 years ago and built upon the foundational principles that have been passed on to Arturo since childhood when Arturo would stand in Mr. Reichard’s office with visions of one day continuing the legacy.

When not at work, Arturo enjoys nothing more than spending time with his wife and children. He is a member of the Tampa Jesuit Bar Association, National Football League Players’ Association, and Knights of Columbus.

attorneys.name: Basil A. Valdivia
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Orlando, FL
attorneys.bio:
Basil Valdivia began his Legal career with the City of Orlando in 1992, when he was appointed Special Assistant Police Legal Advisor/City Prosecutor. In 1993 Mr. Valdivia accepted a position to serve as an Assistant State attorney for the Ninth Judicial Circuit serving Orange and Osceola County. During the six years with the State Attorney's Office Mr. Valdivia served in many capacities from Osceola County Juvenile Division Prosecutor; Orange County Felony Trial Division; and Sex Crimes Unit Prosecutor. As a prosecutor, Mr. Valdivia successfully prosecuted hundreds of cases and had over one hundred trials.

In 1999 Mr. Valdivia was appointed by Gov. Jeb Bush to serve on the Capital Punishment Commission. The Commission's task was to look at the Death Penalty as it was applied in Florida and to make recommendations. The Commission after many meetings and hours of testimony made recommendations some of which were enacted by the Florida legislature in the following legislative session.

Mr. Valdivia Joined the firm of Morgan and Morgan in 1999, where he has been able to help hundreds of clients who have been injured. Mr. Valdivia currently heads the Workers' Compensation Department for the Orlando office. Mr. Valdivia has continued to be involved in public service by being a member of and serving on the boards of non-profits agencies. Mr. Valdivia lives in Windermere, Florida with his wife Emily Raleen Huhne and their two children Isabella, and Henry.

attorneys.name: George A. Vaka
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
George A. Vaka has been practicing since 1983. He has long been honored by his peers as one of the "Best Lawyers in America," and in 2014, 2017, 2019 and 2023 was named "Lawyer of the Year" for insurance law by that same organization. He has been an "AV Rated Preeminent Lawyer" by Martindale-Hubbell for more than twenty-five consecutive years, and has been recognized as a "Florida Super Lawyer" in both appellate practice and insurance law. Mr. Vaka was named a Fellow of the American College of Coverage and Extracontractual Counsel, a privilege bestowed on less than 300 attorneys nationwide. He has been recognized as "Legal Elite" for his years of work and superior legal accomplishments. Mr. Vaka is a member of "The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100 Trial Lawyers;" an invitation-only, nationwide organization that extends membership to only the select few of the most qualified attorneys from each state who exemplify superior qualifications of leadership, reputation, influence, stature and profile as a civil plaintiff trial lawyer. His reputation as a legal expert began when he was defending Fortune 500 companies and the insurance industry at trial and appellate levels. He has represented clients in a wide variety of civil legal matters ranging from mass tort product liability cases, medical device litigation, aircraft disasters, environmental torts to medical malpractice. His representation of insurance companies was likewise diverse ranging from automobile insurance, professional liability insurance to petroleum and environmental cleanups, just to name a few.

Mr. Vaka's reputation as a legal expert grew when he was able to dedicate his practice to his passion for helping others. His practice is now limited to representing small businesses and individuals who often find themselves in "David vs. Goliath" disputes against corporate and insurance company giants. He has frequently volunteered his assistance to colleagues and peers and shared his legal acumen through presentations in the classroom and the publication of numerous articles on a statewide and national level. Mr. Vaka has been recognized in Florida courts as an expert in matters relating to torts, insurance and appellate practice. In addition, he is a circuit court and appellate court mediator certified by the Florida Supreme Court and appointed by the United States District Court.

Mr. Vaka is also recognized as a leader outside the courtroom. When elected President of the Florida Defense Lawyers Association; he was, at the time, the youngest person selected for the honor. His colleagues in the Plaintiffs' bar also recognized his leadership skills appointing him to the Board of Directors and Chair of the Appellate Practice Section of the Academy of the Florida Trial Lawyers for three consecutive years. Mr. Vaka's experience serving at the executive board level of Florida's two largest and competing trial lawyer associations is unique among Florida's trial bar.

Most telling of his reputation is the frequent description of him by his colleagues as a "Lawyer's Lawyer," a compliment recognizing his superior legal skills and extraordinary professionalism.

Mrs. Valente has been admitted to practice in Florida for more than 30 years. She started in a general civil practice before focusing for many years on worker's compensation cases, first from a defense standpoint and then from a claimant's perspective. During her tenure as a Worker's Compensation claimant's lawyer, Karen tried or resolved four cases for over one million dollars and two for more than 3 million dollars. Settlements like these were taken away by the Florida legislature with changes to the workers compensations system and Karen refocused her practice to the handling of Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice, Defamation, and Commercial cases. A seasoned litigator, Karen has handled depositions of the highest level medical and expert witnesses and first chair trials of workers compensation and exposure cases. Karen is equally involved in the handling of all of the firm's largest medical malpractice, commercial, defamation and professional malpractice cases. Together with Philip Valente Jr. , they form the trial team for all of the firm's cases taken to trial.

attorneys.practice_type: Construction Litigation Lawyers in Jacksonville, FL
attorneys.bio:
Tracy began her carrier with this firm as a summer law clerk in 1997. She enjoyed her experience and learned so much during that summer that she has been a part of the firm ever since. After passing the Florida Bar she joined the firm as an associate in 1998 and became a shareholder of Heekin Litigation Group in January of 2004. Tracy’s practice includes representing businesses, both large and small, individuals and insurance companies. She has a broad range of experience in construction matters, real estate disputes, contract drafting and disputes, business litigation and franchise disputes. She also has experience representing both commercial and residential associations. She likes to say when asked about her practice areas, “unless you’ve been arrested, I can probably help you”.

Since 1998, Tracy has gained valuable experience representing clients through all phases of litigation, including bench and jury trials as well as numerous arbitrations and mediations. attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in West Palm Beach, FL
attorneys.bio:
Philip L. Valente Jr. is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law. He is the primary litigator for the firm and personally handles all aspects of the firm's pre-trial and trial cases. His focus is in civil trial matters involving complex personal injury cases and wrongful death claims including car crashes, accidents involving trucks, aviation crashes and medical malpractice cases.  He has successfully litigated against the country's strongest and most significant insurance companies as well as the state's best lawyers and biggest law firms.  In addition to injury cases, Mr. Valente also handles legal malpractice,

accountant malpractice and other professional malpractice cases.  He is regularly called upon by some of the state's finest lawyers to assist in litigating their cases.

Mr. Valente has a long track record of recovering million and multimillion-dollar settlements in state and federal court over a span of 30-plus years.  He has successfully prosecuted significant damages cases in Florida as well as Georgia and Oklahoma. Mr Valente also handles business cases, defamation cases, and first party insurance cases. He also provides yearly litigation and nonlitigation legal services to small and medium sized companies.

Mr. Valente was selected as one of the state's Super Lawyers, is AV rated by Martindale-Hubbell and carries a 9.8 rating with AVVO. He has been asked to join the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, and is a part of Legal Elite and Best Accident Lawyers.

While many lawyers can take a great case and get what it is worth, Mr. Valente and his wife and law partner Karen have a strong history taking on and winning cases that many lawyers have previously rejected. They are known for making the most out of every case they take on.

Mr. Valente represents local businesses and trades and formed a leads/networking group called Welleads. Welleads has produced in excess of 16 million dollars in gross sales among its members in just under 7 years.

attorneys.name: Leticia "Letty" Valdes
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Letty Valdes has been practicing law since 1992 and is admitted to the Florida Bar and the Washington, D.C. Bar. Ms. Valdes is a Board Certified Civil Trial Attorney, an honor that only a small percentage of lawyers achieve. In Florida, board certified lawyers are legal experts dedicated to professional excellence who are tested for expertise and have met rigorous standards for experience and professionalism set by the Florida Supreme Court.

Ms. Valdes graduated from Florida International University. She then attended Drake University Law School. She began her legal career as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Florida in Tallahassee. She then worked for ten years as an Assistant Attorney General in Washington, D.C. In 2006, she completed a program in negotiation and dispute resolution at the Harvard Law School Program on Negotiation. Following her government service, she worked for both Allstate and Travelers as a claims litigation attorney specializing in personal injury claims. She also worked for three years for a firm in Tampa where she represented hundreds of clients who were injured as a result of the negligence of others.

Ms. Valdes dedicates her practice to representing individuals and families that have been injured or lost a family member due to the negligence of others.

attorneys.name: Marcio W. Valladares
attorneys.practice_type: Class Action Lawyers in Tampa, FL
attorneys.bio:
Born in Managua, Nicaragua, Marcio Valladares emigrated to the United States during Nicaragua's civil war. In 1990, he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in psychology from the University of Florida. In 1993, he obtained his Juris Doctor degree, magna cum laude, from Florida State University. He is pursuing a Masters in Law (LL.M.) degree from Columbia University, focusing his studies in federal and comparative law.

Before joining Morgan & Morgan, Mr. Valladares worked in both the public and private sectors. For five years, he served as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable Steven D. Merryday, United States District Judge, Middle District of Florida. For two years, he served as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable Susan H. Black, United States Circuit Court Judge, Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. For five years, he served as an Assistant United States Attorney for the Middle District of Florida. In the private sector, he practiced commercial litigation and insurance defense at Holland & Knight LLP. Mr. Valladares also worked as in-house counsel for the Mayo Clinic.

Mr. Valladares served on the Florida Bar's Grievance Committee in Orange County (2011-2012) and was the Judicial Relations Chair for the Hispanic Bar Association of Central Florida (2009-2012).

He is fluent in English and Spanish. He brings his diverse experience and vantage to Morgan & Morgan's Complex Litigation Group, handling class actions, mass torts, complex litigation, and consumer protection cases.

attorneys.name: Peter F. Valori
attorneys.firm_name: Damian & Valori LLP | Culmo Trial Attorneys
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Miami, FL
attorneys.bio:
Peter F. Valori is the Managing Partner of Damian & Valori LLP. Mr. Valori focuses his practice on business litigation with a particular emphasis on complex corporate, contract, real estate, employment, professional negligence, and trademark litigation. He is a member of the Florida bar and is admitted to practice before the United States District Courts for the Southern, Middle and Northern Districts of Florida; the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Florida, and the United States Court of Appeals, Eleventh Circuit.

Mr. Valori is a Past President of the Miami Beach Bar Association. He is Past Chair of The Florida Bar Membership Committee, the Past Chair of The Florida Bar Communications Committee and the Past Chair of the Business Litigation Committee for The Florida Bar Business Law Section. He also served a Liaison from The Florida Bar Business Law Section Business Litigation Committee to Florida Bar Business Law Section E-Discovery Rules Committee. He is also the Past Chair of the Federal Courts Committee of the Dade County Bar. And, he is the Past Co-Chair of the Business Torts Subcommittee and Former Chair of the Newsletter Subcommittee for The American Bar Association Business Law Section’s Business and Corporate Litigation Committee. Mr. Valori is a frequent speaker and author on the topics of business torts and financial fraud litigation, non-compete agreements, injunctions, and electronic discovery.

Mr. Valori has been named as a Super Lawyer from 2006 to 2017; a Legal Elite lawyer by Florida Trend Magazine in 2006 to 2011 and 2017; and a Top Lawyer by South Florida Legal Guide in 2015. Mr. Valori has received an AV Preeminent® Rating from Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™.

Mr. Valori is a member of the Board of Directors and Chair of the Strategic Planning Committee of Educate Tomorrow, a non-profit organization dedicated to assisting youth-in-need to obtain higher education. Mr. Valori also represents abused and neglected children in dependency proceedings through Lawyers for Children America, Inc.

He graduated from Pennsylvania State University (B.S., 1991) and the University of Miami School of Law (J.D., magna cum laude, 1994) where he was a member of the University of Miami Law Review.

attorneys.name: Amy B. Van Fossen Esq.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Amy B. Van Fossen, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Melbourne, FL
attorneys.bio:
Amy B. Van Fossen established The Law Office of Amy B. Van Fossen P.A. (formerly The Law Office of Amy B. Jackson P.A.) in 2004. Amy was born and raised in southeastern Ohio and has two daughters, Katie, and Savannah, who both share her passion for our elder community. Savannah provides medical care to the elder community as an RN. Katie is a second-generation attorney, chairing the Probate, Medicaid & VA departments at the Law Office of Amy B. Van Fossen, P.A.

Ms. Van Fossen received her undergraduate degree in Organizational Behavior from Rollins College and earned her JD from Barry University School of Law in 2003. She is licensed to practice in Florida. Her firm practices in the areas of Estate Planning, Case Management, Guardianship, Probate and Trust Administration, VA Planning, Medicaid Planning, Trust Funding, and Civil Litigation.

Ms. Van Fossen is accredited by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs for the preparation and presentation of Aid and Attendance claims, making her one of the few VA accredited attorneys in Brevard County.

Ms. Van Fossen is a member of the Florida Bar Association; the Brevard County Bar Association; Elder Counsel; American Businesswomen’s Association; and the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys.

Amy’s personal interests involve our community’s youth, supporting those with special needs, and the rescue of animals. Locally, Ms. Van Fossen serves her community in each of these areas. Amy is an Emeritus member of the Board of Directors for Club Esteem, a youth organization with a mission to “inspire youth from economically disadvantaged communities to embrace the highest standards of academic and personal excellence.” (Mission Statement for Club Esteem) Amy also has a strong Business Partnership with Brevard County Schools, supporting our students through professional counseling and local sponsorship. One of her favorite adventures has been the sponsorship of a race car driver, 16-year-old Garrett Manes, who is working to achieve his dream while living with Autism. Her efforts extend to supporting many of our local animal shelters through events, fundraising and adoption advocacy.

attorneys.name: Christian Van Riper
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Stuart, FL
attorneys.bio:
Christian Van Riper – Criminal Defense, DUI, Civil Litigation, Family & Dependency Attorney

Christian Van Riper is a seasoned Florida trial attorney who brings exceptional experience, accessibility, and compassion to every case. He focuses his practice on criminal defense, DUI defense, family law, and dependency law, representing clients throughout the Treasure Coast and South Florida. Christian’s background as both a former Florida Prosecutor and a former investigator with the Department of Children and Families (DCF) gives him unique insight into the courtroom, law enforcement procedures, and the human side of the cases he handles.

As a Prosecutor, Christian litigated hundreds of criminal cases for the State of Florida and was quickly promoted from the misdemeanor to the felony division in under seven months—a testament to his skill and tenacity in the courtroom. He has successfully argued motions and appeals and has tried numerous jury and non-jury cases involving charges ranging from DUI, BUI (boating under the influence), drug offenses, and domestic violence to grand theft, arson, robbery, battery, and attempted murder. His ability to see cases from both sides makes him an effective and strategic advocate for those accused of crimes.

Before his time as a Prosecutor, Christian served as an intern for the Supreme Court of Florida, where he worked directly with the justices, analyzing petitions and advising on complex legal issues in both civil and criminal matters. Earlier still, as a DCF investigator, Christian handled child abuse and neglect cases, developing a deep understanding of family dynamics and the child welfare system. That investigative experience now serves him well in both family and dependency law cases, where protecting clients’ children and families is his top priority.

Known for his accessibility and dedication, Christian ensures that every client has his personal cell phone number, reflecting his belief that strong communication and trust are essential to effective representation. His clients appreciate his proactive approach, honesty, and ability to explain difficult legal issues in plain language.

Christian’s blend of courtroom experience, investigative skill, and personal commitment make him a powerful advocate, whether defending clients in criminal or DUI cases, guiding families through divorce and custody disputes, or protecting parents and children in dependency matters.

attorneys.name: Melora G. Vandersluis
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Oviedo, FL
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Melora G. Vandersluis has been a resident of Central Florida since 2012 and is a Florida Supreme Court certified mediator. She graduated cum laude from Barry University School of Law where she earned the distinction of "Outstanding Senior Editor" on Law Review and competed nationally while on the Moot Court Honors Board. She was awarded the highest grade in Torts I, Torts II, and Mediation. She completed an externship in federal court with The Honorable John Antoon II.

Prior to attending law school, she served in Higher Education for fifteen years as an English professor, department chair, and associate dean. Her work in university administration included strategic planning, personnel management, contract review, and compliance & control. She has published a number of articles, book chapters, and reviews.

Attorney Vandersluis currently serves in the Estate Planning Department at Vollrath Law, P.A. She and her husband have three children.
